Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Kaccāyanabyākaraṇaṃ

Kaccāyana's Grammar.

1. Sandhi

1. Euphonic Combination.

1, 1. Attho [M 0.0001] akkharasaññāto.

Meaning is known by letters.

2, 2. Akkharāpādayo ekacattālisaṃ.

The letters and so forth are forty-one.

3, 3 Tatthodantā sarā aṭṭha.

Therein, the vowels are eight.

4, 4. Lahumattā tayo rassā.

Three of light measure are short.

5, 5. Aññe dīghā.

The others are long.

6, 8. Sesā byañjanā.

The remaining are consonants.

7, 9. Vaggā pañcapañcaso mantā.

The classes are known as five by five.

8, 10. Aṃiti niggahitaṃ.

'Aṃ' is the niggahita.

9, 11. Parasamaññā payoge.

In application, the terminology of others [is used].

10, 12. Pubbamadhoṭhitamassaraṃ sarena viyojaye.

One should separate the preceding consonant, situated below, from the vowel.

11, 14. Naye paraṃ yutte.

One should join the subsequent when suitable.

Iti sandhikappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus, the first section in the chapter on Sandhi.

12, 13. Sarā [M 0.0002] sare lopaṃ.

A vowel is elided before a vowel.

13, 15. Vā paro asarūpo.

Optionally the subsequent, if not of the same form.

14, 16. Kvacāsavaṇṇaṃ lutte.

Sometimes, when a dissimilar vowel has been elided.

15, 17. Dīghaṃ.

[It becomes] long.

16, 18. Pubbo ca.

And the preceding [vowel is elided].

17, 19. Yamedantassādeso.

'Y' is the substitute for a final 'e'.

18, 20. Vamodudantānaṃ.

'V' is the substitute for those ending in 'o' and 'u'.

19. 22. Sabbo caṃ ti.

19. And every [vowel] becomes 'aṃ' [before 'ti'].

20, 27. Do dhassa ca.

And 'd' for 'dh'.

21, 22. Ivaṇṇo yaṃ navā.

The letter 'i' optionally becomes 'y'.

22, 28. Evādissa ri pubbo ca rasso.

For 'eva' and so forth, 'ri' [is the substitute for 'e'], and the preceding [vowel] becomes short.

Iti sandhikappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus, the second section in the chapter on Sandhi.

23, 36. Sarā pakati byañjane.

Vowels remain in their natural state before a consonant.

24, 35. Sare kvaci.

Sometimes before a vowel.

25, 37. Dīghaṃ.

[It becomes] long.

26, 38. Rassaṃ.

It becomes short.

27, 39. Lopañca tatrākāro.

And there, the letter 'ā' is elided.

28, 40. Para dvebhāvo ṭhāne.

The subsequent consonant is doubled in its place.

29, 42. Vagge ghosāghosānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā.

In a class, a voiced consonant becomes the third letter, and an unvoiced consonant becomes the first letter.

Iti sandhikappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section on Sandhi.

30, 58. Aṃ [M 0.0003] byañjane niggahitaṃ.

The niggahita (ṃ) occurs before a consonant.

31. 49. Vaggantaṃ vā vagge.

31. Alternatively, before a class consonant, it becomes the final letter of that class.

32, 50. Ehe ñaṃ.

Before 'h', it becomes 'ñ'.

33. 51. Sa ye ca.

33. And also before 'y'.

34, 52. Madā sare.

'm' and 'd' are inserted before a vowel.

35, 34. Ya va ma da na ta ra lā cāgamā.

'y', 'v', 'm', 'd', 'n', 't', 'r', and 'l' are also insertions.

36, 47. Kvaci o byañjane.

Sometimes, 'o' is inserted before a consonant.

37, 57. Niggahitañca.

And the niggahita is also inserted.

38, 53. Kvaci lopaṃ.

Sometimes, there is elision.

39, 54. Byañjane ca.

And also before a consonant.

40, 55. Paro vā saro.

Alternatively, the subsequent vowel is elided.

41, 56. Byañjano ca visaññogo.

And there is disjunction of a consonant.

Iti sandhikappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fourth section on Sandhi.

42, 32. Gosare puthassāgamo kvaci.

Sometimes, before 'go', there is the insertion of 'puthu'.

43, 33. Pāssa canto rasso.

The final vowel of 'pā' is shortened.

44, 24 Abbho abhi.

'Abhi' becomes 'abbho'.

45, 25. Ajjho adhi.

'Adhi' becomes 'ajjho'.

46, 26. Te na vā ivaṇṇe.

These two do not occur before the letter 'i'.

47, 23. Atissa cantassa.

Of 'ati', the final vowel is elided.

48, 43. Kvaci [M 0.0004] paṭi patissa.

Sometimes, 'pati' becomes 'paṭi'.

49, 44. Puthassu byañjane.

Before a consonant, 'puthu' becomes 'u'.

50, 45. O avassa.

'Ava' becomes 'o'.

51, 59. Anupadiṭṭhānaṃ vuttayogato.

For that which is not explicitly taught, it is to be understood from usage.

Iti sandhikappe pañcamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fifth section on Sandhi.

Sandhisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter on Sandhi is concluded.

2. Nāma

2. Noun.

52, 60. Jinavacanayuttaṃ hi.

Indeed, it is connected with the word of the Victor.

53, 61. Liṅgañca nippajjate.

And the stem is formed.

54, 62. Tato ca vibhattiyo.

And from that, the case endings.

55, 63. Si yo aṃ yo nā hi sa naṃ smā hi sanaṃ smiṃ su.

Si, yo, aṃ, yo, nā, hi, sa, naṃ, smā, hi, sanaṃ, smiṃ, su.

56, 64. Tadanuparodhena.

Without conflicting with that.

57, 71. Ālapane si gasañño.

In the vocative, si is designated ga.

58, 29. Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā.

The vowels i and u are designated jhalā.

59, 182. Te itthidhyā po.

They are designated po in the feminine.

60, 177. Ā gho.

Ā is designated gho.

61, 86. Sāgamo se.

There is the insertion of s before se.

62, 206. Saṃsāsvekavacanesu ca.

And in the singular cases saṃ and sāsu.

63, 217. Etimāsami[M 0.0005].

For eta and imā, there is sami.

64, 216. Tassā vā.

Optionally, tassā.

65, 215. Tato sassa ssāya.

From that, sa becomes ssāya.

66, 205. Gho rassaṃ.

Gho is shortened.

67, 229. No ca dvādito naṃmhi.

And not no after dvi and so on, when naṃ follows.

68, 184. Amā pato smiṃsmānaṃ vā.

Optionally, amā and pato before smiṃ, smā, and naṃ.

69, 186. Ādito o ca.

And o is prefixed.

70, 30. Jhalānamiyuvā sare vā.

Optionally, for jhalā, there is iya and uva before a vowel.

71, 489. Yavakārā ca.

And the letters y and v.

72, 185. Pasaññassa ca.

And of that which is designated pa.

73, 174. Gāva se.

Gāva before se.

74, 169. Yosu ca.

And before yo.

75, 170. Avaṃmhi ca.

And ava before aṃ.

76, 171. Āvassu vā.

Optionally, āva before su.

77, 175, Tato namaṃ patimhālutte ca samāse.

Then, from pati, when there is elision in a compound, it is a nominal stem.

78, 31. O sare ca.

And o before a vowel.

79, 46. Tabbiparītūpapade byañjane ca.

And when a consonant follows, and in a preceding word which is the reverse of that.

80, 173. Goṇa naṃmhi vā.

Optionally, goṇa before naṃ.

81, 172. Suhināsu ca.

And before `su`, `hi`, and `nāsu`.

82, 149. Aṃmo [M 0.0006] niggahitaṃ jhalapehi.

The niggahita (ṃ) becomes `o` before `jhala` and `pa` consonants.

83, 67. Saralopo mādesapaccayādimhi saralope tu pakati.

Elision of a vowel occurs before a substitution, suffix, and so forth; but when a vowel is elided, the preceding consonant remains in its natural state.

84, 144. Agho rassamekavacanayosvapi ca.

And the `a` of a `gha`-stem is also shortened in the singular and before `yo` and `su`.

85, 150. Na sismimanapuṃsakāni.

Not for `si` and `smiṃ` in non-neuter genders.

86, 227. Ubhādito naminnaṃ.

After `ubha` and so forth, `naṃ` becomes `innaṃ`.

87, 231. Iṇṇamiṇṇannaṃ tīhi saṅkhyāhi.

After the three numerals, `iṇṇaṃ` and `iṇṇannaṃ` are substituted for the genitive plural.

88, 147. Yāsu katanikāralopesu dīghaṃ.

Before `yāsu`, when `ka`, `ta`, `nika`, and `āra` are elided, the preceding vowel is lengthened.

89, 87. Sunaṃhisu ca.

And before `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi`.

90, 252. Pañcādīnamattaṃ.

Of `pañca` and so forth, the final vowel becomes `a`.

91, 194. Patissinīmhi.

Of `pati`, before the `inī` suffix.

92, 100. Ntussanto yosu ca.

And the `ntu` of the present participle becomes `nto` before `yo` and `su`.

93, 106. Sabbassa vā aṃsesu.

Optionally for the pronoun `sabba` before the endings `aṃ` and `se`.

94, 105. Simhi vā.

Optionally before `si` and `mhi`.

95, 145. Aggissini.

Of `aggi`, before the `inī` suffix.

96, 148. Yosvakatarasso jho.

Before `yo` and `su`, the vowel of a `jha`-stem is shortened, except for `katara`.

97, 156. Vevosu lo ca.

And elision of the final vowel occurs before `ve`, `vo`, and `su`.

98, 189. Mātulādīnamānattamīkāre.

For `mātula` and so forth, the final vowel becomes `āna` before the `ī` suffix.

99, 81. Smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi vā.

Optionally, `smā` is substituted by `mhā`, `hi` by `bhi`, and `smiṃ` by `mhi`.

100, 214. Na timehi katākārehi.

Not for these three when the final vowel has been made `a`.

101, 80. Suhisvakāro [M 0.0007] e.

Before `su` and `hi`, the vowel `a` becomes `e`.

102, 202. Sabbanāmānaṃ naṃmhi ca.

And for all pronouns, before `naṃ` and `mhi`.

103, 79. Ato nena.

After a stem ending in `a`, the instrumental singular ending is `ena`.

104, 66. So.

After an `a`-stem, the nominative singular `si` becomes `o`.

105, 0. So vā.

Optionally, after an `a`-stem, the nominative singular `si` becomes `o`.

106, 302. Dīghorehi.

By lengthening the vowel, or by substituting `o` or `e`.

107, 69. Sabbayonīnamāe.

For all classes of nouns, the `yo` endings become `ā` and `e`.

108, 90. Smāsmiṃnaṃ vā.

Optionally, for `smā`, `smiṃ`, and `naṃ`.

109, 295. Āya catutthekavacanassa tu.

But for the dative singular, the ending is `āya`.

110, 201. Tayo neva ca sabbanāmehi.

111, 179. Ghato nādīnaṃ.

The suffix gha is for the nādī stems.

112, 173. Pato yā.

The suffix pa is for yā.

113, 132. Sakhato gasse vā.

After sakha, gassa is an optional form.

114, 178. Ghate ca.

And in the case of ghaṭa.

115, 181. Na ammādito.

Not from ammā and so forth.

116, 157. Akatarassā lato yvālapanassavevo.

For akatara, the suffix is la; and for the vocative, ve and vo.

117, 124. Jhalato sassa no vā.

After a jhala consonant, na optionally replaces sa.

118, 146. Ghapato ca yonaṃ lopo.

And after ghapa stems, there is elision of the yo endings.

119, 115. Lato vokāro ca.

And after la, the substitution is vo.

Iti nāmakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section of the Noun Chapter.

120, 243. Amhassa [M 0.0008] mamaṃ savibhattissa se.

For amha with its case ending, and for mamaṃ, se is the substitute.

121, 233. Mayaṃ yomhi paṭhame.

In the first case, mayaṃ is the substitute for the ending yo.

122, 99. Ntussa nto.

'Ntu' becomes 'nto'.

123, 103. Ntassa se vā.

For nta, the substitute is optionally se.

124, 98. Ā simhi.

Ā is the substitute for si.

125, 198. Aṃ napuṃsake.

'Aṃ' is used in the neuter.

126, 101. Avaṇṇā ca ge.

And the vowel a is used in the case of the ending ge.

127, 102. To titā sasmiṃnāsu.

The substitutes to and titā are used for the endings sa, smiṃ, and nā.

128, 104. Naṃmhi taṃ vā.

Taṃ is optionally the substitute for naṃ.

129, 222. Imassidamaṃsisu napuṃsake.

In the neuter, 'idaṃ' is substituted for 'ima' before the endings 'aṃ' and 'si'.

130, 225. Amussāduṃ.

'Amu' becomes 'āduṃ'.

131, 0. Itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhyaṃ.

Feminine, masculine, neuter, and number.

132, 228. Yosu dvinnaṃ dve ca.

And for dvi, dve is the substitute before the yo endings.

133, 230. Ticatunnaṃ tisso catasso tayocattāro tīṇi cattāri.

Of ti and catu, the forms are: tisso, catasso; tayo, cattāro; tīṇi, cattāri.

134, 251. Pañcādīnamakāro.

The letter a of pañca and so forth.

135, 118. Rājassā rañño rājino se.

For the stem rāja, before the ending sa, the forms are rañño and rājino.

136, 119. Raññaṃ naṃmhi vā.

Optionally, raññaṃ is the form for the ending naṃ.

137, 116. Nāmhi raññā vā.

Optionally, raññā is the form for the ending nā.

138, 121. Smiṃmhi raññe rājini.

For the ending smiṃ, the forms are raññe and rājini.

139, 245. Tumhamhākaṃ [M 0.0009] tayi mayi.

Of tumha and amha, the forms are tayi and mayi.

140, 232. Tvamahaṃ simhi ca.

And `tvaṃ` and `ahaṃ` are the substitutes before the endings `si` and `mhi`.

141, 241. Tava mama se.

`Tava` and `mama` are the substitutes before the ending `sa`.

142, 242. Tuyhaṃ mayhañca.

And also `tuyhaṃ` and `mayhaṃ`.

143, 235. Taṃmamaṃmhi.

`Taṃ` and `mamaṃ` are the substitutes before the ending `aṃ`.

144, 234. Tavaṃmamañca na vā.

And `tavaṃ` and `mamaṃ` are also optional substitutes.

145, 238. Nāmhi tayā mayā.

`Tayā` and `mayā` are the substitutes before the ending `nā`.

146, 236. Tumhassa tuvaṃtvamamhi.

147, 246. Padato dutiyācatutthīchaṭṭhīsu vo no.

After a word, `vo` and `no` are the substitutes in the accusative, dative, and genitive cases.

148, 247. Hemekavacanesu ca.

And `te` and `me` are the substitutes in the singular cases.

149, 248. Na aṃmhi.

Not before the ending `aṃ`.

150, 249. Vā tatiye ca.

And optionally also in the third case.

151, 250. Bahuvacanesu vo no.

`Vo` and `no` are used in plural forms.

152, 136. Pumantassā simhi.

Of a stem ending in `puman`, `ā` is the substitute for the final part before the ending `si`.

153, 138. Amālapanekavacane.

The ending `aṃ` is used in the vocative singular.

154, 0. Samāse ca vibhāsā.

And optionally in a compound.

155, 137. Yosvāno.

`Āno` is the substitute before the endings `yo` and `su`.

156, 142. Āne smiṃmhi vā.

Optionally, `āne` is the substitute before the endings `smiṃ` and `mhi`.

157, 140. Hivibhatthimhi ca.

And in the `hi` case ending.

151, 143. Susmimā [M 0.0010] vā.

Optionally, `ā` is the substitute before the endings `su` and `ssa`.

159, 139. U nāmhi ca.

And `u` is the substitute before the ending `nā`.

160, 197. Akammantassa ca.

And of a stem ending in the vowel `a`.

Iti nāmakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the second section of the Noun Chapter.

161, 244. Tumhamhehi namākaṃ.

For the stems `tumha` and `amha`, the substitutes are `naṃ` and `ākaṃ`.

162, 237. Vā yvappaṭhamo.

Optionally, the nominative plural ending `yo` is used instead of the singular.

163, 240. Sassaṃ.

The ending `aṃ` is substituted for the genitive singular ending `sa`.

164, 200. Sabbanāmakārate paṭhamo.

For pronouns ending in `a`, this concerns the nominative case.

165, 208. Dvandaṭṭhā vā.

Optionally, when it stands in a dvanda compound.

166, 209. Nāññaṃ sabbanāmikaṃ.

167, 210. Bahubbīhimhi ca.

And also in a bahubbīhi compound.

168, 203. Sabbato naṃ saṃsānaṃ.

170, 220. Sabbassimasse vā.

171, 219. Animi nāmhi ca.

172, 218. Anapuṃsakassā yaṃ simhi.

173, 223. Amussa mo saṃ.

For `amu`, `mo` is substituted before the `saṃ` ending.

174, 211. Etatesaṃ to.

For `eta` and `ta`, `to` is the ablative suffix.

175, 212. Tassa vā nattaṃ sabbattha.

Alternatively, for `ta`, `nattaṃ` is the substitute in all instances.

176, 213. Sasmāsmiṃsaṃsāsvattaṃ 0.0011.

177, 221. Imasaddassa ca.

178, 224. Sabbato ko.

180, 207. Netāhi smimāyayā.

182, 97. Sassa co.

For `sa`, `co` is the substitute.

183, 48. Etesamo lope.

184, 96. Sa sare vāgamo.

185, 112. Santasaddassā so bhe bo cante.

189, 113. Syā ca.

190, 114. Yonamāno.

192, 135. Smime.

198, 123. Uttaṃ sanāsu.

201, 163. Vā naṃmhi.

202. 164. Satthunattañca.

202. And for satthu, natta is the substitute.

204, 167. Sakkamandhātādīnañca.

205, 160. Tato yonamo tu.

207, 161. Nā ā.

211, 126. Attanto hismimanattaṃ.

212, 129. Tato smiṃ ni.

213, 127. Sassano.

214, 128. Smā [M 0.0013] nā.

The ending smā is substituted by nā.

215, 141. Jhalato ca.

218, 196. Ato niccaṃ.

219, 195. Siṃ.

222, 327. Pumassa liṅgādīsu samāsesu.

224, 153. Naṃ jhato katarassā.

225, 151. Yonaṃ no.

226, 154. Smiṃni.

227, 270. Kissa ka ve ca.

228, 272. Ku hiṃ haṃsu ca.

228, 272. And 'ku', 'hiṃ', 'haṃsu'.

229, 226. Sesesu ca.

229, 226. And in the remaining cases.

230, 262. Tra to thesu ca.

230, 262. And in 'tra', 'to', 'thesu'.

231, 263. Sabbassetassākāro vā.

231, 263. Or 'ā' is the final vowel for 'sabba' and 'eta'.

232, 267. Tre niccaṃ.

232, 267. In the case of 'tra', it is constant.

233, 264. E tothesu ca.

233, 264. And in 'e', 'to', 'thesu'.

234, 265. Imassi [M 0.0014] thaṃ dāni ha to dhesu ca.

234, 265. And in 'imassim', 'thaṃ', 'dāni', 'ha', 'to', 'dhesu'.

235, 281. A dhunāmhi ca.

235, 281. And in 'adhunā' and 'amhi'.

236, 280. Eta rahimhi.

236, 280. In 'etarahi' and 'amhi'.

237, 176. Itthiyamato āpaccayo.

237, 176. In the feminine, the suffix 'ā' is used after a stem ending in 'a'.

238, 187. Nadādito vā ī.

238, 187. Or 'ī' after 'nadī' and so forth.

239, 190. Ṇava ṇika ṇeyya ṇantuhi.

239, 190. With 'ṇava', 'ṇika', 'ṇeyya', and 'ṇantu'.

240, 193. Patibhikkhurājīkārantehi inī.

240, 193. The suffix 'inī' is used after 'pati', 'bhikkhu', 'rāja', and stems ending in 'īkāra'.

241, 191. Ntussa tadhīkāre.

241, 191. Of the suffix '-nt', in the governing section.

242, 192. Bhavato bhoto.

242, 192. 'Bhavato' becomes 'bhoto'.

243, 110. Bho ge tu.

243, 110. 'Bho', 'ge', and 'tu'.

244, 72. Akārapitādyantānamā.

244, 72. For stems ending in 'a' and for 'pitar' and so forth, the vocative ending is 'ā'.

245, 152. Jhalapā rassaṃ.

245, 152. 'Jhalapā' is short.

246, 73. Ākāro vā.

246, 73. Or it is 'ā'.

Iti nāmakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fourth section in the Chapter on Nouns.

247, 261. Tvādayo vibhattisaññāyo.

247, 261. 'Tvā' and so forth are designated as case-endings.

248, 260. Kvaci to pañcamyatthe.

248, 260. Sometimes 'to' is used in the sense of the fifth case.

249, 266. Tratha sattamiyā sabbanāmehi.

249, 266. The suffixes 'tra' and 'tha' are used with all pronouns in the sense of the seventh case.

250, 268. Sabbato dhi.

250, 268. After 'sabba', the suffix is 'dhi'.

251, 269. Kiṃsmā vo.

251, 269. 'Kiṃsmā' becomes 'vo'.

252, 271. Hiṃhaṃhiñcanaṃ

252, 271. 'Hiṃ', 'haṃ', 'hiñcana'.

253, 273. Tamhā [M 0.0015] ca.

253, 273. And from 'ta'.

254, 274. Imasmā hadhā ca.

254, 274. And after 'ima', the suffixes 'ha' and 'dhā'.

255, 275. Yato hiṃ.

255, 275. After 'ya', the suffix is 'hiṃ'.

256, 0. Kāle.

256, 0. In the sense of time.

257, 276. Kiṃsabbaññekayakuhi dādācanaṃ.

257, 276. After `kiṃ`, `sabba`, `añña`, `eka`, `ya`, and `ku`, [the suffixes] `dā` and `dācanaṃ` [are affixed].

258, 278. Tamhā dāni ca.

258, 278. And after `ta`, [the suffix] `dāni`.

259, 279. Imasmā rahidhunādāni ca.

259, 279. And after `ima`, [the suffixes] `rahi`, `dhunā`, and `dāni`.

260, 277. Sabbassa so dāmhi vā.

260, 277. To `sabba`, `so` or `dāmhi` [are affixed].

261, 369. Avaṇṇo ye lopañca.

261, 369. Before `ye`, the final `a` [of the stem] is also elided.

262, 391. Vuḍḍhassa jo iyiṭṭhesu.

262, 391. In place of `vuḍḍha`, `jo` [is substituted] before [the suffixes] `iyya` and `iṭṭha`.

263, 392. Pasatthassa so ca.

263, 392. And in place of `pasattha`, `so` [is substituted].

264, 393. Antikassa nedo.

264, 393. In place of `antika`, `nedo` [is substituted].

265, 394. Bāḷhassa sādho.

265, 394. In place of `bāḷha`, `sādho` [is substituted].

266, 395. Appassa kaṇa.

266, 395. In place of `appa`, `kaṇa` [is substituted].

267, 396. Yuvānañca.

267, 396. And in place of `yuvan`.

268, 397. Vantumantuvīnañca lopo.

268, 397. And there is elision of [the suffixes] `vantu`, `mantu`, and `vī`.

269, 41. Yavataṃ talaṇadakārānaṃ byañjanāni calañajakārattaṃ.

269, 41. The consonants `t`, `l`, `ṇ`, `d`, and `k` become, respectively, `c`, `l`, `ñ`, `j`, and `k`.

270, 120. Amha tumha ntu rāja brahmatta sakha satthu– pitādīhi smā nāva.

270, 120. After `amha`, `tumha`, stems ending in `-ntu`, `rāja`, `brahma`, `atta`, `sakha`, `satthu`, `pitā`, and others, `smā` or `nā` [are the ablative endings].

Iti nāmakappe pañcamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fifth section in the Chapter on Nouns.

Nāmasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Discourse on Nouns is concluded.

3. Kāraka

3. Case Relations

271, 88. Yasmā [M 0.0016] dapetiṃ bhayamādatte vā tadapādānaṃ. (308)

271, 88. That from which one departs, fears, or takes, is the `apādāna` (the ablative case).

272, 309. Dhātunāmānamupasaggayogādīsvapi ca.

272, 309. And also in connection with roots, nouns, prefixes, and so forth.

273, 310. Rakkhaṇatthānamicchitaṃ.

273, 310. [The ablative is used for that] from which one desires to protect [something].

274, 311. Yena vā dassanaṃ

274, 311. Or [the ablative is used for that] from which one wishes to hide.

275, 312. Dūrantikaddhakāla nimmāna tvālopa disā yoga vibhattārappayoga suddhappamocanahetu vivittappamāṇapubbayoga bandhanaguṇavacana pañhakathana thokātattūsu ca.

275, 312. And also in the senses of: distance, proximity, path and time, measure, elision of the `-tvā` suffix, connection with direction, substitution for another case ending, 'beginning from', purity, cause of release, separation, measure, prior connection, binding, statement of a quality, asking and telling, 'a little', and difference.

276, 302. Yassa dātukāmo rocate dhārayate pā taṃ sampadānaṃ.

276, 302. That to whom one wishes to give, to whom something is pleasing, to whom one owes, or whom one protects, is the `sampadāna` (the dative case).

277, 303. Silāgha hanu ṭhā sapa dhāra piha kudha duhisso ssūya rādhikkha paccāsuṇa anupatigiṇa pubbakattārocanattha tadattha tumatthālamattha maññānādarappāṇini gatyatthakammaniāsisatthasammutibhiyyasattamyatthesu ca.

277, 303. And also in connection with [verbs or nouns meaning]: praise, anger, waiting for, cursing, owing, desiring, anger, hostility, envy, detraction, fault-finding, promising, assenting; and in the senses of: informing a previous agent, for the purpose of, for that purpose, the infinitive of purpose, adequacy, thinking, disrespect, towards an inanimate object, the object of verbs of motion, blessing, consent, 'more', and the locative case.

278, 320. Yodhāro tamokāsaṃ.

278, 320. That which is the support is the `okāsa` (the locative case).

279, 292. Yena vā kayirate taṃ karaṇaṃ.

279, 292. Or that by which an action is done is the `karaṇa` (the instrumental case).

280, 285, Yaṃ karoti taṃ kammaṃ.

280, 285. That which one does is the `kamma` (the accusative case).

281, 294. Yo karoti sa kattā.

281, 294. He who acts is the `kattā` (the agent).

282, 295. Yo kārehi sa hetu.

282, 295. He who causes to act is the `hetu` (the instigator).

283, 316. Yassa [M 0.0017] vā pariggaho taṃ sāmī.

283, 316. Or he to whom possession belongs is the `sāmī` (the owner).

284, 283. Liṅgatthe paṭhamā.

284, 283. The first (case) is in the sense of the nominal stem.

285, 70. Ālapane ca.

285, 70. And in the vocative.

286, 291. Karaṇe tatiyā.

286, 291. The third (case) is in the sense of the instrument.

287, 296, Sahādiyoge ca.

287, 296. And in connection with 'saha' and so forth.

288, 293. Kattari ca.

288, 293. And in the sense of the agent.

289, 297. Hetvatthe ca.

289, 297. And in the sense of cause.

290, 298. Sattamyatthe ca.

290, 298. And in the sense of the seventh (case).

291, 299. Yenaṅgavikāro.

291, 299. By which (there is) a defect of a limb.

292, 300. Visesane ca.

292, 300. And in specification.

293, 301. Sampadāne catutthī.

293, 301. The fourth (case) is in the sense of the recipient (dative).

294, 305. Namoyogādīsvapi ca.

294, 305. And also in connection with 'namo' and so forth.

295, 307. Apādāne pañcamī.

295, 307. The fifth (case) is in the sense of the point of separation (apādāna).

296, 314. Kāraṇatthe ca.

296, 314. And in the sense of reason.

297, 284. Kammatthe dutiyā.

297, 284. The second (case) is in the sense of the object.

298. 287. Kāladdhānamaccantasaṃyoge.

298. 287. In continuous connection with time and distance.

299, 288. Kammappavacanīyayutte.

299, 288. In connection with prepositions governing the object (kammappavacanīya).

300, 286. Gati buddhi bhuja paṭha hara kara sayādīnaṃkā rite vā.

300, 286. Optionally, for the agent of the non-causative form of verbs of going, knowing, eating, reciting, taking, doing, sleeping, and so forth.

301, 315. Sāmismiṃ chaṭṭhī

301, 315. The sixth (case) is in the sense of ownership.

302, 319. Okāse [M 0.0018] sattamī.

302, 319. The seventh (case) is in the sense of location (locus).

303, 321. Sāmissarādhipati dāyāda sakkhī pathibhū pasuta kusalehi ca.

303, 321. And with (words such as) master, lord, sovereign, heir, witness, surety, one who is devoted, and one who is skilled.

304, 322. Niddhāraṇe ca.

304, 322. And in specification (of one from a group).

305, 323. Anādare ca.

305, 323. And in the sense of disregard.

306, 289. Kvaci dutiyā chaṭṭhīnamatthe.

306, 289. Sometimes the second (case) is in the sense of the sixth.

307, 290. Tatiyāsattamīnañca.

307, 290. And of the third and seventh.

308, 317. Chaṭṭhī ca.

308, 317. And the sixth (case).

309, 318. Dutiyāpañcamīnañca.

309, 318. And of the second and fifth.

310, 324. Kammakaraṇanimittatthesu sattamī.

310, 324. The seventh (case) is in the senses of object, instrument, and cause.

311, 325. Sampadāne ca.

311, 325. And in the sense of the recipient (dative).

312, 326. Pañcamyatthe ca.

312, 326. And in the sense of the fifth (case).

313, 327. Kālabhāvesu ca.

313, 327. And in the senses of time and state.

314, 328. Upa’dhyādhikissaravacane.

314, 328. In the sense of upa, adhi, and issara.

315, 329. Maṇḍitussukkesu tatiyā ca.

315, 329. And the instrumental case is used with 'maṇḍita' and 'ussukka'.

Iti nāmakappe kārakakappo chaṭṭho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the sixth section, the Chapter on Case Relations, in the Chapter on Nouns.

Kārakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Discourse on Case Relations is concluded.

4. Samāsa

4. Compounds

316, 331. Nāmāna samāso yuttattho.

316, 331. The compounding of nouns is for connected meaning.

317, 332. Tesaṃ vibhattiyo lopā ca.

317, 332. And there is elision of their case-endings.

318, 333. Pakati cassa sarantassa.

318, 333. And for a word ending in a vowel, its original form remains.

319, 330. Upasagganipātapubbako [M 0.0019] abyayībhāvo.

319, 330. The Avyayībhāva is a compound preceded by a prefix or a particle.

320, 335. So napuṃsakaliṅgo.

320, 335. It is of the neuter gender.

321. 349. Digussekattaṃ.

321. 349. The Digu compound is singular.

322, 359. Tathā dvande pāṇi tūriye yogga senaṅga khuddajantuka vividha viruddha visabhāgatthādīnañca.

322, 359. Likewise in a Dvanda compound, for those denoting limbs of the body, musical instruments, vehicles, constituents of an army, small creatures, various things, opposites, and other things of dissimilar meaning.

323, 360. Vibhāsā rukkha tiṇa pasu dhana dhañña janapadā dīnañca.

323, 360. And optionally for trees, grass, cattle, wealth, grain, countries, and so forth.

324, 339. Dvipade tulyādhikaraṇe kammadhārayo.

324, 339. A Kammadhāraya is a two-word compound whose members are in apposition.

325, 348. Saṅkhyāpubbo digu.

325, 348. The Digu is that which is preceded by a numeral.

326, 341. Ubhe tappurisā.

326, 341. Both are Tappurisa compounds.

327, 351. Amādayo parapadebhi.

327, 351. Words ending in the accusative case and so on, with subsequent words.

328, 352. Aññapadatthesu bahubbīhi.

328, 352. A Bahubbīhi is in the sense of another word.

329, 357. Nāmānaṃ samuccayo dvando.

329, 357. A Dvanda is an aggregation of nouns.

330, 340. Mahataṃ mahā tulyādhikaraṇe pade.

330, 340. 'Mahant' becomes 'mahā' when in apposition with another word.

331, 353. Itthiyaṃ bhāsitapumitthī pumāva ce.

331, 353. A feminine word that has a corresponding masculine form is treated as if it were masculine.

332, 343. Kammadhārayasaññe ca.

332, 343. And also when designated as a Kammadhāraya.

333, 344. Attaṃ nassa tappurise.

333, 344. 'Na' becomes 'a' in a Tappurisa compound.

334, 345. Sare ana.

334, 345. It becomes 'an' when a vowel follows.

335, 346. Kadi kussa.

335, 346. 'Ku' is substituted by 'ka' or 'kad'.

336, 347. Kā’ppatthesu ca.

336, 347. And 'kā' is used in the sense of 'a little'.

337, 350. Kvaci [M 0.0020] samāsanta gatānamakāranto.

337, 350. Sometimes, words at the end of a compound end in 'a'.

338, 356. Nadimhā ca.

338, 356. And so from 'nadī'.

339, 358. Jāyāya tudaṃ jāni patimhi.

339, 358. 'Jāyā' becomes 'tudaṃ' or 'jāni' when 'pati' follows.

340, 355. Dhanumhā ca.

340, 355. And so from 'dhanu'.

341, 336. Aṃvibhattīnamakārantā abyāyitāvā.

Optionally, words ending in 'a' with the 'aṃ' inflection are not indeclinables.

342, 337. Saro rasso napuṃsake.

A vowel is short in the neuter gender.

343, 338. Aññasmā lopo ca.

And elision from another [form].

Iti nāmakappe samāsakappo sattamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the seventh section, the chapter on compounds, in the Noun Division.

Samāsasutthaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The rules on compounds are concluded.

5. Taddhita

5. Taddhita

244, 361. Vā ṇā’pacce.

Optionally, 'ṇā' [is used] in the sense of offspring.

345, 366. Ṇāyana ṇāna vacchādito.

'Ṇāyana' and 'ṇāna' [are used] after 'vaccha' and so forth.

346, 367. Ṇeyyo kattiyādīhi.

'Ṇeyya' [is used] after 'kattiya' and so forth.

347, 368. Ato ṇi vā.

Optionally, 'ṇi' [is used] after that.

348, 371. Ṇavopakvādīhi.

[A suffix is used] after 'ṇavopaka' and so forth.

349, 372. Ṇera vidhavādito.

'Ṇera' [is used] after 'vidhavā' and so forth.

350, 373. Yena vā saṃsaṭṭhaṃ tarati carati vahati ṇiko.

Optionally, 'ṇika' [is used] in the sense of that by which one mixes, crosses, moves, or carries.

351, 374. Tamadhīte tenakatādhi sannidhānaniyoga sippa bhaṇḍa jīvikatthesu ca.

And [the suffix 'ṇika' is used] in the senses of 'studies that', 'made by that', proximity, assignment, craft, goods, and livelihood.

352, 376. Ṇa [M 0.0021] rāgā tassedamaññatthesu ca.

'Ṇa' [is used] after a word signifying color, and in the senses of 'this is his' and other meanings.

353, 378. Jātādīnamimiyā ca.

And 'ima' and 'iya' [are used] after 'jāta' and so forth.

354, 379. Samūhatthe kaṇa ṇā.

In the sense of a collection, 'kaṇa' and 'ṇā' [are used].

355, 380. Gāma jana bandhu sahāyādīhi tā.

'Tā' [is used] after 'gāma', 'jana', 'bandhu', 'sahāya', and so forth.

356, 381. Tadassa ṭhānamiyo ca.

And 'iya' [is used] in the sense of 'that is its place'.

357, 382. Upamatthāyitattaṃ.

'tta' [is used] in the sense of likeness.

358, 383. Tannissitatthe lo.

'La' [is used] in the sense of 'dependent on that'.

359, 384. Ālu tabbahule.

'Ālu' [is used] in the sense of 'having an abundance of that'.

360, 387. Ṇuttatā bhāve tu.

But 'ṇu', 'tta', and 'tā' [are used] in the sense of state.

361, 388. Ṇa visamādīhi.

'Ṇa' [is used] after 'visama' and so forth.

362, 389. Ramaṇīyādito kaṇa

'Kaṇa' [is used] after 'ramaṇīya' and so forth.

363, 390. Visese taratamisikiyiṭṭhā.

In the sense of distinction, 'tara', 'tama', 'isika', 'iya', and 'iṭṭha' [are used].

364, 398. Tadassatthīti vī ca.

And 'vī' [is used] in the sense of 'possessing that'.

365, 399. Tapādito sī.

'Sī' [is used] after 'tapa' and so forth.

366, 400. Daṇḍādito ika ī.

'Ika' and 'ī' [are used] after 'daṇḍa' and so forth.

367, 401. Madhvādito ro.

'Ra' [is used] after 'madhu' and so forth.

368, 402. Guṇādito vantu.

The suffix `vantu` is used after `guṇa` and so forth.

369, 403. Satyādīhi mantu.

The suffix `mantu` is used after `satya` and so forth.

370, 405. Saddhādito ṇa.

The suffix `ṇa` is used after `saddhā` and so forth.

371, 404. Āyussukārāsa mantumhi.

The suffix `mantu` is used after the stem `āyus`.

372, 385. Tappakativacane [M 0.0022] mayo.

The suffix `maya` is used in the sense of 'its nature'.

373, 406. Saṅkhyāpūraṇe mo.

The suffix `ma` is used in the sense of completing a number (ordinal).

374, 408. Sa chassa vā.

Or `sa` for `cha`.

375, 412. Ekādito dasassī.

After `eka` and so forth, the suffix `ī` is used for `dasa`.

376, 257. Dase so niccañca.

And `dasa` always becomes `so`.

377, 0. Ante niggahitañca.

And also a final niggahita.

378, 414. Ti ca.

And `ti`.

379, 258. La da rānaṃ.

`La` and `da` for `ra`.

380, 255. Vīsati dasesu bā dvissa tu.

But `dvi` becomes `bā` before `vīsati` and the tens.

381, 254. Ekādito dassa ra saṅkhyāne.

In counting, after `eka` and so forth, `dasa` becomes `ra`.

382, 259. Aṭṭhādito ca.

And after `aṭṭha` and so forth.

383, 353. Dvekaṭṭhānamākāro vā.

For `dvi`, `eka`, and `aṭṭha`, their final vowel optionally becomes `ā`.

384, 407. Catucche hi tha ṭhā.

Indeed, `tha` and `ṭha` are used for `catu` and `cha`.

385, 409. Dvitīhi tiyo.

The suffix `tiya` is used after `dvi` and `ti`.

386, 410. Tiye dutāpi ca.

And `duta` also is used for `ti`.

387, 411. Tesamaḍḍhūpapadena aḍḍhuḍḍhadivaḍḍha diyaḍḍha’ ḍḍhatiyā.

For them, with `aḍḍha` as a preceding member: `aḍḍhuḍḍha` (one and a half), `divaḍḍha` (one and a half), `diyaḍḍha` (one and a half), and `aḍḍhatiyā` (two and a half).

388, 68. Sarūpāna mekasesvasakiṃ.

For similar forms, in ekasesa, not once but repeatedly.

389, 413. Gaṇanedasassa dvi ti catu pañca cha satta aṭṭhanavakānaṃ vī ti cattāra paññā cha sattāsanavā yosu yonañcīsamāsaṃṭhiritītuti.

In counting, for the formation of the tens, for the numerals two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine, forms such as `vī`, `ti`, `cattāra`, `paññā`, `cha`, `sattāsa`, and `navā` are used.

390, 256. Catūpapadassa [M 0.0023] lopo tu’ttarapadādicassa cu copi navā.

But optionally, there is elision of `catu` as a preceding member and of the initial part of the subsequent word; and `cu` and `co` are also optionally used.

391, 423. Yadanupapannā nipātanā sijjhanti.

What is not formed according to rule is established by convention.

392, 418. Dvādito ko’nekatthe ca.

The suffix `ka` is used after `dva` and so forth, and in various meanings.

393, 415. Dasadasakaṃ sataṃ dasakānaṃ sataṃ sahassañca yomhi.

Ten tens is a hundred; a hundred tens is a thousand.

394, 416. Yāva taduttari dasaguṇitañca.

And beyond that, each is multiplied by ten.

395, 417. Sakanāmehi.

By their own names.

396, 363. Tesaṃ ṇo lopaṃ.

For them, there is elision of the `ṇa` suffix.

397, 420. Vibhāge dhā ca.

And `dhā` is used in the sense of division.

398, 421. Sabbanāmehi pakāravacane tu thā.

398, 421. The suffix 'thā' is used with all pronouns in the sense of manner.

399, 422. Kimimehi thaṃ.

399, 422. The suffix 'thaṃ' is used with 'kiṃ' and 'ima'.

400, 364. Vuddhādisarassa vā’saṃyogantassa saṇe ca.

400, 364. And the suffix 'saṇa' is used for a word with a strengthened initial vowel, or for one not ending in a conjunct consonant.

401, 375. Māyūnamāgamo ṭhāne.

401, 375. An augment for 'māyu' occurs in the proper place.

402. 377. Āttañca.

402. 377. And 'ātta'.

403, 354. Kvacādimajjhuttarānaṃ dīgharassa paccayesu ca.

403, 354. And sometimes, in the case of suffixes, there is lengthening and shortening of initial, middle, and final vowels.

404, 370. Tesu vuddhi lopāgama vikāra viparitādesā ca.

404, 370. And among these occur vuddhi, lopa, āgama, vikāra, viparita, and ādesa.

405, 365. Ayuvaṇṇānañcāyo vuddhi.

405, 365. And vuddhi is the strengthening of the vowels 'a', 'i', 'u' to 'ā', 'e', 'o'.

Iti nāmakappe taddhitakappo aṭṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus in the Noun Division ends the eighth section, the chapter on Taddhita.

Taddhitasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Suttas on Taddhita are concluded.

6. Ākhyāti

6. Verbs

406, 429. Atha [M 0.0024] pubbāni-vibhattīnaṃ cha parassapadāni.

406, 429. Now, of the preceding sets of endings, six are parassapada.

407, 439. Parāṇuttanopadāni.

407, 439. The latter ones are attanopada.

408, 430. Dve dve paṭhamamajjhimuttamapurisā.

408, 430. Two each are the third, second, and first persons.

409, 441. Sabbesamekābhidhāne paro puriso.

409, 441. When all are designated together, the latter person is used.

410, 432. Nāmamhi payujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe paṭhamo.

410, 432. Even when a noun is used in apposition, the third person is used.

411, 436. Tumhe majjhimo.

411, 436. With 'tumha', the second person is used.

412, 437. Amhe uttamo.

412, 437. With 'amha', the first person is used.

413, 426. Kāle.

413, 426. In the sense of time.

414, 428. Vattamānā paccuppanne.

414, 428. The Vattamānā is for the present.

415, 451. Āṇātyāsiṭṭhe’nuttakāle pañcamī.

415, 451. The Pañcamī is used for command and blessing in non-past time.

416, 454. Anumatiparikappetthesu sattamī.

416, 454. The Sattamī is used in the meanings of permission and supposition.

417, 460. Apaccakkhe parokkhā’tīte.

417, 460. The Parokkhā is for the indirect past.

418, 456. Hiyyopabhuti paccakkhe hiyyattanī.

418, 456. The Hiyyattanī is for the direct past, from yesterday onwards.

419, 469. Samīpe’jjatanī.

419, 469. The Ajjatanī is for the recent past.

420, 471. Māyoge sabbakāle ca.

420, 471. And in conjunction with 'mā', it is used for any time.

421, 473. Anāgate bhavissantī.

421, 473. The Bhavissantī is for the future.

422, 475. Kriyātipanne’tīte kālātipatti.

422, 475. The Kālātipatti is used when an action was unfulfilled in the past.

423, 426. Vattamānā tī anti, si tha, mi ma te ante, sevhe, e mhe.

423, 426. The Vattamānā endings are: ti, anti; si, tha; mi, ma; te, ante; se, vhe; e, mhe.

424, 450. Pañcamī [M 0.0025] tu antu, hi tha, mi ma, taṃ antaṃ, ssu vho, e āmase.

424, 450. The Pañcamī endings are: tu, antu; hi, tha; mi, ma; taṃ, antaṃ; ssu, vho; e, āmase.

425, 453. Sattamī eyya eyyuṃ, eyyāsi eyyātha, eyyāmi eyyāma, etha eraṃ, etho eyyāvho, eyyaṃ eyyāmhe.

425, 453. The seventh (i.e., optative): eyya, eyyuṃ; eyyāsi, eyyātha; eyyāmi, eyyāma; etha, eraṃ; etho, eyyāvho; eyyaṃ, eyyāmhe.

426, 459. Parokkhā a u, e ttha, aṃ mha, ttha re, ttho vho, iṃ mhe.

426, 459. Parokkhā (perfect): a, u; e, ttha; aṃ, mha; ttha, re; ttho, vho; iṃ, mhe.

427, 455. Hiyyattanī ā ū, o ttha, aṃ mhā, ttha tthuṃ, sevhaṃ, iṃ mhase.

427, 455. Hiyyattanī (imperfect): ā, ū; o, ttha; aṃ, mhā; ttha, tthuṃ; se, vhaṃ; iṃ, mhase.

428, 468. Ajjatanī īñaṃ ottha, iṃ mhā, ā ū, se vhaṃ, aṃ mhe.

428, 468. Ajjatanī (aorist): ī, uṃ; o, ttha; iṃ, mhā; ā, ū; se, vhaṃ; aṃ, mhe.

429, 472. Ssavissantī ssati ssanti, ssasi ssatha, ssāmi ssāma, ssate ssante, ssase ssavhe, ssaṃ ssāmhe.

429, 472. Bhavissantī (future): ssati, ssanti; ssasi, ssatha; ssāmi, ssāma; ssate, ssante; ssase, ssavhe; ssaṃ, ssāmhe.

430, 474. Kālātipatti ssā ssaṃsu, sse ssatha, ssaṃ ssāmā, ssatha ssisu, ssase ssavhe, ssiṃ ssāmhase.

430, 474. Kālātipatti (conditional): ssā, ssaṃsu; sse, ssatha; ssaṃ, ssāmā; ssatha, ssisu; ssase, ssavhe; ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

431, 428. Hiyyattanī sattamī pañcamī vattamānā sabbadhātukaṃ.

431, 428. The Hiyyattanī (imperfect), Sattamī (optative), Pañcamī (imperative), and Vattamānā (present) are universal (i.e., applicable to all roots).

Iti ākhyātakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section in the chapter on verbs.

432, 362. Dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā.

432, 362. Suffixes come after verbal roots and nominal stems.

433, 528. Tijagupakitamānehi khachasā vā.

433, 528. From roots such as tija, gupa, kita, and māna, the suffixes kha, cha, and sa are optionally added.

434, 534. Bhujaghasaharasupādīhitumicchatthesu.

434, 534. From roots such as bhuja, ghasa, hara, supa, etc., in the sense of desideration.

435, 536. Āya [M 0.0026] nāmato kattūpamānādācāre.

435, 536. The suffix āya is added to a noun in the sense of acting like an agent, comparison, or conduct.

436, 537. Īyū’pamānā ca.

436, 537. And the suffix īya from a noun which is an object of comparison.

437, 538. Nāmamhā’tticchatthe.

437, 538. From a noun, in the sense of desiring something for oneself.

438, 540. Dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya ṇāpe ṇāpayā kāritāni hetvatthe.

438, 540. From roots, the causative suffixes ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, and ṇāpaya are added in the causative sense.

439, 539. Dhāturūpe nāmasmā ṇa yo ca.

439, 539. And from a noun, the suffixes ṇa and yo are added, giving it the form of a root.

440, 445. Bhāvakammesu yo.

440, 445. The suffix yo is used in impersonal and passive constructions.

441, 447. Tassa cavaggayakāravakārattaṃ sadhātvantassa.

441, 447. With it (i.e., the suffix yo), the final consonant of the root becomes a consonant of the ca-group, or y, v, or t.

442, 448. Ivaṇṇāgamo vā.

442, 448. Or there is the augment i.

443, 449. Pubbarūpañca.

443, 449. And assimilation to the preceding form.

444, 511. Tathā kattari ca.

444, 511. Likewise also in the active voice.

445, 433. Bhūvādito a.

445, 433. From the bhū-class of roots, the suffix a is added.

446, 509. Rudhādito niggahitapubbañca.

446, 509. And from the rudh-class of roots, with a preceding niggahīta.

447, 510. Divādito yo.

447, 510. From the div-class of roots, the suffix yo is added.

448, 512. Svādito ṇuṇā uṇā ca.

448, 512. And from the su-class of roots, the suffixes ṇu, ṇā, and uṇā are added.

449, 513. Kiyādito nā.

449, 513. From the kī-class of roots, the suffix nā is added.

450, 517. Gahādito ppaṇhā.

450, 517. From the gah-class of roots, the suffix ṇhā is added.

451, 520. Tanādito oyirā.

451, 520. From the tan-class of roots, the suffixes o and yirā are added.

452, 525. Curādito ṇe ṇayā.

452, 525. From the cur-class of roots, the suffixes ṇe and ṇaya are added.

453, 444. Attanopadāni bhāve ca kammani.

453, 444. The attanopada endings are used in the impersonal and passive voices.

454, 440. Kattari ca.

454, 440. And in the agentive voice.

455, 530. Dhātuppaccayehi [M 0.0027] vibhattiyo.

455, 530. Inflections arise from verbal roots and suffixes.

456, 420. Kattari parassapadaṃ.

456, 420. The parassapada endings are used in the agentive voice.

457, 424. Bhūvādayo dhātavo.

457, 424. The roots are bhū and the like.

Iti ākhyātakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the second section on verbs.

458, 461. Kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo.

458, 461. In some cases, there is a doubling of the initial letters of roots with a single vowel.

459, 462. Pubbo’ bbhāso.

459, 462. The former part is the reduplicative syllable.

460, 506. Rasso.

460, 506. It becomes short.

461, 464. Dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā.

461, 464. The second and fourth consonants become the first and third.

462, 467. Kavaggassa cavaggo.

462, 467. A consonant of the ka-class becomes a consonant of the ca-class.

463, 532. Mānakitānaṃ va tattaṃ vā.

463, 532. For the roots mā, na, ki, and ta, `va` or `tattaṃ` is optionally substituted.

464, 504. Hassa jo.

464, 504. Ha becomes ja.

465, 463. Antassivaṇṇākāro vā.

465, 463. Optionally, the final vowel becomes `i` or `ā`.

466, 489. Niggahitañca.

466, 489. And the niggahīta.

467, 533. Tato pāmānānaṃ vāmaṃ sesu.

467, 533. Then, for pā and māna, vā and maṃ are substituted in the remaining cases.

468, 492. Ṭhā tiṭṭho.

468, 492. Ṭhā becomes tiṭṭha.

469, 494. Pā pivo.

469, 494. Pā becomes piva.

470, 514. Ñāssa jājaṃnā.

470, 514. Ñā becomes jā or jaṃnā.

471, 483. Disassa passa dissa dakkhā vā.

471, 483. The root dis optionally becomes passa, dissa, or dakkhā.

472, 531. Byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu ca.

472, 531. And for a consonant-ending root, `a` is added before the six suffixes.

473, 529. Ko khe ca.

473, 529. And ka becomes kha.

474, 535. Harassa gī se.

474, 535. For the root har, `gī` is substituted before the `se` ending.

475, 465. Brūbhūnamāhabhūvā [M 0.0028] parokkhāyaṃ.

475, 465. Brū, bhū, nam, āha, and bhū are used in the parokkhā (perfect) tense.

476, 442. Gamissanto ccho vā sabbāsu.

476, 442. For the root gam, `ccha` is optionally substituted in all inflections.

477, 479. Vacassa’jjatanimhi makārā o.

477, 479. For the root vac, in the ajjatanī tense, the `ma` ending becomes `o`.

478, 438. Akāro dīghaṃ himimesu.

478, 438. The vowel `a` becomes long before the `hi`, `mi`, and `me` endings.

479, 452. Hi lopaṃ vā.

479, 452. The `hi` ending is optionally elided.

480, 490. Hotissare’ ho’he bhavissantimhi ssassa ca.

480, 490. For the root hū, in the future tense, the substitutes are `ho` or `he`, and for the suffix `ssa`.

481, 524. Karassa sappaccayassa kāho.

481, 524. For the root kar with its suffix, `kāha` is substituted.

Iti ākhyātakappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section on verbs.

482, 508. Dādantassaṃ mimesu.

For a root ending in dā, a change occurs before the endings mi and me.

483, 527. Asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite.

For a root not ending in a conjunct consonant, lengthening occurs in the causative.

484, 542. Ghaṭādīnaṃ vā.

Or for roots such as ghaṭa and others.

485, 434. Aññesu ca.

And in other cases.

486, 543. Guhadusānaṃ dīghaṃ.

For the roots guh and dus, the vowel becomes long.

487, 478. Vaca vasa vahādīnamukāro vassaye.

For vac, vas, vah, and other such roots, u is substituted.

488, 481. Ha vipariyayo lo vā.

For the root ha, there is optionally metathesis or elision.

489, 519. Gahassa ghe ppe.

The root gah becomes ghe or ppe.

490, 518. Halopo ṇhāmhi.

The ha is elided in ṇhā.

491, 523. Karassa kāsattamajjatanimhi.

For the root kar, kā is substituted in the ajjatanī (aorist) tense.

492, 499. Asasmā mimānaṃ mimhā’ntalopo ca.

After the root as, before the endings mi and ma, the final letter of the root is elided.

493, 498. Thassa tthatthaṃ.

The ending tha becomes ttha or attha.

494, 495. Tissa [M 0.0029] tissa tthitthaṃ.

The ending ti becomes ttha or ittha.

495, 500. Tussa tthuttaṃ.

The ending tu becomes tthu or uttaṃ.

496, 497. Simhi ca.

And in the case of the ending si.

497, 477. Labhasmā īaṃnaṃ tthattaṃ.

After the root labh, the endings ī and aṃ become ttha.

498, 480. Kusasmā dī cchi.

After the root kus, dī or cchi are substituted.

499, 480. Dā dhātussa dajjaṃ.

For the root dā, dajjaṃ is substituted.

500, 486. Vadassa vajjaṃ.

The root vad becomes vajjaṃ.

501, 443. Gamissa ghammaṃ.

The root gam becomes ghammaṃ.

502, 493. Yamhi dā dhā mā ṭhā hā pā maha mathādīnamī.

When the suffix ya follows, for dā, dhā, mā, ṭhā, hā, pā, maha, matha, and other such roots, the vowel becomes ī.

503, 485. Yajassādissi.

The root yaj becomes ādis.

504, 470. Sabbato uṃ iṃsu.

After all roots, the endings are uṃ or iṃsu.

505, 482. Jaramarānaṃ jīra jīyya mīyyā vā.

For the roots jara and mara, the substitutes are optionally jīra, jīyya, or mīyyā.

506, 496. Sabbatthā’sassādilopo ca.

And everywhere, there is elision of the initial a of assa.

507, 501. Asabbadhātuke ñā.

The suffix ñā is used before an asabbadhātuka affix.

508, 515. Yeyyassa ñāto iyā ñā.

After the suffix ñā, the optative ending eyya becomes iyā or ñā.

509, 516. Nāssa lopo yakārattaṃ.

For the suffix nā, there is elision or it becomes ya.

510, 487. Lopañcettamakāro.

And there is elision of this a-vowel.

511, 521. Uttamokāro.

In the first person, the vowel becomes o.

512, 522. Karassākāro ca.

And the vowel of the root kar becomes ā.

513, 435. O ava sare.

O becomes ava when a vowel follows.

514, 491. E aya.

E becomes aya.

515, 541. Te [M 0.0030] āvāyā kārite.

Te becomes āvāyā in the causative.

516, 466. Ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhi.

The augment i is added before a non-sabbadhātuka affix.

517, 488. Kvaci dhātuvibhattippaccayānaṃ dīghaviparītādesa lopāgamā ca.

Sometimes there is lengthening, reversal, substitution, elision, and augmentation of roots, endings, and suffixes.

518, 446. Attanopadāni parassapadattaṃ.

The attanopada endings are used as parassapada endings.

519, 457. Akārāgamo hiyyatthanīajjatanīkālātipattīsu.

The augment a is added in the hiyattanī (imperfect), ajjatanī (aorist), and kālātipatti (conditional) tenses.

520, 502. Brūto ī timhi.

From the root brū, ī is substituted for the ending ti.

521, 425. Dhātussanto lopo’ nekasarassa.

The final vowel of a multi-syllabic root is elided.

522, 476. Isuyamūnamanto ccho vā.

The final vowel of the roots isu and yamū optionally becomes ccho.

523, 526. Kāritānaṃ ṇo lopaṃ.

The ṇ of causative forms is elided.

Iti ākhyātakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fourth section of the chapter on verbs.

Ākhyātasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The treatise on verbs is concluded.

7. Kibbidhāna

7. The Kibbidhāna Section

524, 561. Dhātuyā kammādimhi ṇo.

The suffix ṇa is added to a root in the sense of object, etc.

525, 565. Saññāyama nu.

The suffix nu is added in the sense of a name.

526, 567. Pure dadā ca iṃ.

And the suffix iṃ is added to the root dā when preceded by the prefix pura.

527, 568. Sabbato ṇvutvā’vī vā.

From all roots, the suffixes ṇvu, tvā, and āvī are optionally added.

528, 577. Visa ruja padādito ṇa.

The suffix ṇa is added to the roots vis, ruj, pad, and so on.

529, 580. Bhāve ca.

And in the sense of an abstract noun.

530, 584. Kvi ca.

And the suffix kvi.

531, 589. Dharādīhi [M 0.0031] rammo.

From the roots dhara and so on, the suffix ramma is added.

532, 590. Tassīlādīsu ṇī tvā vī ca.

In the sense of 'one who has the habit of', etc., the suffixes ṇī, tvā, and vī are also added.

533, 591. Sadda kudha cala maṇḍattha rucādīhi yu.

From the roots sadda, kudh, cal, maṇḍ, aṭṭh, ruc, and so on, the suffix yu is added.

534, 592. Pārādigamimhā rū.

From the root gam when preceded by the prefix pāra, etc., the suffix rū is added.

535, 593. Bhikkhādito ca.

And from bhikkha and so on.

536, 594. Hanatyādīnaṃ ṇuko.

To the root han and others, the affix ṇuka is added.

537, 566. Nu niggahitaṃ padante.

At the end of a word, the suffix nu becomes niggahīta.

538, 595. Saṃhanā’ññāya vā ro gho.

From the root han with the prefix saṃ, and from another root, the suffixes ra and gha are optionally added.

539, 558. Ramhi ranto rādino.

The suffixes are ramhi, ranto, and rādino.

540, 545. Bhāvakammesu tabbā’nīyā.

The suffixes tabba and anīya are employed in the impersonal and passive senses.

541, 552. Ṇyo ca.

And also the suffix ṇya.

542, 557. Karamhā ricca.

After the root kar, the suffix is ricca.

543, 555. Bhūto’bba.

After the root bhū, the suffix is abba.

544, 556. Vada mada gamu yuja garahākārādīhi jja mmaggayheyyāvāro vā.

After the roots vad, mad, gam, yuj, garahā, kāra, and others, the suffixes jja, magga, eyya, or avāra are optionally employed.

545, 548. Te kiccā.

These are termed gerundives (kicca).

546, 562. Aññe kita.

Other suffixes are termed kita.

547, 596. Nandādīhi yu.

After nanda and others, the suffix is yu.

548, 597. Kattukaraṇapadesesu ca.

And also in the senses of agent, instrument, and location.

549, 550. Rahādito ṇa.

After the root rah and others, the suffix is ṇa.

Iti kibbidhānakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Here ends the first section in the chapter on primary suffixes.

550, 549. Ṇādayo [M 0.0032] tekālikā.

The suffixes beginning with ṇa are applicable to all three tenses.

551, 598. Saññāyaṃ dādhāto i.

In the sense of a designation, after the roots dā and dhā, the suffix is i.

552, 609. Ti kiccā’siṭṭhe.

The suffix ti is employed with a gerundive in the sense of censure.

553, 599. Itthiyamatiyavo vā.

In the feminine, the suffixes ati and yava are optionally employed.

554, 601. Karato ririya.

After the root kar, the suffix is ririya.

555, 612. Atīte ta tavantu tāvī.

In the past tense, the suffixes are ta, tavantu, and tāvī.

556, 622. Bhāvakammesu ta.

The suffix ta is employed in the impersonal and passive senses.

557, 606. Budhagamāditthe kattari.

After the roots budh, gam, and others, the suffix [ta] is used in the agentive sense.

558, 602. Jito ina sabbattha.

After the root ji, the suffix ina is employed universally.

559, 603. Supato ca.

And also after the root sup.

560, 604. Īsaṃdusūhi kha.

After the prefixes īsaṃ, du, and su, the suffix is kha.

561, 636. Icchatthesu samānakattukesu tave tuṃ vā.

When there is a common agent, in the sense of 'desiring', the suffixes tave or tuṃ are optionally employed.

562, 638. Arahasakkādīsu ca.

And also with verbs such as arah and sakk.

563, 639. Pattavacane alamatthesu ca.

And also with words expressing what is fitting, and in the sense of 'sufficient'.

564, 640. Pubbakāle’kakattukānaṃ tuna tvāna tvā vā.

To denote a prior action, when there is a single agent, the suffixes tuna, tvāna, or tvā are optionally employed.

565, 646. Vattamāne māna’ntā.

In the present tense, the suffixes are māna and anta.

566, 574. Sāsādīhi ratthu.

After the root sās and others, the suffix is ratthu.

567, 575. Pātito ritu.

After the root pā, the suffix is ritu.

568, 576. Mānādīhi [M 0.0033] rātu.

568, 576. From māna and so on, 'rātu' is added.

569, 610. Āgamā tuko.

569, 610. From āgama, 'tuka' is added.

570, 611. Bhabbe ika.

570, 611. In the sense of 'possible', 'ika' is added.

Iti kibbidhānakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the second section of the Kibbidhāna chapter.

571, 624. Paccayādaniṭṭhā nipātanā sijjhanti.

571, 624. Irregular forms of suffixes and so on are established by special rule.

572, 625. Sāsadisato tassa riṭṭho ca.

572, 625. And from sāsa, disa, and so on, 'riṭṭha' is added to it.

573, 626. Sādisanta puccha bhanja hantādīhi ṭṭho.

573, 626. From sādisanta, puccha, bhanja, hanta, and so on, 'ṭṭha' is added.

574, 613. Vasato uttha.

574, 613. From vasa, 'uttha' is added.

575, 614. Vasa vāvu.

575, 614. From vasa, 'vāvu' is added.

576, 607. Dha ḍha bha he hi dhaḍḍhā ca.

576, 607. And the suffixes are 'dha', 'ḍha', 'bha', 'he', 'hi', and 'dhaḍḍhā'.

577, 628. Bhanjato ggo ca.

577, 628. And from bhanja, 'gga' is added.

578, 560. Bhujādīnamanto no dvi ca.

578, 560. The final letter of bhuja and so on becomes 'no', and it is doubled.

579, 629. Vaca vā vu.

579, 629. From vaca, 'vā' or 'vu' is added.

580, 630. Gupādīnañca.

580, 630. And this also applies to gupa and so on.

581, 616. Tarādīhi iṇṇo.

581, 616. From tara and so on, 'iṇṇa' is added.

582, 631. Bhidādito inna anna īṇā vā.

582, 631. From bhida and so on, 'inna', 'anna', or 'īṇā' is optionally added.

583, 617. Susa paca sakato kkha kkā ca.

583, 617. From susa, paca, and saka, 'kkha' and 'kkā' are added.

584, 618. Pakkamādīhi nto ca.

584, 618. And from pakkama and so on, 'nta' is added.

585, 619. Janādīna mā timhi ca.

585, 619. And for jana and so on, 'mā' is substituted before the suffix 'ti'.

586, 600. Gama khana hana ramādīnamanto.

586, 600. The final letter of gama, khana, hana, rama, and so on is subject to modification.

587, 632. Rakāro ca.

587, 632. And also the letter 'ra'.

588, Ṭhāpānamiī [M 0.0034] ca.

588. And of the roots ṭhā and pā, the suffixes are 'i' and 'ī'.

589, 621. Hantehi ho hassa ḷo vā adahanahānaṃ.

589, 621. For the root han, 'ho' is substituted; or for the 'ha' of adahana and hana, 'ḷo' is substituted.

Iti kibbidhānakappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section of the Kibbidhāna chapter.

590, 579. Ṇamhi ranjassa jo bhāvakaraṇesu.

590, 579. When the suffix 'ṇa' follows, for the root rañj, 'jo' is substituted in the abstract and instrumental senses.

591, 544. Hanassa ghāto.

591, 544. For han, 'ghāta' is substituted.

592, 503. Vadho vā sabbattha.

592, 503. Or, 'vadha' is substituted everywhere.

593, 564. Ākārantānamāyo.

593, 564. For roots ending in 'ā', the suffix is 'āyo'.

594, 582. Purasamupaparīhi karotissa kha kharā vā tappaccayesu ca.

594, 582. After the prefixes pura, sama, upa, and pari, for the root kar, 'kha' or 'khara' is substituted, and also when those suffixes follow.

595, 637. Tavetunādīsu kā.

595, 637. Before the suffixes 'tave', 'tuṃ', and so on, 'kā' is substituted.

596, 551. Gamakhanahanādīnaṃ tuṃtabbādīsu na.

For the roots gam, khan, han, and so on, there is no application in the case of the suffixes tuṃ, tabba, and so on.

597, 641. Sabbehi tunādīnaṃ yo.

After all roots, the suffix ya is used instead of tūna and so on.

598, 643. Canantehi raccaṃ.

After roots ending in ca, the suffix is racca.

599, 644. Disā svānasvantalopo ca.

After the root dis, the suffixes are svāna and svanta, and there is also elision.

600, 645. Mahadabhehi mma yha jja bbha ddhā ca.

After mahat, abbha, and so on, the suffixes are mma, yha, jja, bbha, and ddhā.

601, 334. Taddhitasamāsakitakā nāmaṃ vā’tavetunādīsu ca.

The taddhita derivatives, compounds, and kitaka derivatives are designated as nouns, as are optionally those ending in the suffixes atave, tuna, and so on.

602, 6. Dumhi garu.

In the case of du, it is a heavy syllable.

603, 7. Dīgho [M 0.0035] ca.

And a long vowel [is heavy].

604, 684. Akkharehi kāra.

After letters, the suffix kāra is used.

605, 547. Yathāgamamikāro.

The augment, the letter i, is inserted according to tradition.

606, 642. Dadhantato yo kvaci.

After a root ending in da or dha, the suffix ya is sometimes used.

Iti kibbidhānakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus the fourth chapter in the Kibbidhānakappa.

607, 578. Niggahita saṃyogādi no.

Not so before a niggahīta or an initial conjunct consonant.

608, 623. Sabbattha ge hī.

Everywhere, the suffixes are ge and hī.

609, 484. Sadassa sīdatthaṃ.

The root sad has the meaning of sīdati.

610, 627. Yajassa sarassi ṭṭhe.

For the root yaj, the suffixes are sarassi and ṭṭha.

611, 608. Hacatutthānamantānaṃ do dhe.

For h and the fourth letters of the classes, and for roots ending in them, do and dhe are substituted.

612, 615. Ḍho ḍhakāre.

Ḍha is the substitute when the letter ḍha follows.

613, 583. Gahassa ghara ṇe vā.

For the root gah, ghara is optionally substituted when the suffix ṇe follows.

614, 581. Dahassa do ḷaṃ.

For the root dah, do or ḷa is substituted.

615, 586. Dhātvantassa lopo kvimhi.

The final letter of a root is elided when the suffix kvi follows.

616, 587. Vidante ū.

For the root vid at the end of a compound, ū is substituted.

617, 633. Na ma ka rānamantānaṃ niyuttatamhi.

The preceding rule does not apply to the suffixes ma, ka, rāna, nor to roots ending in them, when they are regularly employed.

618, 571. Na ka vatthaṃ ca jā ṇvumhi.

The suffixes ka, vattha, and jā are not used when ṇvu follows.

619, 573. Karassa ca tattaṃ thusmiṃ.

And for the root kar, it becomes katta when the suffix thu follows.

620, 549. Tuṃtunatabbesu vā.

Optionally, in the case of the suffixes tuṃ, tuna, and tabba.

621, 553. Kāritaṃ [M 0.0036] viya ṇānubandho.

A suffix with the indicatory letter ṇ functions like the causative (kārita).

622, 570. Anakā yu ṇvūnaṃ.

For the suffixes yu and ṇvu, the substitute is anaka.

623, 554. Ka gā ca jānaṃ.

And for the roots ka, gā, and jā.

Iti kibbidhānakappe pañcamo kaṇḍo.

Thus the fifth chapter in the Kibbidhānakappa.

Kibbidhānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Kibbidhānasutta is finished.

8. Uṇādikappa

8. The Chapter on Uṇādi Suffixes

624, 563. Kattari kitta.

The kitta suffixes are used in the agentive sense.

625, 605. Bhāvakammesu kiccattakkhatthā.

The suffixes kicca, tta, and kkha are used in the sense of state (bhāva) and object (kamma).

626, 634. Kammani dutiyāya tto.

The suffix tto is used in the sense of object, with the second case.

627, 652. Khyādīhi mana ma ca to vā.

The suffixes mana, ma, and to are optionally used after the roots khyā and others.

628, 653. Samādīhi thamā.

The suffix thamā is used after the roots samā and others.

629, 569. Gahassu’padhasse vā.

Optionally, after `gahassu` and `upadhassu`.

630, 654. Masussa sussa ccharaccherā.

The suffixes `masussa`, `sussa`, `cchara`, and `cchera` are used.

631, 655. Āpubbacarassa ca.

And after the root `car` preceded by the prefix `ā`.

632, 656. Ala kala salehi la yā.

After the roots `ala`, `kala`, and `sala`, the suffixes `la` and `yā` are used.

633, 657. Yāṇa lāṇā.

The suffixes `yāṇa` and `lāṇā` are also used.

634, 658. Mathissa thassa lo ca.

And for the `th` of the root `math`, it is substituted by `l`.

635, 559. Pesātisaggapattakālesu kiccā.

The kicca suffixes are used in the senses of command, permission, and proper time.

636, 659. Avassakādhamiṇesu ṇī ca.

And the suffix ṇī is used in the senses of necessity and being a debtor.

637, 0. Arahasakkādīhi tuṃ.

The suffix tuṃ is used after `araha`, `sakka`, and others.

638, 668. Vajādīhi pabbajjādayo nippajjante.

Words such as pabbajjā are formed from roots such as vaj.

639, 585. Kvilopo [M 0.0037] ca.

And there is elision of the suffix kvi.

640, 0. Sacajānaṃ ka gā ṇānubandhe.

For the roots sac and aj, ka and gā are the respective substitutes when the suffix has the indicator ṇa.

641, 572. Nudādīhi yu ṇvūna manā na nā kā na na kā sakāritehi ca.

After the roots nud and others, and after causative verbs, the suffixes yu, ṇvūna, manā, na, nā, kā, na, na, kā are used.

642, 588. I ya ta ma kiṃ esānamantassaro dīghaṃ kvaci dusassa guṇaṃ doraṃ sa kkhī ca.

For `i`, `ya`, `ta`, `ma`, and `kiṃ`, the final vowel is sometimes lengthened; for `dus`, there is guṇa strengthening, and the substitutions `dora`, `sa`, and `kkhī` are also used.

643, 635. Bhyādīhi mati budhi pūjādīhi ca tto.

The suffix tto is used after the roots bhī and others, and after mati, budhi, pūjā, and others.

644, 661. Vepu sī dava vamu ku dā bhūtvādīhi thuttima ṇimā nibbatte.

The suffixes thutti, ma, ṇi, mā are formed from vepu, sī, dava, vamu, ku, dā, bhūtvā, and others.

645, 662. Akkose namhāni.

The suffix namhāni is used in the sense of abuse.

646, 419. Ekādito sakissa kkhattuṃ.

The suffix kkhattuṃ is used after eka and other numerals, and for the word saki.

647, 663. Sunassunasso ṇa vānuvānūnanakhunānā.

The suffixes are `sunassu`, `nasso`, `ṇa`, `vā`, `nu`, `vā`, `nūna`, and `nakhunānā`.

648, 664. Taruṇassa susu ca.

And for the word taruṇa, the suffix susu is used.

649, 665. Yuvassuvassuvuvānanūnā.

The suffixes are `yuvassu`, `vassu`, `vuvā`, and `nanūnā`.

650, 651. Kāle vattamānātīte ṇvādayo.

The suffixes beginning with ṇva are used in the sense of present and past time.

651, 647. Bhavissati gamādīhi ṇī ghiṇa.

In the future tense, the suffixes ṇī and ghiṇa are used after the roots gam and others.

652, 648. Kriyāyaṃ ṇvu tavo.

652, 648. The suffixes ṇvu and tavu are used in the sense of action.

653, 307. Bhāvavācimhi catutthī.

653, 307. The dative case is used in expressions of state (bhāva).

654, 649. Kammani ṇo.

654, 649. The suffix ṇo is used in the sense of object (kamma).

655, 650. Sese ssaṃ ntu mānānā.

655, 650. In the remaining senses, the suffixes ssaṃ, ntu, mānā, and nā are used.

656, 666. Chadādīhi ta traṇa.

656, 666. The suffixes ta and traṇa are used after chada and other roots.

657, 667. Vadādīhi ṇitto gaṇe.

657, 667. The suffix ṇitto is used after the group of roots beginning with vada.

658, 668. Midādīhi tti tiyo.

658, 668. The suffixes tti and tiyo are used after mida and other roots.

659, 669. Usuranjadasānaṃ [M 0.0038] daṃsassa daḍḍho ḍhaṭhā ca.

659, 669. For the root daṃsa, when preceded by usu, rañja, and dasa, it is replaced by daḍḍha and ḍhaṭhā.

660, 670. Sūvusānamūvusānamato tho ca.

660, 670. And the suffixes mato and tho are used after sūvusāna and mūvusāna.

661, 671. Ranjudādīhi dhadiddakirā kvaci jadalopo ca.

661, 671. After rañjudā and other roots, the suffix dhadiddakirā is sometimes used, and there is elision of jada.

662, 672. Paṭito hissa heraṇa hīraṇa.

662, 672. For the root hi, when preceded by paṭi, it becomes heraṇa and hīraṇa.

663, 673. Kaḍhādīhi ko.

663, 673. The suffix ko is used after kaḍhā and other roots.

664, 674. Khādāmagamānaṃ khandhandhagandhā.

664, 674. For khādāma and gama, they become khandha, andha, and gandha.

665, 675. Paṭādīlyalaṃ.

665, 675. The suffix alaṃ is used after paṭa and other roots.

666, 676. Puthassa puthu pathā mo vā.

666, 676. For putha, it optionally becomes puthu, pathā, or mo.

667, 677. Sasvādīhi tu davo.

667, 677. But the suffix davo is used after sasvā and other roots.

668, 678. Cyādīhi īvaro.

668, 678. The suffix īvaro is used after cyā and other roots.

669, 679. Munādīhi ci.

669, 679. The suffix ci is used after munā and other roots.

670, 680. Vidādīlyūro.

670, 680. The suffix ūro is used after vidā and other roots.

671, 681. Hanādīhi nu ṇu tavo.

671, 681. The suffixes nu, ṇu, and tavu are used after hanā and other roots.

672, 682. Kuṭādīhi ṭho.

672, 682. The suffix ṭho is used after kuṭa and other roots.

673, 683. Manupūrasuṇādīhi ussanusisā.

673, 683. The suffixes ussa, nusi, and sā are used after manu, pūra, suṇa and other roots.

Iti kibbidhānakappe uṇādikappo chaṭṭho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the sixth section, the Uṇādikappa, in the Kibbidhāna chapter.

Uṇādisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Uṇādisutta is concluded.

Mahākaccāyanasaddāpāṭha

Mahākaccāyana's Text on Grammar

1. Sandhikappa

1. The Chapter on Sandhi

Paṭhamakaṇḍa

First Section

(Ka)

(Ka)

Seṭṭhaṃ [M 0.0039] tilokamahitaṃ abhivandiyaggaṃ,

Buddhañca dhammamamalaṃ gaṇamuttamañca;

Satthussa tassa vacanatthavaraṃ subuddhuṃ,

Vakkhāmi suttahitamettha susandhikappaṃ.

Having paid homage to the Buddha—the best, the foremost, revered by the three worlds—and to the stainless Dhamma and the supreme Sangha; having well understood the excellent meaning of that Teacher's words, I shall explain here the good Sandhikappa, which is beneficial for the suttas.

(Kha)

(Kha)

Seyyaṃ jineritanayena budhā labhanti,

Tañcāpi tassa vacanatthasubodhanena;

Atthañca akkharapadesu amohabhāvā,

Seyyatthiko padamato vividhaṃ suṇeyyaṃ.

The wise attain the excellent by the method taught by the Victor, and also by a thorough understanding of the meaning of his words. And since the meaning is understood through non-delusion regarding the letters and their parts, one who seeks the excellent should listen to the various teachings from this text.

1, 1. Attho akkharasaññāto.

1, 1. The meaning is known through the letters.

Sabbavacanānamattho akkhareheva saññāyate. Akkharavipattiyaṃ hi atthassa dunnayathā hoti, tasmā akkharakosallaṃ bahūpakāraṃ suttantesu.

The meaning of all words is known only through the letters. For when there is a defect in the letters, the meaning becomes difficult to ascertain. Therefore, skill in letters is very helpful in the Suttas.

2, 2. Akkharāpādayo [M 0.0040] ekacattālīsaṃ.

2, 2. The letters, beginning with 'a', are forty-one.

Te ca kho akkharā api akārādayo ekacattā līsa suttantesu sopakārā.

And indeed, these letters, beginning with 'a', are forty-one, and are helpful in the Suttas.

Taṃ yathā? A ā i ī u ū e o, ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va sa ha ḷa aṃ, iti akkharā nāma.

Namely: a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, o, ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va sa ha ḷa aṃ. These are called letters.

Tena kvattho? Attho akkharasaññāto.

What is its application? The meaning is known through the letters.

3, 3. Tatthodantā sarā aṭṭha.

3, 3. Among them, the vowels ending in 'o' are eight.

Tattha akkharesu akārādīsu odantā aṭṭha akkharā sarā nāma honti.

Among those letters, the eight letters beginning with 'a' and ending with 'o' are called vowels.

Taṃ yathā? A ā i ī u ū e o, iti sarā nāma.

Namely: a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, o. These are called vowels.

Tena kvattho? Sarā sare lopaṃ.

What is its application? A vowel is elided before a following vowel.

4, 4. Lahumattā tayo rassā.

4, 4. Three are short due to their light measure.

Tattha aṭṭhasu saresu lahumattā tayo sarā rassā nāma honti.

Among those eight vowels, three vowels of light measure are called short.

Taṃ yathā? A i u, iti rassā nāma.

Namely: a, i, u. These are called short.

Tena kvattho? Rassaṃ.

What is its application? Shortening.

5, 5. Aññe [M 0.0041] dīghā.

5, 5. The others are long.

Tattha aṭṭhasu saresu rassehi aññe pañca sarā dīghā nāma honti.

Among those eight vowels, the five vowels other than the short ones are called long.

Taṃ yathā? Ā ī ū e o, iti dīghā nāma.

Namely: ā, ī, ū, e, o. These are called long.

Tena kvattho? Dīghaṃ.

What is its application? Lengthening.

6, 8. Sesā byañjanā.

6, 8. The remaining are consonants.

Ṭhapetvā aṭṭha sare sesā akkharā kakārādayo niggahitantā byañjanā nāma honti.

Excluding the eight vowels, the remaining letters, beginning with 'ka' and ending with the niggahita, are called consonants.

Taṃ yathā? Ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va sa ha ḷa aṃ, iti byañjanā nāma.

Namely: ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va sa ha ḷa aṃ. These are called consonants.

Tena kvattho? Sarā pakati byañjane.

What is its application? A vowel remains unchanged before a consonant.

7, 9. Vaggā pañcapañcaso mantā.

7, 9. The classes are five by five, ending in 'ma'.

Tesaṃ kho byañjanānaṃ kakārādayo makārantā pañcapañcaso akkharavanto vaggā nāma honti.

Among these consonants, those beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'ma', having five letters each, are called classes.

Taṃ yathā? Ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, iti vaggā nāma.

Namely: ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma. These are called classes.

Tena kvattho? Vaggantaṃ vā vagge.

What is its application? The class-nasal is optionally used before a consonant of the same class.

8, 10. Aṃ [M 0.0042] iti niggahitaṃ.

8, 10. 'Aṃ' is the niggahita.

Aṃ iti niggahitaṃ nāma hoti.

'Aṃ' is called the niggahita.

Tena kvattho? Aṃ byañjane niggahitaṃ.

What is its application? 'Aṃ' is the niggahita before a consonant.

9, 11. Parasamaññā payoge.

9, 11. Other designations are used in application.

Yā ca pana paresu sakkataganthesu samaññā ghosāti vā aghosāti vā, tā payoge sati etthāpi yujjante.

And whatever designations, such as 'voiced' or 'unvoiced', are found in other Sanskrit texts, those also apply here when in use.

Tattha ghosā nāma-ga gha ṅa, ja jha ña, ḍa ḍha ṇa, da dha na, ba bha ma, ya ra la va ha ḷa, iti ghosā nāma. Aghosā nāma-ka kha, ca cha, ṭa ṭha, ta tha, pa pha, sa, iti aghosā nāma.

Here, the voiced consonants are: ga gha ṅa, ja jha ña, ḍa ḍha ṇa, da dha na, ba bha ma, ya ra la va ha ḷa. These are called voiced. The unvoiced consonants are: ka kha, ca cha, ṭa ṭha, ta tha, pa pha, sa. These are called unvoiced.

Tena kvattho? Vagge ghosāghosānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā.

What is its application? In a class, the third and first consonants are used for voiced and unvoiced respectively.

10, 12. Pubbamadhoṭhita massaraṃ sarena viyojaye.

10, 12. One should separate the preceding consonant, placed below, from its vowel.

Tattha sandhiṃ kattukāmo pubbabyañjanaṃ adhoṭhitaṃ assaraṃ katvā sarañca upari katvā sarena viyojaye.

Here, one wishing to perform sandhi should make the preceding consonant vowel-less and place it below, and having placed the vowel above, should separate it from the vowel.

Tatrāyamādi.

This is the beginning of that process.

11, 14. Naye [M 0.0043] paraṃ yutte.

11, 14. One should lead the following letter when appropriate.

Assaraṃ kho byañjanaṃ adhoṭhataṃ parakkharaṃ naye yutte. Tatrābhiratimiccheyya.

Indeed, one should lead the vowel-less consonant, placed below, to the following letter when appropriate. One should desire delight in that.

Yuttetikasmā? Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me. Ettha pana yuttaṃ na hoti.

Why the word 'yutte' (appropriate)? As in: 'He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.' Here, however, sandhi is not appropriate.

Iti sandhikappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section in the Sandhikappa.

Dutiyakaṇḍa

Second Section

12, 13. Sarā sare lopaṃ.

12, 13. A vowel before a vowel is elided.

Sarā kho sare pare lopaṃ papponti.

Vowels, indeed, when followed by other vowels, undergo elision.

Yassindriyāni samathaṅgatāni. No hetaṃ bhante sametāyasmā saṅghena.

“Whose faculties are calmed.” “No, venerable sir, the venerable one is not in agreement with the Saṅgha.”

13, 15. Vā paro asarūpā.

13, 15. Optionally the following, after a dissimilar vowel.

Saramhā asarūpā paro saro lopaṃ pappoti vā.

After a dissimilar vowel, the following vowel optionally undergoes elision.

Cattāro’me bhikkhave dhammā, kinnu’ māvasamaṇiyo. Vāti kasmā? Pañcindriyāni, tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti.

Cattāro’me bhikkhave dhammā; kinnu’ māvasamaṇiyo. Why 'vā' (optionally)? Pañcindriyāni; tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti.

14, 16. Kvacāsacaṇṇaṃ [M 0.0044] lutte.

14, 16. Sometimes, upon elision, there is dissimilation.

Saro kho paro pubbasare lutte kvaci asavaṇṇaṃ pappoti.

A following vowel, when the preceding vowel is elided, sometimes becomes dissimilar.

Saṅkhyaṃ nopeti vedagū, bandhusseva samāgamo.

The sage is beyond reckoning; it is like the gathering of relatives.

Kvacīti kasmā? Yassindriyāni, tathūpamaṃ dhammavaraṃ adesayi.

Why 'sometimes'? Yassindriyāni; tathūpamaṃ dhammavaraṃ adesayi.

15, 17. Dīghaṃ.

15, 17. Lengthening.

Saro kho paro pubbasare lutte kvaci dīghaṃ pappoti. Saddhīdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, anāgārehi cūbhayaṃ.

A following vowel, when a preceding vowel is elided, sometimes becomes long. “Faith here is the best wealth for a person”; “and for both householders and renunciates.”

Kvacīti kasmā? Pañcahupāli aṅgehi samannāgato. Natthaññaṃ kiñci.

Why 'sometimes'? “Endowed with five qualities, O Upāli.” “There is nothing else.”

16, 18. Pubbo ca.

16, 18. And the preceding.

Pubbo ca saro parasaralope kate kvaci dīghaṃ pappoti.

And the preceding vowel sometimes becomes long when the following vowel is elided.

Kiṃsūdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, sādhūti paṭissuṇitvā, kvacīti kasmā? Itissa muhuttampi.

Kiṃsūdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ; sādhūti paṭissuṇitvā. Why 'sometimes'? Itissa muhuttampi.

17, 19. Yamedantassādeso[M 0.0045].

17, 19. The substitution of 'y' for a final 'e'.

Ekārassa antabhūtassa sare pare kvaci yakārādeso hoti.

For a final 'e', when a vowel follows, there is sometimes the substitution of 'y'.

Adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo, tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadeyyaṃ, tyāssa pahīnā honti.

This Dhamma has indeed been attained by me; I would say thus to them; for him, those things are abandoned.

Kvacīti kasmā? Ne’nāgatā, iti nettha.

Why 'sometimes'? Not future, thus not here.

18, 20. Vamodudantānaṃ.

18, 20. Of 'v' for those ending in 'o' and 'u'.

Okārukārānaṃ antabhūtānaṃ sare pare kvaci vakārādeso hoti.

For a final 'o' or 'u', 'v' is sometimes substituted when a vowel follows.

Atha khvassa, svassa hoti, bahvābādho, vatthvettha vihitaṃ niccaṃ cakkhāpāthamāgacchati.

Then indeed for him; it becomes his; much affliction; the object arranged here constantly comes into the range of vision.

Kvacītikasmā? Cattāro’me bhikkhave dhammā, kinnumāva samaṇiyo.

Why 'sometimes'? 'These four things, O bhikkhus'; 'Why indeed, these female ascetics?'

19, 22. Sabbo caṃti.

19, 22. The whole of 'iti' [becomes] 'ca'.

Sabbo icceso tisaddo byañjano sare pare kvaci cakāraṃ pappoti.

The entire word 'iti' sometimes becomes the sound 'c' when a vowel follows.

Iccetaṃ [M 0.0046] kusalaṃ, iccassa vacanīyaṃ, paccuttaritvā, paccāharati.

Thus this is skillful; thus it is to be spoken for him; having replied, one withdraws.

Kvacīti kasmā? Itissa muhuttampi.

Why 'sometimes'? 'Thus for him, even for a moment.'

20, 27. Do dhassa ca.

20, 27. 'Da' for 'dha', and 'ca'.

Dhaiccetassa sare pare kvaci dakārādeso hoti.

For the sound 'dha', the sound 'da' is sometimes substituted when a vowel follows.

Ekamidāhaṃ bhikkhave samayaṃ.

At one time, bhikkhus, I...

Kvacīti kasmā? Idheva maraṇaṃ bhavissati.

Why 'sometimes'? Death will occur right here.

Vaggahaṇena dhakārassa hakārādeso hoti sāhu dassana mariyānaṃ.

By the class-rule, the substitution of 'ha' for 'dha' occurs: 'Good is the sight of the noble ones'.

Suttavibhāgena bahudhā siyā-

By analysis of the rules, it may occur in many ways.

To dassa, yathā? Sugato.

'Ta' for 'da', how? Sugato.

Ṭo tassa, yathā? Dukkaṭaṃ.

'Ṭa' for 'ta', how? Dukkaṭaṃ.

Dho tassa, yathā? Gandhabbo.

'Dha' for 'ta', how? Gandhabbo.

Tro ttassa, yathā? Atrajo.

'Tra' for 'tta', how? Atrajo.

Ko gassa, yathā? Kulūpako.

'Ka' for 'ga', how? Kulūpako.

Lo [M 0.0047] rassa, yathā? Mahāsālo.

'La' for 'ra', how? Mahāsālo.

Jo yassa, yathā? Gavajo.

'Ja' for 'ya', how? Gavajo.

Bbo vassa, yathā? Kubbato.

'Bba' for 'va', how? Kubbato.

Ko yassa, yathā? Sake.

'Ka' for 'ya', how? Sake.

Yo jassa, yathā? Niyaṃputtaṃ.

'Ya' for 'ja', how? Niyaṃputtaṃ.

Ko tassa, yathā? Niyako.

'Ka' for 'ta', how? Niyako.

Cco ttassa, yathā bhacco.

'Cca' for 'tta', as in 'bhacco'.

Pho passa, yathā? Nipphatti.

'Pha' for 'pa', how? Nipphatti.

Kho kassa, yathā? Nikkhamati. Iccevamādī yojetabbā.

'Kha' for 'ka', how? Nikkhamati. Thus, these and others should be applied.

21, 21. Ivaṇṇo yaṃ navā.

21, 21. The i-vowel becomes 'ya', optionally.

Pubbo ivaṇṇo sare pare yakāraṃ pappoti navā. Paṭisunthāravutyassa, sabbā vityānubhūyate.

A preceding i-vowel, when a vowel follows, optionally becomes 'ya'. Paṭisunthāravutyassa; sabbā vityānubhūyate.

Navāti kasmā? Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato, muttacāgī anuddhato.

Why 'optionally'? Endowed with five qualities; liberal, unagitated.

22, 28. Evādissa ri pubbo ca rasso.

22, 28. For the initial 'e' of 'eva', 'ri' is substituted, and the preceding vowel is shortened.

Saramhā parassa evassa ekārassa ādissa rikāro hoti, pubbo ca saro rasso hoti navā.

For the initial 'e' of 'eva' that follows a vowel, 'ri' is substituted, and the preceding vowel is optionally shortened.

Yathariva [M 0.0048] vasudhātalañca sabbaṃ, tathariva guṇavā supūjaniyo.

Just as the entire earth, so too is the virtuous one highly venerable.

Navāti kasmā? Yathā eva, tathā eva.

Why 'optionally'? Just as it is, so it is.

Iti sandhikappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the second section in the chapter on Sandhi.

Tatiyakaṇḍa

The Third Section

23, 26. Sarā pakati byañjane.

23, 26. Vowels remain unchanged before a consonant.

Sarā kho byañjane pare pakatirūpāni honti.

Vowels, indeed, remain in their natural form when a consonant follows.

Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, pamādo maccuno padaṃ, tiṇṇo pāraṅgato ahu.

Mind precedes all mental states. Heedlessness is the path to death. He has crossed over and gone beyond.

24, 35. Sare kvaci.

24, 35. Sometimes before a vowel.

Sarā kho sare pare kvaci pakatirūpāni honti.

Vowels, indeed, sometimes remain in their natural form when a vowel follows.

Ko imaṃ pathaviṃ vicessati.

Who will comprehend this earth?

Kvacīti kasmā? Appassutāyaṃ puriso.

Why 'sometimes'? This person is unlearned.

25, 37. Dīghaṃ.

25, 37. Lengthening.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci dīghaṃ papponti.

Vowels, indeed, are sometimes lengthened when a consonant follows.

Sammā [M 0.0049] dhammaṃ vipassato, evaṃ gāme munī care, khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā.

For one who rightly discerns the Dhamma; thus should a sage fare in the village; patience, forbearance, is the highest austerity.

Kvacīti kasmā? Idha modati pecca modati, patilīyati, paṭihaññati.

Why 'sometimes'? Here one rejoices, hereafter one rejoices; one shrinks back, one is afflicted.

26, 38. Rassaṃ.

26, 38. Shortening.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci rassaṃ papponti.

Vowels, indeed, are sometimes shortened when a consonant follows.

Bhovādināma so hoti, yathābhāvi guṇena so.

He is one named 'Bhovādī'; he is so by his inherent quality.

Kvacīti kasmā? Sammāsamādhi, sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ, upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu.

Why 'sometimes'? Right concentration; the Sāvitrī is the chief of meters; life is led on, short is the lifespan.

27, 39. Lopañca tatrākāro.

27, 39. And elision, and thereupon the insertion of 'a'.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci lopaṃ papponti. Tatra ca lope kate akārāgamo hoti.

Vowels, indeed, when a consonant follows, sometimes undergo elision. And when that elision has occurred, the vowel 'a' is inserted.

Sa sīlavā. Sa paññavā esa dhammo sanantano, sa ve kasāvamarahati, sa mānakāmopi bhaveyya, sa ve muni jātibhayaṃ adassi.

He is virtuous. He is wise. This is the eternal Dhamma. He indeed deserves the saffron robe. He might even be one desirous of honor. He indeed, the sage, has seen the fear of birth.

Kvacīti [M 0.0050] kasmā? So muni, eso dhammo padissati, na so kāsāvamarahati.

Why 'sometimes'? That sage; this Dhamma is seen; he does not deserve the saffron robe.

28, 40. Para dvebhāvo ṭhāne.

28, 40. The following consonant is sometimes doubled.

Saramhā parassa byañjanassa dvebhāvo hoti ṭhāne.

A consonant that follows a vowel is sometimes doubled.

Idhappamādo, purisassa jantuno, pabbajjaṃ kittayissāmi, cātuddasi, pañcaddasi, abhikkantataro cando.

Here, heedfulness, of a person, of a living being. I will proclaim the going forth. On the fourteenth, on the fifteenth, the moon is more radiant.

Ṭhāneti kasmā? Idha modati pecca modati.

Why 'in place'? Here he rejoices, hereafter he rejoices.

29, 42. Vagge ghosāghosānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā.

29, 42. In a class, the third and first of voiced and voiceless consonants.

Vagge kho pubbesaṃ byañjanānaṃ ghosāghosabhūtānaṃ saramhā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ tatiyapaṭhamakkharā dvebhāvaṃ gacchanti ṭhāne.

In a class, indeed, of preceding consonants, being voiced and voiceless, from a vowel, respectively, the third and first letters undergo doubling in place.

Eseva cajjhānapphalo, yatraṭṭhitaṃ nappasaheyya maccu, sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito, cattāriṭṭhānāni naro pamatto.
