This indeed is the fruit of meditation, where death cannot overpower one who stands firm. Like one standing on a mountain peak, a heedless man encounters four dangers.

Ṭhāneti kasmā? Idha cetaso daḷhaṃ gaṇhāti thāmasā.

Why 'in place'? Here, he firmly grasps the mind with strength.

Iti sandhikappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section in the chapter on Sandhi.

Catutthakaṇḍa

Fourth Section

30, 58. Aṃ [M 0.0051] byañjane niggahitaṃ.

30, 58. The niggahita becomes 'aṃ' before a consonant.

Niggahitaṃ kho byañjane pare aṃ iti hoti.

The niggahita, indeed, becomes 'aṃ' when a consonant follows.

Evaṃ vutte, taṃ sādhūti paṭissuṇitvā.

When this was said, having assented with 'Good!'

31, 49. Vaggantaṃ vā vagge.

31, 49. Optionally, the niggahita becomes the class-final nasal before a consonant of the same class.

Vaggabhūte byañjane pare niggahitaṃ kho vaggantaṃ vā pappoti.

When a class-consonant follows, the niggahita, indeed, optionally attains the class-final nasal.

Tanniccutaṃ, dhammañcare sucaritaṃ, cirappavāsiṃ purisaṃ. Santantassa manaṃ hoti, taṅkāruṇikaṃ, evaṅkho bhikkhave sikkhitabbaṃ.

That which is certain; one should practice the well-practiced Dhamma; a person long away from home. His mind becomes tranquil; that compassionate one; thus, indeed, monks, should you train.

Vāggahaṇenaniggahitaṃ kho lakārādeso hoti. Puggalaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'vā', the niggahita, indeed, is optionally substituted by the letter 'l'. Puggalaṃ.

Vāti kasmā? Na taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu.

Why 'vā'? That deed is not well done.

32, 50. Ehe uṃ.

32, 50. Before 'e' and 'h', the niggahita becomes 'ñ'.

Ekārahakāre pare niggahitaṃ kho ñakāraṃ pappoti vā.

When the letter 'e' or 'h' follows, the niggahita, indeed, optionally becomes the letter 'ñ'.

Paccattaññeva parinibbāyissāmi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi, evañhi vo bhikkhave sikkhitabbaṃ. Tañhi tassa musā hoti.

I will attain Parinibbāna for myself alone; I will ask just that here; thus, indeed, monks, should you train. For that would be a lie for him.

Vāti [M 0.0052] kasmā? Evametaṃ abhiññāya, evaṃ hoti subhāsitaṃ.

Why 'vā'? Having fully known this thus; thus is well spoken.

33, 50. Saye ca.

33, 50. And with 'ya'.

Niggahitaṃ kho yakāre pare saha yakārena ñakāraṃ pappoti vā.

Indeed, when the letter 'ya' follows, the niggahita is optionally changed to the letter 'ñ'.

Saññogo, saññuttaṃ.

Connection, conjoined.

Vāti kasmā? Saṃyogo, saṃyuttaṃ.

Why 'vā'? Union, united.

34, 52. Madā sare.

34, 52. Before a vowel, the niggahita becomes 'm' or 'd'.

Niggahitassa kho sare pare makāradakārādesā honti vā.

Of the niggahita, indeed, when a vowel follows, substitutions of the letters 'm' and 'd' optionally occur.

Tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ, etadavoca satthā.

Him I call a brahmin; thus spoke the Teacher.

Vāti kasmā? Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me.

Why 'vā'? He abused me, he struck me, he overcame me, he robbed me.

35, 34. Ya va ma da na ta ra lā cāgamā.

35, 34. The letters y, v, m, d, n, t, r, and l are augments.

Sare pare yakāro vakāro makāro dakāro nakāro takāro rakāro lakāro ime āgamā honti vā.

When a vowel follows, the letters y, v, m, d, n, t, r, and l are optional augments.

Nayimassa vijjā, yathayidaṃ cittaṃ. Migī bhantā vudikkhati, sittā te lahu messati, asittā te garu messati. Asso [M 0.0053] bhadro kasāmiva, sammadaññā vimuttānaṃ. Manasādaññā vimuttānaṃ, attadatthamabhiññāya. Ciraṃnāyati, ito nāyati. Yasmātiha bhikkhave, tasmātiha bhikkhave, ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ. Sabbhireva samāsetha, āraggeriva sāsapo, sāsaporiva āraggā. Chaḷabhiññā, saḷāyatanaṃ.

There is no knowledge for this one, just as this mind is. A bewildered doe looks on; if sprinkled, it will be light for you; if unsprinkled, it will be heavy for you. Like a noble horse under the whip, having rightly understood the liberated ones. Having understood the liberated ones with the mind, having fully known one's own welfare. It leads for a long time; it leads from here. Therefore, O monks, therefore, O monks, from today onward, as long as life lasts. One should associate only with the good, like a mustard seed on the tip of an awl, like a mustard seed on the tip of an awl. The six higher knowledges, the six sense spheres.

Vāti kasmā? Evaṃ mahiddhiyā esā, akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me, ajeyyo anugāmiko.

Why 'vā'? Thus, this one is of great power. He abused me, he struck me, he overcame me, he robbed me, unconquerable, a follower.

Caggahaṇena idheva makārassa pakāro hoti. Cirappavāsiṃ purisaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', here indeed the letter 'm' becomes the letter 'p'. A man long absent.

Kakārassa ca dakāro hoti. Sadatthapasuto siyā.

And the letter 'k' becomes the letter 'd'. One should be devoted to one's own welfare.

Dakārassa ca takāro hoti, sugato.

And the letter 'd' becomes the letter 't', Sugato.

36, 47. Kvaci o byañjane.

36, 47. Sometimes 'o' before a consonant.

Byañjane pare kvaci okārāgamo hoti.

When a consonant follows, the augmentation of 'o' sometimes occurs.

Atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ. Parosahassaṃ.

Indeed, it is too early to go for alms in Sāvatthī. Over a thousand.

Kvacīki [M 0.0054] kasmā? Etha passathimaṃ lokaṃ, andhībhūto ayaṃ loko.

Why 'sometimes'? Come, see this world! This world has become blind.

37, 57. Niggahitañca.

37, 57. And the niggahita.

Niggahitañcāgamo hoti sare vā byañjane vā pare kvaci.

And the augmentation of the niggahita sometimes occurs when a vowel or a consonant follows.

Cakkhuṃudapādi, avaṃsiro, yāvañcidha bhikkhave purimaṃ jātiṃ sarāmi, aṇuṃthūlāni sabbaso, manopubbaṅgamā dhammā.

The eye arose; head downward; as far, O monks, as I here remember a previous birth; subtle and gross, entirely; phenomena are preceded by mind.

Kvacīti kasmā? Idheva naṃ pasaṃsanti, pecca sagge pamodati, na hi etehi yānehi, gaccheyya agataṃ disaṃ.

Why 'sometimes'? Here indeed they praise him; after death he rejoices in heaven. Surely, by these vehicles one would not go to the unattained region.

Caggahaṇena visaddassa ca pakāro hoti. Pacessati, vicessati vā.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the letter 'p' also occurs for 'visadda'. Pacessati, or vicessati.

38, 53. Kvaci lopaṃ.

38, 53. Sometimes elision.

Niggahitaṃ kho sare pare kvaci lopaṃ pappoti.

The niggahita, indeed, when a vowel follows, sometimes undergoes elision.

Tāsāhaṃ santike, vidūnaggamiti.

I am near them; the foremost among the wise.

Kvacīti kasmā? Ahameva nūna bālo etamatthaṃ viditvāna.

Why 'sometimes'? I indeed am surely a fool, having known this matter.

39, 54. Byañjane [M 0.0055] ca.

39, 54. And before a consonant.

Niggahitaṃ kho byañjane pare kvaci lopaṃ pappoti.

The niggahita, indeed, when a consonant follows, sometimes undergoes elision.

Ariyasaccānadassanaṃ, etaṃ buddhānasāsanaṃ.

The non-seeing of the Noble Truths; this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

Kvacīti kasmā? Etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ, taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante.

Why 'sometimes'? This is the highest blessing; that I tell you, O fortunate sirs.

40, 55. Paro vāsaro.

40, 55. Optionally, the following vowel.

Niggahitamhā paro saro lopaṃ pappoti vā.

The vowel following a niggahita optionally undergoes elision.

Bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti, uttattaṃva, yathābījaṃva, yathādhaññaṃva.

They delight in what was spoken; like something heated; like a seed; like grain.

Vāti kasmā? Ahameva nūna bālo, etadahosi.

Why 'vā'? I indeed am surely a fool; this was so.

41, 56. Byañjano ca visaññogo.

41, 56. And the consonant is disjoined.

Niggahitamhā parasmiṃ sare lutte yadi byañjano sasaññogo visaññogo hoti.

When the vowel following a niggahita is elided, if the consonant is conjoined, it becomes disjoined.

Evaṃsa te āsavo, pupphaṃsā uppajji.

Thus for him is your taint; his flower arose.

Lutteti kasmā? Evamassa vidūnaggamiti.

Why 'elided'? Thus for him it is the foremost among the wise.

Caggahaṇena [M 0.0056] tiṇṇaṃ byañjanānamantare ye sarūpā, tesampi lopo hoti. Agyāgāraṃ, paṭisanthāravutyassa.

By the inclusion of 'ca', among three consonants, the elision of those that are identical also occurs. Examples: Agyāgāraṃ, paṭisanthāravutyassa.

Iti sandhikappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fourth section in the chapter on Sandhi.

Pañcamakaṇḍa

Fifth Section

42, 32. Gosare puthassāgamo kvaci.

For `putha`, the augment `ga` is sometimes inserted when a vowel follows.

Puthaiccetassa ante sare pare kvaci gakārāgamo hoti.

For this word `putha`, when a vowel follows, there is sometimes the augment `ga`.

Puthage va.

Example: Puthageva.

43, 33. Pāssa canto rasso.

For `pā`, and the final is short.

Pāiccetassa ante sare pare kvaci gakārāgamo hoti, anto ca saro rasso hoti.

When `pā` is followed by a vowel, sometimes the augment `ga` is inserted, and its final vowel becomes short.

Pageva vutyassa.

Example: Pageva.

Kvacīti kasmā? Pā eva vutyassa.

Why 'sometimes'? [For the counter-example:] Pā eva.

44, 24. Abbho abhi.

`Abhi` becomes `abbho`.

Abhiiccetassa sare pare abbhādeso hoti. Abbhudīritaṃ, abbhuggacchati.

When `abhi` is followed by a vowel, it is replaced by `abbha`. Examples: Abbhudīritaṃ, abbhuggacchati.

45, 25. Ajjho [M 0.0057] adhi.

`Adhi` becomes `ajjho`.

Adhiiccetassa sare pare ajjhādeso hoti.

When `adhi` is followed by a vowel, it is replaced by `ajjha`.

Ajjhokāse, ajjhāgamā.

Examples: Ajjhokāse, ajjhāgamā.

46, 26. Te na vā ivaṇṇe.

Those two [substitutions occur] optionally when an `i`-vowel follows.

Te ca kho abhiadhiiccete ivaṇṇe pare abbho ajjhoitivuttarūpā naṃ honti vā.

Indeed, these two, `abhi` and `adhi`, when followed by an `i`-vowel, optionally do not take the forms `abbho` and `ajjho` as stated.

Abhicchitaṃ, adhīritaṃ.

Examples: Abhicchitaṃ, adhīritaṃ.

Vāti kasmā? Abbhīritaṃ, ajjhiṇamutto.

Why `vā` (optionally)? Examples: Abbhīritaṃ, ajjhiṇamutto.

47, 23. Atissa cantassa.

And for the final of `ati` [there is no lengthening].

Atiiccetassa antabhūtassa tisaddassa ivaṇṇe pare “sabbo caṃ tī”ti vuttarūpaṃ na hoti.

For this `ati`, when its final `ti` is followed by an `i`-vowel, the form `tī` prescribed by the rule `sabbo caṃ tī` does not occur.

Atīsigaṇo, atīritaṃ.

Examples: Atīsigaṇo, atīritaṃ.

Ivaṇṇeti kasmā? Accantaṃ.

Why `ivaṇṇe` (when an `i`-vowel follows)? Example: Accantaṃ.

48, 43. Kvaci paṭi patissa.

Sometimes `pati` becomes `paṭi`.

Patiiccetassa sare vā byañjane vā pare kvaci paṭiādeso hoti.

For this `pati`, when followed by either a vowel or a consonant, it is sometimes replaced by `paṭi`.

Paṭaggi dātabbo, paṭihaññati.

Examples: Paṭaggi dātabbo, paṭihaññati.

Kvacīti [M 0.0058] kasmā? Paccantimesu janapadesu, patilīyati, patirūpadesavāso ca.

Why 'sometimes'? Examples: Paccantimesu janapadesu, patilīyati, patirūpadesavāso ca.

49, 44. Puthassu byañjane.

For `putha`, the final vowel becomes `u` before a consonant.

Puthaiccetassa anto saro byañjane pare ukāro hoti.

For this `putha`, when a consonant follows, the final vowel becomes `u`.

Puthujjano, puthubhūtaṃ.

Examples: Puthujjano, puthubhūtaṃ.

Antaggahaṇena aputhassāpi sare pare antassa ukāro hoti, manuññaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'anta', even for a word other than 'putha', its final becomes 'u' when a vowel follows; for example, 'manuññaṃ'.

50, 45. O avassa.

50, 45. 'Ava' becomes 'o'.

Avaiccetassa byañjane pare kvaci okāro hoti.

When 'ava' is followed by a consonant, it sometimes becomes 'o'.

Andhakārena onaddhā.

For example: 'andhakārena onaddhā'.

Kvacīti kasmā? Avasussatu me sarīre maṃsalohitaṃ.

Why 'sometimes'? For example: 'avasussatu me sarīre maṃsalohitaṃ'.

51, 59. Anupadiṭṭhānaṃ vuttayogato.

51, 59. For those not explicitly stated, apply according to the stated method.

Anupadiṭṭhānaṃ upasagganipātānaṃ sarasandhīhi byañjanasandhīhi vuttasandhīhi ca yathāyogaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

For prefixes and particles not explicitly mentioned, vowel sandhi, consonant sandhi, and other stated sandhi rules should be applied as appropriate.

Pāpanaṃ[M 0.0059], parāyaṇaṃ, upāyanaṃ, upāhanaṃ, nyāyogo, nigupadhi, anubodho, duvūpasantaṃ, suvūpasantaṃ, dvālayo, svālayo, durākhyātaṃ, svākhyāto, udīritaṃ, samuddiṭṭhaṃ, viyaggaṃ, vijjhaggaṃ, byaggaṃ, avayāgamanaṃ, anveti, anupaghāto, anacchariyaṃ, pariyesanā, parāmāso, evaṃ sare ca honti.

For example: 'pāpanaṃ', 'parāyaṇaṃ', 'upāyanaṃ', 'upāhanaṃ', 'nyāyogo', 'nigūpadhi', 'anubodho', 'duvūpasantaṃ', 'suvūpasantaṃ', 'dvālayo', 'svālayo', 'durākhyātaṃ', 'svākhyāto', 'udīritaṃ', 'samuddiṭṭhaṃ', 'viyaggaṃ', 'vijjhaggaṃ', 'byaggaṃ', 'avayāgamanaṃ', 'anveti', 'anupaghāto', 'anacchariyaṃ', 'pariyesanā', 'parāmāso'—thus they also occur in the case of vowels.

Pariggaho, paggaho, pakkamo, parakkamo, nikkamo, nikkasāvo, nillayanaṃ, dullayanaṃ, dumbhikkhaṃ, dubbuttaṃ, sandiṭṭhaṃ, duggaho, viggaho, niggato, abhikkamo, paṭikkamo, evaṃ byañjane ca. Sesā sabbe yojetabbā.

For example: 'pariggaho', 'paggaho', 'pakkamo', 'parakkamo', 'nikkamo', 'nikkasāvo', 'nillayanaṃ', 'dullayanaṃ', 'dumbhikkhaṃ', 'dubbuttaṃ', 'sandiṭṭhaṃ', 'duggaho', 'viggaho', 'niggato', 'abhikkamo', 'paṭikkamo'—thus also in the case of consonants. All remaining ones should be applied.

Iti sandhikappe pañcamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the Fifth Section in the Chapter on Sandhi.

Sandhikappo niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Sandhi is concluded.

2. Nāmakappa

2. The Chapter on Nouns

Paṭhamakaṇḍa

First Section

52, 60. Jinavacanayuttaṃ [M 0.0060] hi.

52, 60. Indeed, in accordance with the Conqueror's word.

“Jinavacanayuttaṃ hi” iccetaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

'Jinavacanayuttaṃ hi'—this should be understood as a governing rule.

53, 61. Liṅgañca nippajjate.

53, 61. And the gender is formed.

Yathā yathā jinavacanayuttaṃ hi liṅgaṃ, tathā tathā idha liṅgañca nippajjate.

Just as the gender is in accordance with the Conqueror's word, so too is the gender formed here.

Taṃ yathā? Eso no satthā, brahmā attā, sakhā, rājā.

How so? For example: 'eso no satthā', 'brahmā attā', 'sakhā', 'rājā'.

54, 62. Tato ca vibhattiyo.

54, 62. And from that, the case endings.

Tato jinavacanayuttehi liṅgehi vibhattiyo parā honti.

From those genders that are in accordance with the Conqueror's word, the case endings follow.

55, 63. Si yo, aṃ yo, nā hi, sa naṃ, smā hi, sa naṃ, smiṃ su.

55, 63. Si, yo; aṃ, yo; nā, hi; sa, naṃ; smā, hi; sa, naṃ; smiṃ, su.

Kā ca pana tāyo vibhattiyo? Si, yo iti paṭhamā, aṃ, yoiti dutiyā, nā hi iti tatiyā, sa, naṃiti catutthī, smā, hi iti pañcamī, sa, naṃ iti chaṭṭhī, smiṃ, su iti sattamī.

And what, then, are those case endings? 'Si', 'yo' are the first; 'aṃ', 'yo' are the second; 'nā', 'hi' are the third; 'sa', 'naṃ' are the fourth; 'smā', 'hi' are the fifth; 'sa', 'naṃ' are the sixth; 'smiṃ', 'su' are the seventh.

Vibhattiiccanena [M 0.0061] kvattho? Amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se.

What is the purpose of the term 'vibhatti'? For such rules as 'amhassa mamaṃ' and 'savibhattissa se'.

56, 64. Tadanuparodhena.

56, 64. Without conflicting with that.

Yathā yathā tesaṃ jinavacanānaṃ anuparodho. Tathā tathā idha liṅgañca nippajjate.

Insofar as there is no conflict with those words of the Conqueror, so is the gender also formed here.

57, 71. Ālapane si ga sañño.

57, 71. In the vocative, 'si' is designated 'ga'.

Ālapanatthe si gasañño hoti.

In the sense of address, 'si' has the designation 'ga'.

Bhoti ayye, bhoti kaññe, bhoti kharādiye.

For example: 'bhoti ayye', 'bhoti kaññe', 'bhoti kharādiye'.

Ālapaneti kimatthaṃ? Sā ayyā.

Why 'ālapane' (in the vocative)? For example: 'sā ayyā'.

Sīti kimatthaṃ? Bhotiyo ayyāyo.

Why 'si'? For example: 'bhotiyo ayyāyo'.

Gaiccanena kvattho? Ghate ca.

What is the purpose of the designation 'ga'? In 'ghate ca'.

58, 29. Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā.

58, 29. The vowels 'i' and 'u' are designated 'jha'.

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇāiccete jhalasaññā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

These, the vowels 'i' and 'u', are designated 'jha' respectively.

Isino[M 0.0062], aggino, gahapatino, daṇḍino. Setuno, ketuno, bhikkhuno. Sayambhuno, abhibhuno.

For example: 'isino', 'aggino', 'gahapatino', 'daṇḍino'; 'setuno', 'ketuno', 'bhikkhuno'; 'sayambhuno', 'abhibhuno'.

Jhalaiccanena kvattho? Jhalato sassa no vā.

What is the purpose of the designation 'jha'? In the rule 'jhalato sassa no vā'.

59, 182. Te itthikhyā po.

59, 182. Those (vowels 'i' and 'u'), when denoting the feminine, are designated 'pa'.

Te ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā yadā itthikhyā, tadā pasaññā honti.

Those vowels 'i' and 'u', when they denote the feminine, are designated 'pa'.

Rattiyā, itthiyā, dhenuyā, vadhuyā.

For example: 'rattiyā', 'itthiyā', 'dhenuyā', 'vadhuyā'.

Itthikhyāti kimatthaṃ? Isinā, bhikkhunā.

Why the specification 'denoting the feminine'? For example: 'isinā', 'bhikkhunā'.

Saiccanena [M 0.0063] kvattho? Pato yā.

What is the purpose of the designation 'pa'? In the rule 'pato yā'.

60, 177. Ā gho.

60, 177. The vowel 'ā' is designated 'gha'.

Ākāro yadā itthikhyo, tadā ghasañño hoti.

The vowel 'ā', when it denotes the feminine, is designated 'gha'.

Saddhāya, kaññāya, vīṇāya, gaṅgāya, disāya sālāya, mālāya, tulāya, dolāya, pabhāya, sobhāya, paññāya, karuṇāya nāvāya, kapālikāya.

For example: 'saddhāya', 'kaññāya', 'vīṇāya', 'gaṅgāya', 'disāya', 'sālāya', 'mālāya', 'tulāya', 'dolāya', 'pabhāya', 'sobhāya', 'paññāya', 'karuṇāya', 'nāvāya', 'kapālikāya'.

Āti kimatthaṃ? Rattiyā, itthiyā.

Why the specification 'ā'? For example: 'rattiyā', 'itthiyā'.

Itthikhyoti kimatthaṃ? Satthārā desito ayaṃ dhammo.

Why the specification 'denoting the feminine'? For example: 'satthārā desito ayaṃ dhammo'.

Ghaiccanena kvattho? Ghato nādīnaṃ.

What is the purpose of the designation 'gha'? In the rule 'ghato nādīnaṃ'.

61, 86. Sāgamo se.

61, 86. The augment 'sa' comes before 'se'.

Sakārāgamo hoti se vibhattimhi.

The augment 'sa' occurs before the case ending 'se'.

Purisassa, aggissa, isissa, daṇḍissa, bhikkhussa, sayambhussa, abhibhussa.

For example: 'purisassa', 'aggissa', 'isissa', 'daṇḍissa', 'bhikkhussa', 'sayambhussa', 'abhibhussa'.

Seti kimattaṃ? Purisasmiṃ.

Why the specification 'se'? For example: 'purisasmiṃ'.

62, 206. Saṃsāsvekavacanesu ca.

62, 206. And also before the singular case endings 'saṃ' and 'sā'.

Saṃsāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu sakārāgamo hoti.

Before the singular case ending substitutes 'saṃ' and 'sā', the augment 'sa' occurs.

Etissaṃ, etissā imissaṃ, imissā, tissaṃ, tissā,

For example: 'etissaṃ', 'etissā', 'imissaṃ', 'imissā', 'tissaṃ', 'tissā'.

Tassaṃ tassā, yassaṃ, yassā, amussaṃ, amussā.

For example: 'tassaṃ', 'tassā', 'yassaṃ', 'yassā', 'amussaṃ', 'amussā'.

Saṃsāsvīti kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā.

Why the specification 'before saṃ and sā'? For example: 'agginā', 'pāṇinā'.

Ekavacanesvīti kimatthaṃ? Tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

Why the specification 'in the singular'? For example: 'tāsaṃ', 'sabbāsaṃ'.

Vibhattādesesvīti kimatthaṃ? Manasā, vacasā, thāmasā.

Why the specification 'before case ending substitutes'? For example: 'manasā', 'vacasā', 'thāmasā'.

63, 217. Etimāsami.

63, 217. Of 'eta' and 'ima', the final vowel becomes 'i'.

Etāimāiccetesamanto saro ikāro hoti saṃsāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

Of these, 'eta' and 'ima', the final vowel becomes 'i' before the singular case ending substitutes 'saṃ' and 'sā'.

Etissaṃ, etissā, imissaṃ, imissā.

For example: 'etissaṃ', 'etissā', 'imissaṃ', 'imissā'.

Saṃsāsvīti [M 0.0064] kimatthaṃ? Etāya, imāya.

For what purpose is the specification 'in saṃ and sā'? For example: etāya, imāya.

Ekavacanesvīti kimatthaṃ? Etāsaṃ, imāsaṃ.

For what purpose is the specification 'in the singular'? For example: etāsaṃ, imāsaṃ.

64, 216. Tassā vā.

Of tā, optionally i.

Tassā itthiyaṃ vattamānassa antassa ākārassa ikāro hoti vā saṃsāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

Of the pronoun ta when it denotes the feminine, its final ā optionally becomes i before the singular case-ending substitutes saṃ and sā.

Tissaṃ, tissā, tassaṃ, tassā.

For example: tissaṃ, tissā, tassaṃ, tassā.

65, 215. Tato sassa ssāya.

After these, sa becomes ssāya.

Tato tā etā imāto sassa vibhattissa ssāyādeso hoti vā.

After these pronouns, tā, etā, and imā, the case ending sa is optionally substituted by ssāya.

Tissāya, etissāya, imissāya.

For example: tissāya, etissāya, imissāya.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Tissā, etissā, imissā.

For what purpose is the specification 'optionally'? For example: tissā, etissā, imissā.

66, 205. Gho rassaṃ.

The gha group is shortened.

Gho rassamāpajjate saṃsāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

The gha group becomes short before the singular case-ending substitutes saṃ and sā.

Tassaṃ, tassā, yassaṃ, yassā, sabbassaṃ, sabbassā.

For example: tassaṃ, tassā, yassaṃ, yassā, sabbassaṃ, sabbassā.

Saṃsāsvīti kimatthaṃ? Tāya, sabbāya.

For what purpose is the specification 'in saṃ and sā'? For example: tāya, sabbāya.

Ekavacanesvīti kimatthaṃ? Tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

For what purpose is the specification 'in the singular'? For example: tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

67, 229. No [M 0.0065] ca dvādito naṃmhi.

And the augment na occurs after numerals from dvi onwards, before naṃ.

Dviiccevamādito saṅkhyāto nakārāgamo hoti naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

After numerals beginning with dvi and so on, the augment na occurs before the case ending naṃ.

Dvinnaṃ, tinnaṃ, catunnaṃ, pañcannaṃ, channaṃ, sattannaṃ, aṭṭhannaṃ, navannaṃ, dasannaṃ.

For example: dvinnaṃ, tinnaṃ, catunnaṃ, pañcannaṃ, channaṃ, sattannaṃ, aṭṭhannaṃ, navannaṃ, dasannaṃ.

Dvāditoti kimatthaṃ? Sahassānaṃ.

For what purpose is the specification 'from dvi onwards'? For example: sahassānaṃ.

Naṃmhīti kimatthaṃ? Dvīsu, tīsu.

For what purpose is the specification 'before naṃ'? For example: dvīsu, tīsu.

Caggahaṇenassañcāgamo hoti. Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ.

By the inclusion of ca, the augment assañca also occurs. For example: catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ.

68, 184. Amā pato smiṃsmānaṃ vā.

After pa-group stems, smiṃ and smā optionally become aṃ and ā respectively.

Paiccetasmā smiṃsmāiccetesaṃ aṃāādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

After these pa-group stems, for smiṃ and smā, the substitutes aṃ and ā optionally occur, respectively.

Matyaṃ, matiyaṃ, matyā, matiyā, nikatyaṃ. Nikatiyaṃ, nikatyā, nikatiyā, vikatyaṃ, vikatiyaṃ, vikatyā, vikatiyā, viratyaṃ, viratiyaṃ, viratyā, viratiyā, ratyaṃ, ratiyaṃ, ratyā, ratiyā, puthabyaṃ, puthaviyaṃ, puthabyā, puthaviyā, pavatyaṃ, pavatyā, pavattiyaṃ, pavattiyā.

For example: matyaṃ, matiyaṃ, matyā, matiyā, nikatyaṃ, nikatiyaṃ, nikatyā, nikatiyā, vikatyaṃ, vikatiyaṃ, vikatyā, vikatiyā, viratyaṃ, viratiyaṃ, viratyā, viratiyā, ratyaṃ, ratiyaṃ, ratyā, ratiyā, puthabyaṃ, puthaviyaṃ, puthabyā, puthaviyā, pavatyaṃ, pavatyā, pavattiyaṃ, pavattiyā.

69, 186. Ādito o ca.

After ādi and so on, also o.

Ādiiccetasmā smiṃvacanassa aṃoādesā honti vā.

After ādi and so on, for the ending smiṃ, the substitutes aṃ and o optionally occur.

Ādīṃ[M 0.0066], ādo.

For example: ādīṃ, ādo.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Ādismiṃ, ādimhi nāthaṃ namassitvāna,

For what purpose is the specification 'optionally'? Ādismiṃ, ādimhi. Having paid homage to the Lord,

Caggahaṇena aññasmāpi smiṃ vacanassa ā o aṃādesā honti. Divā ca ratto ca haranti ye bali. Bārāṇasiṃ ahu rājā.

By the inclusion of ca, the substitutes ā, o, and aṃ also occur for the smiṃ ending after other stems. For example: Divā ca ratto ca haranti ye bali (By day and by night, those who bring tribute carry it). Bārāṇasiṃ ahu rājā (There was a king in Bārāṇasī).

70, 30. Jhalānamiyuvā sare vā.

Of jhala-group vowels, iya and uva are the optional substitutes when a vowel follows.

Jhalaiccetesaṃ iya uvaiccete ādesā honti vā sare pare yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

For these jhala-group vowels, iya and uva are the optional substitutes, respectively, when a vowel follows.

Tiyantaṃ pacchiyāgāre, aggiyāgāre, bhikkhuvāsane nisīdati, vuthuvāsane nisīdati.

Tiyantaṃ, in the back room, in the fire-hut, he sits in the monk's dwelling, he sits in the dwelling of one who has resided.

Sareti kimatthaṃ? Timalaṃ, tiphalaṃ, ticatukkaṃ, tidaṇḍaṃ, tilokaṃ, tinayanaṃ, tipāsaṃ, tihaṃsaṃ, tibhavaṃ, tikhandhaṃ, tipiṭakaṃ, tivedanaṃ, catuddisaṃ, puthubhūtaṃ.

For what purpose is 'sare' (when a vowel follows)? [As counter-examples:] Timalaṃ, tiphalaṃ, ticatukkaṃ, tidaṇḍaṃ, tilokaṃ, tinayanaṃ, tipāsaṃ, tihaṃsaṃ, tibhavaṃ, tikhandhaṃ, tipiṭakaṃ, tivedanaṃ, catuddisaṃ, puthubhūtaṃ.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Pañcahaṅgehi tīhākārehi. Cakkhāyatanaṃ.

For what purpose is 'vā' (optionally)? [As examples where the option is not taken:] With five factors, in three aspects. The eye-base.

Vāti vikappanatthaṃ, ikārassa ayādeso hoti, vatthuttayaṃ.

The word 'vā' is for the purpose of option; for the letter 'i', the substitution 'aya' occurs. Vatthuttayaṃ (the threefold object).

71, 505. Yavakārā ca.

And the letters 'ya' and 'va'.

Jhalānaṃ yakāra vakārādesā honti sare pare yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

For 'jhala' vowels, the substitutions 'ya' and 'va' occur respectively when a vowel follows.

Agyāgāraṃ[M 0.0067], pakkhāyatanaṃ, svāgataṃ, te mahāvīra.

Agyāgāraṃ (fire-hut), pakkhāyatanaṃ, svāgataṃ (welcome), te mahāvīra (O great hero).

Caggahaṇaṃ sampiṇḍanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of combination.

72, 185. Pasaññassa ca.

And for a 'pasañña' stem.

Pasaññassa ca ivaṇṇassa vibhattādese sare pare yakārādeso hoti.

For the 'i'-vowel of a 'pasañña' stem, the substitution 'ya' also occurs when a vowel that is a substitute for a case-ending follows.

Puthabyā, ratyā, matyā.

Puthabyā, ratyā, matyā.

Sareti kimatthaṃ? Puthaviyaṃ.

For what purpose is 'sare' (when a vowel follows)? [As a counter-example:] Puthaviyaṃ.

73, 174. Gāva se.

Gāva before se.

Goiccetassa okārassa āvādeso hoti se vibhattimhi.

For the letter 'o' of the stem 'go', the substitution 'āva' occurs when the 'se' case-ending is present.

Gāvassa.

Gāvassa.

74, 169. Yosu ca.

And before the 'yo' endings.

Goiccetassa okārassa āvādeso hoti yoiccetesu paresu.

For the letter 'o' of the stem 'go', the substitution 'āva' occurs when the 'yo' endings follow.

Gāvo gacchanti, gāvo passanti, gāvī gacchanti, gāvī passanti.

Gāvo gacchanti (the kine go), gāvo passanti (the kine see), gāvī gacchanti (the kine go), gāvī passanti (the kine see).

Caggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Nāsmāsmiṃsu vacanesu āvā deso hoti.

For what purpose is the inclusion of 'ca'? The substitution 'āva' occurs with the case endings nā, smā, smiṃ, and su.

Gāvena, gāvā, gāve, gāvesu.

Gāvena, gāvā, gāve, gāvesu.

75, 170. Avamhi [M 0.0068] ca.

And 'ava' before the 'aṃ' ending.

Goiccetassa okārassa āvaavaiccete ādesā honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the letter 'o' of the stem 'go', the substitutions 'āva' and 'ava' occur when the 'aṃ' case-ending is present.

Gāvaṃ, gavaṃ.

Gāvaṃ, gavaṃ.

Caggahaṇena sādisesesu pubbuttavacanesu goiccetassa okārassa avādeso hoti.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the substitution 'ava' also occurs for the letter 'o' of the stem 'go' in the remaining similar cases mentioned before.

Gavassa, gavo, gavena, gavā, gave, gavesu.

Gavassa, gavo, gavena, gavā, gave, gavesu.

76, 171. Āvassu vā.

For 'āva', 'u' [is substituted for the final vowel], optionally.

Āvaiccetassa gāvādesassa anta sarassa ukārādeso hoti vā aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the final vowel of the substitute 'gāva', the letter 'u' is optionally substituted when the 'aṃ' case-ending is present.

Gāvuṃ, gāvaṃ.

Gāvuṃ, gāvaṃ.

Āvasseti kimatthaṃ? Gāvo tiṭṭhanti.

For what purpose is 'āvassa' specified? [As a counter-example:] Gāvo tiṭṭhanti (The kine are standing).

77, 175. Tato namaṃ patimhā lutte ca samāse.

After 'pati', 'naṃ' [is substituted for 'aṃ']; and in a compound where elision has occurred.

Tato gosaddato naṃvacanassa aṃādeso hoti, goiccetassa okārassa avādeso hoti patimhi pare alutte ca samāse.

From that word 'go', the substitution 'aṃ' occurs for the 'naṃ' case ending; and for the 'o' of 'go', the substitution 'ava' occurs when 'pati' follows, and in a non-elided compound.

Gavapati.

Gavapati.

Alutteti [M 0.0069] kimatthaṃ? Gopati.

For what purpose is 'alutte' (in a non-elided compound) stated? Gopati.

Caggahaṇena asamāsepi naṃvacanassa aṃādeso hoti, goiccetassa okārassa avādeso hoti.

By the inclusion of 'ca', even in a non-compound, the substitution 'aṃ' occurs for the 'naṃ' case ending, and for the 'o' of 'go', the substitution 'ava' occurs.

Gavaṃ.

Gavaṃ.

78, 3. Osare ca.

78, 3. And when a vowel follows.

Goiccetassa okārassa avādeso hoti samāse ca sare pare.

For the 'o' of 'go', the substitution 'ava' occurs in a compound and when a vowel follows.

Gavassakaṃ, gaveḷakaṃ, gavājinaṃ.

Gavassakaṃ, gaveḷakaṃ, gavājinaṃ.

Caggahaṇena uvaṇṇaiccevamantānaṃ liṅgānaṃ uvaavaurādesā honti smiṃyoiccetesu kvaci.

By the inclusion of 'ca', for stems ending in the vowel 'u' and so forth, the substitutions 'uva', 'ava', and 'ura' sometimes occur for the case endings 'smiṃ', 'yo', and so forth.

Bhuvi, pasavo, guravo, caturo.

Bhuvi, pasavo, guravo, caturo.

Sareti kimatthaṃ? Godhano, govindo.

For what purpose is 'sare' (when a vowel follows) stated? Godhano, govindo.

79, 46. Tabbiparītūpapade byañjane ca.

79, 46. And when that which is its opposite is a prefix, and when a consonant follows.

Tassa avasaddassa yadā upapade tiṭṭhamānassa tassa okārassa viparīto hoti byañjane pare.

For that word 'ava', when it stands as a prefix, its reverse occurs when a consonant follows.

Uggate sūriye, uggacchati, uggahetvā.

Uggate sūriye, uggacchati, uggahetvā.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ. Avasāne, avakiraṇe, avakirati.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of restriction. Avasāne, avakiraṇe, avakirati.

80, 173. Goṇa [M 0.0070] naṃmhi vā.

80, 173. 'Goṇa' optionally, when 'naṃ' follows.

Sabbasseva gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

The substitution 'goṇa' optionally occurs for the entire word 'go' when the case ending 'naṃ' follows.

Goṇānaṃ sattannaṃ.

Goṇānaṃ sattannaṃ.

Vāti kimatthaṃ?

For what purpose is 'vā' (optionally) stated?

Gonañce taramānānaṃ, ujuṃ gacchati puṅgavo.

Gonañce taramānānaṃ, ujuṃ gacchati puṅgavo.

Sabbā gāvī ujuṃ yanti, nette ujuṃ gate sati.

Sabbā gāvī ujuṃ yanti, nette ujuṃ gate sati.

Yogavibhāgena aññatrāpi goṇādeso hoti. Goṇabhūtānaṃ.

By splitting the rule, the substitution 'goṇa' occurs even elsewhere. Goṇabhūtānaṃ.

81, 172. Suhināsu ca.

81, 172. And when 'su', 'hi', and 'nā' follow.

Suhināiccetesu sabbassa gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā.

When 'su', 'hi', 'nā', and so forth follow, the substitution 'goṇa' optionally occurs for the entire word 'go'.

Goṇesu, goṇehi, goṇebhi, goṇena.

Goṇesu, goṇehi, goṇebhi, goṇena.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Gosu, gohi, gobhi, gavena.

For what purpose is 'vā' (optionally) stated? Gosu, gohi, gobhi, gavena.

Caggahaṇena syādisesesu pubbuttaravacanesupi goṇa gu gavayādesā honti. Goṇo, goṇā, goṇaṃ, goṇe, goṇassa, goṇamhā. Goṇamhi, gunnaṃ, gavayehi, gavayebhi.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the substitutions 'goṇa', 'gu', and 'gavaya' occur in the remaining 'syādi' case endings and also in preceding and subsequent words. Goṇo, goṇā, goṇaṃ, goṇe, goṇassa, goṇamhā, goṇamhi, gunnaṃ, gavayehi, gavayebhi.

82, 149. Aṃmo [M 0.0071] niggahitaṃ jhalapehi.

82, 149. 'Aṃ' and 'ma' become niggahita before 'jha', 'la', and 'pa'.

Aṃvacanassa makārassa ca jhalapaiccetehi niggahitaṃ hoti

The ending 'aṃ' and the letter 'ma' become a niggahita when followed by 'jha', 'la', 'pa', and so forth.

Aggiṃ, isiṃ, gahapatiṃ, daṇḍiṃ, mahesiṃ, bhikkhuṃ, paṭuṃ, sayambhuṃ, abhibhuṃ, rattiṃ, itthiṃ, vadhuṃ, pulliṅgaṃ, pumbhāvo, puṅkokilo.

Aggiṃ, isiṃ, gahapatiṃ, daṇḍiṃ, mahesiṃ, bhikkhuṃ, paṭuṃ, sayambhuṃ, abhibhuṃ, rattiṃ, itthiṃ, vadhuṃ, pulliṅgaṃ, pumbhāvo, puṅkokilo.

Aṃmoti kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā, bhikkhunā, rattiyā, itthiyā, vadhuyā.

What is the purpose of 'aṃ'? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Agginā, pāṇinā, bhikkhunā, rattiyā, itthiyā, vadhuyā.

Jhalapehīti kimatthaṃ? Sukhaṃ, dukkhaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'jhalapehi'? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Sukhaṃ, dukkhaṃ.

Punārambha haṇaṃ vibhāsānivattanatthaṃ. Aggiṃ, paṭuṃ, buddhiṃ, vadhuṃ.

The re-statement is for the purpose of preventing optionality. (Examples:) Aggiṃ, paṭuṃ, buddhiṃ, vadhuṃ.

83, 67. Saralopo’ mādesa paccayādimhi saralope tu pakati.

83, 67. Elision of a vowel occurs when `aṃ` as a substitute, a suffix, and so on follow; but when a vowel has been elided, the preceding form remains unchanged.

Saralopo hoti amādesapaccayādimhi sara lope tu pakati hoti.

Elision of a vowel occurs when `aṃ` as a substitute, a suffix, and so on follow; but when a vowel has been elided, the preceding form remains unchanged.

Purisaṃ, purise, pāpaṃ, pāpe, pāpiyo, pāpiṭṭho.

Purisaṃ, purise, pāpaṃ, pāpe, pāpiyo, pāpiṭṭho.

Amādesapaccayādimhīti ki tthaṃ? Appamādo amataṃ padaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'amādesapaccayādimhi'? (Example where the rule does not apply:) Appamādo amataṃ padaṃ.

Saralopeti kimatthaṃ? Purisassa, daṇḍinaṃ.

For what purpose is the condition 'saralope' (when a vowel is elided)? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Purisassa, daṇḍinaṃ.

Tuggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ. Bhikkhunī, gahapatānī.

The inclusion of 'tu' is for the purpose of restriction. (Examples:) Bhikkhunī, gahapatānī.

Pakatiggahaṇasāmatthena [M 0.0072] puna sandhibhāvo ca hoti. Seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

By the force of including 'pakati' (original form), a sandhi operation also occurs again. (Examples:) Seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

84, 144. Aghorassamekavacanayosvapi ca.

84, 144. And also, a non-`gha` vowel becomes short before the singular and `yo` suffixes.

Agho saro rassamāpajjate ekavacanayoiccetesu.

A non-`gha` vowel becomes short in these cases: the singular and the `yo` suffix.

Itthiṃ, itthiyo, itthiyā. Vadhuṃ, vadhuyo, vadhuyā. Daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍino, daṇḍinā. Sayambhuṃ, sayambhuvo, sayambhunā.

Itthiṃ, itthiyo, itthiyā. Vadhuṃ, vadhuyo, vadhuyā. Daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍino, daṇḍinā. Sayambhuṃ, sayambhuvo, sayambhunā.

Aghoti kimatthaṃ? Kaññaṃ, kaññāyo, kaññāya.

What is the purpose of 'agho' (non-`gha`)? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Kaññaṃ, kaññāyo, kaññāya.

Ekavacanayosvīti kimatthaṃ? Itthīhi, sayambhūhi.

What is the purpose of 'ekavacanayosu' (in the singular and `yo` cases)? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Itthīhi, sayambhūhi.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ. Nadiṃ, nadiyo, nadiyā.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of restriction. (Examples:) Nadiṃ, nadiyo, nadiyā.

Apiggahaṇena na rassamāpajjate. Itthī, bhikkhunī.

By the inclusion of 'api', it does not become short. (Examples:) Itthī, bhikkhunī.

85, 150. Na sismimanapuṃsakāni.

85, 150. Not for non-neuter (stems) in the `si` and `smiṃ` cases.

Sismiṃ anapuṃsakāni liṅgāni na rassamāpajjante. Itthī, bhikkhunī, vadhū, daṇḍī, sayambhū.

In the `si` and `smiṃ` cases, non-neuter genders do not become short. (Examples:) Itthī, bhikkhunī, vadhū, daṇḍī, sayambhū.

Sismiṃnti kimatthaṃ? Bhoti itthi, bhoti vadhu, bho daṇḍi, bho sayambhu.

What is the purpose of 'sismiṃ'? (Examples where the rule does not apply:) Bhoti itthi, bhoti vadhu, bho daṇḍi, bho sayambhu.

Anapuṃsakānīti [M 0.0073] kimatthaṃ? Sukhakāri dānaṃ, sukhakāri sīlaṃ, sīghayāyi cittaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'anapuṃsakāni' (non-neuter)? Sukhakāri dānaṃ, sukhakāri sīlaṃ, sīghayāyi cittaṃ.

86, 227. Ubhādito naminnaṃ.

86, 227. After `ubha` and so on, `naṃ` becomes `innaṃ`.

Ubhaiccevamādito saṅkhyāto naṃvacanassa innaṃ hoti.

After the numeral `ubha` and so on, the suffix `naṃ` becomes `innaṃ`.

Ubhinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ.

Ubhinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ.

Ubhāditoti kimatthaṃ? Ubhayesaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'ubhādito'? Ubhayesaṃ.

87, 231. Iṇṇamiṇṇannaṃ tīhi saṅkhyāhi.

87, 231. After the numeral 'three', (`naṃ` becomes) `iṇṇaṃ` and `iṇṇannaṃ`.

Naṃvacanassa iṇṇaṃ iṇṇannaṃ iccete ādesā honti tīhi saṅkhyāhi.

For the suffix `naṃ`, the substitutions `iṇṇaṃ` and `iṇṇannaṃ` occur after the numeral 'three'.

Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ.

Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ.

Tīhīti kimatthaṃ? Dvinnaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'tīhi'? Dvinnaṃ.

88, 147. Yosu katanikāralopesu dīghaṃ.

88, 147. Before the `yo` suffixes, when the `in`-suffix has been elided, lengthening occurs.

Sabbe sarā yosu katanikāralopesu dīghamāpajjante.

All vowels are lengthened before the `yo` endings when the final vowel of the stem has been elided.

Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāgū, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni, āyū, āyūni, sabbāni, yāni, tāni, kāni, katamāni, etāni, apūni, imāni.

Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāgū, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni, āyū, āyūni, sabbāni, yāni, tāni, kāni, katamāni, etāni, apūni, imāni.

Yosvīti [M 0.0074] kimatthaṃ? Aggi, bhikkhu, ratti, yāgu, sabbo, yo, so, ko, amuko.

For what purpose is 'yosu' [stated]? Aggi, bhikkhu, ratti, yāgu, sabbo, yo, so, ko, amuko.

Katanikāralopesvīti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyo, vadhuyo, sayambhuvo.

For what purpose is 'katanikāralopesu' [stated]? Itthiyo, vadhuyo, sayambhuvo.

Punārambhaggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Niccadīpanatthaṃ. Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāni, tāni, katamāni.

For what purpose is the re-statement? To indicate invariability. Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāni, tāni, katamāni.

89, 87. Sunaṃhisu ca.

89, 87. And before `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi`.

Sunaṃhiiccetesu sabbe sarā dīghamāpajjante.

Before these, namely `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi`, all vowels are lengthened.

Aggīsu, aggīnaṃ, aggīhi, rattīsu, rattīnaṃ, rattīhi. Bhikkhūsu, bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhūhi. Purisānaṃ.

Aggīsu, aggīnaṃ, aggīhi, rattīsu, rattīnaṃ, rattīhi. Bhikkhūsu, bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhūhi. Purisānaṃ.

Etesvītī kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā, daṇḍinā.

For what purpose is 'etesu' [stated]? Agginā, pāṇinā, daṇḍinā.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ. Sukhettesu brahmacārisu, dhammamakkhāsi bhagavā bhikkhunaṃ datvā sakehi pāṇibhi.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of restriction. In good fields, among spiritual practitioners; the Blessed One declared the Dhamma to the monks; having given with his own hands.

90, 252. Pañcādīnamattaṃ.

90, 252. The final vowel `a` for `pañca` and so on.

Pañcādīnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ anto attamāpajjate sunaṃhiiccetesu.

For the numerals `pañca` and so on, the final vowel becomes `a` before these endings: `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi`.

Pañcasu, pañcannaṃ, pañcahi, chasu, channaṃ, chahi, sattasu, sattannaṃ, sattahi, aṭṭhasu, aṭṭhannaṃ, aṭṭhahi, navasu, navannaṃ, navahi, dasasu, dasannaṃ, dasahi.

In five, of five, by five; in six, of six, by six; in seven, of seven, by seven; in eight, of eight, by eight; in nine, of nine, by nine; in ten, of ten, by ten.

Pañcādīnamīti kimatthaṃ? Dvīsu, dvinnaṃ, dvīhi.

For what purpose is 'pañcādīnaṃ' [stated]? Dvīsu, dvinnaṃ, dvīhi.

Attamitibhāvaniddeso [M 0.0075] ubhayassāgamanatthaṃ, anto ukāro attamāpajjate. Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ. Tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ.

The specification of `atta` as a state is for the purpose of its application to both [genders]; the final `u` also becomes `a`. `Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ`. `Tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ`.

91, 194. Patissinīmhi.

91, 194. For `pati`, before `inī`.

Patissanto attamāpajjate inīmhi paccaye pare.

The final vowel of `pati` becomes `ā` when the suffix `inī` follows.

Gahapatānī.

The householder's wife.

Inīmhīti kimatthaṃ? Gahapati.

For what purpose is 'inīmhi' [stated]? Gahapati.

92, 100. Ntussanto yosuca.

92, 100. For the final vowel of `ntu`, before `yo` and `su`.

Ntupaccayassa anto attamāpajjate sunaṃhiyoiccetesu paresu.

The final vowel of the `ntu` suffix becomes `a` when these endings follow: `su`, `naṃ`, `hi`, and `yo`.

Guṇavantesu, guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavantehi, guṇavantā, guṇavante.

In the virtuous, of the virtuous, by the virtuous; the virtuous (nominative plural), the virtuous (accusative plural).

Ntusseti kimatthaṃ? Isīnaṃ.

For what purpose is 'ntu' [stated]? Isīnaṃ.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Guṇavā.

For what purpose is 'etesu' [stated]? Guṇavā.

Caggahaṇena aññesu vacanesu attañca hoti. Guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantena.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the change to `a` also occurs in other cases. Guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantena.

Antaggahaṇena ntupaccayassa anto attamāpajjate, yonañca ikāro hoti. Guṇavanti.

By the inclusion of 'anta' (end), the final vowel of the `ntu` suffix becomes `a`, and for the `yo` ending, `i` occurs. Guṇavantī.

93, 106. Sabbassa [M 0.0076] vā aṃsesu.

93, 106. Of the whole [suffix], optionally before `aṃ` and `sa`.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa attaṃ hoti vā aṃsaiccetesu.

The entire `ntu` suffix is optionally replaced by `a` before these endings: `aṃ` and `sa`.

Satimaṃ bhikkhu, satimantaṃ bhikkhuṃ vā, bandhumaṃ rājānaṃ, bandhumantaṃ rājānaṃ vā, satimassa bhikkhuno, satimato bhikkhuno vā, bandhumassa rañño suṅkaṃ, bandhumato rañño vā suṅkaṃ deti.

A mindful monk, or a mindful monk; a king with relatives, or a king with relatives; of a mindful monk, or of a mindful monk; one gives the toll of a king with relatives, or of a king with relatives.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Satimā bhikkhu, bandhumā rājā.

For what purpose is 'etesu' [stated]? Satimā bhikkhu, bandhumā rājā.

94, 105. Simhi vā.

94, 105. Optionally, when si follows.

Ntupaccayassa antassa attaṃ hoti vā simhi vibhattimhi.

The final part of a stem formed with the suffix -ntu optionally becomes atta when the si inflection follows.

Himavanto pabbato.

The Himavanta mountain.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Himavā pabbato.

What is the purpose of vā? Himavā pabbato.

95, 145. Aggissini[M 0.0077].

95, 145. For aggi, ini.

Aggissantassa ini hoti vā simhi vibhattimhi.

For the stem aggi, the ending optionally becomes ini when the si inflection follows.

Purato aggini, pacchato aggini, dakkhiṇato aggini, vāmato aggini.

In front is fire, behind is fire, to the right is fire, to the left is fire.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Aggi.

What is the purpose of vā? Aggi.

96, 148. Yosvakatarasso jho.

96, 148. When the yo inflections follow, jho is substituted for a preceding long vowel.

Yosu akatarasso jho attamāpajjate.

When the yo inflections follow, a long vowel becomes jho.

Aggayo munayo, isayo, gahapatayo.

Fires, sages, seers, householders.

Yosvīti kimatthaṃ? Aggīsu.

What is the purpose of yosu? Aggīsu.

Akatarassoti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍino.

What is the purpose of akatarasso? Daṇḍino.

Jhoti kimatthaṃ? Rattiyo.

What is the purpose of jho? Rattiyo.

97, 156. Vevosu lo ca.

97, 156. And lo is substituted when ve or vo follows.

Vevoiccetesu akatarasso lo attamāpajjate.

When these, namely ve and vo, follow, a long vowel becomes lo.

Bhikkhave, bhikkhavo, hetave, hetavo.

O monks, O monks, O cause, O causes.

Akatarassoti kimatthaṃ? Sayambhuvo, vessabhuvo, parābhibhuvo.

What is the purpose of akatarasso? Sayambhuvo, vessabhuvo, parābhibhuvo.

Vevosvīti kimatthaṃ? Hetunā, ketunā, setunā.

What is the purpose of vevosu? Hetunā, ketunā, setunā.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of ca is for the purpose of carrying forward from the previous rule.

98, 186. Mātulādīnamānattamīkāre.

98, 186. For mātula and other such stems, ānatta is substituted when the suffix ī follows.

Mātulaiccevamādīnaṃ anto ānattamāpajjate īkāre paccaye pare.

The final part of mātula and other such stems becomes ānatta when the suffix ī follows.

Mātulānī[M 0.0078], ayyakānī, varuṇānī.

Maternal aunt, grandmother, Varuṇa's wife.

Īkāreti kimatthaṃ? Bhikkhunī, rājinī, jālinī, gahapatānī.

What is the purpose of īkāre? Bhikkhunī, rājinī, jālinī, gahapatānī.

Ānattaggahaṇena nadīiccetassa dīsaddassa jjojjā ādesā honti saha vibhattiyā yonāsaiccetesu. Najjo sandanti, najjā kataṃ taraṅgaṃ, najjā nerañjarāya tīre.

By the inclusion of ānatta, for the sound dī of the word nadī, the substitutions jjo and jjā occur, replacing the stem ending and the inflection, when yo, nā, sa, and other such inflections follow. For example: Najjo sandanti (The rivers flow), najjā kataṃ taraṅgaṃ (a wave made by the river), najjā nerañjarāya tīre (on the bank of the river Nerañjarā).

99, 81. Smāhismiṃnaṃmhābhimhivā.

99, 81. For smā, hi, and smiṃ, there are optionally mhā, bhi, and mhi.

Sabbato liṅgato smāhismiṃ iccetesaṃ mhābhimhiiccete ādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

In all genders, for the inflections smā, hi, and smiṃ, the substitutions mhā, bhi, and mhi optionally occur, respectively.

Purisamhā, purisasmā, purisebhi, purisehi, purisamhi, purisasmiṃ.

From the man, from the man; by the men, by the men; in the man, in the man.

Smāhismiṃnamiti kimatthaṃ? Vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ viruḷhapupphaṃ, mahantaṃ chattaṃ mahāchattaṃ, mahantaṃ dhajaṃ mahādhajaṃ.

What is the purpose of specifying smā, hi, smiṃ, naṃ? For example: Vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ viruḷhapupphaṃ (a colorful, scentless, full-blown flower); mahantaṃ chattaṃ mahāchattaṃ (a great umbrella becomes a great-umbrella); mahantaṃ dhajaṃ mahādhajaṃ (a great banner becomes a great-banner).

100, 214. Na timehi katākārehi.

100, 214. Not for the stems ta and ima when their final vowel has been made long (ā).

Ta imaiccetehi katākārehi smāsmiṃ naṃmhāmhiiccete ādesā neva honti.

For these stems, 'ta', 'ima', and so forth, which have been formed with a final 'ā', these substitutions—'smā', 'smiṃ', 'naṃ', 'mhā', and 'mhi'—do not occur.

Asmā ṭhānā bhayaṃ uppajjati, asmiṃ ṭhāne bhayaṃ tiṭṭhati, asmā, asmiṃ.

From this source fear arises, in this source fear persists; from this, in this.

Katākārehīti [M 0.0079] kimatthaṃ? Tamhā, tamhi, imamhā, imamhi.

Why is 'katākārehi' stated? Tamhā, tamhi, imamhā, imamhi.

101, 80. Suhisvakāro e.

101, 80. Before 'su' and 'hi', the vowel 'a' becomes 'e'.

Suhiiccetesu akāro ettamāpajjate.

Before these suffixes, namely 'su' and 'hi', the vowel 'a' becomes 'e'.

Sabbesu, yesu, tesu, kesu, purisesu, imesu, kusalesu, tumhesu, amhesu, sabbehi, yehi, tehi, kehi, purisehi, imehi, kusalehi, tumhehi, amhehi.

In all, in which, in those, in whom, in men, in these, in the skillful, in you, in us; with all, with which, with those, with whom, with men, with these, with the skillful, with you, with us.

102, 202. Sabbanāmānaṃ naṃmhi ca.

102, 202. And of pronouns, before 'naṃ'.

Sabbesaṃ sabbanāmānaṃ anto akāro ettamāpajjate naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

Of all pronouns, the final vowel 'a' becomes 'e' before the case ending 'naṃ'.

Sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, yesaṃ, yesānaṃ, tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, itaresaṃ, itaresānaṃ, katamesaṃ, katamesānaṃ. Sabbanāmānamiti kimatthaṃ? Buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āciṇṇasamāciṇṇo.

Of all, of all; of whom, of whom; of them, of them; of these, of these; of whom, of whom; of others, of others; of which, of which. Why is 'of pronouns' stated? Buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āciṇṇasamāciṇṇo.

Akāroti kimatthaṃ? Amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ.

Why is 'akāro' stated? Amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ.

Naṃmhīti kimatthaṃ? Sabbe, ime.

Why is 'naṃmhi' stated? Sabbe, ime.

Caggahaṇa manukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing forward.

103, 79. Ato [M 0.0080] nena.

103, 79. After 'a', 'ena' for 'nā'.

Tasmā akārato nāvacanassa enādeso hoti.

Therefore, after the vowel 'a', the substitution 'ena' occurs for the ending 'nā'.

Sabbena, yena, tena, kena, anena, purisena, rūpena.

By all, by which, by that, by whom, by this, by a man, by form.

Atoti kimatthaṃ? Muninā, amunā, bhikkhunā.

Why is 'ato' stated? Muninā, amunā, bhikkhunā.

Nāti kimatthaṃ? Tasmā.

Why is 'nā' stated? Tasmā.

104, 66. So.

104, 66. 'si' becomes 'o'.

Tasmā akārato sivacanassa okārādeso hoti.

Therefore, after the vowel 'a', the substitution 'o' occurs for the ending 'si'.

Sabbo, yo, so, ko, amuko, puriso.

All, who, that one, who, such-and-such, a man.

Sīti kimatthaṃ? Purisānaṃ.

Why is 'si' stated? Purisānaṃ.

Atoti kimatthaṃ? Sayambhū.

Why is 'ato' stated? Sayambhū.

105, 0. So vā.

105, 0. 'so' optionally.

Tasmā akārato nāvacanassa soādeso hoti vā.

Therefore, after the vowel 'a', the substitution 'so' optionally occurs for the ending 'nā'.

Atthaso dhammaṃ jānāti, byañjanaso atthaṃ jānāti, akkharaso, suttaso, padaso, yasaso. Upāyaso, sabbaso, thāmaso, ṭhānaso.

One knows the Dhamma according to the meaning; one knows the meaning according to the phrasing; according to the letters, according to the suttas, according to the words, according to glory. According to method, in all ways, with force, according to the grounds.

Vāti [M 0.0081] kimatthaṃ? Pādena vā pādārahena vā atirekapādena vā yo bhikkhu theyyacittena parassa bhaṇḍaṃ gaṇhāti, so bhikkhu pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso.

Why is 'vā' stated? Pādena vā pādārahena vā atirekapādena vā yo bhikkhu theyyacittena parassa bhaṇḍaṃ gaṇhāti, so bhikkhu pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso.

106, 313. Dīghorehi.

106, 313. After 'dīgha', 'ora', and so forth.

Dīghaoraiccetehi smāvacanassa soādeso hoti vā.

After these words, 'dīgha', 'ora', and so forth, the substitution 'so' optionally occurs for the ending 'smā'.

Dīghaso, oraso, dīghamhā, oramhā.

From afar, from this side; from afar, from this side.

Dīghorehiti kimatthaṃ? Saramhā, vacanamhā.

Why is 'dīghorehi' stated? Saramhā, vacanamhā.

107, 69. Sabbayonīnamāe.

107, 69. Of all origins, ā and e.

Tasmā akārato sabbesaṃ yonīnaṃāe ādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Therefore, from the 'a' vowel, the substitutions 'ā' and 'e' optionally occur for all origins/classes, respectively.

Purisā, purise, rūpā, rūpe.

Men, O men; forms, O forms.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Aggayo, munayo, isayo.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? Aggayo, munayo, isayo.

Yonīnanti kimatthaṃ? Purisassa, rūpassa.

What is the purpose of 'yonīnaṃ'? Purisassa, rūpassa.

Akāratoti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍino, aṭṭhīni, aggī pajjalanti, munī caranti.

What is the purpose of 'akārato'? Daṇḍino, aṭṭhīni, aggī pajjalanti, munī caranti.

108, 90. Smāsmiṃnaṃvā.

108, 90. Optionally for smā, smiṃ, and naṃ.

Tasmā akārato sabbesaṃ smāsmiṃiccetesaṃ ā e ādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Therefore, from a-stems, for all of these suffixes, namely `smā` and `smiṃ`, the substitutions `ā` and `e` optionally occur, respectively.

Purisā[M 0.0082], purisasmā, purise, purisasmiṃ.

From a man, from a man; in a man, in a man.

Akāratoti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍinā, daṇḍismiṃ, bhikkhunā, bhikkhusmiṃ.

What is the purpose of 'akārato'? By a staff-bearer, in a staff-bearer; by a monk, in a monk.

109, 304. Āya catutthekavacanassatu.

109, 304. For the fourth singular case, however, āya.

Tasmā akārato catutthekavacanassa āyādeso hoti vā.

Therefore, from a-stems, the substitution āya optionally occurs for the fourth singular case ending.

Atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ buddho loke uppajjati.

For the benefit, for the welfare, for the happiness of gods and humans, the Buddha arises in the world.

Atoti kimatthaṃ? Isissa.

What is the purpose of 'ato'? (As in) isissa.

Catutthīti kimatthaṃ? Purisassa mukhaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'catutthī' (fourth case)? (As in) purisassa mukhaṃ (a man's face).

Ekavacanasseti kimatthaṃ? Purisānaṃ dadāti.

What is the purpose of 'ekavacanassa' (singular)? (As in) purisānaṃ dadāti (he gives to men).

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? He is a giver to a recluse or a brahmin.

Tuggahaṇenatthañca hoti. Atthatthaṃ, hitatthaṃ, sukhatthaṃ.

And by the inclusion of 'tu', the suffix -tthaṃ is also indicated. Atthatthaṃ, hitatthaṃ, sukhatthaṃ.

110, 201. Tayo neva ca sabbanāmehi.

110, 201. And the three do not apply to pronouns.

Tehi sabbanāmehi akārantehi smāsmiṃ saiccetesaṃ tayo ā e āyādesā neva honti.

From those pronouns ending in 'a', the three substitutions ā, e, and āya do not occur for the case endings smā, smiṃ, and sa.

Sabbasmā[M 0.0083], sabbasmiṃ, sabbassa. Yasmā, yasmiṃ, yassa. Tasmā, tasmiṃ, tassa. Kasmā, kasmiṃ, kassa. Imasmā, imasmiṃ, imassa.

From all, in all, of all. From which, in which, of which. From that, in that, of that. From what, in what, of what. From this, in this, of this.

Sabbanāmehīti kimatthaṃ? Pāpā, pāpe, pāpāya.

What is the purpose of 'sabbanāmehi'? From evil, in evil, for evil.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in (other elements).

111, 179. Ghato nādīnaṃ.

111, 179. From `gha`, for the `nadī` class.

Tasmā ghato nādīnamekavacanānaṃ vibhattigaṇānaṃ āyādeso hoti.

Therefore, from `gha`, for the group of singular case endings of the `nadī` class, the substitution `āya` occurs.

Kaññāya kataṃ kammaṃ, kaññāya dīyate, kaññāya nissaṭaṃ vatthaṃ. Kaññāya pariggaho, kaññāya patiṭṭhitaṃ sīlaṃ.

An act done by a maiden; something given to a maiden; cloth released from a maiden; a maiden's possession; virtue established in a maiden.

Ghatoti kimatthaṃ? Rattiyā, itthiyā, dhenuyā, vadhuyā.

What is the purpose of 'ghato'? Rattiyā, itthiyā, dhenuyā, vadhuyā.

Nādīnamiti kimatthaṃ? Kaññaṃ passati, vijjaṃ, vīṇaṃ, gaṅgaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'nādīnaṃ'? He sees a maiden, knowledge, a lute, the Ganges.

Ekavacanānamiti kimatthaṃ? Sabbāsu, yāsu, tāsu, kāsu, imāsu, pabhāsu.

What is the purpose of 'ekavacanānaṃ'? In all, in which, in those, in what, in these, in radiances.

112, 183. Pato yā.

112, 183. From `pa`, yā.

Tasmā pato nādīnamekavacanānaṃ vibhattigaṇānaṃ yāādeso hoti.

Therefore, for the singular case endings of nouns in the `nadī` group, which are from the `pa` group, the substitution `yā` occurs.

Rattiyā[M 0.0084], itthiyā, deviyā, dhenuyā, yāguyā, vadhuyā.

Of the night, of the woman, of the goddess, of the cow, of the gruel, of the bride.

Nādīnamiti kimatthaṃ? Rattī, rattiṃ, itthī, itthiṃ.

What is the purpose of stating `nādīnam`? [As in:] `Rattī`, `rattiṃ`; `itthī`, `itthiṃ`.

Patoti kimatthaṃ? Kaññāya, vīṇāya, gaṅgāya, pabhāya, sobhāya.

What is the purpose of stating `pato`? For a maiden, for a lute, for the Ganges, for brightness, for splendor.

Ekavacanānamiti kimatthaṃ? Rattīnaṃ, itthīnaṃ.

What is the purpose of stating `ekavacanānaṃ`? Of nights, of women.

113, 132. Sakhato gasse vā.

113, 132. After `sakha`, for the vocative ending `ga`, optionally.

Tasmā sakhato gassa akāra ākāra ikāra īkāra ekārādesā honti vā.

Therefore, after `sakha`, for `ga`, the substitutions `a`, `ā`, `i`, `ī`, and `e` occur optionally.

Bho sakha, bho sakhā, bho sakhi, bho sakhī, bho sakhe.

O friend, O friend, O friend, O friend, O friend.

114, 178. Ghate ca.

114, 178. And for the `gha` group.

Tasmā ghato gassa ekārādeso hoti.

Therefore, after a noun of the `gha` group, the substitution `e` occurs for the vocative ending `ga`.

Bhoti ayye, bhoti kaññe, bhoti kharādiye.

O good noble lady; O good maiden; O good Kharādiyā.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ, sanniṭṭhānaṃ.

The inclusion of `ca` is for the purpose of restriction, a definitive conclusion.

115, 181. Na ammādito.

115, 181. Not after `ammā` and so on.

Tato ammādito gassa ekārattaṃ na hoti.

Therefore, after `ammā` and so on, the substitution of `e` for the vocative ending `ga` does not occur.

Bhoti [M 0.0085] ammā, bhoti annā, bhoti ambā, bhoti tātā.

O good mother, O good nurse, O good mother, O good father.

Ammāditoti kimatthaṃ? Bhoti kaññe.

What is the purpose of stating `ammādito`? [As in:] O good maiden.

116, 157. Akatarassā lato yvālapanassa vevo.

116, 157. After a stem ending in short `a` or `u`, for the vocative `yo`, the substitutions are `ve` and `vo`.

Tasmā akatarassā lato yvālapanassa vevoādesā honti.

Therefore, after a stem ending in short `a` or `u`, the substitutions `ve` and `vo` occur for the vocative `yo`.

Bhikkhave, bhikkhavo, hetave, hetavo.

O monks, O monks; O causes, O causes.

Akatarassāti kimatthaṃ? Sayambhuvo.

What is the purpose of stating `akārarassā` (ending in a short `a` or `u`)? [As in:] `Sayambhuvo`.

Latoti kimatthaṃ? Nāgiyo, dhenuyo, yāguyo.

What is the purpose of stating `lato`? [As in:] `Nāgiyo`, `dhenuyo`, `yāguyo`.

Ālapanasseti kimatthaṃ? Te hetavo, te bhikkhavo.

What is the purpose of stating `ālapanassa`? [As in:] Those causes, those monks.

117, 124. Jhalato sassano vā.

117, 124. After a `jhala` stem, `no` is optionally substituted for `sa`.

Tasmā jhalato sassa vibhattissa no ādeso hoti vā.

Therefore, after a `jhala` stem, the substitution `no` optionally occurs for the case ending `sa`.

Aggino, aggissa, sakhino, sakhissa, daṇḍino, daṇḍissa, bhikkhuno, bhikkhussa, sayambhuno, sayambhussa.

Aggino, aggissa; sakhino, sakhissa; daṇḍino, daṇḍissa; bhikkhuno, bhikkhussa; sayambhuno, sayambhussa.

Sasseti kimatthaṃ? Isinā, bhikkhunā.

What is the purpose of stating `sassa`? [As in:] By a seer, by a monk.

Jhalatoti kimatthaṃ? Purisassa.

What is the purpose of stating `jhalato`? [As in:] `Purisassa`.

118, 146. Ghapato [M 0.0086] ca yonaṃ lopo.

118, 146. And after `gha` and `pa` stems, elision of `yo`.

Tehi ghapajhalaiccetehi yonaṃ lopo hoti vā.

After those stems of the `gha`, `pa`, and `jhala` groups, elision of `yo` occurs optionally.

Kaññā, kaññāyo. Rattī, rattiyo, itthī, itthiyo, yāgū, yāguyo, vadhū, vadhuyo. Aggī, aggayo. Bhikkhū, bhikkhavo. Sayambhū, sayambhuvo. Aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni, āyū, āyūni.

Kaññā, kaññāyo; Rattī, rattiyo; itthī, itthiyo; yāgū, yāguyo; vadhū, vadhuyo; Aggī, aggayo; Bhikkhū, bhikkhavo; Sayambhū, sayambhuvo. Aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni; āyū, āyūni.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in.

119, 155. Lato vokāro ca.

119, 155. And after `la`, the substitution `vo`.

Tasmā lato yonaṃ vokāro hoti vā.

Therefore, after a stem of the `la` class, the substitution `vo` optionally occurs for the `yo` ending.

Bhikkhavo, bhikkhū, sayambhuvo, sayambhū.

Bhikkhus, bhikkhus; self-originated ones, self-originated ones.

Kāraggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Yonaṃ no ca hoti. Jantuno.

For what purpose is the inclusion of `-kāra`? Also, `no` is not substituted for `yo`. For example: `jantuno`.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ, amū purisā tiṭṭhanti, amū purise passatha.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of emphasis. Those men stand. See those men.

Iti nāmakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section in the Nāmakappa.

Dutiyakaṇḍa

The Second Section

120, 243. Amhassa mamaṃ sapibhattissa se.

120, 243. For `amha` together with its case ending, `mamaṃ` is substituted when the ending is `se`.

Sabbasseva amhasaddassa savibhattissa mamaṃ ādeso hoti se vibhattimhi.

For the entire word `amha` together with its case ending, the substitution `mamaṃ` occurs when the case ending is `se`.

Mamaṃ [M 0.0087] dīyate purisena, mamaṃ pariggaho.

It is given to me by a man; my possession.

121, 233. Mayaṃ yomhi paṭhame.

121, 233. `Mayaṃ` is substituted when the ending is `yo` in the first case.

Sabbasseva amhasaddassa savibhattissa mayaṃādeso hoti yomhi paṭhame.

For the entire word `amha` together with its case ending, the substitution `mayaṃ` occurs when the ending is `yo` in the first case.

Mayaṃ gacchāma, mayaṃ dema.

We go; we give.

Amhasseti kimatthaṃ? Purisā tiṭṭhanti.

For what purpose is `amhassa` stated? Men stand.

Yomhīti kimatthaṃ? Ahaṃ gacchāmi.

For what purpose is `yomhi` stated? I go.

Paṭhameti kimatthaṃ? Amhākaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

For what purpose is `paṭhame` stated? You see us.

122, 99. Ntussa nto.

122, 99. For `ntu`, `nto` is substituted.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa ntoādeso hoti yomhi paṭhame.

For the entire `ntu` suffix together with its case ending, the substitution `nto` occurs when the ending is `yo` in the first case.

Guṇavanto tiṭṭhanti.

The virtuous ones stand.

Ntusseti kimatthaṃ? Sabbe sattā gacchanti.

For what purpose is `ntussa` stated? All beings go.

Paṭhameti kimatthaṃ? Guṇavante passanti janā.

For what purpose is `paṭhame` stated? People see the virtuous ones.

123, 103. Ntassa se vā.

123, 103. For `ntu`, `ntassa` is substituted when the ending is `se`, optionally.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa ntassādeso hoti vā se vibhattimhi.

For the entire `ntu` suffix together with its case ending, the substitution `ntassa` optionally occurs when the case ending is `se`.

Sīlavantassa jhāyino, sīlavato jhāyino vā.

Of the virtuous meditator, or of the virtuous meditator.

Seti kimatthaṃ? Sīlavā tiṭṭhati.

For what purpose is `se` stated? The virtuous one stands.

124, 98. Ā [M 0.0088] simhi.

124, 98. For `ntu`, `ā` is substituted when the ending is `si`.

Sabbassevantupaccayassa savibhattissa āādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire `ntu` suffix together with its case ending, the substitution `ā` occurs when the case ending is `si`.

Guṇavā, paññavā, sīlavā, balavā, dhanavā, matimā, satimā, dhitimā.

The virtuous one, the wise one, the ethical one, the strong one, the wealthy one, the intelligent one, the mindful one, the resolute one.

Ntusseti kimatthaṃ? Puriso tiṭṭhati.

For what purpose is `ntussa` stated? A man stands.

Simhīti kimatthaṃ? Sīlavanto tiṭṭhanti.

What is the purpose of 'when it is si'? The virtuous ones stand.

125, 198. Aṃ napuṃsake.

In the neuter gender, aṃ [is substituted for the -ntu suffix].

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa aṃādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi napuṃsake vattamānassa.

For the entire inflected -ntu suffix, the substitution aṃ occurs when the si case ending is present and it is in the neuter gender.

Guṇavaṃ cittaṃ tiṭṭhati, rucimaṃ pupphaṃ virocati.

A virtuous mind stands; a beautiful flower shines.

Simhiti kimatthaṃ? Vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ virūḷhapupphaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'when it is si'? You see a colorful, scentless, fully-blossomed flower.

126, 101. Avaṇṇā ca ge.

In the vocative, the vowels a and ā are also [substituted for the -ntu suffix].

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa aṃ avaṇṇā ca honti ge pare.

For the entire inflected -ntu suffix, the substitutions aṃ and the vowels a and ā occur when the ge case ending follows.

Bho guṇavaṃ, bho guṇava, bho guṇavā.

O virtuous one, O virtuous one, O virtuous one.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of ca is for the purpose of drawing forward [from a previous rule].

127, 102. To [M 0.0089] ti tā sa smiṃ nāsu.

For the -ntu suffix, to, ti, and tā are substituted when the sa, smiṃ, and nā case endings follow, respectively.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa totitāādesā honti vā sasmiṃ nāiccetesu yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

For the entire inflected -ntu suffix, the substitutions to, ti, and tā optionally occur respectively when the sa, smiṃ, and nā case endings are present.

Guṇavato, guṇavantassa, guṇavati, guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavatā, guṇavantena, satimato, satimantassa, satimati, satimantasmiṃ, satimatā, satimantena.

Of the virtuous one, of the virtuous one; in the virtuous one, in the virtuous one; by the virtuous one, by the virtuous one. Of the mindful one, of the mindful one; in the mindful one, in the mindful one; by the mindful one, by the mindful one.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Guṇavā. Satimā.

What is the purpose of 'in these [cases]'? The virtuous one. The mindful one.

128, 104. Naṃmhi taṃ vā.

When the naṃ case ending follows, taṃ is optionally [substituted for the -ntu suffix].

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa taṃādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected -ntu suffix, the substitution taṃ optionally occurs when the naṃ case ending is present.

Guṇavataṃ, guṇavantānaṃ, satimataṃ, satimantānaṃ.

Of the virtuous ones, of the virtuous ones; of the mindful ones, of the mindful ones.

Naṃmhīti kimatthaṃ? Guṇavanto tiṭṭhanti, satimanto tiṭṭhanti.

What is the purpose of 'when it is naṃ'? The virtuous ones stand, the mindful ones stand.

129, 222. Imassidamaṃsisu napuṃsake.

For ima, idaṃ is substituted in the neuter gender when the aṃ or si case endings are present.

Sabbasseva imasaddassa savibhattissa idaṃādeso hoti vā aṃsisu napuṃsake vattamānassa.

For the entire inflected word ima, the substitution idaṃ optionally occurs when the aṃ or si case endings are present and it is in the neuter gender.

Idaṃ cittaṃ passasi, idaṃ cittaṃ tiṭṭhati, imaṃ cittaṃ passasi. Imaṃ cittaṃ tiṭṭhati.

You see this mind; this mind stands. You see this mind; this mind stands.

Nathuṃsaketi [M 0.0090] kimatthaṃ? Imaṃ purisaṃ passasi. Ayaṃ puriso tiṭṭhati.

What is the purpose of 'in the neuter gender'? You see this man. This man stands.

138, 225. Amussāduṃ.

For amu, aduṃ [is substituted].

Sabbasseva amusaddassa savibhattissa aduṃādeso hoti aṃsisu napuṃsake vattamānassa.

For the entire inflected word amu, the substitution aduṃ occurs when the aṃ or si case endings are present and it is in the neuter gender.

Aduṃ pupphaṃ passasi, aduṃ pupphaṃ virocati.

You see that flower; that flower shines.

Napuṃsaketi kimatthaṃ? Amuṃ rājānaṃ passasi, asu rājā tiṭṭhati.

What is the purpose of 'in the neuter gender'? You see that king; that king stands.

131, 0. Itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhyaṃ.

Feminine, Masculine, and Neuter Numerals.

“Itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhyaṃ” iccetaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

This, namely 'Feminine, Masculine, and Neuter Numerals,' should be understood as a governing heading.

132, 228. Yosu dvinnaṃ dve ca.

For dvi, dve is also substituted in the yo cases.

Dvinnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ dve hoti yoiccetesu.

For the number two, when occurring in feminine, masculine, or neuter genders with their inflections, dve occurs in the yo cases.

Dve itthiyo, dve dhammā. Dve rūpāni.

Two women, two principles, two forms.

Yosvīti kimatthaṃ? Dvīsu.

For what purpose is 'yosu'? In the case of 'dvi'.

Caggahaṇena duve dvaya ubha ubhaya duvi ca honti yonāanamiccetesu. Duve samaṇā. Duve brāhmaṇā[M 0.0091], duve janā, dvayena, dvayaṃ, ubhinnaṃ, ubhayesaṃ duvinnaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', 'duve', 'dvaya', 'ubha', 'ubhaya', and 'duvi' also occur in the case of the 'yo', 'nā', and 'aṃ' endings. Two ascetics. Two brahmins, two people, by two, a pair, of both, of both, of two.

133, 230. Ti catunnaṃ tisso catasso tayo cattāro tīṇi cattāri.

For 'ti' and 'catu', 'tisso', 'catasso', 'tayo', 'cattāro', 'tīṇi', and 'cattāri' are substituted.

Ticatunnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tisso catasso tayo cattāro tīṇi cattāriiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ yoiccetesu.

For the numbers 'ti' and 'catu', when occurring in the feminine, masculine, and neuter genders with their inflections, the substitutions 'tisso', 'catasso', 'tayo', 'cattāro', 'tīṇi', and 'cattāri' occur respectively, in the case of the 'yo' endings.

Tisso vedanā catasso disā, tayo janā, jane, cattāro purisā, purise, tīṇi āyatanāni, cattāri ariyasaccāni.

Three feelings, four directions, three people, three people, four men, four men, three sense bases, four noble truths.

Yosvīti kimatthaṃ? Tīsu, catūsu.

For what purpose is 'yosu'? In the case of 'tīsu' and 'catūsu'.

134, 251. Pañcādīnamakāro.

For 'pañca' and so forth, 'a' is substituted.

Pañcādīnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānānaṃ savibhattissa antassa sarassa akāro hoti yoiccetesu.

For the numbers 'pañca' and so forth, when occurring in the feminine, masculine, or neuter genders, for the final vowel of the inflected stem, 'a' is substituted in the case of the 'yo' endings.

Pañca, pañca, cha, cha, satta, satta, aṭṭha, aṭṭha, nava, nava, dasa, dasa.

Five, five; six, six; seven, seven; eight, eight; nine, nine; ten, ten.

Pañcādīnamiti kimatthaṃ? Dve, tayo.

For what purpose is 'pañcādīnaṃ'? Two, three.

135, 118. Rājassa [M 0.0092] rañño rājino se.

For 'rājassa', 'rañño' and 'rājino' are substituted in the case of 'se'.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa rañño rājinoiccete ādesā honti se vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected word 'rāja', the substitutions 'rañño' and 'rājino' occur when the 'se' inflection is present.

Rañño, rājino.

Rañño, rājino.

Seti kimatthaṃ? Raññā.

For what purpose is 'se'? By the king.

136, 119. Raññaṃ naṃmhi vā.

'Raññaṃ' is optionally substituted for 'rāja' when the 'naṃ' inflection is present.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññaṃādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected word 'rāja', the substitution 'raññaṃ' optionally occurs when the 'naṃ' inflection is present.

Raññaṃ, rājūnaṃ idaṃ raṭṭhaṃ.

This kingdom is of the kings (raññaṃ), of the kings (rājūnaṃ).

137, 116. Nāmhiraññā vā.

When 'nā' is the inflection, 'raññā' is optionally substituted for 'rāja'.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññāādeso hoti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected word 'rāja', the substitution 'raññā' optionally occurs when the 'nā' inflection is present.

Tena raññā kataṃ. Rājena vā kataṃ.

Done by that king (raññā). Or done by the king (rājena).

Nāmhīti kimatthaṃ? Rañño santakaṃ.

For what purpose is 'nāmhi'? Belonging to the king.

138, 121. Smiṃmhi raññe rājini.

When 'smiṃ' or 'mhi' are the inflections, 'raññe' and 'rājini' are substituted for 'rāja'.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññerājiniiccete ādesā honti smiṃmhivibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected word 'rāja', the substitutions 'raññe' and 'rājini' occur when the 'smiṃ' or 'mhi' inflection is present.

Raññe, rājini sīlaṃ tiṭṭhati.

Virtue abides in the king (raññe), in the king (rājini).

139, 245. Tumhākaṃ [M 0.0093] tayimayi.

For 'tumha' and 'amha', 'tayi' and 'mayi' are substituted.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amha saddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tayi mayiiccete ādeso honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ smiṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tayi' and 'mayi' occur respectively when the 'smiṃ' or 'mhi' inflection is present.

Tayi, mayi.

Tayi, mayi.

Smiṃmhīti kimatthaṃ? Tvaṃ bhavasi, ahaṃ bhavāmi.

For what purpose is 'smiṃmhi'? You are, I am.

140, 232. Tvamahaṃ simhi ca.

Also, 'tvaṃ' and 'ahaṃ' are substituted for 'tumha' and 'amha' when the 'si' inflection is present.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tvaṃ ahaṃiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ simhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tvaṃ' and 'ahaṃ' occur respectively when the 'si' inflection is present.

Tvaṃ, ahaṃ.

You, I.

Simhiti kimatthaṃ? Tayi, mayi.

What is the purpose of 'si'? In you, in me.

Caggahaṇena tuvaṃ ca hoti. Tuvaṃ satthā.

By the inclusion of 'ca', 'tuvaṃ' also occurs. You are the teacher.

141, 241. Tava mamase.

For 'tumha' and 'amha', 'tava' and 'mama' are substituted before the 'se' case ending.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tavamamaiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ se vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tava' and 'mama' occur respectively before the 'se' case ending.

Tava, mama.

Yours, mine.

Seti kimatthaṃ? Tayi, mayi.

What is the purpose of 'se'? In you, in me.

142, 242. Tuyhaṃ [M 0.0094] mayhañca.

And 'tuyhaṃ' and 'mayhaṃ'.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tuyhaṃ mayhaṃiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ se vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tuyhaṃ' and 'mayhaṃ' occur respectively before the 'se' case ending.

Tuyhaṃ, mayhaṃ dhanaṃ dīyate.

To you, to me, wealth is given.

Seti kimatthaṃ? Tayā, mayā.

What is the purpose of 'se'? By you, by me.

143, 235. Taṃ mamaṃmhi.

For 'tumha' and 'amha', 'taṃ' and 'maṃ' are substituted before the 'aṃ' case ending.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ taṃ maiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'taṃ' and 'maṃ' occur respectively before the 'aṃ' case ending.

Taṃ, maṃ.

You, me.

Aṃmhīti kimatthaṃ? Tayā mayā.

What is the purpose of 'aṃmhi'? By you, by me.

144, 234. Tavaṃ mamañca navā.

And 'tavaṃ' and 'mamaṃ', optionally.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tavaṃ mamaṃiccete ādesā honti navā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tavaṃ' and 'mamaṃ' optionally occur respectively before the 'aṃ' case ending.

Tavaṃ, mamaṃ passati.

He sees you, he sees me.

Navāti kimatthaṃ? Taṃ, maṃ passati.

What is the purpose of 'navā'? He sees you, he sees me.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing down.

145, 238. Nāmhī tayā mayā.

Before 'nā', 'tayā' and 'mayā' are substituted.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tayā mayāiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ nāmhi vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', the substitutions 'tayā' and 'mayā' occur respectively before the 'nā' case ending.

Tayā[M 0.0095], mayā kataṃ.

Done by you, done by me.

Nāmhiti kimatthaṃ? Tumhehi, amhehi.

What is the purpose of 'nāmhi'? By you, by us.

146, 236. Tumhassa tuvaṃ tvamaṃmhi.

For 'tumha', 'tuvaṃ' and 'tvaṃ' are substituted before 'aṃ'.

Sabbassa tumhasaddassa savibhattissa tuvaṃ tvaṃ iccete ādesā honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire inflected word 'tumha', 'tuvaṃ' and 'tvaṃ' are the substitutes before the 'aṃ' case ending.

Kaliṅgarassa tuvaṃ maññe, kaṭṭhassa tvaṃ maññe.

You, I think, are of the king of Kaliṅga; you, I think, are of wood.

147, 246. Padato dutiyā catutthī chaṭṭhīsu vono.

After a word, in the second, fourth, and sixth cases, 'vo' and 'no' are substituted.

Sabbesaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yadā padasmā paresaṃ vo noādesā honti navā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ dutiyā catutthīchaṭṭhīiccetesu bahuvacanesu.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha', when they follow a word, 'vo' and 'no' are optionally the substitutes respectively, in the plural of the second, fourth, and sixth cases.

Pahāya vo bhikkhave gamissāmi, mā no ajja vikantiṃsu, rañño sūdā mahānase, evaṃ dutiyatthe.

“Leaving you, O monks, I will go.” “Let them not cut us today.” “The king’s cooks are in the great kitchen.” Thus in the sense of the second case.

Dhammaṃ vo bhikkhave desessāmi, saṃvibhajetha no rajjena, evaṃ catutthyatthe.

“I will teach you the Dhamma, monks.” “Share the kingdom with us.” — Thus in the sense of the fourth case.

Tuṭṭhosmi vo bhikkhave pakatiyā, satthā no bhagavā anuppatto, evaṃ chaṭṭhyatthe.

“I am pleased with you, monks, by nature.” “Our Teacher, the Blessed One, has arrived.” — Thus in the sense of the sixth case.

Navāti [M 0.0096] kimatthaṃ? Eso amhākaṃ satthā.

Why is 'optionally' stated? He is our teacher.

Tumhamhākamiti kimatthaṃ? Ete isayo passasi.

Why are 'tumha' and 'amha' stated? You see these sages.

Padatoti kimatthaṃ? Tumhākaṃ satthā.

Why is 'padato' stated? Your teacher.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Gacchatha tumhe.

Why is 'in these' stated? You go.

148, 247. Temekavacanesu ca.

And 'te' and 'me' in the singular cases.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yadā padasmā paresaṃ te me ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ catutthīchaṭṭhīiccetesu ekavacanesu.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha,' when they follow a word, 'te' and 'me' are the substitutes respectively in the singular forms of the fourth and sixth cases.

Dadāmi te gāmavarāni pañca, dadāhi me gāmavaraṃ, idaṃ te raṭṭhaṃ, ayaṃ me putto.

“I give you five excellent villages.” “Give me an excellent village.” “This is your kingdom.” “This is my son.”

Padatoti kimatthaṃ? Tava ñāti, mama ñāti.

Why is 'padato' stated? Your relative, my relative.

149, 148. Na aṃmhi.

Not in the 'aṃ' case.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yadā padasmā paresaṃ te meādesā na honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha,' when they follow a word, 'te' and 'me' are not substitutes when the 'aṃ' case ending is present.

Passeyya taṃ vassasataṃ arogaṃ, so maṃ bravīti.

“May you be seen for a hundred years, free from illness.” “He tells me.”

150, 249. Vā [M 0.0097] tatiye ca.

And optionally in the third case.

Sabbesaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yadā padasmā paresaṃ temeādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ tatiyekavacane pare.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha,' when they follow a word, 'te' and 'me' are optionally the substitutes, respectively, when the third singular case is present.

Kataṃ te pāpaṃ, kataṃ me pāpaṃ, kataṃ tayā pāpaṃ, kataṃ mayā pāpaṃ.

“Evil was done by you.” “Evil was done by me.” “Evil was done by you.” “Evil was done by me.”

Padatoti kimatthaṃ? Tayā kataṃ, mayā kataṃ.

Why is 'padato' stated? Done by you, done by me.

151, 250. Bahuvacanesu vono.

In the plural cases, 'vo' and 'no'.

Sabbesaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yadā padasmā paresaṃ vonoādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ tatiyābahuvacanesu paresu.

For all inflected forms of the words 'tumha' and 'amha,' when they follow a word, 'vo' and 'no' are the substitutes respectively, when the third plural cases are present.

Kataṃ vo kammaṃ, kataṃ no kammaṃ.

“The deed was done by you.” “The deed was done by us.”

Padatoti kimatthaṃ? Tumhehi kataṃ, amhehi kataṃ.

Why is 'padato' stated? Done by you, done by us.

Bahuvacanaggahaṇena yomhi paṭhame vo noādesā honti. Gāmaṃ vo gaccheyyātha, gāmaṃ no gaccheyyāma.

By the mention of 'plural,' 'vo' and 'no' are also substitutes in the nominative plural ('yo'). “May you go to the village.” “May we go to the village.”

152, 236. Pumantassā simhi.

For a stem ending in 'puman,' 'ā' is the substitute when 'si' follows.

Pumaiccevamantassa savibhattissa āādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi.

For an inflected stem ending in 'puman,' the substitute 'ā' occurs when the 'si' case ending is present.

Pumā [M 0.0098] tiṭṭhati.

The man stands.

Simhīti kimatthaṃ? Pumāno tiṭṭhanti.

Why is 'simhi' stated? The men stand.

Antaggahaṇena maghava yuvaiccevamādīnamantassasavibhattissa āādeso hoti. Maghavā, yuvā.

By the mention of 'ending,' the substitute 'ā' occurs for inflected stems ending in 'maghavan,' 'yuvan,' and so forth. Examples: Maghavā, Yuvā.

153, 138. Amālapanekavacane.

'Aṃ' is the substitute in the vocative singular.

Pumaiccevamantassa savibhattissa aṃādeso hoti ālapanekavacane pare.

For an inflected stem ending in 'puman,' the substitute 'aṃ' occurs when the vocative singular is present.

He pumaṃ.

O man.

Ālapaneti kimatthaṃ? Pumā.

Why is 'vocative' stated? 'A man.'

Ekavacaneti kimatthaṃ? He pumāno.

Why is 'singular' stated? 'O men.'

154, 0. Samāse ca vibhāsā.

154. And optionally in a compound.

Pumaiccevamantassa samāse ca aṃādeso hoti vibhāsā samāse kate.

For a word ending thus 'puman', the substitute 'aṃ' occurs optionally when a compound is formed.

Itthī ca pumā ca napuṃsakaṃ ca itthipumanapuṃsakāni. Itthipumanapuṃsakānaṃ samūho itthipumanapuṃsakasamūho.

A woman, a man, and a neuter gender word are 'itthipumanapuṃsakāni'. A collection of 'itthipumanapuṃsakāni' is 'itthipumanapuṃsakasamūho'.

Vibhāsāti kimatthaṃ? Itthipumanapuṃsakāni.

Why is 'optionally' stated? 'Itthipumanapuṃsakāni.'

155, 137. Yosvāno[M 0.0099].

155. For the 'yo' case endings, 'āno' is the substitute.

Pumaiccevamantassa savibhattissa ānoādeso hoti yosu vibhattīsu.

For a word ending thus 'puman', together with its inflection, the substitute 'āno' occurs for the 'yo' case endings.

Pumāno, he pumāno.

Men; O men.

Yosvīti kimatthaṃ? Pumā.

Why is 'for the yo case endings' stated? 'A man.'

156, 142. Āne smiṃmhi vā.

156. 'Āne' is the substitute optionally for the 'smiṃ' or 'mhi' case endings.

Pumaiccevamantassa savibhattissa āne ādeso hoti vā smiṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For a word ending thus 'puman', together with its inflection, the substitute 'āne' occurs optionally for the 'smiṃ' or 'mhi' case ending.

Pumāne, pume vā.

Pumāne, or pume.

157, 140. Hivibhattimhi ca.

157. And for the 'hi' case ending.

Pumaiccevamantassa hivibhattimhi ca āneādeso hoti.

For a word ending thus 'puman', the substitute 'āne' also occurs for the 'hi' case ending.

Pumānehi, pumānebhi.

Pumānehi, pumānebhi.

Puna vibhattiggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Savibhattiggahaṇanivattanatthaṃ. Pumānehi.

Why is 'case ending' mentioned again? For the purpose of annulling the inclusion of 'together with its inflection'. For example: 'Pumānehi.'

Caggahaṇena maghava yuvaiccevamādīnamantassa ānaādeso hoti si yo aṃyo iccetesu vibhattīsu, pumakammathāmantassa cukāro hoti sasmā su vibhattīsu. Maghavāno, maghavānā. Maghavānaṃ, maghavāne[M 0.0100]. Yuvāno, yuvānā, yuvānaṃ, yuvāne, pumuno, pumunā. Kammuno, kammunā, thāmuno, thāmunā.

By the inclusion of 'ca', for words ending in 'maghavan', 'yuvan', and so forth, the substitute 'āna' occurs for the 'si', 'yo', 'aṃ', and 'yo' case endings; and for words ending in 'puman', 'kamman', and 'thāman', the letter 'u' occurs for the 'sa', 'smā', and 'su' case endings. Maghavāno, maghavānā; maghavānaṃ, maghavāne. Yuvāno, yuvānā; yuvānaṃ, yuvāne. Pumuno, pumunā. Kammuno, kammunā. Thāmuno, thāmunā.

158, 143. Susmimā vā.

158. For 'su' and 'smiṃ', 'ā' is the substitute optionally.

Pumaiccevamantassa suiccetasmiṃvibhattimhi āādeso hoti vā.

For a word ending thus 'puman', the substitute 'ā' occurs optionally for this 'su' case ending.

Pumāsu, pumesu vā.

Pumāsu, or pumesu.

156, 139. Unāmhi ca.

159. And 'u' and 'ā' for the 'nā' case ending.
