Pumaiccevamantassa āuādesā honti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi.

For a word ending thus 'puman', the substitutes 'ā' and 'u' occur optionally for the 'nā' case ending.

Pumānā, pumunā, pumena vā.

Pumānā, pumunā, or pumena.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in other rules.

160, 167. A kammantassa ca.

160. And 'a' for a word ending in 'kamman'.

Kammaiccevamantassa ca ua ādesā honti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi.

And for a word ending thus 'kamman', the substitutes 'u' and 'a' occur optionally for the 'nā' case ending.

Kammunā, kammanā, kammena vā.

Kammunā, kammanā, or kammena.

Caggahaṇena maghavayuvaiccevamantassa āāde so hoti kvaci nāsuiccetesu vibhattīsu. Maghavānā, maghavāsu, maghavesu, maghavena vā. Yuvānā, yuvāsu, yuvesu, yuvena vā.

By the inclusion of 'ca', for words ending in 'maghavan', 'yuvan', and so forth, the substitute 'ā' occurs sometimes for these case endings 'nā' and 'su'. Maghavānā, maghavāsu, maghavesu, or maghavena. Yuvānā, yuvāsu, yuvesu, or yuvena.

Iti nāmakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the second section in the chapter on nouns.

Tatiyakaṇḍa

The Third Section

161, 244. Tumha’mhehi [M 0.0101] namākaṃ.

After 'tumha' and 'amha', 'naṃ' becomes 'ākaṃ'.

Tehi tumhaamhehi naṃvacanassa ākaṃ hoti.

After those 'tumha' and 'amha', the ending 'naṃ' becomes 'ākaṃ'.

Tumhākaṃ, amhākaṃ.

Tumhākaṃ, amhākaṃ.

Namiti kimatthaṃ? Tumhehi, amhehi.

Why 'naṃ'? As in: Tumhehi, amhehi.

162, 237. Vā yvappaṭhamo.

Optionally, for the non-nominative 'yo'.

Tehi tumhaamhehi yo appaṭhamo ākaṃhoti vā.

After those 'tumha' and 'amha', the ending 'yo', when not in the nominative case, optionally becomes 'ākaṃ'.

Tumhākaṃ passāmi, tumhe passāmi vā. Amhākaṃ passasi, amhe passasi vā.

Tumhākaṃ passāmi, or tumhe passāmi. Amhākaṃ passasi, or amhe passasi.

Yoti kimatthaṃ? Tumhehi, amhehi.

Why 'yo'? As in: Tumhehi, amhehi.

Appaṭhamoti kimatthaṃ? Gacchatha tumhe, gacchāma mayaṃ.

Why 'appaṭhamo'? As in: Gacchatha tumhe, gacchāma mayaṃ.

Vātivikappanatthena yonaṃ aṃ ānaṃ honti. Tumhaṃ tumhānaṃ. Amhaṃ, amhānaṃ.

By the force of the option 'vā', for the ending 'naṃ', the forms 'aṃ' and 'ānaṃ' also occur. Tumhaṃ, tumhānaṃ. Amhaṃ, amhānaṃ.

163, 240. Sassaṃ.

For 'ssa', 'aṃ'.

Tehi humhaamhehi sassa vibhattissa aṃ ādeso hoti vā.

After those 'tumha' and 'amha', for the ending 'ssa', there is optionally the substitution 'aṃ'.

Tumhaṃ dīyate, tava dīyate. Tumhaṃ pariggaho, tava pariggaho. Amhaṃ dīyate, mama dīyate. Amhaṃ pariggaho, mama pariggaho.

Tumhaṃ dīyate, or tava dīyate. Tumhaṃ pariggaho, or tava pariggaho. Amhaṃ dīyate, or mama dīyate. Amhaṃ pariggaho, or mama pariggaho.

Sasseti [M 0.0102] kimatthaṃ? Tumhesu, amhesu.

Why 'sassa'? As in: Tumhesu, amhesu.

164, 200. Sabbanāma’kārate paṭhamo.

After a pronoun ending in 'a', the nominative plural becomes 'e'.

Sabbesaṃ sabbanāmānaṃ akārato yo paṭhamo ettamāpajjate.

For all pronouns ending in 'a', the nominative plural ending 'yo' becomes 'e'.

Sabbe, ye, te, ke, tumhe, amhe, ime.

Sabbe, ye, te, ke, tumhe, amhe, ime.

Sabbanāmāti kimatthaṃ? Devā, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā, manussā.

Why 'sabbanāma'? As in: Devā, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā, manussā.

Akāratoti kimatthaṃ? Amū purisā tiṭṭhanti.

Why 'akārato'? As in: Amū purisā tiṭṭhanti.

Yoti kimatthaṃ? Sabbo, yo, so, ko, ayaṃ.

Why 'yo'? As in: Sabbo, yo, so, ko, ayaṃ.

Paṭhamaggahaṇaṃ uttarasuttatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'paṭhama' is for the purpose of the following rule.

165, 208. Dvandaṭṭhā vā.

When in a dvanda compound, optionally.

Tasmā sabbanāma’kārato dvandaṭṭhā yo paṭhamo ettamāpajjate vā.

After a pronoun ending in 'a', when it is part of a dvanda compound, the nominative plural ending 'yo' optionally becomes 'e'.

Katarakatame, katarakatamā vā.

Katarakatame, or katarakatamā.

Sabbanāmāti kimatthaṃ? Devāsuranāga gandhabbamanussā.

Why 'sabbanāma'? As in: Devāsuranāgagandhabbamanussā.

Dvandaṭṭhāti kimatthaṃ te, sabbe.

Why 'dvandaṭṭhā'? As in: te, sabbe.

166, 209. Nāññaṃ [M 0.0103] sabbanāmikaṃ.

No other pronominal operation.

Sabbanāmikānaṃ dvandaṭṭhe nāññaṃ kāriyaṃ hoti,

For pronominal words in a dvanda compound, no other pronominal operation occurs.

Pubbāparānaṃ, pubbuttarānaṃ, adharuttarānaṃ.

Pubbāparānaṃ, pubbuttarānaṃ, adharuttarānaṃ.

167, 210. Bahubbīhimhi ca.

And in a Bahubbīhi compound.

Bahubbīhimhi ca samāse sabbanāmavidhānañca nāññaṃ kāriyaṃ hoti.

And in a Bahubbīhi compound, the rule for pronouns applies, and no other operation is to be performed.

Piyapubbāya, piyapubbānaṃ, piyapubbe, piyapubbassa.

Piyapubbāya, piyapubbānaṃ, piyapubbe, piyapubbassa.

Ceti kimatthaṃ? Sabbanāmavidhānaṃ hoti, dakkhiṇa pubbassaṃ, dakkhiṇapubbassā, uttarapubbassaṃ, uttarapubbassā.

Why 'ca'? Because the rule for pronouns applies. Dakkhiṇapubbassaṃ, dakkhiṇapubbassā, uttarapubbassaṃ, uttarapubbassā.

168, 203. Sabbato naṃ saṃ sānaṃ.

From all pronouns, for 'naṃ', 'saṃ' and 'sānaṃ' are substituted.

Sabbato sabbanāmato naṃvacanassa saṃsānaṃiccete ādesā honti.

From all pronouns, for the ending 'naṃ', these substitutions, 'saṃ' and 'sānaṃ', occur.

Sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ. Yesaṃ, yesānaṃ, yāsaṃ, yāsānaṃ. Tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, tāsaṃ, tāsānaṃ. Kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kāsaṃ, kāsānaṃ. Imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, imāsaṃ, imāsānaṃ. Amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ.

Sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ, sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ. Yesaṃ, yesānaṃ, yāsaṃ, yāsānaṃ. Tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, tāsaṃ, tāsānaṃ. Kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kāsaṃ, kāsānaṃ. Imesaṃ, imesānaṃ, imāsaṃ, imāsānaṃ. Amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ.

Namiti kimatthaṃ? Sabbassa, yassa, tassa, kassa. Evaṃ sabbattha.

Why 'naṃ'? As in: sabbassa, yassa, tassa, kassa. Thus everywhere.

169, 117. Rājassa [M 0.0104] rāju sunaṃhisu ca.

For 'rāja', 'rāju' is substituted before 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa rājuādeso hoti sunaṃhiiccetesu.

For the entire word 'rāja', the substitution 'rāju' occurs before these endings: 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'.

Rājūsu, rājūnaṃ, rājūhi, rājūbhi.

Rājūsu, rājūnaṃ, rājūhi, rājūbhi.

Sunaṃhisūti kimatthaṃ? Rājā.

Why 'sunaṃhisu'? As in: rājā.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ. Rājesu, rājānaṃ, rājehi rājebhi.

The inclusion of 'ca' is to indicate an option. Rājesu, rājānaṃ, rājehi, rājebhi.

170, 220. Sabbassimasse vā.

For the entire word 'ima', 'e' is optionally substituted.

Sabbasseva imasaddassa ekāro hoti vā sunaṃhiiccetesu.

For the entire word 'ima', the letter 'e' is optionally substituted before these endings: 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'.

Esu, imesu, esaṃ, imesaṃ, ehi, ebhi, imehi, imebhi.

Esu, imesu, esaṃ, imesaṃ, ehi, ebhi, imehi, imebhi.

Imasseti kimatthaṃ? Etesu, etesaṃ, etehi, etebhi.

Why 'imassa'? As in: etesu, etesaṃ, etehi, etebhi.

171, 219. Animi nāmhi ca.

For 'ima', 'ana' and 'imi' are substituted before 'nā'.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva ana imiiccete ādesā honti nāmhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire word 'ima', these substitutions, 'ana' and 'imi', occur before the case ending 'nā'.

Anena dhammadānena. Sukhitā hotu sā pajā.

Anena dhammadānena. Sukhitā hotu sā pajā.

Iminā buddhapūjena, patvāna amataṃ padaṃ.

Iminā buddhapūjena, patvāna amataṃ padaṃ.

Nāmhīti kimatthaṃ? Imesu, imesaṃ, imehi, imebhi.

Why 'nāmhi'? As in: imesu, imesaṃ, imehi, imebhi.

172, 218. Anapuṃsakassā [M 0.0105] yaṃ simhi.

For the non-neuter, 'ayaṃ' is substituted before 'si'.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva anapuṃsakassa ayaṃādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi.

For the entire word 'ima', in the non-neuter gender, the substitution 'ayaṃ' occurs before the case ending 'si'.

Ayaṃ puriso, ayaṃ itthī.

Ayaṃ puriso, ayaṃ itthī.

Anapuṃsakasseti kimatthaṃ? Idaṃ cittaṃ tiṭṭhati.

Why 'anapuṃsakassa'? As in: idaṃ cittaṃ tiṭṭhati.

Simhiti kimatthaṃ? Imaṃ purisaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

Why 'simhi'? As in: imaṃ purisaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

173, 223. Amussa mo saṃ.

For 'amu', 'm' becomes 's'.

Amusaddassa anapuṃsakassa makāro sakāramāpajjate vā simhi vibhattimhi.

For the word 'amu', in the non-neuter gender, the letter 'm' optionally becomes the letter 's' before the case ending 'si'.

Asu rājā, asu itthī, amuko rājā, amukā itthī.

Asu rājā, asu itthī, amuko rājā, amukā itthī.

Anapuṃsakasseti kimatthaṃ? Aduṃ pupphaṃ virocati.

For what purpose is anapuṃsakassa stated? [As in:] Aduṃ pupphaṃ virocati.

Amusseti kimatthaṃ? Ayaṃ puriso tiṭṭhati.

For what purpose is amussa stated? [As in:] Ayaṃ puriso tiṭṭhati.

Simhiti kimatthaṃ? Amhaṃ purisaṃ passasi.

For what purpose is simhi stated? [As in:] Amhaṃ purisaṃ passasi.

174, 211. Etatesaṃ to.

174, 211. Of eta and ta, the `t` [is replaced by `s`].

Eta taiccetesaṃ anapuṃsakānaṃ takāro sakāramāpajjate simhi vibhattimhi.

Of these, eta and ta, when they are not neuter, the letter `t` is replaced by `s` when the case ending si follows.

Eso puriso, esā itthī, so puriso, sā itthī.

Eso puriso (this man), esā itthī (this woman); so puriso (that man), sā itthī (that woman).

Etatesamiti [M 0.0106] kimatthaṃ? Itaro puriso, itarā itthī.

For what purpose is etatesaṃ stated? [As in:] Itaro puriso, itarā itthī.

Anapuṃsakānamiti kimatthaṃ? Etaṃ cittaṃ, etaṃ rūpaṃ. Taṃ cittaṃ, taṃ rūpaṃ.

For what purpose is anapuṃsakānaṃ stated? [As in:] Etaṃ cittaṃ, etaṃ rūpaṃ; Taṃ cittaṃ, taṃ rūpaṃ.

157, 212. Tassa vā nattaṃ sabbattha.

157, 212. Of that (ta), optionally, [the `t` becomes] `n` everywhere.

Tassa sabbanāmassa takārassa nattaṃ hoti vā sabbattha liṅgesu.

Of that pronoun (ta), the letter `t` optionally becomes `n` everywhere in all genders.

Nāya, tāya, naṃ, taṃ, ne, te, nesu, tesu, namhi, tamhi, nāhi, tāhi, nābhi, tābhi.

Nāya, tāya; naṃ, taṃ; ne, te; nesu, tesu; namhi, tamhi; nāhi, tāhi; nābhi, tābhi.

176, 213. Sasmāsmiṃsaṃsāsvattaṃ.

176, 213. In sasmā, smiṃ, saṃ, and sā, [there is] replacement by a.

Tassa sabbanāmassa takārassa sabbasseva attaṃ hoti vā sasmāsmiṃ saṃsāiccetesu sabbattha liṅgesu.

Of that pronoun (ta), the entire [stem] is optionally replaced by a when these [case endings] sasmā, smiṃ, saṃ, and sā follow, in all genders.

Assa, tassa, asmā, tasmā, asmiṃ, tasmiṃ, assaṃ, tassaṃ, assā, tassā.

Assa, tassa; asmā, tasmā; asmiṃ, tasmiṃ; assaṃ, tassaṃ; assā, tassā.

Takārasseti kimatthaṃ? Amussaṃ, amussā.

For what purpose is takārassa stated? [As in:] Amussaṃ, amussā.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Nesu, tesu.

For what purpose is etesu stated? [As in:] Nesu, tesu.

177, 221. Imasaddassa ca.

177, 221. And of ima.

Imasaddassa ca sabbasseva attaṃ hoti vā sasmāsmiṃ saṃ sāiccetesu sabbattha liṅgesu.

And of ima, the entire [stem] is optionally replaced by a when these [case endings] sasmā, smiṃ, saṃ, and sā follow, in all genders.

Assa[M 0.0107], imassa, asmā, imasmā, asmiṃ, imasmiṃ, assaṃ, imissaṃ, assā, imissā.

Assa, imassa; asmā, imasmā; asmiṃ, imasmiṃ; assaṃ, imissaṃ; assā, imissā.

Imasaddasseti kimatthaṃ? Etissaṃ, etissā.

For what purpose is imasaddassa stated? [As in:] Etissaṃ, etissā.

178, 22. Sabbato ko.

178, 22. From all [pronouns], ka.

Sabbato sabbanāmato kakārāgamo hoti vā simhi vibhattimhi.

After all pronouns, the augment ka optionally occurs when the case ending si follows.

Sabbako, yako, sako, amuko, asuko.

Sabbako, yako, sako, amuko, asuko.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Sabbo, yo, so, ko.

For what purpose is vā stated? [As in:] Sabbo, yo, so, ko.

Sabbanāmatoti kimatthaṃ? Puriso.

For what purpose is sabbanāmato stated? [As in:] Puriso.

Puna sabbatoggahaṇena aññasmāpi kakārāgamo hoti, hīnako, potako.

Furthermore, by the inclusion of sabbato, the augment ka also occurs after other [stems], [as in:] hīnako, potako.

179, 204. Yapato smiṃsānaṃ saṃsā.

179, 204. After gha and pa [stems], for smiṃ and sā, [the replacements are] saṃ and sā.

Sabbato sabbanāmato ghapasaññato smiṃsaiccetesaṃ saṃsā ādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

After all [stems] designated gha and pa, for smiṃ and sā respectively, saṃ and sā are the optional replacements.

Sabbassaṃ, sabbassā, sabbāyaṃ, sabbāya, imissaṃ, imissā, imāyaṃ, imāya, amussaṃ, amussā, amuyaṃ, amuyā.

Sabbassaṃ, sabbassā, sabbāyaṃ, sabbāya; imissaṃ, imissā, imāyaṃ, imāya; amussaṃ, amussā, amuyaṃ, amuyā.

Sabbanāmatoti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyaṃ, itthiyā.

For what purpose is sabbanāmato stated? [As in:] Itthiyaṃ, itthiyā.

Smiṃsānamiti kimatthaṃ? Amuyo.

Why 'smiṃsānaṃ'? [As in] 'amuyo'.

180, 207. Netāhi [M 0.0108] smimāya yā.

For these, `smiṃ` does not become `āya` or `yā`.

Etehi sabbanāmehi ghapasaññehi smiṃvacanassa neva āya yāādesā honti.

For these pronouns designated 'ghapa', the substitutions `āya` and `yā` do not occur for the `smiṃ` ending.

Etissaṃ, etāyaṃ, imissaṃ, imāyaṃ, amussaṃ, amuyaṃ.

Etissaṃ, etāyaṃ, imissaṃ, imāyaṃ, amussaṃ, amuyaṃ.

Smiṃnti kimatthaṃ? Tāya itthiyā mukhaṃ.

Why 'smiṃ'? [As in] 'tāya itthiyā mukhaṃ'.

Etāhīti kimatthaṃ? Kaññāya, vīṇāya, gaṅgāya, kapālikāya.

Why 'etāhi'? [As in] 'kaññāya,' 'vīṇāya,' 'gaṅgāya,' 'kapālikāya'.

181, 95. Manogaṇādito smiṃnānamiā.

After the `mano` group and so on, `smiṃ` and `nā` become `i` and `ā`.

Tasmā manogaṇādito smiṃnāiccetesaṃ ikāraākārādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Therefore, after the `mano` group and so on, for `smiṃ` and `nā`, the substitutions `i` and `ā` optionally occur respectively.

Manasi, manusmiṃ, sirasi, sirasmiṃ, manasā, manena, vacasā, vacena, sirasā, sirena, sarasā, sarena, tapasā, tapena, vayasā, vayena, yasasā, yasena, tejasā, tejena, urasā, urena, thāmasā, thāmena.

Manasi, manusmiṃ, sirasi, sirasmiṃ, manasā, manena, vacasā, vacena, sirasā, sirena, sarasā, sarena, tapasā, tapena, vayasā, vayena, yasasā, yasena, tejasā, tejena, urasā, urena, thāmasā, thāmena.

Smiṃnānamiti kimatthaṃ? Mano, siro, tamo, tapo, tejo.

Why 'smiṃnānaṃ'? [As in] 'mano,' 'siro,' 'tamo,' 'tapo,' 'tejo'.

Ādiggahaṇena aññāsmāpi smiṃnānaṃ ikāraākārādesā honti, bilasi, bilasā, padasi, padasā.

By the inclusion of 'ādi', the substitutions `i` and `ā` for `smiṃ` and `nā` also occur after other stems; for example: bilasi, bilasā, padasi, padasā.

182, 97. Sassa [M 0.0109] co.

And `o` for `sa`.

Tasmā manogaṇādito sassa ca okāro hoti.

Therefore, after the `mano` group and so on, for `sa` also, `o` occurs.

Manaso, thāmaso, tapaso.

Manaso, thāmaso, tapaso.

183, 48. Etesamo lope.

For these, `o` [occurs] on elision.

Etesaṃ manogaṇādīnaṃ anto ottamāpajjate vibhattilope kate.

For these of the `mano` group and so on, the ending becomes `o` when the case ending is elided.

Manomayaṃ, ayomayaṃ, tejosamena, tapoguṇena, siroruhena.

Manomayaṃ, ayomayaṃ, tejosamena, tapoguṇena, siroruhena.

Ādiggahaṇaṃkimatthaṃ? Aññesamanto ottamāpajjate. Āposamena, vāyosamena.

Why the inclusion of 'ādi'? For others also, the ending becomes 'o'. [For example,] āposamena, vāyosamena.

Lopeti kimatthaṃ? Padayā, tapasā, yasasā, vacasā, manasā, evamaññepi yojetabbā.

Why 'lope' (on elision)? [As in] padayā, tapasā, yasasā, vacasā, manasā. Thus it should be applied to others also.

184, 96. Sa sare vāgamo.

The augment `s` occurs optionally before a vowel.

Eteheva manogaṇādīhi vibhattādese sare pare sakārāgamo hoti vā.

After these very words of the `mano` group and so on, the augment `s` optionally occurs when a vowel that is a substitute for a case ending follows.

Manasā, vacasā, manasi, vacasi.

Manasā, vacasā, manasi, vacasi.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Manena, tejena, vasena,

Why 'vā' (optionally)? [As in] manena, tejena, vasena.

Sareti [M 0.0110] kimatthaṃ? Mano, tejo, yaso.

Why 'sare' (before a vowel)? [As in] mano, tejo, yaso.

Puna ādiggahaṇena aññasmimpi paccaye pare sakārāgamo hoti. Mānasikaṃ, vācasikaṃ.

Again, by the inclusion of 'ādi', the augment `s` also occurs when another suffix follows, for example: mānasikaṃ, vācasikaṃ.

185, 112. Santasaddassa so te bo cante.

For `santa`, the whole word becomes `sa` before `bhi`, and `b` is at the end.

Sabbassa santasaddassa sakārādeso hoti bhakāre pare, ante ca bakārāgamo hoti.

For the entire word `santa`, the substitution `sa` occurs when `bha` follows, and the augment `b` occurs at the end.

Sabbhireva samāsetha,

Associate only with the good,

Sabbhikubbetha santhavaṃ.

Foster intimacy with the good.

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya,

Having known the true Dhamma of the good,

Seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.

Better it is, not worse.

Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā.

Indeed, well-adorned royal chariots wear out.

Atho sarīrampi jaraṃ upeti.

So too, the body comes to old age.

Satañca dhammo na jaraṃ upeti,

But the Dhamma of the good does not come to old age,

Santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.

The good indeed make it known among the good.

Sabbhūto, sabbhāvo.

Wholly become, the nature of all.

Bheti kimatthaṃ? Santehi pūjito bhagavā.

Why 'bha'? As in 'santehi pūjito bhagavā'.

Caggahaṇaṃ kvaci sakārasseva pasiddhatthaṃ. Sakkāro, sakkato.

The inclusion of 'ca' is sometimes for the purpose of the established form with the letter 'sa'. For example: sakkāro, sakkato.

196, 107. Simhigacchantādīnaṃ [M 0.0111] ntasaddo aṃ.

196, 107. For stems such as 'gacchanta', before 'siṃ', the sound 'nta' becomes 'aṃ'.

Simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo amāpajjate vā.

For stems such as 'gacchanta', before 'siṃ', the sound 'nta' optionally becomes 'aṃ'.

Gacchaṃ, gacchanto, mahaṃ, mahanto, caraṃ, caranto, khādaṃ, khādanto.

Gacchaṃ, gacchanto; mahaṃ, mahanto; caraṃ, caranto; khādaṃ, khādanto.

Gacchantādīnamiti kimatthaṃ? Anto, danto, vanto, santo.

Why 'gacchanta and so on'? For example: anto, danto, vanto, santo.

187, 108. Sesesu ntuva.

187, 108. In the remaining cases, 'ntu' optionally.

Gacchantādīnaṃntasaddontuppaccayova daṭṭhabbo sesesu vibhattippaccayesu.

For stems such as 'gacchanta', the sound 'nta' should be understood as the suffix 'ntu' in the remaining case endings.

Gacchato, mahato, gacchati, mahati, gacchatā, mahatā.

Of the going one, of the great one; in the going one, in the great one; by the going one, by the great one.

Sesesūti kimatthaṃ? Gacchaṃ, mahaṃ, caraṃ, khādaṃ.

Why 'in the remaining cases'? For example: gacchaṃ, mahaṃ, caraṃ, khādaṃ.

188, 115. Brahmatta sakha rājādito amānaṃ.

188, 115. After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so on, 'aṃ' becomes 'ānaṃ'.

Brahma atta sakha rājaiccevamādito aṃvacanassa ānaṃ hoti vā.

After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so on, the ending 'aṃ' optionally becomes 'ānaṃ'.

Brahmānaṃ, brahmaṃ, attānaṃ, attaṃ, sakhānaṃ, sakhaṃ, rājānaṃ, rājaṃ.

Brahmānaṃ, brahmaṃ; attānaṃ, attaṃ; sakhānaṃ, sakhaṃ; rājānaṃ, rājaṃ.

Amiti kimatthaṃ? Rājā.

Why 'aṃ'? For example: rājā.

189, 113. Syā [M 0.0112] ca.

189, 113. And 'si' becomes 'ā'.

Brahma atta sakha rājaiccevamādito sivacanassa ā ca hoti.

After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so on, the ending 'si' also becomes 'ā'.

Brahmā, attā, sakhā, rājā, ātumā.

Brahmā, attā, sakhā, rājā, ātumā.

190, 114. Yonamāno.

190, 114. For 'yo', 'āno'.

Brahmaatta sakha rājaiccevamādito yonaṃ ānoādeso hoti.

After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so on, the substitute 'āno' occurs for 'yo'.

Brahmāno, attāno, sakhāno, rājāno, ātumāno.

Brahmāno, attāno, sakhāno, rājāno, ātumāno.

191, 130. Sakhato cāyo no.

191, 130. After 'sakha', also 'āyo' and 'no'.

Tasmā sakhato ca yonaṃ āyo no ādesā honti.

Therefore, after 'sakha', the substitutes 'āyo' and 'no' also occur for 'yo'.

Sakhāyo, sakhino.

Sakhāyo, sakhino.

Yonamiti kimatthaṃ? Sakhā.

Why 'for yo'? For example: sakhā.

192, 135. Smime.

For smiṃ, there is e.

Tasmā sakhato smiṃvacanassa ekāro hoti. Sakhe.

Therefore, after sakha, the case ending smiṃ becomes e. For example: sakhe.

193, 122. Brahmato [M 0.0113] gassa ca.

And after brahma, for ga.

Tasmā brahmato gassa ca ekāro hoti. He brahme.

Therefore, after brahma, for the vocative singular ending ga also, there is e. For example: he brahme.

194, 131. Sakhantassi no nā naṃ sesu.

For the final vowel of sakha, there is i when the case endings no, nā, naṃ, and sa follow.

Tassa sakhantassa ikāro hoti nonānaṃsaiccetesu.

For that stem sakha, the letter i is substituted when these case endings, namely no, nā, naṃ, and sa, follow.

Sakhino, sakhinā, sakhīnaṃ, sakhissa.

Of friends, by a friend, of friends, of a friend.

Etesvīti kimatthaṃ? Sakhārehi.

Why is etesu ('in these') stated? For example: sakhārehi.

195, 134. Āro himhi vā.

Optionally, āra is the substitute when hi follows.

Tassa sakhantassa āro hoti vā himhi vibhattimhi. Sakhārehi, sakhehi.

For that stem sakha, āra is optionally substituted when the case ending hi follows. For example: sakhārehi, sakhehi.

196, 133. Sunamaṃsu vā.

Optionally, when su, naṃ, and aṃ follow.

Tassa sakhantassa āro hoti vā sunaṃ aṃiccetesu.

For that stem sakha, āra is optionally substituted when these case endings, namely su, naṃ, and aṃ, follow.

Sakhāresu, sakhesu, sakhārānaṃ, sakhīnaṃ, sakhāraṃ, sakhaṃ.

Among friends, among friends; of friends, of friends; a friend, a friend.

197, 125. Brahmato tu smiṃ ni.

But after brahma, ni is the substitute for smiṃ.

Tasmā brahmato smiṃvacanassa niādeso hoti. Brahmani.

Therefore, after brahma, the substitution ni occurs for the case ending smiṃ. For example: brahmani.

Tuggahaṇena [M 0.0114] abrahmatopi smiṃ vacanassa ni hoti. Kammani, cammani, muddhani.

By the inclusion of tu, even after stems other than brahma, the case ending smiṃ becomes ni. For example: kammani, cammani, muddhani.

198, 123. Uttaṃ sanāsu.

The final vowel becomes u when sa and nā follow.

Tassa brahmasaddassa anto uttamāpajjate sanāiccetesu.

The final vowel of that word brahma becomes u when these case endings, namely sa and nā, follow.

Brahmuno, brahmunā.

Of Brahmā, by Brahmā.

Sanāsūti kimatthaṃ? Brahmā.

Why is sanāsu stated? For example: Brahmā.

199, 158. Satthupitādīnamā sismiṃsilopoca.

For satthu, pitu, and other such stems, the final vowel becomes ā when si (nominative singular) and smiṃ (locative singular) follow, and there is elision of si.

Satthupituādīnamanto attamāpajjate sismiṃ, silopo ca hoti.

The final vowel of satthu, pitu, and other such stems becomes ā when si and smiṃ follow, and there is elision of si.

Satthā, pitā, mātā, bhātā, kattā.

Teacher, father, mother, brother, maker.

Sisminti kimatthaṃ? Satthussa, pitussa, mātussa, bhātussa, kattussa.

Why is si-smiṃ stated? For example: satthussa, pitussa, mātussa, bhātussa, kattussa.

200, 159. Aññesvārattaṃ.

In other cases, the final vowel becomes āra.

Satthupituādīnamanto aññesu vacanesu ārattamāpajjate.

The final vowel of satthu, pitu, and other such stems becomes āra in other case endings.

Satthāraṃ, pitaraṃ, mātaraṃ, bhātaraṃ, kattāraṃ, satthārehi, pitarehi, mātarehi, bhātarehi, kattārehi.

The Teacher, the father, the mother, the brother, the maker; by the teachers, by the fathers, by the mothers, by the brothers, by the makers.

Aññesvīti [M 0.0115] kimatthaṃ? Satthā, pitā, mātā, bhātā, kattā.

Why is aññesu ('in other cases') stated? For example: satthā, pitā, mātā, bhātā, kattā.

201, 163. Vā naṃmhi.

Optionally, when naṃ follows.

Satthupituādīnamanto ārattamāpajjate vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

The final vowel of satthu, pitu, and other such stems optionally becomes āra when the case ending naṃ follows.

Satthārānaṃ, pitarānaṃ, mātarānaṃ, bhātarānaṃ.

Of teachers, of fathers, of mothers, of brothers.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Satthānaṃ, pitūnaṃ, mātūnaṃ, bhātūnaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? For 'satthānaṃ', 'pitūnaṃ', 'mātūnaṃ', 'bhātūnaṃ'.

202, 164. Satthunattañca.

202, 164. And for 'satthu', 'atta' is the substitute [before 'naṃ'].

Tassa satthusaddassa anto attamāpajjate vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For that word 'satthu', the final vowel optionally becomes 'atta' before the case ending 'naṃ'.

Satthānaṃ, pitānaṃ, mātānaṃ, bhātānaṃ, kattānaṃ.

Of teachers, of fathers, of mothers, of brothers, of makers.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Satthārānaṃ, pitarānaṃ, mātarānaṃ, bhātarānaṃ, dhītarānaṃ.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? For 'satthārānaṃ', 'pitarānaṃ', 'mātarānaṃ', 'bhātarānaṃ', 'dhītarānaṃ'.

Caggahaṇaṃ aññesampi saṅgahaṇatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of including others.

203, 162. Usasmiṃ salopo ca.

203, 162. Before 'sa' and 'smiṃ', 'u' [is substituted], and there is elision of 's'.

Satthupituiccevamādīnamantassa uttaṃ hoti vā sasmiṃ, salopo ca.

For 'satthu', 'pitu', and so on, the final vowel optionally becomes 'u' before 'sa' and 'smiṃ', and the 's' of the ending is elided.

Satthu[M 0.0116], satthussa, satthuno dīyate, pariggaho vā. Pitu, pitussa, pituno dīyate, pariggaho vā. Bhātu, bhātussa, bhātuno dīyate, pariggaho vā.

To/of the teacher ('satthu, satthussa, satthuno'); it is given, or it is a possession. To/of the father ('pitu, pitussa, pituno'); it is given, or it is a possession. To/of the brother ('bhātu, bhātussa, bhātuno'); it is given, or it is a possession.

Caggahaṇaṃ dutiyasampiṇḍanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of a second combination.

204, 167. Sakkamandhātādīnañca.

204, 167. And for 'Sakkamandhātu' and so on.

Sakkamandhātuiccevamādīnamanto uttamāpajjate sasmiṃ, salopo ca hoti.

For 'Sakkamandhātu' and so on, the final vowel becomes 'u' before 'sa' and 'smiṃ', and the 's' of the ending is elided.

Sakkamandhātu iva assa rājino vibhavo. Evaṃ kattu, gantu, dātu iccevamādī.

The glory of that king was like that of Sakkamandhātu. Similarly for 'kattu', 'gantu', 'dātu', and so on.

Punārambhaggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Niccadīpanatthaṃ. Sakkamandhātu.

What is the purpose of stating a new rule? For the purpose of indicating that it is obligatory. For example: 'Sakkamandhātu'.

Caggahaṇaṃ dutiyasampiṇḍanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of a second combination.

205, 160. Tato yonamo tu.

205, 160. After that, 'o' is the substitute for 'yo' and 'naṃ', however.

Tato ārādesato sabbesaṃ yo naṃ okārādeso hoti.

After that 'āra' substitute, for all such stems, the substitute 'o' occurs for 'yo' and 'naṃ'.

Satthāro, pitaro, mātaro, bhātaro, kattāro, vattāro.

Teachers, fathers, mothers, brothers, makers, speakers.

Tuggahaṇena aññasmāpi yonaṃ okāro hoti. Caturo janā, gāvo, ubho purisā.

By the inclusion of 'tu', the ending 'yo' becomes 'o' even for other stems. For example: 'caturo janā', 'gāvo', 'ubho purisā'.

206, 165. Tato [M 0.0117] smimi.

206, 165. After that, 'i' is the substitute for 'smiṃ'.

Tato ārādesato smiṃvacanassa ikārādeso hoti.

After that 'āra' substitute, the substitute 'i' occurs for the ending 'smiṃ'.

Satthari, pitari, mātari, dhītari, bhātari, kattari, vattari.

In the teacher, in the father, in the mother, in the daughter, in the brother, in the maker, in the speaker.

Puna tatogahaṇena aññasmāpi smiṃvacanassa ikāro hoti. Bhuvi.

Again, by the inclusion of 'tato', the ending 'smiṃ' becomes 'i' even for other stems. For example: 'bhuvi'.

207, 161. Nā ā.

207, 161. 'ā' is the substitute for 'nā'.

Tato ārādesato nāvacanassa āādeso hoti.

After that 'āra' substitute, the substitute 'ā' occurs for the ending 'nā'.

Satthārā, pitarā, mātarā, bhātarā, dhītarā, kattārā, vattārā.

By the teacher, by the father, by the mother, by the brother, by the daughter, by the maker, by the speaker.

208, 166. Āro rassamikāre.

208, 166. 'āra' becomes short before 'i'.

Ārādeso rassamāpajjate ikāre pare.

The 'āra' substitute becomes short when 'i' follows.

Satthari, pitari, mātari, dhītari, kattari, vattari.

In the teacher, in the father, in the mother, in the daughter, in the maker, in the speaker.

209, 168. Pitādīnamasimhi.

209, 168. For `pitu` and so on, in `asi` (instrumental singular) and `smiṃ` (locative singular).

Pitādīna mārādeso rassamāpajjate asimhi vibhattimhi.

For `pitā` and the like, the substitute `ārā` is shortened when the case ending `asi` follows.

Pitarā, mātarā, bhātarā, mītarā pitaro, mātaro, bhātaro, dhītaro.

By the father, by the mother, by the brother, by the daughter; fathers, mothers, brothers, daughters.

Asimhiggahaṇaṃ [M 0.0118] tomhi pare ikārādesañāpanatthaṃ. Mātito, pitito, bhātito, duhitito.

The mention of `asimhi` is for the purpose of indicating the substitution of `i` when `to` follows. From the mother, from the father, from the brother, from the daughter.

210, 239. Tayātayīnaṃ takāro tvattaṃ vā.

210, 239. For `tayā` and `tayī`, the `t` optionally becomes `tv`.

Tayātayi iccetesaṃ takāro tvattamāpajjate vā.

For `tayā` and `tayī`, the `t` optionally becomes `tv`.

Tvayā, tayā, tvayi, tayi.

By you, by you; in you, in you.

Etesamiti kimatthaṃ? Tuvaṃ, tavaṃ.

Why 'of these'? So that it does not apply to `tuvaṃ`, `tavaṃ`.

Iti nādhakappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section in the Nādhakappa.

Catutthakaṇḍa

The Fourth Section

211, 126. Attanto hismi’manattaṃ.

211, 126. The end of `atta` becomes `anatta` before `hi`.

Tassa attano anto anattamāpajjate himhi vibhattimhi.

The end of that `atta` becomes `anatta` when the case ending `hi` follows.

Attanehi, attanebhi.

By themselves, by themselves.

Attantoti kimatthaṃ? Rājehi, rājebhi.

Why 'the end of `atta`'? So that it does not apply to `rājehi`, `rājebhi`.

Hisminti kimatthaṃ? Attano.

Why 'before `hi`'? So that it does not apply to `attano`.

Anattamitibhāvaniddesena attasaddassa sakādeso hoti sabbāsu vibhattīsu. Sako, sakā, sakaṃ, sake.

By the instruction indicating the state `anatta`, the word `atta` has `saka` as a substitute in all case endings. One's own (masculine), one's own (feminine), one's own (neuter), one's own (vocative).

212, 329. Tato [M 0.0119] smiṃni.

212, 329. After that, `smiṃ` becomes `ni`.

Tato attato smiṃvacanassa ni hoti. Attani.

After that, that is, after `atta`, the ending `smiṃ` becomes `ni`. In the self.

213, 127. Sassa no.

213, 127. `sa` becomes `no`.

Tatoattato sassa vibhattissa no hoti, attano.

After that `atta`, the case ending `sa` becomes `no`; `attano`.

214, 128. Smā nā.

214, 128. `smā` becomes `nā`.

Tato attato smā vacanassa nā hoti. Attanā.

After that `atta`, the ending `smā` becomes `nā`. By oneself.

Puna tatogahaṇena tassa attano takārasseva rakāro hoti sabbesu vacanesu. Atrajo, atrajaṃ.

Again, by the inclusion of `tato`, the `t` of `atta` itself becomes `r` in all words. `Atrajo`, `atrajaṃ`.

215, 141. Jhalato ca.

215, 141. And after `jhala`.

Jhalaiccetehi smāvacanassa nā hoti.

After these `jhala` nouns, the ending `smā` becomes `nā`.

Agginā, daṇḍinā, bhikkhunā, sayambhunā.

With fire, by the staff-bearer, by the monk, by the Self-Existent One.

Smāti kimatthaṃ? Aggayo, munayo, isayo.

Why `smā`? So that it does not apply to `aggayo`, `munayo`, `isayo`.

216, 180. Ghapato smiṃ yaṃ vā.

216, 180. After `ghapa`, `smiṃ` optionally becomes `yaṃ`.

Tasmā ghapato smiṃ vacanassa yaṃ hoti vā.

After that `ghapa`, the ending `smiṃ` optionally becomes `yaṃ`.

Kaññāyaṃ[M 0.0120], kaññāya. Rattiyaṃ, rattiyā. Itthiyaṃ, itthiyā. Yāguyaṃ, yāguyā. Vakhuyaṃ, vadhuyā.

Kaññāyaṃ, kaññāya. Rattiyaṃ, rattiyā. Itthiyaṃ, itthiyā. Yāguyaṃ, yāguyā. Vadhuyāṃ, vadhuyā.

217, 199. Yonaṃ ni napuṃsakehi.

For the 'yo' endings, 'ni' is substituted with neuter nouns.

Sabbesaṃ yonaṃ ni hoti vā napuṃsakehi liṅgehi.

For all 'yo' endings, 'ni' is optionally substituted with neuter genders.

Aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhī, āyūni, āyū.

'Bones', 'bones'. 'Lifespans', 'lifespans'.

Napuṃsakehīti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyo.

Why 'with neuter nouns'? (So that it does not apply to) 'itthiyo'.

218, 196. Ato niccaṃ.

From 'a', always.

Akārantehi napuṃsakaliṅgehi yonaṃ ni hoti niccaṃ.

For neuter genders ending in the letter 'a', 'ni' is always substituted for the 'yo' endings.

Yāni, yāni. Tāni, tāni. Kāni, kāni. Bhayāni, bhayāni. Rūpāni, rūpāni.

Yāni (whatever things); tāni (those things); kāni (which things); bhayāni (fears); rūpāni (forms).

219, 196. Siṃ.

Of 'si', 'aṃ' is the substitute.

Akārantehi napuṃsakaliṅgehi sivacanassa aṃ hoti niccaṃ.

With neuter genders ending in the letter 'a', the ending 'si' always becomes 'aṃ'.

Sabbaṃ, yaṃ, taṃ, kaṃ, rūpaṃ.

Sabbaṃ (all); yaṃ (whatever); taṃ (that); kaṃ (what); rūpaṃ (form).

220, 74. Sesato lopaṃ pasipi.

Of the remainder, elision, as in 'pasipi'.

Tato niddiṭṭhehi ligehi sesakhatā gasiiccete lopamāpajjante.

After those specified genders, the remaining endings, such as the vocative 'si', undergo elision.

Bhoti [M 0.0121] itthi, sā itthī. Bho daṇḍi, so daṇḍī. Bho sattha, so satthā. Bho rāja, so rājā. Sesatoti kimatthaṃ? Puriso gacchati.

'Bhoti itthi' (O lady), 'sā itthī' (that lady). 'Bho daṇḍi' (O ascetic), 'so daṇḍī' (that ascetic). 'Bho sattha' (O teacher), 'so satthā' (that teacher). 'Bho rāja' (O king), 'so rājā' (that king). Why 'of the remainder'? (So that it does not apply to) 'puriso gacchati'.

Gasīti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyā, satthussa.

Why 'vocative si'? (So that it does not apply to) 'itthiyā', 'satthussa'.

221, 282. Sabbāsamāvuso pasagganipātādīhi ca.

Of all, with 'āvuso', and with prefixes, particles, and so forth.

Sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ ekavacanabahuvacanānaṃ paṭhamā dutiyātatiyā catutthī pañcamī chaṭṭhī sattamīnaṃ lopo hoti, āvuso upasagga nipātaiccevamādīhi ca,

Of all case endings, singular and plural—nominative, accusative, instrumental, dative, ablative, genitive, and locative—elision occurs with the word 'āvuso', and with prefixes, particles, and so on.

Tvaṃ panāvuso, tumhe panāvuso, padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya, vihāraṃ sve upagaccheyya.

Examples: 'Tvaṃ panāvuso' (But you, friend), 'tumhe panāvuso' (but you all, friends). 'Padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya' (One should recite the Dhamma word by word). 'Vihāraṃ sve upagaccheyya' (One should go to the monastery tomorrow).

Pa, parā, ni, nī, u, du, saṃ, vi, ava, anu, pari, adhi, abhi, pati, su, ā, ati, api, apa, upa, pahāro, parābhavo, nihāro, nīhāro, uhāro, duhāro, saṃhāro, vihāro, avahāro, anuhāro, parihāro, adhihāro, abhihāro, patihāro, suhāro, āhāro, atihāro, apihāro, apahāro, upahāro, evaṃ vīsati upasaggehi ca.

Pa, parā, ni, nī, u, du, saṃ, vi, ava, anu, pari, adhi, abhi, pati, su, ā, ati, api, apa, upa, pahāro, parābhavo, nihāro, nīhāro, uhāro, duhāro, saṃhāro, vihāro, avahāro, anuhāro, parihāro, adhihāro, abhihāro, patihāro, suhāro, āhāro, atihāro, apihāro, apahāro, upahāro; and thus with these twenty prefixes.

Yathā, tathā, evaṃ, khalu, kho, tatra, atho, atha, hi, tu ca, vā, vo, haṃ, abhaṃ, alaṃ, eva, ho aho, he[M 0.0122], ahe, re, are, evamādīhi nipātehi ca yojetabbāni.

Yathā, tathā, evaṃ, khalu, kho, tatra, atho, atha, hi, tu, ca, vā, vo, haṃ, abhaṃ, alaṃ, eva, ho, aho, he, ahe, re, are; and with these and similar particles, application should be made.

Caggahaṇama vadhāraṇatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of emphasis.

222, 342. Pumassa liṅgādīsu samāsesu.

Of 'puma', elision occurs when followed by 'liṅga' and so on in compounds.

Pumaiccetassa anto lopamāpajjate liṅgādīsu parapadesu samāsesu.

The final part of the word 'puma' undergoes elision in compounds when 'liṅga' and so on are the subsequent members.

Pulliṅgaṃ, pumbhāvo, puṅkokilo.

Pulliṅgaṃ (masculine gender); pumbhāvo (masculinity); puṅkokilo (male cuckoo).

Pumasseti kimatthaṃ? Itthiliṅgaṃ, napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ.

Why 'of puma'? (So that the rule does not apply to) 'itthiliṅgaṃ', 'napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ'.

Liṅgādīsūti kimatthaṃ? Pumitthī.

Why 'when followed by liṅga and so on'? (So that it does not apply to) 'pumitthī'.

Samāsesūti kimatthaṃ? Pumassa liṅgaṃ.

Why 'in compounds'? (So that it does not apply to) 'pumassa liṅgaṃ'.

223, 188. Aṃ yamīto pasaññato.

The ending 'aṃ' becomes 'yaṃ' after a stem ending in 'ī' that has the designation 'pa'.

Aṃ vacanassa yaṃ hoti vā īto pasaññato.

The ending 'aṃ' optionally becomes 'yaṃ' after a stem ending in 'ī' that has the designation 'pa'.

Itthiyaṃ, itthiṃ.

Itthiyaṃ, itthiṃ (the woman).

Pasaññatoti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍinaṃ, bhoginaṃ.

Why 'from a 'pa'-designated stem'? (So that it does not apply to) 'daṇḍinaṃ', 'bhoginaṃ'.

Amiti kimatthaṃ? Itthīhi.

Why is 'aṃ' specified? So that it does not apply to 'itthīhi'.

224, 153. Naṃ jhato katarassā.

After a 'jha' stem and 'katara', 'naṃ' is substituted.

Tasmā jhato katarassā aṃ vacanassa naṃ hoti.

Therefore, after a 'jha' stem and after 'katara', the ending 'aṃ' becomes 'naṃ'.

Daṇḍinaṃ[M 0.0123], bhoginaṃ.

The staff-bearer, the enjoyer.

Jhatoti kimatthaṃ? Vessabhuṃ.

Why is 'after a jha stem' specified? So that it does not apply to 'Vessabhuṃ'.

Katarassāti kimatthaṃ? Kucchiṃ.

Why is 'after katara' specified? So that it does not apply to 'Kucchiṃ'.

225, 151. Yonaṃ no.

For the 'yo' endings, 'no' is substituted.

Sabbesaṃ yonaṃ jhato katarassā no hoti.

For all 'yo' endings, 'no' is substituted after a 'jha' stem and after 'katara'.

Daṇḍino bhogino, he daṇḍino, he bhogino.

The staff-bearers, the enjoyers; O staff-bearers, O enjoyers.

Katarassāti kimatthaṃ? Aggayo, munayo, isayo.

Why is 'after katara' specified? So that it does not apply to 'aggayo', 'munayo', 'isayo'.

Jhatoti kimatthaṃ? Sayambhuno.

Why is 'after a jha stem' specified? So that it does not apply to 'Sayambhuno'.

Yonanti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍinā, bhoginā.

Why is 'yonaṃ' specified? So that it does not apply to 'Daṇḍinā', 'bhoginā'.

226, 154. Smiṃni.

For 'smiṃ', 'ni' is substituted.

Tasmā jhato katarassā smiṃvacanassa niāde so hoti.

Therefore, after a 'jha' stem and after 'katara', 'ni' is substituted for the ending 'smiṃ'.

Daṇḍini, bhogini.

In the one with a stick, in the one possessing wealth.

Katarassāti kimatthaṃ? Byādhimhi.

Why is 'after katara' specified? So that it does not apply to 'byādhimhi'.

227, 270. Kissa kaveca.

For 'kiṃ', 'ka' is substituted when 'va' follows, and also in other cases.

Kimiccetassa ko ca hoti vapaccaye pare.

For 'kiṃ', 'ko' is also substituted when the 'va' suffix follows.

Kva [M 0.0124] gatosi tvaṃ devānaṃ piyatissa.

Where have you gone, O Tissa, beloved of the gods?

Caggahaṇena avapaccaye parepi ko ca hoti. Ko taṃninditu marahati, kathaṃ bodhayituṃ dhammaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', 'ko' is also substituted even when a non-'va' suffix follows. Who is able to blame him? How to teach the Dhamma?

Veti kimatthaṃ? Kuto āgatosi tvaṃ.

Why is 'va' specified? So that it does not apply to 'Kuto āgatosi tvaṃ'.

228, 272. Kuhiṃ haṃ su ca.

'Ku' is substituted for 'kiṃ' when the suffixes 'hiṃ', 'haṃ', and 'su' follow, and also in other cases.

Kimiccetassa ku hoti hiṃ haṃiccetesu ca. Kuhiṃ gacchasi, kulaṃ gacchasi.

For 'kiṃ', 'ku' is substituted when 'hiṃ', 'haṃ', and other such suffixes follow. Where do you go? You go to a family.

Caggahaṇena hiñcanaṃdācanaṃ paccayesu paresu aññatthāpi ku hoti. Kuhiñcanaṃ, kudācanaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', 'ku' is also substituted elsewhere when suffixes such as 'hiñcanaṃ' and 'dācanaṃ' follow. Wherever, whenever.

229, 226. Sesesu ca.

And in the remaining cases.

Kimiccetassa ko hoti sesesu vibhattipaccayesu paresu.

For 'kiṃ', 'ko' is substituted when the remaining case endings and suffixes follow.

Ko pakāro kathaṃ, kaṃ pakāraṃ kathaṃ.

What mode? How. What mode? How.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of extension.

230, 262. Trabhothesu ca.

And when the suffixes 'tra', 'to', and 'tha' follow.

Kimiccetassa ku hoti tratotha iccetesu ca.

For 'kiṃ', 'ku' is substituted when the suffixes 'tra', 'to', 'tha', and others follow.

Kutra, kuto, kuttha.

Where, whence, where.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ,

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in other elements.

231, 263. Sabbassetassa[M 0.0125], kāro vā.

231, 263. For the entire stem 'eta', 'a' is optionally substituted.

Sabbassa etasaddassa akāro hoti vā tothaiccetesu.

For the entire stem 'eta', 'a' is optionally substituted when the suffixes 'to', 'tha', and so on follow.

Ato, attha, etto, ettha.

From there, there, from here, here.

232, 267. Tre niccaṃ.

232, 267. Before 'tra', always.

Sabbassa etasaddassa akāro hoti niccaṃ trapaccaye pare.

For the entire stem 'eta', 'a' is always substituted when the suffix 'tra' follows.

Atra.

Here.

233, 264. E tothesu ca.

233, 264. And 'e' before 'to', 'tha', and so on.

Sabbassa etasaddassa ekāro hoti vā tothaiccetesu.

For the entire stem 'eta', 'e' is optionally substituted when the suffixes 'to', 'tha', and so on follow.

Etto, ato, ettha, attha.

From here, from there, here, there.

234, 265. Imassi thaṃ dāni ha to dhesu ca.

234, 265. For 'ima', 'i' is substituted before the suffixes `thaṃ`, `dāni`, `ha`, `to`, and `dha`.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva ikāro hoti thaṃ dānihato dhaiccetesu.

For the entire stem 'ima', 'i' is substituted when the suffixes `thaṃ`, `dāni`, `ha`, `to`, `dha`, and so on follow.

Itthaṃ, idāni, iha, ito, idha.

Thus, now, here, from here, here.

235, 281. Adhunāmhi [M 0.0126] ca.

235, 281. And 'a' before `dhunā`.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva akāro hoti dhunāmhi paccaye pare.

For the entire stem 'ima', 'a' is substituted when the suffix `dhunā` follows.

Adhunā.

Now.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of determination.

236, 280. Eta rahimhi.

236, 280. Before `rahi`, `eta` is substituted.

Sabbasseva imasaddassa etādeso hoti rahimhi paccaye pare.

For the entire stem 'ima', the substitution 'eta' occurs when the suffix `rahi` follows.

Etarahi.

Now.

237, 176. Itthiyamato āpaccayo.

237, 176. In the feminine, the suffix 'ā' is added after 'a'.

Itthiyaṃ vattamānāya akārato āpaccayo hoti.

When denoting the feminine, the suffix 'ā' is added after a stem-final 'a'.

Sabbā, yā, sā, kā. Katarā.

All, which, she, who? Which (of two)?

238, 187. Nadādito vā ī.

238, 187. From the `nadī` group, 'ī' is an optional suffix.

Nadādito vāanadāditovā itthiyaṃ vattamānāya īpaccayo hoti.

When denoting the feminine, the suffix 'ī' is optionally added to words of the `nadī` group and to others.

Nadī, mahī, kumārī, taruṇī, sakhī, itthī.

River, earth, maiden, young woman, female friend, woman.

239, 190. Ṇava [M 0.0127] ṇika ṇeyya ṇa ntuhi.

239, 190. After `ṇava`, `ṇika`, `ṇeyya`, `ṇa`, and `ntu`.

Ṇava ṇika ṇeyya ṇa ntuiccetehi itthiyaṃ vattamānehi īpaccayo hoti.

After these suffixes, `ṇava`, `ṇika`, `ṇeyya`, `ṇa`, and `ntu`, when denoting the feminine, the suffix 'ī' is added.

Māṇavī, paṇḍavī, nāvikī, venateyyī, kunteyyī, gotamī, guṇavatī, sāmāvatī.

Maiden, female descendant of Paṇḍu, boatwoman, female descendant of Vinatā, female descendant of Kuntī, Gotamī, virtuous woman, Sāmāvatī.

240, 193. Pati bhikkhurājīkārantehi inī.

From `pati`, `bhikkhu`, `rājī`, and words ending in `kāra`, the suffix `inī` is employed.

Pati bhikkhu rājīkārantehi itthiyaṃ vattamānehi inīpaccayo hoti.

After `pati`, `bhikkhu`, `rājī`, and words ending in `kāra`, when denoting the feminine, the suffix `inī` is employed.

Gahapatānī, bhikkhunī, rājinī, hatthinī, daṇḍinī, medhāvinī, tapassinī.

A householder's wife, a nun, a queen, a female elephant, a woman with a staff, a wise woman, a female ascetic.

241, 191. Ntussa tamīkāre.

For `ntu`, `ta` is the substitute when `ī` follows.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa takāro hoti vā īkāre pare.

For the entire `ntu` suffix, the letter `ta` occurs optionally when `ī` follows.

Guṇavatī, guṇavantī, kulavatī, kulavantī, satimatī. Satimantī, mahatī, mahantī, gottamatī, gottamantī.

A virtuous woman (guṇavatī), a virtuous woman (guṇavantī); a woman of good family (kulavatī), a woman of good family (kulavantī); a mindful woman (satimatī), a mindful woman (satimantī); a great woman (mahatī), a great woman (mahantī); a woman of good lineage (gottamatī), a woman of good lineage (gottamantī).

242, 192. Bhavato bhoto.

For `bhavant`, `bhot` is the substitute.

Sabbasseva bhavantasaddassa bhotādeso hoti īkāre itthigate pare.

For the entire word `bhavant`, the substitution `bhot` occurs when `ī` follows, denoting the feminine.

Bhoti ayye, bhoti kaññe, bhoti kharādiye.

O noble lady, O maiden, O Kharādiya.

243, 110. Bhoge [M 0.0128] tu.

And `bho` is the substitute in the vocative singular.

Sabbasseva bhavantasaddassa bhoādeso hoti ge pare.

For the entire word `bhavant`, the substitution `bho` occurs when the vocative singular suffix `gi` follows.

Bho purisa, bho aggi, bho rāja, bho sattha, bho daṇḍi, bho sayambhu.

O man, O fire, O king, O teacher, O staff-bearer, O self-originated one.

Geti kimatthaṃ? Bhavatā, bhavaṃ.

For what purpose is `gi` mentioned? To prevent the rule applying to forms such as `bhavatā` and `bhavaṃ`.

Tuggahaṇena aññasmimpi vacane sabbassa bhavantasaddassa bhonta bhante bhonto bhadde bhotā bho toiccete ādesā honti.

By the inclusion of `tu`, also in other numbers, for the entire word `bhavant` these substitutions occur: `bhonta`, `bhante`, `bhonto`, `bhadde`, `bhotā`, `bho`, and `to`.

Bhonta, bhante, bhonto, bhadde, bhotā, bhoto.

Bhonta, bhante, bhonto, bhadde, bhotā, bhoto.

244, 72. Akārapitādyantānamā.

Of the final `ā` and of words such as `pitar`, the ending becomes `a`.

Akāro ca pitādīnamanto ca attamāpajjate ge pare.

The vowel `ā` and the ending of words such as `pitar` become `a` when the vocative singular suffix `gi` follows.

Bho purisā, bho rājā, bho pitā, bho mātā, bho satthā.

O men, O king, O father, O mother, O teacher.

245, 152. Jhalapā rassaṃ.

The vowels denoted by `jha`, `la`, and `pa` are shortened.

Jhalapaiccete rassamāpajjante ge pare.

These vowels, denoted by `jha`, `la`, and `pa`, are shortened when the vocative singular suffix `gi` follows.

Bho daṇḍi, bho sayambhu, bhoti itthi, bhotivadhu,

O staff-bearer, O self-originated one, O woman, O bride.

246, 73. Ākāro [M 0.0129] vā.

The vowel `ā` is optionally shortened.

Ākāro rassamāpajjate vā ge pare.

The vowel `ā` is optionally shortened when the vocative singular suffix `gi` follows.

Bho rāja, bho rājā, bho atta, bho attā, bho sakha, bho sakhā, bho sattha, bho satthā.

O king (rāja), O king (rājā); O self (atta), O self (attā); O friend (sakha), O friend (sakhā); O teacher (sattha), O teacher (satthā).

Iti nāmakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the fourth section in the chapter on nouns.

Pañcamakaṇḍa

The Fifth Section

247, 261. Tvādayo vibhattisaññāyo.

`Tvā` and so forth have the designation `vibhatti`.

Toādi yesaṃ paccayānaṃ, te honti tvādayo. Te paccayā tvādayo vibhattisaññāva daṭṭhabbā.

Those suffixes which begin with `to` are called `tvādayo`. These suffixes, `tvā` and so forth, should be understood as having the designation `vibhatti` (case-ending).

Sabbato, yato, tato, kuto, ato, ito, sabbadā, yadā, tadā, kadā, idha, idāni.

From all, from which, from that, from where?, from this, from here, always, when, then, when?, here, now.

248, 260. Kvaci to pañcamyatthe.

Sometimes the suffix `to` is used in the sense of the ablative case.

Kvaci topaccayo hoti pañcamyatthe.

Sometimes the suffix 'to' occurs in the sense of the ablative case.

Sabbato, yato, tato, kuto, ato, ito.

From all, from which, from that, from what, from this, from here.

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Sabbasmā, imasmā.

Why 'sometimes'? Sabbasmā, imasmā.

249, 266. Tra [M 0.0130] tha sattamiyā sabbanāmehi.

After all pronouns, the suffixes 'tra' and 'tha' occur in the locative case.

Trathaiccete paccayā honti sattamyatthe sabba nāmehi.

These suffixes 'tra' and 'tha' occur after all pronouns in the sense of the locative case.

Sabbatra, sabbattha, yatra, yattha, tatra, tattha.

Everywhere, everywhere, where, where, there, there.

250, 268. Sabbato dhi.

After 'sabba', 'dhi'.

Sabbaiccetasmā dhipaccayo hoti kvaci sattamyatthe. Sabbadhi, sabbasmiṃ.

After 'sabba', the suffix 'dhi' sometimes occurs in the sense of the locative case. Sabbadhi, sabbasmiṃ.

251, 269. Kiṃ smā vo.

After 'kiṃ', 'va'.

Kimiccetasmā vapaccayo hoti sattamyatthe.

After 'kiṃ', the suffix 'va' occurs in the sense of the locative case.

Kva gatosi tva devānaṃpiyatissa.

Where have you gone, O Tissa, dear to the gods?

252, 271. Hiṃ haṃ hiñcanaṃ.

'Hiṃ', 'haṃ', and 'hiñcanaṃ'.

Kimiccetasmā hiṃhaṃhiñcanaṃiccete paccayā honti sattamyatthe.

After 'kiṃ', these suffixes 'hiṃ', 'haṃ', and 'hiñcanaṃ' occur in the sense of the locative case.

Kuhiṃ, kulaṃ, kuhiñcanaṃ.

Where, where, anywhere.

253, 273. Tamhā ca.

And after 'ta'.

Tamhā ca hi haṃiccete paccayā honti sattamyatthe. Tahiṃ, tahaṃ.

And after 'ta', these suffixes 'hiṃ' and 'haṃ' occur in the sense of the locative case. Tahiṃ, tahaṃ.

Caggahaṇaṃ [M 0.0131] hiñcanaggahaṇanivattanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of excluding 'hiñcanaṃ'.

254, 274. Imasmā ha dhā ca.

And after 'ima', 'ha' and 'dha'.

Imasmā hadhaiccete paccayā honti sattamyatthe. Iha, idha.

After 'ima', these suffixes 'ha' and 'dha' occur in the sense of the locative case. Iha, idha.

Caggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of specification.

255, 275. Yato hiṃ.

After 'ya', 'hiṃ'.

Tasmā yato hiṃpaccayo hoti sattamyatthe. Yahiṃ.

After 'ya', the suffix 'hiṃ' occurs in the sense of the locative case. Yahiṃ.

256, 0. Kāle.

Regarding time.

“Kāle”iccetaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

This term 'kāle' should be understood as a heading.

257, 279. Kiṃsabbaññekayakuhidādācanaṃ.

After 'kiṃ', 'sabba', 'añña', 'eka', 'ya', and 'ku', the suffixes 'dā' and 'dācanaṃ'.

Kiṃ sabbaañña eka ya kuiccetehi dā dācanaṃiccete paccayā honti kāle sattamyatthe.

After 'kiṃ', 'sabba', 'añña', 'eka', 'ya', and 'ku', the suffixes 'dā' and 'dācanaṃ' occur in the sense of the locative case regarding time.

Kadā, sabbadā, aññadā, ekadā, yadā, kudācanaṃ.

When, always, at another time, once, when, ever.

258, 278. Tamhā dāni ca.

And after 'ta', 'dāni'.

Taiccetasmā dāni dāiccete paccayā honti, kāle sattamyatthe.

After 'ta', the suffixes 'dāni' and 'dā' occur in the sense of the locative case regarding time.

Tadāni[M 0.0132], tadā.

Then, then.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in other elements.

259, 279. Imasmā rahi dhunā dāni ca.

After 'ima': 'rahi', 'dhunā', and 'dāni'.

Imasmā rahi dhunā dāniiccete paccayā honti kāle sattamyatthe.

After 'ima', these suffixes 'rahi', 'dhunā', and 'dāni' occur in the sense of the locative case, signifying time.

Terahi, adhunā, idāni.

Then, now, now.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in other elements.

260, 277. Sabbassa so dāmhi vā.

For 'sabba', 'sa' is the optional substitute when 'dā' follows.

Sabbaiccetassa sakārādeso hoti vā dāmhi paccaye pare.

For 'sabba', the substitution 'sa' occurs optionally when the suffix 'dā' follows.

Sadā, sabbadā.

Always, at all times.

261, 369. Avaṇṇo ye lopañca.

The vowel 'a' is elided before 'ya'.

Avaṇṇo ye paccaye pare lopamāpajjate.

The vowel 'a' undergoes elision when the suffix 'ya' follows.

Bāhussaccaṃ, paṇḍiccaṃ, vepullaṃ, kāruññaṃ, kosallaṃ, sāmaññaṃ, sohajjaṃ.

Great learning, wisdom, extensiveness, compassion, skill, asceticism, friendship.

262, 391. Vuḍḍhassa jo iyiṭṭhesu.

For 'vuḍḍha', 'ja' is the substitute before 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Sabbasseva vuḍḍhasaddassa joādeso hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'vuḍḍha', the substitution 'ja' occurs before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Jeyyo[M 0.0133], jeṭṭho.

Elder, eldest.

263, 392. Pasatthassa so ca.

For 'pasattha', 'sa' is a substitute, and also the preceding one.

Sabbasseva pasatthasaddassa soādeso hoti, jādeso ca iyaiṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'pasattha', the substitution 'sa' occurs, and also the substitution 'ja', before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

Better, best; superior, chief.

264, 393. Antikassa nedo.

For 'antika', 'neda' is the substitute.

Sabbassa antikasaddassa nedādeso hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'antika', the substitution 'neda' occurs before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Nediyo, nediṭṭho.

Nearer, nearest.

265, 394. Bāḷhassa sādho.

For 'bāḷha', 'sādha' is the substitute.

Sabbassa bāḷhasaddassa sādhādeso hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'bāḷha', the substitution 'sādha' occurs before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Sādhiyo, sādhiṭṭho.

Stronger, strongest.

266, 395. Appassa kaṇa.

For 'appa', 'kaṇa' is the substitute.

Sabbassa appasaddassa kaṇa ādeso hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'appa', the substitution 'kaṇa' occurs before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Kaṇiyo, kaṇiṭṭho.

Younger, youngest.

267, 396. Yuvānañca[M 0.0134].

And for 'yuvan'.

Sabbassa yuvasaddassa kaṇa ādeso hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

For the entire word 'yuvan', the substitution 'kaṇa' occurs before the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha'.

Kaniyo, kaniṭṭho.

Younger, youngest.

Caggahaṇamanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of drawing in other elements.

268, 397. Vantumantu vīnañca lopo.

The elision of 'vantu', 'mantu', and 'vī'.

Vantumantuvīiccetesaṃ paccayānaṃ lopo hoti iyaiṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu.

Of these suffixes 'vantu', 'mantu', and 'vī', elision occurs when the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha' follow.

Guṇiyo, guṇiṭṭho, satiyo, satiṭṭho, medhiyo, medhiṭṭho.

More virtuous, most virtuous. More mindful, most mindful. More sagacious, most sagacious.

269, 401. Yavataṃ ta la ṇa dakārānaṃ byañjanāni ca la ña jakārattaṃ.

Transformation of the consonants t, l, ṇ, d, and of 'ya', into l, ñ, j.

Yakāravantānaṃ ta la ṇa dakārānaṃ byañjanāni ca la ña jakārattamāpajjante yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

When the letter 'ya' follows, the consonants t, l, ṇ, and d become l, ñ, and j respectively.

Bāhussaccaṃ, paṇḍiccaṃ, vepullaṃ, kāruññaṃ, kosallaṃ, nepuññaṃ, sāmaññaṃ, sohajjaṃ.

Great learning, wisdom, breadth, compassion, skill, cleverness, the state of a recluse, cordiality.

Ya va tamiti kimatthaṃ? Tiṇadalaṃ.

What is the purpose of [the reading] 'ya va taṃ'? A blade of grass.

Ta la ṇa dakārānamiti kimatthaṃ? Ālasyaṃ, ārogyaṃ.

What is the purpose of [the phrase] 'of t, l, ṇ, d'? Laziness, health.

Byañjanānamiti [M 0.0135] kimatthaṃ? Maccunā.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'consonants'? By death.

Kāraggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Yakārassa makārādesañāpanatthaṃ. Opammaṃ.

What is the purpose of using the term 'kāra'? For indicating the substitution of 'ma' for 'ya'. Example: Opammaṃ.

270, 120. Amha tumhanturāja brahmatta sakhasatthu pitādīhismā nāva.

After amha, tumha, stems ending in -antu, rājan, brahman, attan, sakhi, satthu, pitu, and so on, the suffix smā optionally becomes nā.

Amha tumhanturāja brahma atta sakha satthu pituiccevamādīhi smāvacanaṃ nāva daṭṭhabbaṃ.

After amha, tumha, stems ending in -antu, rājan, brahman, attan, sakhi, satthu, pitu, and so on, the suffix 'smā' should be understood to optionally become 'nā'.

Mayā, tayā, guṇavatā, raññā, brahmunā, attanā, sakhinā, satthārā, pitarā, mātarā, bhātarā, dhītarā, kattārā, vattārā.

By me, by you, by the virtuous one, by the king, by Brahmā, by oneself, by a friend, by the Teacher, by a father, by a mother, by a brother, by a daughter, by a maker, by a speaker.

Etehīti kimatthaṃ? Purisā.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'etehi' (after these)? Purisā.

Iti nāmakappe pañcamo kaṇḍo

Thus the fifth section in the Chapter on Nouns.

Nāmakappo niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Nouns is completed.

3. Kārakakappa

3. The Chapter on Case Syntax

Chaṭṭhakaṇḍa

The Sixth Section

271, 88, 308. Yasmā [M 0.0136] dapeti bhayamādatte vā tadapādānaṃ.

That from which one departs, from which there is fear, or from which one takes, is the ablative.

Yasmā vā apeti, yasmā vā bhayaṃ jāyate, yasmā vā ādatte, taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

That factor from which one departs, or from which fear arises, or from which one takes, is designated as the ablative.

Taṃ yathā? Gāmā apenti munayo, nagarā niggato rājā, corā bhayaṃ jāyate, ācariyupajjhāyehi sikkhaṃ gaṇhāti sisso.

For example: Sages depart from the village; the king has gone forth from the city; fear arises from thieves; a student receives instruction from teachers and preceptors.

Apādānamiccanena kvattho? Apādāne pañcamī.

What is the purpose of the term 'apādāna' (ablative)? The fifth case ending is used for the ablative.

272, 309. Dhātunā mānamupasaggayogādvīsvapi ca.

And also in connection with verbal roots, nouns, prefixes, and so on.

Dhātunāmānaṃ payoge ca upasaggayogādīsvapi ca taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

In the usage of verbal roots and nouns, and also in connection with prefixes and so on, that factor is designated as the ablative.

Dhātūnaṃ payoge tāva jiiccetassa dhātussa parāpubbassa payoge yo asaho, so apādānasañño hoti.

First, in the usage of verbal roots: when this verbal root 'ji' is used, preceded by 'parā', that which is unbearable is designated as the ablative.

Taṃ yathā? Buddhasmā parājenti aññatitthiyā.

For example: Other sectarians are defeated by the Buddha.

Bhūiccetassa [M 0.0137] dhātussa papubbassa payoge yato acchinnappabhavo, so apādānasañño hoti.

When this verbal root 'bhū' is used, preceded by 'pa', that from which there is an unbroken origin is designated as the ablative.

Taṃ yathā? Himavatā pabhavanti pañca mahānadiyo, anavatattamhā pabhavanti mahāsarā, aciravatiyā pabhavanti kunnadiyo.

For example: From the Himālaya originate the five great rivers; from Anavatatta originate the great lakes; from the Aciravatī originate the small rivers.

Nāmappayogepi taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

Even in the usage of a noun, that factor is designated as the ablative.

Taṃ yathā? Urasmā jāto putto, bhūmito niggato raso, ubhato sujāto putto mātito ca pitito ca.

For example: A son born from the breast, sap emerged from the earth, a son well-born from both – from his mother and from his father.

Upasaggayoge taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

In connection with a prefix, that factor is designated ablative.

Taṃ yathā? Apasālāya āyanti vāṇijā, ābrahmalokā saddo abbhuggacchati upari pabbatā devo vassati, buddhasmā pati sāriputto dhammadesanāya bhikkhū ālapati temāsaṃ, ghatamassa telasmā pati dadāti, uppalamassa padumasmā pati dadāti, kanakamassa hiraññasmā pati dadāti.

How so? Merchants come from the market hall; a sound rises up from the Brahma-world; a god rains from above the mountain; instead of the Buddha, Sāriputta addresses the monks for three months with a teaching of the Dhamma; he gives ghee in exchange for oil; he gives an uppala lotus in exchange for a paduma lotus; he gives gold in exchange for bullion.

Ādiggahaṇena kārakamajjhepi pañcamīvibhatti hoti. Ito pakkhasmā vijjhati migaṃ luddako, kosā vijjhati kuñjaraṃ, māsasmā bhuñjati bhojanaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ādi', the fifth case-ending also occurs even among factors. From this side, the hunter shoots the deer; from the quiver, he shoots the elephant; for a month, he eats the meal.

Apiggahaṇena nipātapayogepi pañcamīvibhatti hoti dutiyā ca tatiyā ca. Rahitā mātujā puññaṃ katvā [M 0.0138] dānaṃ deti, rahitā mātujaṃ, rahitā mātujena vā. Rite saddhammā kuto sukhaṃ labhati, rite saddhammaṃ, rite saddhammena vā. Te bhikkhū nānā kulā pabbajitā, vinā saddhammā natthañño koci nātho loke vijjati, vinā saddhammaṃ, vinā saddhammena vā. Vinā buddhasmā, vinā buddhaṃ, vinā buddhena vā.

By the inclusion of 'api', the fifth case-ending occurs even in the usage of particles, as well as the second and third cases. Without her mother, having performed merit, she gives a gift; or without her mother (acc.), or without her mother (inst.). Without the true Dhamma, whence can one obtain happiness? Or without the true Dhamma (acc.), or without the true Dhamma (inst.). Those monks have gone forth from various families. Without the true Dhamma, no other refuge is found in the world; or without the true Dhamma (acc.), or without the true Dhamma (inst.). Without the Buddha, without the Buddha (acc.), or without the Buddha (inst.).

Caggahaṇena aññatthāpi pañcamīvibhatti hoti. Yatohaṃ bhagini ariyāya jātiyā jāto. Yato sarāmi attānaṃ, yato pattosmi viññutaṃ, yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāsaveyyuṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the fifth case-ending also occurs elsewhere. Since, sister, I was born of a noble birth. Since I remember myself; since I have attained discernment. From which cause, while one dwells with this eye-faculty unrestrained, covetousness and dejection, evil, unwholesome states, might flow in.

273, 310. Rakkhaṇatthānamicchitaṃ.

273, 310. With verbs of protection, the object one wishes to separate.

Rakkhaṇatthānaṃ dhātūnaṃ payoge yaṃ icchitaṃ, taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

In the usage of verbal roots with the meaning of protection, that which one desires to ward off is designated as ablative.

Kāke rakkhanti taṇḍulā, yavā paṭisedhenti gāvo.

Rice is protected from crows; barley is kept away from cattle.

274, 311. Yena vā’ dassanaṃ.

274, 311. Or that from which disappearance is desired.

Yena vā adassanamicchitaṃ, taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

Or from whom disappearance is desired, that factor is designated as ablative.

Upajjhāyā antaradhāyati sisso, mātarā ca pitarā ca antaradhāyati putto.

The student hides from the preceptor; the son hides from his mother and from his father.

Vāti [M 0.0139] kimatthaṃ? Sattamīvibhatyattaṃ. Jetavane antaradhāyati bhagavā.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? For the locative case. The Blessed One disappears in Jetavana.

275, 312. Dūranti kaddha kāla nimmāna tvālopa disāyogavibhattārappayoga suddhappamocana hetu vivittappamāṇa pubbayogabandhana guṇavacana pañha kathana thokākattūsu ca.

275, 312. And in the sense of 'distance,' 'proximity,' 'measuring distance,' 'measuring time,' 'elision of -tvā,' 'direction,' 'separation,' 'abstaining,' 'purity,' 'release,' 'cause,' 'seclusion,' 'measure,' 'prior connection,' 'bondage,' 'expression of quality,' 'question,' 'statement,' 'a small amount,' and 'non-agent'.

Dūratthe, antikatthe, addhanimmāne, kālanimmāne, tvālope, disāyoge, vibhatte, ārappayoge, suddhe, pamocane, hetvatthe, vivittatthe, pamāṇe, pubbayoge, bandhanatthe, guṇavacane, pañhe, kathane, thoke, akattari ca iccetesvatthesu, payogesu ca, taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

In the sense of distance, in the sense of proximity, in measuring distance, in measuring time, in the elision of the -tvā suffix, in connection with direction, in separation, in connection with abstaining, in purity, in release, in the sense of cause, in the sense of seclusion, in measure, in prior connection, in the sense of bondage, in expressing quality, in questions, in statements, in a small amount, and in the non-agentive—in these senses and uses, that factor is designated as ablative.

Dūratthetāva – kīva dūro ito naḷakāragāmo, dūrato vā gamma, ārakā te moghapurisā imasmā dhammavinayā. Dutiyā ca tatiyā ca, dūraṃ gāmaṃ āvato, dūrena gāmena vā āgato. Ārakā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, anena dhammavinayena vā iccevamādi.

First, in the sense of distance—how far is the reed-worker’s village from here? Or, from afar having come... Those misguided men are far from this Dhamma and Discipline. And also the second and third cases: far to the village (acc.), or far by the village (inst.) having come. Far from this Dhamma and Discipline (acc.), or by this Dhamma and Discipline (inst.), and so on.

Antikatthe – antikaṃ gāmā, āsannaṃ gāmā, samīpaṃ gāmā, samīpaṃ saddhammā. Dutiyā ca tatiyā ca, antikaṃ gāmaṃ, antikaṃ gāmena vā. Āsannaṃ gāmaṃ, āsannaṃ gāmena vā. Samīpaṃ gāmaṃ. Samīpaṃ gāmena vā. Samīpaṃ saddhammaṃ, samīpaṃ saddhammena vā iccevamādi.

In the sense of proximity—near to the village, close to the village, adjacent to the village, near to the true Dhamma. And also the second and third cases: near to the village (acc.), or near by the village (inst.). Close to the village (acc.), or close by the village (inst.). Adjacent to the village (acc.), or adjacent by the village (inst.). Near to the true Dhamma (acc.), or near by the true Dhamma (inst.), and so on.

Addhanimmāne [M 0.0140] – ito mathurāya catūsu yojanesu saṅkassaṃ nāma nagaraṃ atthi, tattha bahū janā vasanti iccevamādi.

In measuring distance—from here, at four yojanas from Mathurā, there is a city named Saṅkassa, where many people live, and so on.

Kālanimmāne – ito bhikkhave ekanavutikappe vipassī nāma bhagavā loke udapādi, ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena parinibbāyissati iccevamādi.

In measuring time—Monks, ninety-one eons ago from now, the Blessed One named Vipassī arose in the world; from now, after three months have passed, he will attain final Nibbāna, and so on.

Tvālope kammādhikaraṇesu – pāsādā saṅkameyya, pāsādaṃ abhiruhitvā vā. Pabbatā saṅkameyya, pabbataṃ abhiruhitvā vā. Hatthikkhandhā saṅkameyya, hatthikkhandhaṃ abhiruhitvā vā. Āsanā vuṭṭhaheyya. Āsane nisīditvā vā iccevamādi.

In the elision of -tvā, in the sense of object and location—he might descend from the palace, or having ascended the palace. He might descend from the mountain, or having ascended the mountain. He might descend from the elephant’s back, or having mounted the elephant’s back. He might rise from his seat, or having sat on the seat, and so on.

Disāyoge – avicito yāva uparibhavaggamantare bahū sattanikāyā vasanti, yato khemaṃ tato bhayaṃ, puratthimato, dakkhiṇato, pacchimato, uttarato aggī pajjalanti, yato assosuṃ bhagavantaṃ, uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā iccevamādi.

In connection with direction—from Avīci up to the highest realm of existence, many groups of beings dwell; from where there is safety, from there is danger; from the east, from the south, from the west, from the north, fires blaze; from where they heard the Blessed One; upwards from the soles of the feet, downwards from the crown of the head, and so on.

Vibhatte – yato paṇītataro vā visiṭṭhataro vā natthi. Chaṭṭhī ca, channavutīnaṃ pāsaṇḍānaṃ, dhammānaṃ pavaraṃ yadidaṃ sugatavinayo iccevamādi.

In separation—than which there is nothing more excellent or more distinguished. And also the sixth case: of the ninety-six sects, the foremost of teachings is this, the Well-farer's Discipline, and so on.

Ārappayoge – [M 0.0141] gāmadhammā vasaladhammā asaddhammā ārati virati paṭivirati, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī iccevamādi.

In connection with abstaining—abstinence, refraining, and ceasing from village practices, from base practices, and from false doctrines; abstaining from the destruction of life, and so on.

Suddhe – lobhaniyehi dhammehi suddho asaṃsaṭṭho, mātito ca pitito ca suddho asaṃsaṭṭho anupakuddho agarahito iccevamādi.

In purity—pure and unmixed with enticing states; pure in lineage from his mother's and father's side, unreproached, uncensured, and so on.

Pamocane – parimutto dukkhasmāti vadāmi, muttosmi mārabandhanā, na te muccanti maccunā iccevamādi.

In release—'He is fully freed from suffering,' I declare; 'I am freed from Māra’s bond'; 'they are not freed from death,' and so on.

Hetvatthe – kasmā hetunā, kena hetunā, kissa hetunā, kasmā nu tumhaṃ daharā na mīyare, kasmā idheva maraṇaṃ bhavissati iccevamādi.

In the sense of cause—for what reason? By what cause? For what purpose? Why, indeed, do your young ones not die? Why will death occur right here?—and so on.

Vivittatthe – vivitto pāpakā dhammā, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi iccevamādi.

In the sense of seclusion—secluded from evil states; secluded indeed from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, and so on.

Pamāṇe – dīghaso navavidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā pamāṇikā kāretabbā, majjhimassa purisassa aḍḍha teḷasahatthā iccevamādi.

In measure—nine spans in length are to be made, standard by the Sugata's span; for a man of medium height, thirteen and a half hands, and so on.

Pubbayoge – pubbeva sammodhā iccevamādi.

In prior connection—before the greeting, and so on.

Bandhanatthe – satasmā bandho naro. Tatiyā ca, satena bandho naro raññā iṇatthena iccevamādi.

In the sense of bondage—a person is bound for a hundred. And also the third case: a person is bound by a hundred by the king on account of debt, and so on.

Guṇavacane [M 0.0142] – puññāya sugatiṃ yanti, cāgāya vipulaṃ dhanaṃ, paññāya vimuttimano, issariyāya janaṃ rakkhati rājā iccevamādi.

In expressing quality—through merit, they go to a good destination; through generosity, abundant wealth is obtained; through wisdom, the mind is freed; through sovereignty, the king protects the people, and so on.

Pañhe tvālope kammādhikaraṇesu – abhidhammā pucchanti, abhidhammaṃ sutvā, abhidhamme ṭhatvā vā. Vinayā pucchanti, vinayaṃ sutvā, vinaye ṭhatvā vā. Dutiyā ca tatiyā ca, abhidhammaṃ, abhidhammena vā. Vinayaṃ, vinayena vā. Eva suttā, geyyā, gāthāya, veyyākaraṇā, udānā, itivuttakā, jātakā, abbhutadhammā, vedallā iccevamādi.

In questions, and with elision in matters of action – they ask from the Abhidhamma, having heard the Abhidhamma, or standing firm in the Abhidhamma. They ask from the Vinaya, having heard the Vinaya, or standing firm in the Vinaya. And in the second and third cases, the Abhidhamma, or by means of the Abhidhamma; the Vinaya, or by means of the Vinaya. Likewise, the Suttas, mixed prose and verse, verses, expositions, inspired utterances, thus-saids, birth stories, marvelous events, and catechisms, and so forth.

Kathane tvālope kammādhikaraṇesu – abhidhammā kathayanti, abhidhammaṃ sutvā, abhidhamme ṭhatvā vā. Vinayā kathayanti, vinayaṃ sutvā, vinaye ṭhatvā vā. Dutiyā ca tatiyā ca, abhidhammaṃ, abhidhammena vā. Vinayaṃ vinayena vā. Evaṃ suttā, geyyā, gāthāya, veyyākaraṇā, udānā, itivuttakā, jātakā, abbhutadhammā, vedallā iccevamādi.

In speaking, and with elision in matters of action – they speak from the Abhidhamma, having heard the Abhidhamma, or standing firm in the Abhidhamma. They speak from the Vinaya, having heard the Vinaya, or standing firm in the Vinaya. And in the second and third cases, the Abhidhamma, or by means of the Abhidhamma; the Vinaya, or by means of the Vinaya. Likewise, the Suttas, mixed prose and verse, verses, expositions, inspired utterances, thus-saids, birth stories, marvelous events, and catechisms, and so forth.

Thoke – thokā muccanti. Appamattakā muccanti, kicchā muccanti. Tatiyā ca. Thokena, appamattakena, kicchena vā iccevamādi.

In the sense of 'a little' – they are freed from a little; they are freed from a small amount; they are freed from difficulty. And in the third case: by a little, by a small measure, or with difficulty, and so forth.

Akattarica – kammassa katattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti iccevamādi.

And in the sense of non-agent: due to the deed having been done, accumulated, increased, and become abundant, eye-consciousness arises, and so forth.

Caggahaṇena [M 0.0143] sesesupi ye mayā nopadiṭṭhā apādānapayogikā, te payogavicakkhaṇehi yathāyogaṃ yojetabbā.

By the inclusion of 'ca,' even in the remaining cases not shown by me, those suitable for the ablative case should be applied by those skilled in usage according to what is appropriate.

276, 302. Yassa dātukāmo rocate dhārayate vā taṃ sampadānaṃ.

276, 302. That to whom one wishes to give, or to whom it is pleasing, or to whom one owes, that is the sampadāna.

Yassa vā dātukāmo yassa vārocate, yassa vā dhārayate, taṃ kārakaṃ sampadānasaññaṃ hoti.

To whom one wishes to give, or to whom it is pleasing, or to whom one owes, that factor is designated as sampadāna.

Samaṇassa cīvaraṃ dadāti, samaṇassa rocate saccaṃ, devadattassa suvaṇṇacchattaṃ dhārayate yaññadatto.

He gives a robe to the ascetic. The truth pleases the ascetic. Yaññadatta owes a golden parasol to Devadatta.

Sampadānamiccanena kvattho? Sampadāne catutthī.

What is the purpose of the term 'sampadāna'? The fourth case is used for the sampadāna.

Vāti vikappanatthaṃ, dhātunāmānaṃ payoge vā upasaggappayoge vā nipātappayoge vā sati atthavikappanatthaṃ vāti padaṃ payujjati.

The word 'vā' is for the purpose of indicating an alternative; whether in the use of verbal roots or nouns, or in the use of prefixes, or in the use of particles, the word 'vā' is employed for the purpose of indicating an alternative meaning.

277, 303. Silāgha hanu ṭhā sapa dhāra piha kudha duhissosūya rādhikkha paccāsuṇa anupatigiṇa pubbakattārocanattha tadattha tumatthālamattha maññānādarappāṇini, gatyatthakammani, āsīsattha sammuti bhiyya sattamyatthesu ca.

277, 303. With the roots silāgha, hanu, ṭhā, sapa, dhāra, piha, kudha, duha, issa, usūya, rādha, ikkha, paccāsuṇa, anupatigiṇa; in the prior agent; in the sense of declaring; for that purpose; in the sense of the infinitive of purpose and 'enough'; in the sense of 'thinking' with disregard for inanimate things; in the object of verbs of motion; and in the senses of blessing, convention, abundance, and the locative.

Silāgha hanu ṭhā sapa dhāra piha kudha duha issaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ payoge, usūyatthānañca payoge, rādhikkhappayoge, paccāsuṇaanupatigiṇānaṃ pubbakattari, ārocanatthe[M 0.0144], tadatthe, tumatthe, alamatthe, maññatippayoge anādare appāṇini, gatyatthānaṃ dhātūnaṃ kammani, āsīsatthe ca sammuti bhiyya sattamyatthesu ca, taṃ kārakaṃ sampadānasaññaṃ hoti.

When the roots silāgha, hanu, ṭhā, sapa, dhāra, piha, kudha, duha, and issa are employed, and in the use of those with the meaning of usūya, and in the use of rādha and ikkha, and with the prior agent of paccāsuṇa and anupatigiṇa, and in the sense of declaring, and for the purpose of that, and in the sense of the infinitive of purpose, and in the sense of sufficiency, and in the use of maññati with disregard for inanimate things, and with the object of verbs of motion, and in the senses of blessing, convention, abundance, and the locative, then that factor is designated as sampadāna.

Silāghappayoge tāva – buddhassa silāghate, dhammassa silāghate, saṅghassa silāghate, sakaṃupajjhāyassa silāghate, tava silāghate mama silāghate iccevamādi.

First, in the use of silāgha – he praises the Buddha, he praises the Dhamma, he praises the Saṅgha, he praises his own preceptor, he praises you, he praises me, and so forth.

Hanuppayoge – hanute tuyhameva, hanute mayhameva iccevamādi.

In the use of hanu – he conceals from you alone, he conceals from me alone, and so forth.

Ṭhāpayoge – upatiṭṭheyya sakyaputtānaṃ vaḍḍhakī, bhikkhussa bhuñjantassa pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭheyya bhikkhunī iccevamādi.

In the use of ṭhā – a carpenter should attend upon the Sakyan sons; a nun should attend upon a bhikkhu who is eating, with water or a fan, and so forth.

Sapappayoge – tuyhaṃ sapate, mayhaṃ sapate iccevamādi.

In the use of sapa – he curses you, he curses me, and so forth.

Dhārappayoge – suvaṇṇaṃ te dhārayate iccevamādi.

In the use of dhāra – he owes gold to you, and so forth.

Pihappayoge – buddhassa aññatitthiyā pihayanti, devā dassanakāmā te, yato icchāmi bhaddantassa, samiddhānaṃ pihayanti daliddā iccevamādi.

In the use of piha – followers of other sects envy the Buddha; the devas are desirous of seeing you; since I desire for the venerable one; the poor envy the prosperous, and so forth.

Kudhaduhaissausūyappayoge – kodhayati deva dattassa, tassa kujjha mahāvīra, mā raṭṭhaṃ vinassa idaṃ. Duhayati [M 0.0145] disānaṃ megho, titthiyā samaṇānaṃ issayanti guṇagiddhena, titthiyā samaṇānaṃ issayanti lābhagiddhena, dujjanā guṇavantānaṃ usūyanti guṇagiddhena, kā usūyā vijānataṃ iccevamādi.

In the use of kudha, duha, issa, and usūya – he is angry with Devadatta; great hero, be angry at him, lest this kingdom perish. The cloud is hostile to the regions; followers of other sects envy the ascetics out of greed for virtues; followers of other sects envy the ascetics out of greed for gains; the wicked are jealous of the virtuous out of greed for virtues; what jealousy is there for the wise? and so forth.

Rādha ikkha iccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ payoge yassa akathitassa pucchanaṃ kammavikkhyāpanatthañca, taṃ kārakaṃ sampadānasaññaṃ hoti, dutiyā ca.

In the use of the roots rādha and ikkha, when there is questioning concerning someone unstated, and for the purpose of making an action known, that factor is designated as sampadāna, and also takes the second case (accusative).

Ārādhohaṃ rañño, ārādhohaṃ rājānaṃ, kyāhaṃ ayyānaṃ aparajjhāmi, kyāhaṃ ayye aparajjhāmi, cakkhuṃ janassa dassanāya taṃ viya maññe, āyasmato upālittherassa upasampadāpekkho upatisso, āyasmantaṃ vā iccevamādi.

I have pleased the king; I have pleased the king; how do I offend the noble ones? How do I offend the noble ones? I think it is like an eye for the seeing of people. Upatissa, seeking ordination from the Venerable Upāli Thera, or from the Venerable One, and so forth.

Paccāsuṇa anupatigiṇānaṃ pubbakattari suṇotissa paccāyoge yassa kammuno pubbassa yo kattā, so sampadānasañño hoti.

With `paccāsuṇa` and `anupatigiṇa` in relation to the prior agent: in the responsive use of `suṇoti`, the agent of the prior action is designated as sampadāna.

Taṃ yathā? Bhagavā bhikkhū etadavoca.

How so? The Blessed One said this to the bhikkhus.

Bhikkhūti akathīta kammaṃ, etanti kathitakammaṃ. Yassa kammuno pubbassa yo kattā, so‘bhagavā’ti “yo karoti sa kattā”ti suttavacanena kattusañño. Evaṃ yassa [M 0.0146] kammuno pubbassa yo kattā, so sampadānasañño hoti.

'Bhikkhus' is the secondary object, 'this' is the primary object. The agent of the prior action, 'the Blessed One,' is designated as the agent by the Sutta statement 'He who does, he is the agent.' Thus, the agent of the prior action is designated as sampadāna.

Taṃ yathā? Te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ, āsuṇanti buddhassa bhikkhū.

How so? Those bhikkhus responded to the Blessed One; the bhikkhus listen to the Buddha.

Giṇassa anupatiyoge yassa kammuno pubbassa yo kattā, so sampadānasañño hoti.

In the responsive use of giṇa, the agent of the prior action is designated as sampadāna.

Taṃ yathā? Bhikkhu janaṃ dhammaṃ sāveti, tassa bhikkhuno jano anugiṇāti, tassa bhikkhuno jano patigiṇāti.

How so? A bhikkhu teaches the Dhamma to people; the people assent to that bhikkhu; the people accept from that bhikkhu.

Yo vadeti sa‘kattā’ti,

Vuttaṃ ‘kamma’nti vuccati;

Yo paṭiggāhako tassa,

‘Sampadānaṃ’ vijāniyā.

He who speaks is 'the agent'; what is spoken is called 'the object'; he who is the receiver of that, should be known as 'the sampadāna'.

Iccevamādi.

And so forth.

Ārocanatthe – ārocayāmi vo bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo bhikkhave, paṭivedayāmi vo bhikkhave, ārocayāmi te mahārāja, āmantayāmi te mahārāja, paṭivedayāmi te mahārāja iccevamādi.

In the sense of declaration – I declare to you, bhikkhus; I address you, bhikkhus; I inform you, bhikkhus; I declare to you, great king; I address you, great king; I inform you, great king, and so forth.

Tadatthe – ūnassa pāripūriyā taṃ cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Buddhassa atthāya, dhammassa atthāya, saṅghassa atthāya, jīvitaṃ pariccajāmi iccevamādi.

In the sense of 'for that purpose' – that robe should be set aside for the completion of what is lacking. For the sake of the Buddha, for the sake of the Dhamma, for the sake of the Saṅgha, I relinquish my life, and so on.

Tumatthe [M 0.0147] -lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ buddho loke uppajjati. Bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya vinayo paññatto iccevamādi.

In the sense of 'for the sake of' – the Buddha arises in the world out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of devas and humans. For the comfortable dwelling of the bhikkhus, the Vinaya has been laid down, and so on.

Alamatthappayoge-alamiti arahati paṭikkhittesu. Alaṃ me buddho, alaṃ me rajjaṃ, alaṃ bhikkhu pattassa, alaṃ mallo mallassa, arahati mallo mallassa. Paṭikkhitte alaṃ te rūpaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, alaṃ me hiraññasuvaṇṇena iccevamādi.

In the use of 'alaṃ' – 'alaṃ' is used in the sense of 'is able' and 'is refused.' The Buddha is sufficient for me; kingship is sufficient for me; a bowl is sufficient for a bhikkhu; one wrestler is a match for another wrestler; one wrestler is worthy of another wrestler. In the sense of refusal: Enough of your making this form! Enough of gold and silver for me! and so on.

Maññatippayoge anādare appāṇini-kaṭṭhassa tuvaṃ maññe, kaliṅgarassa tuvaṃ maññe.

In the use of maññati with disregard for inanimate things – I consider you as wood; I consider you as a Kaliṅga log.

Anādareti kimatthaṃ? Suvaṇṇaṃ viya taṃ maññe.

Why 'with disregard'? I consider it as gold.

Appāṇinīti kimatthaṃ? Gadrabhaṃ tuvaṃ maññe iccevamādi.

Why 'inanimate'? I consider you a donkey, and so on.

Gatyatthakammani-gāmassa pādena gato, nagarassa pādena gato, appo saggāya gacchati, saggassa gamanena vā, mūlāya paṭikasseyya saṅgho. Dutiyā ca, gāmaṃ pādena gato, nagaraṃ pādena gato, appo saggaṃ gacchati, saggaṃ gamanena vā, mūlaṃ paṭikasseyya saṅgho iccevamādi.

In the object of verbs of motion – he went to the village by foot; he went to the city by foot; few go to heaven; or by going to heaven; the Saṅgha should be drawn back to the root.
