Sarīre sannidhānā vedanā sārīrikā, sarīre sannidhānā vā, evaṃ mānasikā.

A feeling present in the body is a bodily feeling (sārīrikā); or, a feeling present in the body. Similarly, a mental feeling (mānasikā).

Dvāre niyutto dovāriko, dvāre niyutto vā. Evaṃ bhaṇḍāgāriko, nāgariko, nāvakammiko.

One appointed at the gate is a gatekeeper (dovāriko); or, one appointed at the gate. Similarly, a treasurer (bhaṇḍāgāriko), a townsman (nāgariko), and a supervisor of new works (nāvakammiko).

Vīṇā assa sippaṃ veṇiko, vīṇā assa sippaṃ vā. Evaṃ pāṇaviko, modiṅgiko, vaṃsiko.

The lute is his craft, hence he is a lutenist (veṇiko); or, the lute is his craft. Similarly, a drummer (pāṇaviko), a taborer (modiṅgiko), and a flutist (vaṃsiko).

Gandho assa bhaṇḍaṃ gandhiko, gandho assa bhaṇḍaṃ vā. Evaṃ teliko, goḷiko.

Perfume is his merchandise, hence he is a perfumer (gandhiko); or, perfume is his merchandise. Similarly, an oil-merchant (teliko) and a seller of sweets (goḷiko).

Urabbhaṃ hantvā jīvatīti orabbhiko, urabbhaṃ hantvā jīvati vā. Magaṃ hantvā jīvatīti māgaviko, magaṃ hantvā jīvati vā. Evaṃ sokariko, sākuṇiko.

He lives by killing sheep, hence he is a sheep-butcher (orabbhiko); or, he lives by killing sheep. He lives by killing deer, hence he is a deer-hunter (māgaviko); or, he lives by killing deer. Similarly, a pig-butcher (sokariko) and a fowler (sākuṇiko).

Ādiggahaṇena aññatthāpi ṇika paccayo yojetabbo. Jālena hato jāliko, jālena hato vā.

By the inclusion of 'ādi', the suffix ṇika should be applied in other senses as well. He who kills with a net is a net-hunter (jāliko); or, he who kills with a net.

Suttena bandho suttiko, suttena bandho vā.

He who binds with thread is a thread-worker (suttiko); or, he who binds with thread.

Cāpo [M 0.0189] assa āvudho cāpiko, cāpo assa āvudho vā. Evaṃ tomariko, muggariko, mosaliko.

A bow is his weapon, hence he is an archer (cāpiko); or, a bow is his weapon. Similarly, a spearman (tomariko), a clubman (muggariko), and a pestleman (mosaliko).

Vāto assa ābādho vātiko, vāto assa ābādho vā. Evaṃ semhiko, pittiko.

Wind is his ailment, hence he is one afflicted by wind (vātiko); or, wind is his ailment. Similarly, one afflicted by phlegm (semhiko), and one afflicted by bile (pittiko).

Buddhe pasanno buddhiko, buddhe pasanno vā. Evaṃ dhammiko, saṅghiko.

One who has faith in the Buddha is a Buddhika; or, one who has faith in the Buddha. Similarly, a Dhammika and a Saṅghika.

Buddhassa santakaṃ buddhikaṃ, buddhassa santakaṃ vā. Evaṃ dhammikaṃ, saṅghikaṃ.

That which belongs to the Buddha is a possession of the Buddha (buddhikaṃ); or, that which belongs to the Buddha. Similarly, a possession of the Dhamma (dhammikaṃ), and a possession of the Saṅgha (saṅghikaṃ).

Vatthena kītaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ vatthikaṃ, vatthena kītaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ vā. Evaṃ kumbhikaṃ, phālikaṃ, kiṃ kaṇikaṃ, sovaṇṇikaṃ.

Goods bought with cloth are cloth-purchased goods (vatthikaṃ); or, goods bought with cloth. Similarly, pot-purchased goods (kumbhikaṃ), ploughshare-purchased goods (phālikaṃ), grain-purchased goods (kaṇikaṃ), and gold-purchased goods (sovaṇṇikaṃ).

Kumbho assa parimāṇaṃ kumbhikaṃ, kumbho assa parimāṇaṃ vā.

A pot is its measure, hence it is a pot-measure (kumbhikaṃ); or, a pot is its measure.

Kumbhassa rāsi kumbhikaṃ, kumbhassa rāsi vā.

A heap of pots is a pot-heap (kumbhikaṃ); or, a heap of pots.

Kumbhaṃ arahatīti kumbhiko, kumbhaṃ arahati vā.

He is worthy of a pot, hence he is a Kumbhika; or, he is worthy of a pot.

Akkhena dibbatīti akkhiko, akkhena dibbati vā. Evaṃ sālākiko, tindukiko, ambaphaliko. Kapiṭṭhaphaliko, nāḷikeriko iccevamādi.

He plays with dice, hence he is a dice-player (akkhiko); or, he plays with dice. Similarly, one who plays with sticks (sālākiko), with tinduka fruits (tindukiko), with mango fruits (ambaphaliko), with wood-apple fruits (kapiṭṭhaphaliko), with coconuts (nāḷikeriko), and so forth.

352, 376. Ṇa rāgā tasse damaññatthesu ca.

352, 376. The suffix ṇa is used after words for color, and in the sense of 'this is its...' and in other senses.

Ṇapaccayo hoti vā rāgamhā “tena rattaṃ” iccetasmiṃ atthe, “tassedaṃ” aññatthesu ca.

The suffix ṇa optionally occurs after words for color in the sense of 'dyed by that,' and in the sense of 'this is its...' among other senses.

Kasāvena [M 0.0190] rattaṃ vatthaṃ kāsāvaṃ, kasāvena rattaṃ vatthaṃ vā. Evaṃ kosumbhaṃ, hāliddaṃ, pāṭaṅgaṃ, rattaṅga, mañjiṭṭhaṃ, kuṅkumaṃ.

Cloth dyed with an astringent decoction is kasāva-dyed cloth (kāsāvaṃ); or, cloth dyed with an astringent decoction. Similarly, safflower-dyed (kosumbhaṃ), turmeric-dyed (hāliddaṃ), sappanwood-dyed (pāṭaṅgaṃ), red-dyed (rattaṅgaṃ), madder-dyed (mañjiṭṭhaṃ), and saffron-dyed (kuṅkumaṃ).

Sūkarassa idaṃ maṃsaṃ sokaraṃ, sūkarassa idaṃ maṃsaṃ vā. Evaṃ māhisaṃ.

This meat of a pig is pork (sokaraṃ); or, this meat of a pig. Similarly, buffalo meat (māhisaṃ).

Udumbarassa avidūre pavattaṃ vimānaṃ odumbaraṃ, udumbarassa avidūre pavattaṃ vimānaṃ vā.

A mansion situated not far from an udumbara tree is an odumbara mansion; or, a mansion situated not far from an udumbara tree.

Vidisāya avidūre nivāso vediso, vidisāya avidūre nivāso vā.

A resident not far from Vidisā is a Vedisa resident; or, a resident not far from Vidisā.

Mathurāya jāto māthuro, mathurāya jāto vā.

Born in Mathurā, he is a native of Mathurā (māthuro); or, one born in Mathurā.

Mathurāya āgato māthuro, mathurāya āgato vā.

Arrived from Mathurā, he is one from Mathurā (māthuro); or, one who arrived from Mathurā.

Kattikāya niyutto māso kattiko, kattikāya niyutto māso vā. Evaṃ māgasiro, phusso, māgho, phagguno, citto, vesākho, jeṭṭho, āsaḷho, sāvaṇo, bhaddo, assayujo.

The month connected with the Kattikā constellation is the month of Kattika (kattiko); or, the month connected with the Kattikā constellation. Similarly, Māgasira (māgasiro), Phussa (phusso), Māgha (māgho), Phagguna (phagguno), Citta (citto), Vesākha (vesākho), Jeṭṭha (jeṭṭho), Āsāḷha (āsaḷho), Sāvaṇa (sāvaṇo), Bhadda (bhaddo), and Assayuja (assayujo).

Na vuddhi nīlapītādo, paccaye saṇakārake.

There is no vuddhi gradation for nīla, pīta, and so forth, when a suffix marked with ṇ is the cause.

Phakāro phussasaddassa, “siro”ti sirasaṃ vade.

The letter 'pha' is for the word 'phussa'; one should say 'siro' for 'sirasaṃ'.

Sikkhānaṃ [M 0.0191] samūho sikkho, bhikkhānaṃ samūho bhikkho. Evaṃ kāpoto, māyūro, kokilo.

A group of trainees is sikkho; a group of monks is bhikkho. Similarly, kāpoto is a group of pigeons, māyūro is a group of peacocks, and kokilo is a group of cuckoos.

Buddhe, assa devatā buddho. Evaṃ bhaddo, māro, māhindo, vessavaṇo, yāmo, somo, nārāyaṇo.

The Buddha is his deity, hence he is a Buddha-devotee (buddho). Similarly, one whose deity is Bhadda (bhaddo), Māra (māro), Mahinda (māhindo), Vessavaṇa (vessavaṇo), Yāma (yāmo), Soma (somo), or Nārāyaṇa (nārāyaṇo).

Saṃvaccharamadhīte saṃvaccharo. Evaṃ mohutto, nemitto, aṅgavijjo, veyyākaraṇo, chando, bhāsso, cando.

One who studies for a year is a year-student (saṃvaccharo). Similarly, an astrologer (mohutto), an omen-reader (nemitto), a physiognomist (aṅgavijjo), a grammarian (veyyākaraṇo), a prosodist (chando), one who studies the sun (bhāsso), and one who studies the moon (cando).

Vasādānaṃ visayo deso vāsādo. Evaṃ kumbho, sākunto, ātisāro.

A region that is a sphere of dwelling is a dwelling place (vāsādo). Similarly, a pot (kumbho), a bird-catcher (sākunto), and dysentery (ātisāro).

Udumbarā asmiṃ padese santīti odumbaro. Sāgarehi nibbatto sāgaro. Sāgalamassa nivāso sāgalo. Mathurā assa nivāso māthuro. Mathurāya issaro māthuro. Iccevamādayo yojetabbā.

Udumbara trees exist in this region, hence it is an udumbara region (odumbaro). Born from the ocean is oceanic (sāgaro). Sāgala is his dwelling, hence he is a resident of Sāgala (sāgalo). Mathurā is his dwelling, hence he is a resident of Mathurā (māthuro). The lord of Mathurā is māthuro. In this way, these and similar examples should be applied.

353, 378. Jātādīnamimiyā ca.

353, 378. And the suffixes 'ima' and 'iya' after 'jāta' and so forth.

Jātaiccevamādīnamatthe imaiyapaccayā honti.

The suffixes 'ima' and 'iya' occur in the meanings of 'born' and so forth.

Pacchā jāto pacchimo. Evaṃ antimo, majjhimo, purimo, uparimo, heṭṭhimo, gopphimo. Bodhisattajātiyā jāto bodhisattajātiyo, evaṃ [M 0.0192] assajātiyo, hatthijātiyo, manussajātiyo.

Born afterward is the last (pacchimo). Similarly, the final (antimo), the middle (majjhimo), the former (purimo), the upper (uparimo), the lower (heṭṭhimo), and that which is at the ankle (gopphimo). Born of the Bodhisatta species is one of the Bodhisatta species (bodhisattajātiyo); similarly, of the horse species (assajātiyo), of the elephant species (hatthijātiyo), and of the human species (manussajātiyo).

Ādiggahaṇena niyuttatthāditopi tadassatthāditopi ima iya ika iccete paccayā honti. Anto niyutto antimo. Evaṃ antiyo, antiko.

By the inclusion of 'ādi' (and so forth), the suffixes 'ima', 'iya', and 'ika' also occur in the meaning of 'appointed' and so forth, and in the meaning of 'that exists in him' and so forth. Appointed within is the innermost (antimo). Similarly, antiyo and antiko.

Putto assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti puttimo. Evaṃ puttiyeva, puttiko, kappimo, kappiyo, kappiko.

He has a son, or it exists in him, hence he is one who has a son (puttimo). Similarly, one who has a son (puttiyo), one who has a son (puttiko), that which is proper (kappimo), that which is proper (kappiyo), and that which is proper (kappiko).

Caggahaṇena kiyapaccayo hoti niyuttatthe. Jātiyaṃ niyutto jātikiyo, andhe niyutto andhakiyo, jātiyā andho jaccandho, jaccandhe niyutto jaccandhakiyo.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the suffix 'kiya' occurs in the meaning of 'appointed'. Appointed to birth is jātikiyo; appointed to blindness is andhakiyo; blind by birth is congenitally blind (jaccandho); appointed to congenital blindness is jaccandhakiyo.

354, 379. Samūhatthe kaṇa ṇā.

354, 379. The suffixes 'kaṇa' and 'ṇa' in the collective sense.

Samūhatthe kaṇa ṇaiccete paccayā honti.

The suffixes 'kaṇa' and 'ṇa' occur in the collective sense.

Rājaputtānaṃ samūho rājaputtako. Evaṃ rājaputto, mānussako, mānusso, māyūrako, māyūro, māhiṃsako, māhiṃso.

A group of princes is rājaputtako. Similarly, rājaputto (a group of princes), mānussako (a group of humans), mānusso (a group of humans), māyūrako (a group of peacocks), māyūro (a group of peacocks), māhiṃsako (a group of buffaloes), and māhiṃso (a group of buffaloes).

355, 380. Gāma jana bandhu sahāyādīhitā.

355, 380. The suffix 'tā' after 'gāma', 'jana', 'bandhu', 'sahāya', and so forth.

Gāma jana bandhu sahāyaiccevamādīhi tāpaccayo hoti samūhatthe.

The suffix 'tā' occurs in the collective sense after 'gāma', 'jana', 'bandhu', 'sahāya', and so forth.

Gāmānaṃ [M 0.0193] samūho gāmatā. Evaṃ janatā, bandhutā, sahāyatā, nagaratā.

A collection of villages is gāmatā. Similarly, janatā (a collectivity of people), bandhutā (a collectivity of relatives), sahāyatā (a collectivity of friends), and nagaratā (a collectivity of towns).

356, 381. Tadassa ṭhānamiyo ca.

356, 381. And the suffix 'iya' in the sense of 'that is its place'.

“Tadassa ṭhāna” miccetasmiṃ atthe iyapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'iya' occurs in the meaning 'that is its place'.

Madanassa ṭhānaṃ madaniyaṃ, bandhanassa ṭhānaṃ bandhaniyaṃ, mucchanassa ṭhānaṃ mucchaniyaṃ, evaṃ rajaniyaṃ, kamaniyaṃ, gamaniyaṃ, dussaniyaṃ, dassaniyaṃ.

The place of intoxication is madaniyaṃ; the place of bondage is bandhaniyaṃ; the place of delusion is mucchaniyaṃ. Similarly, rajaniyaṃ (a place of delight), kamaniyaṃ (a place of desire), gamaniyaṃ (a place of going), dussaniyaṃ (a place of corruption), and dassaniyaṃ (a place of sight).

357, 382. Upamatthāyitattaṃ.

357, 382. The suffix 'āyitatta' in the meaning of resemblance.

Upamatthe āyitattapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'āyitatta' occurs in the meaning of resemblance.

Dhūmo viya dissati aduṃ vanaṃ tadidaṃ dhūmāyitattaṃ, timiraṃ viya dissati aduṃ vanaṃ tadidaṃ timirāyitattaṃ.

That forest appears like smoke, hence it is in a smoky state (dhūmāyitattaṃ); that forest appears like darkness, hence it is in a darkened state (timirāyitattaṃ).

358, 383. Tannissitatthe lo.

358, 383. The suffix 'la' in the meaning of 'dependent on that'.

“Tannissitatthe, tadassa ṭhāna”miccetasmiṃ atthe ca lapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'la' occurs in the meaning 'dependent on that' and 'that is its place'.

Duṭṭhu [M 0.0194] nissitaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ, vedaṃ nissitaṃ vedallaṃ, duṭṭhu ṭhānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ, vedassa ṭhānaṃ vedallaṃ.

That which is dependent on wrong is coarse (duṭṭhullaṃ); that which is dependent on the Vedas is Vedalla (vedallaṃ). The place of wrong is coarse (duṭṭhullaṃ); the place of the Vedas is Vedalla (vedallaṃ).

359, 384. Ālu tabbahule.

359, 384. The suffix 'ālu' in the meaning of 'abundant with that'.

Ālupaccayo hoti tabbahulatthe.

The suffix 'ālu' occurs in the meaning of 'abundant with that'.

Abhijjhā assa pakati abhijjhālu, abhijjhā assa bahulā vā abhijjhālu. Evaṃ sītālu, dhajālu, dayālu.

Greed is his nature, hence he is greedy (abhijjhālu); or, greed is abundant in him, hence he is greedy (abhijjhālu). Similarly, one who is sensitive to cold (sītālu), one who is fond of banners (dhajālu), and one who is compassionate (dayālu).

360, 387. Ṇya tta tā bhāve tu.

360, 387. The suffixes ṇya, tta, and tā in the meaning of state.

Ṇyattatāiccete paccayā honti bhāvatthe.

The suffixes ṇya, tta, and tā occur in the meaning of state.

Alasassa bhāvo ālasyaṃ, arogassa bhāvo ārogyaṃ. Paṃsukūlikassa bhāvo paṃsukūlikattaṃ, anodarikassa bhāvo anodarikattaṃ. Saṅgaṇikārāmassa bhāvo saṅgaṇikārāmatā, niddārāmassa bhāvo niddārāmatā.

The state of a lazy one is laziness (ālasyaṃ); the state of a healthy one is health (ārogyaṃ). The state of a rag-robe wearer is rag-robedness (paṃsukūlikattaṃ); the state of one who eats sparingly is abstemiousness in eating (anodarikattaṃ). The state of one delighting in company is delight in company (saṅgaṇikārāmatā); the state of one delighting in sleep is delight in sleep (niddārāmatā).

Tuggahaṇena ttanapaccayo hoti. Puthujjanattanaṃ, vedanattanaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'tu', the suffix ttana occurs. For example, the state of an ordinary person (puthujjanattanaṃ), and the state of feeling (vedanattanaṃ).

361, 388. Ṇa [M 0.0195] visamādīhi.

361, 388. The suffix ṇa from visama and so forth.

Ṇapaccayo hoti visamādīhi “tassa bhāvo”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix ṇa occurs after visama and so forth in the meaning 'its state'.

Visamassa bhāvo vesamaṃ, sucissa bhāvo socaṃ.

The state of unevenness is unevenness (vesamaṃ); the state of purity is purity (socaṃ).

362, 389. Ramaṇīyādito kaṇa.

362, 389. The suffix kaṇa from ramaṇīya and so forth.

Ramaṇīyaiccevamādito kaṇa paccayo hoti “tassa bhāvo”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix kaṇa occurs after ramaṇīya and so forth in the meaning 'its state'.

Ramaṇīyassa bhāvo rāmaṇīyakaṃ, manuññassa bhāvo mānuññakaṃ.

The state of delightfulness is delightfulness (rāmaṇīyakaṃ); the state of pleasingness is pleasingness (mānuññakaṃ).

363, 390. Visese taratamisikiyiṭṭhā.

363, 390. The suffixes tara, tama, isika, iya, and iṭṭha in the meaning of distinction.

Visesatthe tara tama isika iya iṭṭhaiccete paccayā honti.

The suffixes tara, tama, isika, iya, and iṭṭha occur in the meaning of distinction.

Sabbe ime pāpā, ayamimesaṃ visesena pāpoti pāpataro. Evaṃ pāpatamo, pāpisiko, pāpiyo, pāpiṭṭho.

All these are evil; this one is especially evil among them, hence more evil (pāpataro). Similarly, most evil (pāpatamo), somewhat evil (pāpisiko), worse (pāpiyo), and the worst (pāpiṭṭho).

364, 398. Tadassatthīti vī ca.

364, 398. And the suffix vī in the meaning 'that exists in him'.

“Tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe vīpaccayo hoti.

The suffix vī occurs in the meaning 'that exists in him'.

Medhā [M 0.0196] yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatītimedhāvī. Evaṃ māyāvī.

Wisdom exists in him, or is found in him, hence he is wise (medhāvī). Similarly, one who possesses illusion (māyāvī).

Caggahaṇena sopaccayo hoti. Sumedhā yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti sumedhaso.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the suffix so occurs. Good wisdom exists in him, or is found in him, hence he is wise (sumedhaso).

365, 399. Tapādito sī.

365, 399. The suffix sī from tapa and so forth.

Tapādito sīpaccayo hoti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix sī occurs after tapa and so forth in the meaning 'that exists in him'.

Tapo yassa atthi tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti tapassī. Evaṃ yasassī, tejassī.

Austerity exists in him, or is found in him, hence he is austere (tapassī). Similarly, glorious (yasassī), and radiant (tejassī).

266, 400. Daṇḍādito ikaī.

366, 400. The suffixes ika and ī from daṇḍa and so forth.

Daṇḍādito ika īiccete paccayā honti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffixes ika and ī occur from daṇḍa and so on, in the sense of 'that possesses it'.

Daṇḍo yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti daṇḍiko, daṇḍī. Evaṃ māliko, mālī.

He who has a staff, or in whom a staff is found, is a staff-bearer (daṇḍiko) or a staff-possessor (daṇḍī). Similarly, a garland-bearer (māliko), or one who is garlanded (mālī).

367, 401. Madhvādito ro.

367, 401. The suffix ra from madhu and so on.

Madhuiccevamādito rapaccayo hoti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix ra occurs from madhu and so on, in the sense of 'that possesses it'.

Madhu [M 0.0197] yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti madhuro. Evaṃ kuñjaro, muggaro, mukharo, susiro, (sīsaro, sukaro, suṅkaro), subharo, suciro, ruciro.

He who has honey, or in whom honey is found, is honeyed (madhuro). Similarly, elephant (kuñjaro), mallet (muggaro), talkative (mukharo), hollow (susiro), (sīsaro, sukaro, suṅkaro), easily supported (subharo), long-lasting (suciro), bright (ruciro).

368, 402. Guṇādito vantu.

368, 402. The suffix vantu from guṇa and so on.

Guṇaiccevamādito vantupaccayo hoti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix vantu occurs from guṇa and so on, in the sense of 'that possesses it'.

Guṇo yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti guṇavā. Evaṃ yasavā, dhanavā, paññavā, balavā, bhagavā.

He who has virtue, or in whom virtue is found, is virtuous (guṇavā). Similarly, renowned (yasavā), wealthy (dhanavā), wise (paññavā), strong (balavā), the Blessed One (bhagavā).

369, 403. Satyādīhi mantu.

369, 403. The suffix mantu from sati and so on.

Satiiccevamādīhi mantupaccayohoti “tadassatthi” iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix 'mantu' occurs after 'sati' and so on, in the sense of 'that possesses it'.

Sati yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti satimā, evaṃ jutimā, rucimā, thutimā, dhitimā, matimā, bhāṇumā.

He who has mindfulness, or in whom mindfulness is found, is 'satimā' (mindful). Similarly, 'jutimā' (radiant), 'rucimā' (delightful), 'thutimā' (praiseworthy), 'dhitimā' (steadfast), 'matimā' (wise), 'bhāṇumā' (luminous).

370, 405. Saddhāditoṇa.

370, 405. After 'saddhā' and so on, the suffix 'ṇa' is used.

Saddhāiccevamādito ṇa paccayo hoti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe.

The suffix 'ṇa' occurs after 'saddhā' and so on, in the sense of 'that possesses it'.

Saddhā [M 0.0198] yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatībhi saddho, evaṃ pañño, amaccharo.

He who has faith, or in whom faith is found, is 'saddho' (faithful). Similarly, 'pañño' (wise), 'amaccharo' (without avarice).

371, 404. Āyussukārāsa mantumhi.

371, 404. The 'u' of 'āyu' becomes 'a' when the suffix 'mantu' is present.

Āyussa anto ukāro asādeso hotimantumhi paccaye pare.

The final 'u' of 'āyu' is substituted by 'a' when the suffix 'mantu' follows.

Āyu assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti āyasmā.

He who has life, or in whom life is found, is 'āyasmā' (venerable).

372, 385. Tappakativacane mayo.

372, 385. The suffix 'maya' is used in the sense of 'made of that' or 'its nature'.

Tappakativacanatthe mayapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'maya' occurs in the sense of 'made of that' or 'its nature'.

Suvaṇṇena pakataṃ kammaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ. Evaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ jatumayaṃ, rajatamayaṃ, iṭṭhakamayaṃ, ayomayaṃ, mattikā mayaṃ, dārumayaṃ, gomayaṃ.

A work made of gold is 'sovaṇṇamayaṃ' (golden). Similarly, 'rūpiyamayaṃ' (made of silver), 'jatumayaṃ' (made of lacquer), 'rajatamayaṃ' (made of silver), 'iṭṭhakamayaṃ' (made of bricks), 'ayomayaṃ' (made of iron), 'mattikāmayaṃ' (made of clay), 'dārumayaṃ' (made of wood), 'gomayaṃ' (made of cow dung).

373, 406. Saṅkhyāpūraṇe mo.

373, 406. The suffix 'ma' is used for completing a number (ordinal).

Saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe mapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'ma' occurs in the sense of completing a number (ordinal).

Pañcannaṃ pūraṇo pañcamo, evaṃ sattamo, aṭṭhamo, navamo, dasamo.

The one completing five is 'pañcamo' (the fifth). Similarly, 'sattamo' (the seventh), 'aṭṭhamo' (the eighth), 'navamo' (the ninth), 'dasamo' (the tenth).

374, 408. Sa [M 0.0199] chassavā.

374, 408. 'Sa' is optionally substituted for 'cha'.

Chassa sakārādeso hoti vā saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe.

The substitution of 'sa' for 'cha' occurs optionally in the sense of completing a number (ordinal).

Channaṃ pūraṇo saṭṭho, chaṭṭho vā.

The one completing six is 'saṭṭho' or, alternatively, 'chaṭṭho' (the sixth).

375, 412. Ekādito dasassī.

375, 412. After 'dasa' following 'eka' and so on, the suffix 'ī' is used.

Ekādito dasassa ante īpaccayo hoti vā saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe.

The suffix 'ī' occurs optionally at the end of 'dasa' when it follows 'eka' and so on, in the sense of completing a number (ordinal).

Eko ca dasa ca ekādasa, ekādasannaṃ pūraṇī ekādasī. Pañcaca dasa ca pañcadasa, pañcadasannaṃ pūraṇī pañcadasī. Cattāro ca dasa ca catuddasa, catuddasannaṃ pūraṇī cātuddasī.

One and ten are 'ekādasa' (eleven); the one completing eleven is 'ekādasī' (the eleventh). Five and ten are 'pañcadasa' (fifteen); the one completing fifteen is 'pañcadasī' (the fifteenth). Four and ten are 'catuddasa' (fourteen); the one completing fourteen is 'cātuddasī' (the fourteenth).

Pūraṇeti kimatthaṃ? Ekādasa, pañcadasa.

Why is it said 'in the sense of completing a number'? For 'ekādasa' (eleven), 'pañcadasa' (fifteen).

376, 257. Dase so niccañca.

376, 257. And 'sa' is always substituted when 'dasa' follows.

Dasasadde pare niccaṃ chassa so hoti.

When the word 'dasa' follows, 'sa' is always substituted for 'cha'.

Soḷasa.

'Soḷasa' (sixteen).

377, 0. Ante niggahitañca.

377, 0. And a niggahita at the end.

Tāsaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ ante niggahitāgamo hoti.

The augment of a niggahita occurs at the end of those numbers.

Pañcadasi, cātuddasi.

'Pañcadasi' (fifteenth), 'cātuddasi' (fourteenth).

378, 414. Ti [M 0.0200] ca.

378, 414. And 'ti'.

Tāsaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ ante tikārāgamo hoti. Vīsati, tiṃsati.

The augment of the syllable 'ti' occurs at the end of those numbers. For example: 'vīsati' (twenty), 'tiṃsati' (thirty).

379, 258. La darānaṃ.

379, 258. 'La' is substituted for 'da' and 'ra'.

Dakāra rakārānaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ lakārādeso hoti. Soḷasa, cattālīsaṃ.

The letter 'la' is substituted for the letters 'da' and 'ra' in numerals. Examples: soḷasa, cattālīsaṃ.

380, 255. Vīsati dasesu bā dvissa tu.

For 'dvi', 'bā' is the substitute before 'vīsati' and 'dasa'; and also 'tu'.

Vīsati dasaiccetesu dvissa bā hoti.

When 'vīsati' and 'dasa' follow, 'bā' is substituted for 'dvi'.

Bāvīsatindriyāni, bārasa manussā.

Bāvīsatindriyāni (twenty-two faculties), bārasa manussā (twelve humans).

Tuggahaṇena dvissa du di do ādesā ca honti. Durattaṃ, dirattaṃ, diguṇaṃ, dohaḷinī.

By the taking of 'tu' [in the rule], the substitutions 'du', 'di', and 'do' also occur for 'dvi'. Examples: durattaṃ, dirattaṃ, diguṇaṃ, dohaḷinī.

381, 254. Ekādito dassa ra saṅkhyāne.

For the 'da' [of dasa] preceded by 'eka' and so on, 'ra' is the substitute in a numeral.

Ekādito dasassa dakārassa rakāro hoti vā saṅkhyāne.

When preceded by 'eka' and so on, the letter 'da' of 'dasa' optionally becomes 'ra' in a numeral.

Ekārasa, ekādasa, bārasa, dvādasa.

Ekārasa (eleven), ekādasa (eleven), bārasa (twelve), dvādasa (twelve).

Saṅkhyāneti kimatthaṃ? Dvādasāyatanāni.

Why is it stated 'in a numeral'? For the case of: dvādasāyatanāni (the twelve sense-bases).

382, 259. Aṭṭhādito [M 0.0201] ca.

382, 259. And from 'aṭṭha' onwards.

Aṭṭhaiccevamādito ca dasasaddassa dakārassa rakārādeso hoti vā saṅkhyāne.

And when preceded by 'aṭṭha' and so on, the letter 'da' of 'dasa' is optionally substituted by 'ra' in a numeral.

Aṭṭhārasa, aṭṭhadasa.

Aṭṭhārasa (eighteen), aṭṭhadasa (eighteen).

Aṭṭhāditoti kimatthaṃ? Pañcadasa, soḷasa.

Why is it stated 'from aṭṭha onwards'? For the cases of: pañcadasa (fifteen), soḷasa (sixteen).

Saṅkhyāneti kimatthaṃ? Aṭṭhadasiko.

Why is it stated 'in a numeral'? For the case of: aṭṭhadasiko (eighteenfold).

383, 253. Dvekaṭṭhānamākāro vā.

For 'dvi', 'eka', and 'aṭṭha', 'ā' is an optional substitute.

Dvi eka aṭṭhaiccetesamanto ākāro hoti vā saṅkhyāne.

The final letter of 'dvi', 'eka', and 'aṭṭha' optionally becomes 'ā' in a numeral.

Dvādasa, ekādasa, aṭṭhārasa.

Dvādasa (twelve), ekādasa (eleven), aṭṭhārasa (eighteen).

Saṅkhyāneti kimatthaṃ? Dvidanto, ekadanto, ekacchanno, aṭṭhatthambho.

Why is it stated 'in a numeral'? For the cases of: dvidanto (two-tusked), ekadanto (one-tusked), ekacchanno (single-roofed), aṭṭhatthambho (eight-pillared).

384, 407. Catucchehī tha ṭhā.

After 'catu' and 'cha', the suffixes 'tha' and 'ṭha' are added.

Catu chaiccetehi tha ṭhaiccete paccayā honti saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe.

After 'catu' and 'cha', the suffixes 'tha' and 'ṭha' are added in the sense of completing a number (i.e., to form an ordinal).

Catuttho, chaṭṭho.

Catuttho (fourth), chaṭṭho (sixth).

385, 409. Dvitīhi [M 0.0202] tiyo.

After 'dvi' and 'ti', the suffix 'tiya' is added.

Dvi tiiccetehi tiyapaccayo hoti saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe.

After 'dvi' and 'ti', the suffix 'tiya' is added in the sense of completing a number (i.e., to form an ordinal).

Dutiyo, tatiyo.

Dutiyo (second), tatiyo (third).

386, 410. Tiye dutāpi ca.

When 'tiya' follows, 'du' and 'ta' are also the substitutes.

Dvi tiiccetesaṃ du taiccete ādesā honti tiyapaccaye pare.

For 'dvi' and 'ti', 'du' and 'ta' are the respective substitutes when the suffix 'tiya' follows.

Dutiyo, tatiyo.

Dutiyo (second), tatiyo (third).

Apiggahaṇena aññesupi dviiccetassa duādeso hoti. Durattaṃ.

By the taking of 'api' [in the rule], the substitution 'du' for 'dvi' also occurs in other cases. Example: durattaṃ (a period of two nights).

Caggahaṇena dviiccetassa dikāro hoti. Dirattaṃ, diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ pārupetvā.

By the taking of 'ca' [in the rule], 'di' is substituted for 'dvi'. Examples: dirattaṃ (a period of two nights); diguṇaṃ, as in diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ pārupetvā (having put on the twofold outer robe).

387, 411. Tesamaḍḍhūpapadena aḍḍhuḍḍha divaḍḍha diyaḍḍhaḍḍhatiyā.

For those [numerals], when preceded by 'aḍḍha', the resulting forms are aḍḍhuḍḍha, divaḍḍha, diyaḍḍha, and aḍḍhatiyā.

Tesaṃ [M 0.0203] catuttha dutiya tatiyānaṃ aḍḍhūpapadānaṃ aḍḍhaḍḍhudivaḍḍha diyaḍḍha aḍḍhatiyādesā honti, aḍḍhūpapadena sahanippajjante.

For the fourth, second, and third ordinals, when 'aḍḍha' is a prefix, the substitutions 'aḍḍhaḍḍhu', 'divaḍḍha', 'diyaḍḍha', and 'aḍḍhatiya' occur; they are formed together with the prefix 'aḍḍha'.

Aḍḍhena catuttho aḍḍhuḍḍho, aḍḍhena dutiyo divaḍḍho, aḍḍhena dutiyo diyaḍḍho, aḍḍhena tatiyo aḍḍhatiyo.

The fourth with a half is 'aḍḍhuḍḍho' (three and a half); the second with a half is 'divaḍḍho' (one and a half); the second with a half is 'diyaḍḍho' (one and a half); the third with a half is 'aḍḍhatiyo' (two and a half).

388, 68. Sarūpānamekasesvasakiṃ.

Of similar forms, a single remainder occurs, not once.

Sarūpānaṃ padabyañjanānaṃ ekaseso hoti asakiṃ. Puriso ca puriso ca purisā.

Of words and syllables of similar form, a single remainder occurs, not once. For example: 'Puriso ca puriso ca' (a man and a man) becomes 'purisā' (men).

Sarūpānamiti kimatthaṃ? Hatthī ca asso ca ratho ca pattiko ca hatthiassarathapattikā,

Why is it said 'of similar forms'? For example: 'Hatthī ca asso ca ratho ca pattiko ca' (an elephant and a horse and a chariot and a foot soldier) becomes 'hatthiassarathapattikā'.

Asakinti kimatthaṃ? Puriso.

Why is it said 'not once'? Because for a single instance, it is simply 'Puriso' (a man).

389, 413. Gaṇane dasassa dviticatupañcachasattaaṭṭhanavakānaṃ vī ti cattāra paññā cha sattāsanavā yosu, yonañcīsamāsaṃ ṭhi ri tī tuti.

In counting, for 'dasa' preceded by two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine, there are the respective substitutions 'vī', 'ti', 'cattāra', 'paññā', 'cha', 'satta', 'asa', and 'nava' when 'yo' follows; and for 'yo' there are also the substitutions 'īsaṃ', 'āsaṃ', 'ṭhi', 'ri', 'tī', and 'tuti'.

Gaṇane dasassa dvika tika catukka pañcaka chakka sattakaaṭṭhaka navakānaṃ sarūpānaṃ katekasesānaṃ yathāsaṅkhyaṃ vī ti cattāra paññā cha satta asa navaiccādesā honti asakiṃ yosu, yonañca īsaṃ āsaṃ ṭhi ri ti īti utiiccādesā honti. Pacchā puna nippajjante.

In counting, for 'dasa' when combined with the similar forms of the groups of two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine, which have been reduced to a single remainder, the substitutions 'vī', 'ti', 'cattāra', 'paññā', 'cha', 'satta', 'asa', and 'nava' respectively occur, not once, when 'yo' follows; and for 'yo', the substitutions 'īsaṃ', 'āsaṃ', 'ṭhi', 'ri', 'ti', 'īti', and 'uti' also occur. They are subsequently formed.

Vīsaṃ[M 0.0204], tiṃsaṃ, cattālīsaṃ, paññāsaṃ, saṭṭhi, sattari, sattati, asīti, navuti.

Vīsaṃ (twenty), tiṃsaṃ (thirty), cattālīsaṃ (forty), paññāsaṃ (fifty), saṭṭhi (sixty), sattari (seventy), sattati (seventy), asīti (eighty), navuti (ninety).

Asakinti kimatthaṃ? Dasa.

Why is it said 'not once'? Because for a single instance, it is 'dasa' (ten).

Gaṇaneti kimatthaṃ? Dasadasakā purisā.

Why is it said 'in counting'? For example, 'Dasadasakā purisā' (men in groups of ten).

390, 256. Catūpapadassa lopo tuttarapadādicassa cucopi navā.

Of the prefix 'catu', there is elision of 'tu'; and for the initial of the following word, 'cu' and 'co' are also optional substitutes.

Catūpapadassa gaṇane pariyāpannassa tukārassa lopo hoti, uttarapadādicakārassa cucopi ādesā honti navā.

In counting, for the prefix 'catu' that is included, the syllable 'tu' is elided; and for the initial syllable 'ca' of the following word, 'cu' and 'co' are optional substitutions.

Cuddasa, coddasa, catuddasa.

Cuddasa (fourteen), coddasa (fourteen), catuddasa (fourteen).

Apiggahaṇena anupapadassāpi padādicakārassa. Lopohoti navā, cassa cucopi honti. Tālīsaṃ, cattālīsaṃ, cuttālīsaṃ, cottālīsaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'api' in the rule, for the initial 'ca' of a word, even when not preceded by a prefix, elision optionally occurs, and 'cu' and 'co' also occur as substitutes for 'ca'. Examples: Tālīsaṃ (forty), cattālīsaṃ (forty), cuttālīsaṃ (forty), cottālīsaṃ (forty).

391, 423. Yadanupapannā nipātanā sijjhanti.

What is not otherwise derived is established by irregular formation (nipātana).

Ye saddā aniddiṭṭhalakkhaṇā, akkharapadabyañjanato, itthipumanapuṃsakaliṅgato[M 0.0205], nāmupasagganipātato, abyayībhāvasamāsataddhitākhyātato, gaṇanasaṅkhyākālakārakappayogasaññāto, sandhipakativuddhilopāgamavikāraviparitato, vibhattivibhajanato ca, te nipātanā sijjhanti.

Those words whose characteristics are not specified—with respect to letters, words, and syllables; feminine, masculine, and neuter genders; nouns, prefixes, and particles; indeclinable compounds, other compounds, derivatives, and verbs; counting, number, tense, syntactic role, voice, and technical terms; euphonic combination, natural form, vowel strengthening, elision, augmentation, alteration, and inversion; and with respect to case-inflections and their classification—these are established by irregular formation (nipātana).

392, 418. Dvādito ko’nekattheca.

From 'dvi' onwards, the suffix 'ka' is used, and also in the sense of 'many'.

Dviiccevamādito kapaccayo hoti anekatthe ca, nipātanā sijjhanti.

From 'dvi' and so on, the suffix 'ka' occurs, and also in the sense of 'many'; they are established by irregular formation.

Satassa dvikaṃ dvisataṃ, satassa tikaṃ tisataṃ, satassa catukkaṃ catusataṃ, satassa pañcakaṃ pañcasataṃ, satassa chakkaṃ chasataṃ, satassa sattakaṃ sattasataṃ, satassa aṭṭhakaṃ aṭṭhasataṃ, satassa navakaṃ navasataṃ, satassa dasakaṃ dasasataṃ, sahassaṃ hoti.

A group of two of a hundred is two hundred; a group of three of a hundred is three hundred; a group of four of a hundred is four hundred; a group of five of a hundred is five hundred; a group of six of a hundred is six hundred; a group of seven of a hundred is seven hundred; a group of eight of a hundred is eight hundred; a group of nine of a hundred is nine hundred; a group of ten of a hundred is ten hundred, which is a thousand.

393, 415. Dasadasakaṃ sataṃ dasakānaṃ sataṃ sahassañca yomhi.

A group of ten tens is a hundred, and a hundred groups of ten is a thousand, when 'yo' is present.

Gaṇane pariyāpannassa dasadasakassa sataṃ hoti, satadasakassa sahassaṃ hoti yomhi pare.

In counting, for a group of ten tens that is included, it becomes a hundred; for a group of a hundred tens, it becomes a thousand, when 'yo' follows.

Sataṃ, sahassaṃ.

A hundred, a thousand.

Dvikādīnaṃ taduttarapadānañca nippajjante yathāsaṅkhyaṃ. Satassa dvikaṃ (tadidaṃ hoti) dvisataṃ, evaṃ tisataṃ, catusataṃ[M 0.0206], pañcasataṃ, chasataṃ, sattasataṃ, aṭṭhasataṃ, navasataṃ, dasasataṃ, sahassaṃ hoti.

For 'dvi' and so on, and for compounds having them as the final member, the forms are produced in respective order. A group of two of a hundred (that is) two hundred; similarly, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, nine hundred, ten hundred, which is a thousand.

394, 416. Yāva taduttari dasaguṇitañca.

And beyond that, successively multiplied by ten.

Yāva tāsaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ uttari dasaguṇitañca kātabbaṃ.

Beyond those numbers, it should be successively multiplied by ten.

Taṃ yathā? Dasassa gaṇanassa dasaguṇitaṃ katvā sataṃ hoti, satassa dasaguṇitaṃ katvā sahassaṃ hoti, sahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ katvā dasasahassaṃ hoti, dasasahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ katvāsatasahassaṃ hoti, satasahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ katvādasasatasahassaṃ hoti, dasasatasahassassadasaguṇitaṃ katvā koṭi hoti, koṭisatasahassassa sataguṇitaṃ katvā pakoṭi hoti. Evaṃ sesāpi yojetabbā.

How is that? Having multiplied the number ten by ten, it becomes a hundred; having multiplied a hundred by ten, it becomes a thousand; having multiplied a thousand by ten, it becomes ten thousand; having multiplied ten thousand by ten, it becomes a hundred thousand; having multiplied a hundred thousand by ten, it becomes ten hundred thousand; having multiplied ten hundred thousand by ten, it becomes a koṭi; having multiplied a koṭi of a hundred thousand by a hundred, it becomes a pakoṭi. Thus, the rest should also be construed.

Caggahaṇaṃ visesanatthaṃ.

The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of specification.

395, 417. Sakanāmehi.

By their own names.

Yāsaṃ pana saṅkhyānaṃ aniddiṭṭhanāmadheyyānaṃ sakehi sakehi nāmehi nippajjante.

But for those numbers whose names are not specified, they are formed by their own respective names.

Satasahassānaṃ sataṃ koṭi, koṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ pakoṭi, pakoṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ koṭipakoṭi[M 0.0207], koṭipakoṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ nahutaṃ, nahutasatasahassānaṃ sataṃ ninnahutaṃ, ninnahutasatasahassānaṃ sataṃ akkhobhiṇī. Tathā bindu, abbudaṃ, nirabbudaṃ, ahahaṃ, ababaṃ, aṭaṭaṃ, sogandhikaṃ, uppalaṃ, kumudaṃ, padumaṃ, puṇḍarikaṃ, kathānaṃ, mahākathānaṃ, asaṅkhyeyyaṃ.

A hundred hundred-thousands is a koṭi; a hundred hundred-thousand koṭis is a pakoṭi; a hundred hundred-thousand pakoṭis is a koṭipakoṭi; a hundred hundred-thousand koṭipakoṭis is a nahuta; a hundred hundred-thousand nahutas is a ninnahuta; a hundred hundred-thousand ninnahutas is an akkhobhiṇī. Likewise: bindu, abbuda, nirabbuda, ahaha, ababa, aṭaṭa, sogandhika, uppala, kumuda, paduma, puṇḍarika, kathāna, mahākathāna, asaṅkhyeyya.

396, 363. Tesaṃ ṇo lopaṃ.

396, 363. For them, there is elision of ṇo.

Tesaṃ paccayānaṃ ṇo lopamāpajjate.

For those suffixes, the elision of ṇo occurs.

Gotamassa apaccaṃ gotamo. Evaṃ vāsiṭṭho. Venateyyo, ālasyaṃ, ārogyaṃ.

A descendant of Gotama is Gotama. Likewise, Vāsiṭṭha. Venateyya, laziness, health.

397, 420. Vibhāge dhā ca.

397, 420. And dhā in the sense of division.

Vibhāgatthe ca dhāpaccayo hoti.

And in the sense of division, the suffix dhā occurs.

Ekena vibhāgena ekadhā. Evaṃ dvidhā, tidhā, catudhā, pañcadhā, chadhā.

By one division, onefold. Likewise, twofold, threefold, fourfold, fivefold, sixfold.

Ceti kimatthaṃ? Sopaccayo hoti. Suttaso, byañjanaso, padaso.

What is the purpose of 'ca'? The suffix 'so' also occurs. By sutta, by phrase, by word.

398, 421. Sabbanāmehi [M 0.0208] pakāravacane tu thā.

398, 421. But after pronouns, in the sense of manner, thā.

Sabbanāmehi pakāravacanatthe thāpaccayo hoti.

After pronouns, in the sense of expressing manner, the suffix thā is applied.

So pakāro tathā, taṃ pakāraṃ tathā, tena pakārena tathā, tassa pakārassa tathā, tasmā pakārā tathā, tassa pakārassa tathā, tasmiṃ pakāre tathā. Evaṃ yathā, sabbathā, aññathā, itarathā.

That manner is thus; that manner, thus; by that manner, thus; of that manner, thus; from that manner, thus; of that manner, thus; in that manner, thus. Likewise: as, in every way, otherwise, in another way.

Tuggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Tatthāpaccayo hoti. So pakāro tathatthā. Evaṃ yathatthā. Sabbathatthā, aññathatthā, itarathatthā.

What is the purpose of the inclusion of 'tu'? The suffix 'tthā' occurs. That manner is tathatthā. Likewise, yathatthā, sabbathatthā, aññathatthā, itarathatthā.

399, 422. Kimimehi thaṃ.

399, 422. After 'kiṃ' and 'ima', thaṃ.

Kiṃ imaiccetehi thaṃpaccayo hoti pakāravacanatthe.

After 'kiṃ' and 'ima', the suffix 'thaṃ' occurs in the sense of expressing manner.

Ko pakāro kathaṃ, kaṃ pakāraṃ kathaṃ, kena pakārena kathaṃ, kassa pakārassa kathaṃ, kasmā pakārā kathaṃ. Kassa pakārassa kathaṃ, kasmiṃ pakāre kathaṃ, ayaṃ pakāro itthaṃ, imaṃ pakāraṃ itthaṃ, iminā pakārena itthaṃ, imassa pakārassa itthaṃ, imasmā pakārā itthaṃ, imassa pakārassa itthaṃ, imasmiṃ pakāre itthaṃ.

What manner is how; what manner, how; by what manner, how; of what manner, how; from what manner, how; of what manner, how; in what manner, how. This manner is thus; this manner, thus; by this manner, thus; of this manner, thus; from this manner, thus; of this manner, thus; in this manner, thus.

400, 364. Vuddhādisarassa [M 0.0209] vā’saṃyogantassa saṇe ca.

400, 364. And optionally, vuddhi of the initial vowel of a stem not ending in a conjunct consonant, when a ṇa-group suffix follows.

Ādisarassa vā asaṃyogantassa ādibyañjanassa vā sarassa vuddhi hoti saṇakārake paccaye pare.

Optionally, vuddhi of the initial vowel of a stem not ending in a conjunct consonant, or of the vowel of the initial consonant, occurs when a ṇa-group suffix follows.

Ābhidhammiko, venateyyo, vāsiṭṭho, ālasyaṃ, ārogyaṃ.

Ābhidhammiko, venateyyo, vāsiṭṭho, ālasyaṃ, ārogyaṃ.

Asaṃyogantasseti kimatthaṃ? Bhaggavo, manteyyo, kunteyyo.

What is the purpose of 'asaṃyogantassa'? Bhaggavo, manteyyo, kunteyyo.

401, 375. Māyūnamāgamo ṭhāne.

401, 375. For i and u, no augment in place.

Iuiccetesaṃ ādibhūtānaṃ mā vuddhi hoti. Tesu ca e o vuddhāgamo hoti ṭhāne.

For these initial 'i' and 'u', vuddhi does not occur. And in their place, 'e' and 'o' occur as a vuddhi-augment.

Byākaraṇamadhīte veyyākaraṇiko, nyāyamadhīte neyyāyiko, byāvacchassa apaccaṃ veyyāvaccho, dvāre niyutto dovāriko.

One who studies grammar is a grammarian; one who studies logic is a logician; the descendant of Byāvaccha is Veyyāvaccha; one appointed at the door is a doorkeeper.

402, 377. Āttañca[M 0.0210].

402, 377. And substitution by ā.

Iuiccetesaṃ āttañca hoti, rikārāgamo ca ṭhāne.

For these, 'i' and 'u', there is also substitution by 'ā', and the augment 'r' in its place.

Isissa bhāvo ārisyaṃ, iṇassa bhāvo āṇyaṃ, usabhassa bhāvo āsabhaṃ, ujuno bhāvo ajjavaṃ, iccevamādī yojetabbā.

The state of a seer is ārisyaṃ; the state of debt is āṇyaṃ; the state of a bull is āsabhaṃ; the state of uprightness is ajjavaṃ. These and similar examples should be applied.

Yūnamiti kimatthaṃ? Apāyesu jāto āpāyi ko.

What is the purpose of 'yūnaṃ'? One born in the lower realms is āpāyiko.

Ṭhāneti kimatthaṃ? Vematiko, opanayiko, opamāyiko, opāyiko.

What is the purpose of 'ṭhāne'? Vematiko, opanayiko, opamāyiko, opāyiko.

403, 354. Kvacādimajjhuttarānaṃ dīgharassā paccayesu ca.

403, 354. And sometimes, for initial, middle, and final syllables, there is lengthening and shortening, when suffixes follow.

Kvaci ādimajjhauttaraiccetesaṃ dīgharassā honti paccayesu ca apaccayesu ca.

In some cases, for the initial, middle, and final syllables, lengthening and shortening occur, both when a suffix follows and when one does not.

Ādidīgho tāva – pākāro, nīvāro, pāsādo, pākaṭo, pātimokkho, pāṭikaṅkho iccevamādi.

First, initial lengthening: pākāro, nīvāro, pāsādo, pākaṭo, pātimokkho, pāṭikaṅkho, and so on.

Majjhedīgho [M 0.0211] tāva – aṅgamāgadhiko, orabbhamāgavīko iccevamādi.

Middle lengthening—for example: aṅgamāgadhiko (belonging to Aṅga and Magadha), orabbhamāgavīko (belonging to sheep and goats), and so on.

Uttaradīgho tāva – khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, añjanā giri, koṭarā vanaṃ, aṅgulī iccevamādi.

Final lengthening—for example: khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā (patience is the highest austerity), añjanā giri (Añjana mountain), koṭarā vanaṃ (hollow forest), aṅgulī (finger), and so on.

Ādirasso tāva – pageva iccevamādi.

Initial shortening—for example: pageva (previously indeed), and so on.

Majjherasso tāva – sumedhaso suvaṇṇadharehi iccevamādi.

Middle shortening—for example: sumedhaso (the wise), suvaṇṇadharehi (by the gold-bearers), and so on.

Uttararasso tāva – bhovādi nāma so hoti, yathābhāvi guṇena so iccevamādi. Aññepi yathājinavacanānuparodhena yojetabbā.

Final shortening—for example: bhovādi nāma so hoti (he is one who says ‘bho’), yathābhāvi guṇena so (he is according to his quality), and so on. Others also should be applied without contradicting the Buddha’s words.

Caggahaṇena apaccayesu cāti atthaṃ samucceti,

By the inclusion of “ca,” it combines the meaning “also in non-derivatives.”

404, 370. Tesu vuddhilopāgamavikāraviparītādesā ca.

404, 370. Among these, there are also augmentations, elisions, insertions, modifications, inversions, and substitutions.

Tesu ādimajjhuttaresu yathājinavacanānuparodhena kvaci vuddhi hoti, kvaci lopo hoti, kvaci āgamo hoti, kvaci vikāro hoti, kvaci viparīto hoti, kvaci ādeso hoti.

Among these initial, medial, and final elements, in accordance with the Buddha’s teaching and without contradiction, sometimes there is augmentation, sometimes elision, sometimes insertion, sometimes modification, sometimes inversion, and sometimes substitution.

Ādivuddhi tāva – ābhidhammiko, venateyyo iccevamādi.

Initial augmentation—for example: ābhidhammiko (pertaining to the Abhidhamma), venateyyo (descendant of Vinatā), and so on.

Majjhevuddhi [M 0.0212] tāva – sukhaseyyaṃ, sukhakāri dānaṃ, sukhakāri sīlaṃ iccevamādi.

Middle augmentation—for example: sukhaseyyaṃ (comfortable sleep), sukhakāri dānaṃ (giving that causes happiness), sukhakāri sīlaṃ (virtue that causes happiness), and so on.

Uttaravuddhi tāva – kāliṅgo, māgadhiko, paccakkhadhammā iccevamādi.

Final augmentation—for example: kāliṅgo, māgadhiko, paccakkhadhammā, and so on.

Ādilopo tāva – tālīsaṃ iccevamādi.

Initial elision—for example: tālīsaṃ (forty), and so on.

Majjhelopo tāva – kattukāmo, kumbhakāraputto, vedallaṃ iccevamādi.

Middle elision—for example: kattukāmo (desiring to do), kumbhakāraputto (potter's son), vedallaṃ (analytical discourse), and so on.

Uttaralopo tāva – bhikkhu, bhikkhunī iccevamādi.

Final elision—for example: bhikkhu, bhikkhunī, and so on.

Ādiāgamo tāva – vutto bhagavatā iccevamādi.

Initial insertion—for example: vutto bhagavatā (spoken by the Blessed One), and so on.

Majjheāgamo tāva – sasīlavā, sapaññavāiccevamādi.

Middle insertion—for example: sasīlavā (possessing virtue), sapaññavā (possessing wisdom), and so on.

Uttaraāgamo tāva – vedallaṃ iccevamādi.

Final insertion—for example: vedallaṃ (analytical discourse), and so on.

Ādivikāro tāva – ārisyaṃ, āṇyaṃ, āsabhaṃ, ajjavaṃ iccevamādi.

Initial modification—for example: ārisyaṃ (state of a seer), āṇyaṃ (state of debt), āsabhaṃ (state of a bull), ajjavaṃ (state of uprightness), and so on.

Majjhevikāro tāva – varārisyaṃ, parārisyaṃ iccevamādi.

Middle modification—for example: varārisyaṃ, parārisyaṃ, and so on.

Uttaravikāro tāva – yāni, tāni, sukhāni iccevamādi.

Final modification—for example: yāni (which), tāni (those), sukhāni (pleasures), and so on.

Ādiviparīto [M 0.0213] tāva – uggate sūriye uggacchati iccevamādi.

Initial inversion—for example: uggate sūriye uggacchati (when the sun has risen, it rises), and so on.

Majjheviparīto tāva – samuggacchati, samuggate sūriye iccevamādi.

Middle inversion—for example: samuggacchati (it arises together), samuggate sūriye (when the sun has risen together), and so on.

Uttaraviparīto tāva – digu, diguṇaṃ iccevamādi.

Final inversion—for example: digu, diguṇaṃ, and so on.

Ādiādeso tāva – yūnaṃ iccevamādi.

Initial substitution—for example: yūnaṃ, and so on.

Majjheādeso tāva – nyāyogā iccevamādi.

Middle substitution—for example: nyāyogā, and so on.

Uttaraādeso tāva – sabbaseyyo, sabbaseṭṭho, cittaṃ iccevamādi. Evaṃ yathājinavacanānuparodhena sabbattha yojetabbā.

Final substitution—for example: sabbaseyyo, sabbaseṭṭho, cittaṃ, and so on. Thus, without contradicting the word of the Conqueror, they should be applied everywhere.

405, 365. Ayuvaṇṇānañcāyo vuddhi.

405, 365. The vṛddhi augments of the vowels a, i, and u are ā, e, and o.

A iti akāro, i īiti ivaṇṇo, u ūiti uvaṇṇo, tesaṃ akāraivaṇṇuvaṇṇānaṃ ā e ovuddhiyo honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ, ā ī ūvuddhi ca.

The vowel ‘a’ is the a-sound; ‘i’ and ‘ī’ are the i-sound; ‘u’ and ‘ū’ are the u-sound. For these a-sound, i-sound, and u-sound, the vṛddhi augments are ā, e, and o, respectively; and ā, ī, and ū are also vṛddhi.

Ābhidhammiko, venateyyo, oḷumpiko.

Ābhidhammiko, venateyyo, oḷumpiko.

Puna vuddhiggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Uttarapadavuddhibhāvatthaṃ, aṅgamagadhehi āgatāti aṅgamāgadhikā. Nigamajanapadesu jātāti [M 0.0214] negamajānapadā. Purimajanapadesu jātāti porimajānapadā. Sattāhe niyuttoti sattāhikā, catuvijje niyuttoti cātuvijjikā. Iccevamādī yojetabbā.

Again, what is the purpose of including the term vṛddhi? It is for the sake of the vṛddhi of the final member, as in aṅgamāgadhikā (those who come from Aṅga and Magadha). Negamajānapadā (those born in towns and rural areas). Porimajānapadā (those born in eastern regions). Sattāhikā (appointed for a week). Cātuvijjikā (appointed to the four knowledges). These and similar cases should be applied.

Vuddhiiccanena kvattho? Vuddhādisarassa vā’saṃyogantassa saṇe ca.

What is the purpose of the term `vuddhi`? For the `vuddhi` of the initial vowel, or of a non-conjunct final, and in the case of `saṇe`.

Iti nāmakappe taddhitakappo aṭṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus in the Nāmakappa ends the Taddhitakappa, the eighth section.

Taddhitakappo niṭṭhito.

The Taddhitakappa is completed.

6. Ākhyātakappa

6. The Ākhyātakappa

Paṭhamakaṇḍa

First Section

(Ka)

(Ka)

Ākhyātasāgaramathajjatanītaraṅgaṃ[M 0.0215],

Dhātujjalaṃ vikaraṇāgamakālamīnaṃ;

Lopānubandhariyamatthavibhāgatīraṃ,

Dhīrā taranti kavino puthubuddhināvā.

The ocean of verbs, with its `ajjatanī` waves churned up; its water born of roots; its fish the `vikaraṇa` (stem-formatives), `āgama` (augments), and `kāla` (tenses); its shore the division of noble meaning, characterized by `lopa` (elision) and `anubandha` (indicatory letters)—this the wise poets cross with the boat of broad intellect.

(Kha)

(Kha)

Vicittasaṅkhāraparikkhitaṃ imaṃ,

Ākhyātasaddaṃ vipulaṃ asesato;

Paṇamya sambuddhamanantagocaraṃ,

Sugocaraṃ yaṃ vadato suṇātha me.

Having bowed to the Perfectly Enlightened One, whose range is infinite and domain excellent, listen to me as I speak completely of this vast verbal science, adorned with varied formations.

(Ga)

(Ga)

Adhikāre maṅgale ceva, nipphanne cāvadhāraṇe;

Anantare ca pādāne, athasaddo pavattati.

The word `atha` is used in the sense of authority, auspiciousness, accomplishment, determination, immediate sequence, and cause.

416, 429. Atha pubbāni vibhattīnaṃ cha parassapadāni.

416, 429. Now, the first six of the inflections are `parassapada`.

Atha sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ yāni yāni pubbakāni cha padāni, tāni tāni parassapadasaññāni honti.

Now, of all the inflections, whichever six terms are the first, those are designated as `parassapada`.

Taṃ yathā? Ti anti, si tha, mi ma.

What are they? `ti`, `anti`; `si`, `tha`; `mi`, `ma`.

Parassapadamiccanena kvattho? Kattari parassapadaṃ.

What is the purpose of the term `parassapada`? `Parassapada` is used in the active voice.

407, 439. Parāṇyattanopadāni[M 0.0216].

407, 439. The latter are `attanopada`.

Sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ yāni yāni parāni cha padāni. Tāni tāni attanopadasaññāni honti.

Of all the inflections, whichever six terms are the latter, those are designated as `attanopada`.

Taṃ yathā? Te ante, se vhe, e mhe.

What are they? `te`, `ante`; `se`, `vhe`; `e`, `mhe`.

Attanopadamiccanena kvattho? Attanopadāni bhāve ca kammani.

What is the purpose of the term `attanopada`? `Attanopada` is used in the impersonal and passive voices.

408, 431. Dve dve paṭhama majjhimuttamapurisā.

408, 431. Two each are the first, middle, and ultimate persons.

Tāsaṃ sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ parassapadānaṃ, attanopadānañca dve dve padāni paṭhamamajjhimuttamapurisasaññāni honti.

Of all those inflections, two terms each of both the `parassapada` and the `attanopada` are designated as first, middle, and ultimate persons.

Taṃ yathā? Ti anti iti paṭhamapurisā, si tha iti majjhimapurisā, mi ma iti uttamapurisā. Attanopadānampi te ante iti paṭhamapurisā, se vhe iti majjhimapurisā, e mhe iti uttamapurisā. Evaṃ sabbattha.

How is that? `ti` and `anti` are the first person; `si` and `tha` are the middle person; `mi` and `ma` are the ultimate person. Likewise for the `attanopada`: `te` and `ante` are the first person; `se` and `vhe` are the middle person; `e` and `mhe` are the ultimate person. Thus it is in all cases.

Paṭhamamajjhimuttamapurisamiccanena kvattho? Nāmamhi payujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe paṭhamo, tumhe majjhimo, amhe uttamo.

What is the purpose of the terms first, middle, and ultimate person? When a noun is used in coreference, the first person [verb] is used; with the pronoun `tumhe`, the middle person; with the pronoun `amhe`, the ultimate person.

409, 441. Sabbesamekābhidhāne paro puriso.

409, 441. When all are expressed together, the latter person is used.

Sabbesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ paṭhamamajjhimuttama purisānaṃ ekābhidhāne paro puriso gahetabbo.

When all three persons—first, middle, and ultimate—are expressed together, the latter person should be used.

So [M 0.0217] ca paṭhati, tvañca paṭhasi, tumhe paṭhatha. So ca pacati, tvañca pacasi. Tumhe pacatha. Evaṃ sesāsu vibhattīsu paro puriso yojetabbo.

[For example, combining] 'he recites' (`so paṭhati`) and 'you recite' (`tvaṃ paṭhasi`) yields 'you (pl.) recite' (`tumhe paṭhatha`). [Combining] 'he cooks' (`so pacati`) and 'you cook' (`tvaṃ pacasi`) yields 'you (pl.) cook' (`tumhe pacatha`). In this way, the latter person should be applied in the remaining inflections.

410, 432. Nāmamhi payujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe paṭhamo.

410, 432. When a noun is used, even in coreference, the first person [is used].

Nāmamhi payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe paṭhamapuriso hoti.

Whether a noun is stated or unstated, the first person verb is used in coreference with the subject.

So gacchati, te gacchanti.

He goes, they go.

Appayujjamānepi – gacchati, gacchanti.

Even when [the noun is] not stated: he goes, they go.

Tulyādhikaraṇeti kimatthaṃ? Tena haññase tvaṃ devadattena.

For what purpose is the term `tulyādhikaraṇe`? As in: `Tena haññase tvaṃ devadattena` (You are struck by Devadatta).

411, 436. Tumhe majjhimo.

411, 436. With `tumhe`, the middle person.

Tumhe payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe majjhimapuriso hoti.

Whether `tumhe` is expressed or unexpressed, when in apposition, the middle person is used.

Tvaṃ yāsi, tumhe yātha.

You go; you all go.

Appayujjamānepi – yāsi, yātha.

Even when unexpressed: you go, you all go.

Tulyādhikaraṇeti kimatthaṃ? Tayā paccate odano.

For what purpose is the term `tulyādhikaraṇe`? As in: `Tayā paccate odano` (Rice is cooked by you).

412, 437. Amhe [M 0.0218] uttamo.

412, 437. With `amhe`, the first person.

Amhe payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi tulyādhikaraṇe uttamapuriso hoti.

Whether `amhe` is expressed or unexpressed, when in apposition, the first person is used.

Ahaṃ yajāmi, mayaṃ yajāma.

I sacrifice; we sacrifice.

Appayujjamānepi – yajāmi, yajāma.

Even when unexpressed: I sacrifice, we sacrifice.

Tulyādhikaraṇeti kimatthaṃ? Mayā ijjate buddho.

For what purpose is the term `tulyādhikaraṇe`? As in: `Mayā ijjate buddho` (The Buddha is worshipped by me).

413, 427. Kāle.

413, 427. In time.

“Kāle” iccetaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

This term `kāle` should be understood as a governing rule.

414, 428. Vattamānā paccuppanne.

414, 428. The `vattamānā` inflection is used in the present.

Paccuppanne kāle vattamānāvibhatti hoti.

In the present time, the `vattamānā` inflection is used.

Pāṭaliputtaṃ gacchati, sāvatthiṃ pavisati.

He goes to Pāṭaliputta; he enters Sāvatthī.

415, 451. Āṇatyā siṭṭhe’nuttakāle pañcamī.

415, 451. The `pañcamī` inflection is used for command and blessing in non-past time.

Āṇatyatthe ca āsīsatthe ca anuttakāle pañcamī vibhatti hoti.

In the sense of command and blessing, in non-past time, the `pañcamī` inflection is used.

Karotu kusalaṃ, sukhaṃ te hotu.

Let him do good; may happiness be yours.

416, 454. Anumatiparikappatthesu sattamī.

416, 454. The `sattamī` inflection is used in the sense of permission and supposition.

Anumatyatthe ca parikappatthe ca anuttakāle sattamī vibhatti hoti.

In the sense of permission and supposition, in non-past time, the `sattamī` inflection is used.

Tvaṃ [M 0.0219] gaccheyyāsi, kimahaṃ kareyyāmi.

You may go; what should I do?

417, 460. Apaccakkhe parokkhātīte.

417, 460. The `parokkhā` inflection is used for a past time not directly witnessed.

Apaccakkhe atīte kāle parokkhāvibhatti hoti.

For a past time not directly witnessed, the `parokkhā` inflection is used.

Supine kilamāha, evaṃ kila porāṇāhu.

Reportedly, he was weary in a dream; thus, it is said, the ancients spoke.

418, 456. Hiyyopabhuti paccakkhe hiyyattanī.

418, 456. The `hiyattanī` inflection is used for a witnessed past, from yesterday backwards.

Hiyyopabhuti atīte kāle paccakkhe vā apaccakkhe vā hiyyattanī vibhatti hoti.

From yesterday backwards into the past, whether witnessed or unwitnessed, the `hiyattanī` inflection is used.

So agamā maggaṃ, te agamū maggaṃ.

He went on the path; they went on the path.

419, 469. Samīpe’jjatanī.

419, 469. The `ajjatanī` inflection is used for the recent past.

Ajjappabhuti atīte kāle paccakkhe vā apaccakkhe vā samīpe ajjatanīvibhatti hoti.

From today backwards into the past, whether witnessed or unwitnessed, for what is recent, the `ajjatanī` inflection is used.

So maggaṃ agamī, te maggaṃ agamuṃ.

He went on the path; they went on the path.

420, 471. Māyoge sabbakāle ca.

420, 471. And in connection with `mā`, in all times.

Hiyyattanīajjatanīiccetā vibhattiyo yadā māyogā, tadā sabbakāle ca honti.

When the `Hiyyattanī` and `Ajjatanī` inflections are used with `mā`, they occur in all times.

Mā gamā, mā vacā, mā gamī, mā vacī.

Do not go, do not speak; let him not go, let him not speak.

Caggahaṇena [M 0.0220] pañcamīvibhattipi hoti. Mā gacchāhi.

By the inclusion of `ca`, the `pañcamī` inflection also occurs. (As in) `Mā gacchāhi` (Do not go).

421, 473. Anāgate bhavissantī.

421, 473. In the future, the `bhavissantī` (inflection applies).

Anāgate kāle bhavissantī vibhatti hoti.

In future time, the `bhavissantī` inflection occurs.

So gacchissati, karissati. Te gacchissanti, karissanti.

He will go, he will do. They will go, they will do.

422, 475. Kriyātipanne’tīte kālātipatti.

422, 475. When an action in the past is surpassed, the `kālātipatti` (inflection applies).

Kriyātipannamatte atīte kāle kālātipatti vibhatti hoti.

In past time, when an action is just surpassed, the `kālātipatti` inflection occurs.

So ce taṃ yānaṃ alabhissā, agacchissā. Te ce taṃ yānaṃ alabhissaṃsu, agacchissaṃsu.

If he had obtained that vehicle, he would have gone. If they had obtained that vehicle, they would have gone.

423, 426. Vattamānā ti anti, si tha, mi ma, te ante, se vhe, e mhe.

423, 426. The `vattamānā` (inflections are): `ti`, `anti`, `si`, `tha`, `mi`, `ma`, `te`, `ante`, `se`, `vhe`, `e`, `mhe`.

Vattamānā iccesā saññā hoti ti anti, si tha, mi ma, te ante, se vhe, e mhe iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `vattamānā` applies to these twelve terms: `ti`, `anti`, `si`, `tha`, `mi`, `ma`, `te`, `ante`, `se`, `vhe`, `e`, `mhe`.

Vattamānā iccanena kvattho? Vattamānā paccuppanne.

What is the purpose of the term `vattamānā`? `Vattamānā` (applies) in the present time.

424, 450. Pañcamī tu antu, hitha, mima, taṃ antaṃ, ssu vho, e āmase.

424, 450. The `pañcamī` (inflections are): `tu`, `antu`, `hi`, `tha`, `mi`, `ma`, `taṃ`, `antaṃ`, `ssu`, `vho`, `e`, `āmase`.

Pañcamīiccesā [M 0.0221] saññā hoti tu antu, hi tha, mima, taṃ antaṃ, ssu vho, e āmase iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `pañcamī` applies to these twelve terms: `tu`, `antu`, `hi`, `tha`, `mi`, `ma`, `taṃ`, `antaṃ`, `ssu`, `vho`, `e`, `āmase`.

Pañcamīiccanena kvattho? Āṇatyāsiṭṭhe, nuttakāle pañcamī.

What is the purpose of the term `pañcamī`? The `pañcamī` (applies) in the sense of command, blessing, and non-past time.

425, 453. Sattamī eyya eyyuṃ, eyyā si eyyā tha, eyyāmi eyyāma, etha eraṃ, etho eyyāvho, eyyaṃ eyyāmhe.

425, 453. The `sattamī` (inflections are): `eyya`, `eyyuṃ`, `eyyāsi`, `eyyātha`, `eyyāmi`, `eyyāma`, `etha`, `eraṃ`, `etho`, `eyyāvho`, `eyyaṃ`, `eyyāmhe`.

Sattamī iccesā saññā hoti eyya eyyuṃ, eyyāsi eyyātha, eyyāmi eyyāma, etha eraṃ, etho, eyyāvho, eyyaṃ eyyāmhe iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `sattamī` applies to these twelve terms: `eyya`, `eyyuṃ`, `eyyāsi`, `eyyātha`, `eyyāmi`, `eyyāma`, `etha`, `eraṃ`, `etho`, `eyyāvho`, `eyyaṃ`, `eyyāmhe`.

Sattamī iccanena kvattho? Anumatiparikappatthesu sattamī.

What is the purpose of the term `sattamī`? The `sattamī` (applies) in the sense of permission and supposition.

426, 459. Parokkhā au ettha, aṃmha, tthare, ttho vho, iṃ mhe.

426, 459. The `parokkhā` (inflections are): `a`, `u`, `e`, `ttha`, `aṃ`, `mha`, `ttha`, `re`, `ttho`, `vho`, `iṃ`, `mhe`.

Parokkhā iccesā saññā hoti a u, ettha, aṃ mha, ttha re ttho vho, iṃ mhe iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `parokkhā` applies to these twelve terms: `a`, `u`, `e`, `ttha`, `aṃ`, `mha`, `ttha`, `re`, `ttho`, `vho`, `iṃ`, `mhe`.

Parokkhā iccanena kvattho? Apaccakkhe parokkhātīte.

What is the purpose of the term `parokkhā`? The `parokkhā` (applies) to the past which is not directly perceived.

427, 455. Hiyyattanī [M 0.0222] āū, ottha, aṃmhā, tthatthuṃ, se vhaṃ, iṃ mhase.

427, 455. The `Hiyyattanī` (imperfect tense) endings are: `ā`, `ū`, `o`, `ttha`, `aṃ`, `mhā`, `ttha`, `tthuṃ`, `se`, `vhaṃ`, `iṃ`, `mhase`.

Hiyyattanī iccesā saññā hoti ā ū, o ttha, aṃ mhā, ttha tthuṃ, se vhaṃ, iṃ mhase iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `Hiyyattanī` applies to these twelve terms: `ā`, `ū`, `o`, `ttha`, `aṃ`, `mhā`, `ttha`, `tthuṃ`, `se`, `vhaṃ`, `iṃ`, `mhase`.

Hiyyattanī iccanena kvattho? Hiyyopabhuti paccakkhe hiyyattanī.

What is the purpose of the term `Hiyyattanī`? The `Hiyyattanī` (applies) to what has been directly perceived from yesterday onwards.

428, 468. Ajjatanī ī uṃ, o ttha, iṃ mhā, ā ū, se vhaṃ, aṃ mhe.

428, 468. The `Ajjatanī` (aorist) endings are: `ī`, `uṃ`, `o`, `ttha`, `iṃ`, `mhā`, `ā`, `ū`, `se`, `vhaṃ`, `aṃ`, `mhe`.

Ajjatanī iccesā saññā hoti ī uṃ, o ttha, iṃmhā, ā ū, sevhaṃ, aṃ mhe iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The designation `Ajjatanī` applies to these twelve terms: `ī`, `uṃ`, `o`, `ttha`, `iṃ`, `mhā`, `ā`, `ū`, `se`, `vhaṃ`, `aṃ`, `mhe`.

Ajjatanī iccanena kvattho? Samīpejjatanī.

What is the purpose of the term `Ajjatanī`? The `Ajjatanī` (applies) in the recent past.

429, 472. Bhavissantī ssati ssanti, ssasi ssatha, ssāmi ssāma, ssate ssante, ssase ssavhe, ssaṃ ssāmhe.

429, 472. The `Bhavissantī` (future tense) endings are: `ssati`, `ssanti`, `ssasi`, `ssatha`, `ssāmi`, `ssāma`, `ssate`, `ssante`, `ssase`, `ssavhe`, `ssaṃ`, `ssāmhe`.

Bhavissantī iccesā saññā hoti ssati ssanti, ssasi ssatha, ssāmi ssāma, ssate ssante, ssase ssavhe, ssaṃ ssāmhe iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The term 'Bhavissantī' is the designation for these twelve endings: ssati, ssanti, ssasi, ssatha, ssāmi, ssāma, ssate, ssante, ssase, ssavhe, ssaṃ, ssāmhe.

Bhavissantī iccanena kvattho? Anāgate bhavissantī.

What is the meaning of 'Bhavissantī'? The Bhavissantī refers to the future.

430, 373. Kālātipatti [M 0.0223] ssā ssaṃsu, sse ssatha, ssaṃ ssāmhā, ssatha sissu, ssase ssavhe, ssiṃ ssāmhase.

430, 373. The Kālātipatti (conditional) endings are: ssā, ssaṃsu, sse, ssatha, ssaṃ, ssāmhā, ssatha, ssisu, ssase, ssavhe, ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

Kālātipatti iccesā saññā hoti ssā ssaṃsu, sse ssatha, ssaṃ ssāmhā, ssatha ssisu, ssase ssavhe, ssiṃ ssāmhase iccetesaṃ dvādasannaṃ padānaṃ.

The term 'Kālātipatti' is the designation for these twelve endings: ssā, ssaṃsu, sse, ssatha, ssaṃ, ssāmhā, ssatha, ssisu, ssase, ssavhe, ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

Kālātipatti iccanena kvattho? Kriyātipanne’ tīte kālātipatti.

What is the meaning of 'Kālātipatti'? The Kālātipatti refers to the past when an action has lapsed.

431, 458. Hiyyattanī sattamī pañcamī vattamānā sabbadhātukaṃ.

431, 458. The Hiyyattanī, Sattami, Pañcami, and Vattamānā are Sabbadhātuka.

Hiyyattanādayo catasso vibhattiyo sabbadhātuka saññā honti.

These four inflections, beginning with Hiyyattanī, are designated 'sabbadhātuka'.

Agamā, gaccheyya, gacchatu, gacchati.

He came, he might go, let him go, he goes.

Sabbadhātuka iccanena kvattho? Ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhi.

What is the meaning of 'Sabbadhātuka'? The augment 'i' occurs in what is not Sabbadhātuka.

Iti ākhyātakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section on verb conjugation.

Dutiyakaṇḍa

Second Section.

432, 362. Dhātuliṅgehi [M 0.0224] parā paccayā.

432, 362. Affixes come after roots and nominal stems.

Dhātuliṅgaiccetehi parā paccayā honti.

Affixes come after verbal roots and nominal stems.

Karoti, gacchati. Yo koci karoti, taṃ añño “karohi karohi” iccevaṃ bravīti, atha vā karontaṃ payojayati = kāreti. Saṅgho pabbatamiva attānamācarati = pabbatāyati. Taḷākaṃ samuddamiva attānamācarati = samuddāyati, saddo cicciṭamiva attānamācarati = cicciṭāyati, vasiṭṭhassa apaccaṃ vāsiṭṭho. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

He does, he goes. If someone does something, another says, 'Do, do,' or causes the doer to act: this is 'kāreti' (causative). The Saṅgha behaves like a mountain: 'pabbatāyati'. A pond behaves like the ocean: 'samuddāyati'. A sound behaves like a cicciṭa: 'cicciṭāyati'. A descendant of Vasiṭṭha is 'Vāsiṭṭho'. Others should be similarly construed.

433, 528. Tija gupa kita māne hi kha cha sā vā.

433, 528. The roots 'tij', 'gup', 'kit', and 'mān' optionally take the affixes 'kha', 'cha', or 'sa'.

Tija gupa kita mānu iccetehi dhātūhi kha cha sa iccete paccayā honti vā.

The roots 'tij', 'gup', 'kit', and 'mān' optionally take the affixes 'kha', 'cha', and 'sa'.

Titikkhati, jigucchati, tikicchati, vīmaṃsati.

He endures, he is disgusted, he treats, he investigates.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Tejati, gopati, māneti.

What is the purpose of 'vā' (optionally)? He sharpens, he protects, he honors.

434, 534. Bhuja ghasa hara su pādīhi tumicchatthesu.

434, 534. From the roots 'bhuj', 'ghas', 'har', 'su', 'pā', and so on, in the sense of wishing to do.

Bhuja [M 0.0225] ghasa hara su pāiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tumicchatthesu kha cha saiccete paccayā honti vā.

The roots 'bhuj', 'ghas', 'har', 'su', and 'pā', and so on, optionally take the affixes 'kha', 'cha', and 'sa' in the sense of wishing to do something.

Bhottumicchati=bubhukkhati, ghasitumicchati=jighacchati, haritumicchati=jigīsati, sotumicchati=sussusati, pātumicchati=pivāsati.

He desires to eat: 'bubhukkhati'; he desires to consume: 'jighacchati'; he desires to take: 'jigīsati'; he desires to hear: 'sussusati'; he desires to drink: 'pivāsati'.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Bhottumicchati.

What is the purpose of 'vā' (optionally)? He desires to eat.

Tumicchatthesūti kimatthaṃ? Bhuñjati.

What is the purpose of 'tumicchatthesu' (in the sense of wishing to do)? He eats.

435, 536. Āya nāmato kattūpamānādācāre.

435, 536. The suffix 'āya' is used after a nominal stem when it serves as a comparison for the agent's behavior.

Nāmato kattūpamānā ācāratthe āyapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'āya' is applied after a nominal stem when it serves as a comparison, in the sense of an agent's behavior.

Saṅgho pabbatamiva attānamācarati = pabbatāyati, taḷākaṃ samuddamiva attānamācarati = samuddāyati, saddo cicciṭamiva attānamācarati = cicciṭāyati. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

The Saṅgha behaves like a mountain: 'pabbatāyati'; a pond behaves like the ocean: 'samuddāyati'; a sound behaves like a cicciṭa: 'cicciṭāyati'. Others should be similarly construed.

436, 537. Īyūpamānā ca.

436, 537. And the suffix 'īya' is used when the nominal stem is a standard of comparison.

Nāmato upamānā ācāratthe ca īyapaccayo hoti.

And the suffix 'īya' is applied after a nominal stem that is a standard of comparison, in the sense of behavior.

Achattaṃ [M 0.0226] chattamiva ācarati =chattīyati, aputtaṃ puttamiva ācarati=puttīyati.

One without an umbrella behaves like one with an umbrella: 'chattīyati'; one without a son behaves like one with a son: 'puttīyati'.

Upamānāti kimatthaṃ? Dhammaṃ ācarati.

What is the purpose of 'upamānā' (from a standard of comparison)? He practices the Dhamma.

Ācāreti kimatthaṃ? Achattaṃ chattamiva rakkhati. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

For what purpose is 'ācāreti'? He protects one who is without an umbrella as if with an umbrella. Thus, other examples are to be similarly applied.

437, 538. Nāmamhā’tticchatthe.

437, 538. After a nominal stem, in the sense of desiring for oneself.

Nāmamhā attano icchatthe īyapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'īya' occurs after a nominal stem in the sense of desiring for oneself.

Attano pattamicchati = pattīyati. Evaṃ vatthīyati, parikkhārīyati, cīvarīyati, dhanīyati, ghaṭīyati.

He desires his own bowl: 'pattīyati'. Similarly, 'vatthīyati', 'parikkhārīyati', 'cīvarīyati', 'dhanīyati', 'ghaṭīyati'.

Atticchattheti kimatthaṃ? Aññassa pattamicchati. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

For what purpose is 'atticchatthe' (in the sense of desiring for oneself)? He desires another's bowl. Thus, other examples are to be similarly applied.

438, 540. Dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya ṇāpe ṇāpayā kāritāni hetvatthe.

438, 540. After verbal roots, the suffixes ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, and ṇāpaya are designated kārita (causative), in the sense of cause.

Sabbehi dhātūhi ṇeṇaya ṇāpe ṇāpayaiccete paccayā honti kāritasaññā ca hetvatthe.

After all verbal roots, these suffixes, namely ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, and ṇāpaya, occur; and they are designated 'kārita' (causative) in the sense of cause.

Yo koci karoti, taṃ añño “karohi karohi” iccevaṃ bravīti, atha vā karontaṃ payojayati [M 0.0227] = kāreti, kārayati, kārāpeti, kārā payati. Ye keci karonti, te aññe “karotha karotha” iccevaṃ bruvanti = kārenti, kārayanti, kārāpenti, kārāpayanti. Yo koci pacati, taṃ añño “pacāhi pacāhi”iccevaṃ bravīti, atha vā pacantaṃ payojayati = pāceti, pācayati, pācāpeti, pācāpayati. Ye keci pacanti, te aññe “pacatha pacatha” iccevaṃ bruvanti = pācenti, pācayanti, pācāpenti. Pācāpayanti. Evaṃ bhaṇeti, bhaṇayati, bhaṇāpeti, bhaṇāpayati. Bhaṇenti, bhaṇayanti, bhaṇāpenti, bhaṇāpayanti. Tathariva aññepi yojetabbā.

If someone does something, another says to him, 'Do, do,' or otherwise engages the one who is doing, the result is: 'kāreti', 'kārayati', 'kārāpeti', 'kārāpayati'. If some people do something, others say to them, 'Do, do,' thus they say: 'kārenti', 'kārayanti', 'kārāpenti', 'kārāpayanti'. If someone cooks, another says to him, 'Cook, cook,' or otherwise engages the one who is cooking, the result is: 'pāceti', 'pācayati', 'pācāpeti', 'pācāpayati'. If some people cook, others say to them, 'Cook, cook,' thus they say: 'pācenti', 'pācayanti', 'pācāpenti', 'pācāpayanti'. Similarly: 'bhaṇeti', 'bhaṇayati', 'bhaṇāpeti', 'bhaṇāpayati'; 'bhaṇenti', 'bhaṇayanti', 'bhaṇāpenti', 'bhaṇāpayanti'. In the same way, other examples are to be applied.

Hetvattheti kimatthaṃ? Karoti, pacati.

For what purpose is 'hetvatthe' (in the sense of cause)? He does, he cooks.

Atthaggahaṇena alapaccayo hoti, jotalati.

By the inclusion of 'attha' (sense), the suffix 'ala' also occurs, as in 'jotalati'.

439, 539. Dhāturūpe nāmasmā ṇayo ca.

439, 539. And the suffix ṇaya occurs after a nominal stem when it has the form of a verbal root.

Tasmā nāmasmā ṇayapaccayo hoti kāritasañño ca dhāturūpe sati.

The suffix ṇaya occurs after a nominal stem, and it is designated 'kārita' (causative), when the nominal stem takes on the form of a verbal root.

Hatthinā atikkamati maggaṃ = atihatthayati, vīṇāya upagāyati gītaṃ = upavīṇayati, daḷhaṃ karoti vīriyaṃ [M 0.0228] = daḷhayati, visuddhā hoti ratti = visuddhayati.

He crosses the path with an elephant: 'atihatthayati'; he accompanies a song with a lute: 'upavīṇayati'; he makes his effort firm: 'daḷhayati'; the night becomes pure: 'visuddhayati'.

Caggahaṇena āra ālaiccete paccayā honti. Santaṃ karoti = santārati, upakkamaṃ karoti = upakkamālati.

By the inclusion of 'ca' (and), the suffixes 'āra' and 'āla' also occur. He makes peace: 'santārati'; he makes an effort: 'upakkamālati'.

440, 445. Bhāvakammesu yo.

440, 445. The suffix 'ya' occurs in the impersonal and passive voices.

Sabbehi dhātūhi bhāvakammesu yapaccayo hoti.

The suffix 'ya' occurs after all verbal roots in the impersonal and passive voices.

Ṭhīyate, bujjhate, paccate, labbhate, karīyate, yujjate, uccate.

It is stood, it is understood, it is cooked, it is obtained, it is done, it is yoked, it is said.

Bhāvakammesūti kimatthaṃ? Karoti, pacati, paṭhati.

For what purpose is 'bhāvakammesu' (in the impersonal and passive voices)? He does, he cooks, he recites.

441, 447. Tassa cavaggayakāravakārattaṃ sadhātvantassa.

441, 447. That suffix, together with the final consonant of the root, is changed into a letter of the ca-group, ya, or va.

Tassa yapaccayassa cavaggayakāravakārattaṃ hoti dhātūnaṃ antena saha yathāsambhavaṃ.

That suffix 'ya', together with the final consonant of the roots, is changed into a letter of the ca-group, ya, or va, as is appropriate.

Vuccate, vuccante, uccate, uccante, paccate, paccante. Majjate, majjante, yujjate, yujjante. Bujjhate, bujjhante, kujjhate, kujjhante, ujjhate, ujjhante. Haññate, haññante. Kayyate, kayyante. Dibbate, dibbante.

It is said, they are said; it is said, they are said; it is cooked, they are cooked. It is cleansed, they are cleansed; it is yoked, they are yoked. It is understood, they are understood; one is angered, they are angered; it is abandoned, they are abandoned. It is struck, they are struck. It is done, they are done. It is played, they are played.

442, 448. Ivaṇṇāgamo [M 0.0229] vā.

442, 448. And optionally the augment 'i'.

Sabbehi dhātūhi yamhi paccaye, pare ivaṇṇāgamo hoti vā.

After all verbal roots, when the suffix 'ya' follows, the augment 'i' optionally occurs.

Karīyate, karīyati, gacchīyate, gacchīyati.

It is done (karīyate), it is done (karīyati); it is gone to (gacchīyate), it is gone to (gacchīyati).

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Kayyate.

For what purpose is 'vā' (optionally)? Kayyate.

443, 449. Pubbarūpañca.

443, 449. And assimilation to the preceding form.

Sabbehi dhātūhi yapaccayo pubbarūpamāpajjate vā.

After all verbal roots, the suffix 'ya' optionally assimilates to the preceding form.

Vuḍḍhate, phallate, dammate, sakkate, labbhate, dissate.

It is increased, it bears fruit, it is tamed, it is honored, it is obtained, it is seen.

444, 501. Tathā kattari ca.

444, 501. And similarly in the active voice.

Yathā heṭṭhā bhāvakammesu yapaccayassa ādeso hoti tathā kattaripi yapaccayassa ādeso kātabbo.

Just as the substitution of the suffix 'ya' occurs previously in the impersonal and passive voices, so too the substitution of the suffix 'ya' is to be made in the active voice.

Bujjhati, vijjhati, maññati, sibbati.

He understands, he pierces, he thinks, he sews.

445, 433. Bhūvādito a.

445, 433. From the root group beginning with bhū, the suffix a.

Bhūiccevamādito dhātugaṇato apaccayo hoti kattari.

From the root group beginning with bhū, the suffix a occurs in the active voice.

Bhavati[M 0.0230], paṭhati, pacati, jayati.

He becomes, he reads, he cooks, he conquers.

446, 509. Rudhādito niggahitapubbañca.

446, 509. From the root group beginning with rudh, and with a preceding niggahīta.

Rudhaiccevamādito dhātugaṇato apaccayo hoti kattari, pubbe niggahitāgamo hoti.

From the root group beginning with rudh, the suffix a occurs in the active voice, and a niggahīta augment occurs before it.

Rundhati, chindati, bhindati.

He obstructs, he cuts, he breaks.

Caggahaṇena i ī e oiccete paccayā honti niggahitapubbañca.

By the inclusion of ca, these suffixes—i, ī, e, and o—occur, and also with a preceding niggahīta.

Rundhiti, rundhīti, rundheti, rundhoti, sumbhoti, parisumbhoti.

He obstructs, he obstructs, he obstructs, he obstructs, he destroys, he utterly destroys.

447, 510. Divādito yo.

447, 510. From the root group beginning with div, the suffix ya.

Divuiccevamādito dhātugaṇato yapaccayo hoti kattari.

From the root group beginning with div, the suffix ya occurs in the active voice.

Dibbati, thibbati, yujjhati, vijjhati, bujjhati.

He shines, he stiffens, he fights, he pierces, he understands.

448, 512. Svādito ṇu ṇā uṇā ca.

448, 512. From the root group beginning with su, the suffixes ṇu, ṇā, and uṇā.

Suiccevamādito dhātugaṇato ṇu ṇā u ṇāiccete paccayā honti kattari.

From the root group beginning with su, these suffixes—ṇu, ṇā, u, and ṇā—occur in the active voice.

Abhisuṇoti[M 0.0231], abhisuṇāti, saṃvuṇoti, saṃvuṇāti, āvuṇoti, āvuṇāti, pāpuṇoti, pāpuṇāti.

He hears, he hears; he covers, he covers; he covers, he covers; he reaches, he reaches.

449, 513. Kiyādito nā.

449, 513. From the root group beginning with kī, the suffix ṇā.

Kīiccevamādito dhātugaṇato nāpaccayo hoti kattari.

From the root group beginning with kī, the suffix ṇā occurs in the active voice.

Kiṇāti, jināti, dhunāti, munāti, lunāti, punāti.

He buys, he conquers, he shakes, he knows, he cuts, he purifies.

450, 517. Gahādito ppa ṇhā.

450, 517. From the root group beginning with gah, the suffixes ppa and ṇhā.

Gahaiccevamādito dhātugaṇato ppaṇhāiccete paccayā honti kattari.

From the root group beginning with gah, these suffixes—ppa and ṇhā—occur in the active voice.

Gheppati, gaṇhāti.

He takes, he grasps.

451, 520. Tanādito oyirā.

451, 520. From the root group beginning with tan, the suffixes o and yira.

Tanuiccevamādito dhātugaṇato o yiraiccete paccayā honti kattari.

From the root group beginning with tanu, these suffixes—o and yira—occur in the active voice.

Tanoti[M 0.0232], tanohi, karoti, karohi, kayi rati, kayirāhi.

He extends, you extend; he does, you do; he does, you do.

452, 525. Curādito, ṇe ṇayā.

452, 525. From the root group beginning with cur, the suffixes ṇe and ṇaya.

Curaiccevamādito dhātugaṇato ṇe ṇayaiccete paccayā honti kattari, kāritasaññā ca.

From the root group beginning with cur, these suffixes—ṇe and ṇaya—occur in the active voice, and there is also the designation of the causative.

Coreti, corayati, cinteti, cintayati, manteti, mantayati.

He steals, he steals; he thinks, he thinks; he advises, he advises.

453, 444. Attanopadāni bhāve ca kammani.

453, 444. Attanopada endings occur in the impersonal and passive voices.

Bhāve ca kammani ca attanopadāni honti.

Attanopada endings occur in the impersonal and passive voices.

Uccate, uccante, majjate, majjante, yujjate, yujjante, kujjhate, kujjhante, labbhate, labbhante, kayyate, kayyante.

It is said, they are said; it is cleansed, they are cleansed; it is fought, they are fought; one is angry, they are angry; it is obtained, they are obtained; it is done, they are done.

454, 440. Kattari ca.

454, 440. And in the active voice.

Kattari ca attanopadāni honti.

And attanopada endings occur in the active voice.

Maññate, rocate, socate, bujjhate, jāyate.

He thinks, he likes, he grieves, he understands, he is born.

455, 530. Dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo.

455, 530. Verb endings after root suffixes.

Dhātuniddiṭṭhehi paccayehi khādikāritantehi vibhattiyo honti.

Verb endings occur after the suffixes specified for roots, such as the desiderative and causative suffixes.

Titikkhati[M 0.0233], jigucchati, vīmaṃsati, samuddāyati, puttīyati, kāreti, pāceti.

He endures, he is disgusted, he investigates, he makes a loud sound, he desires a son, he causes to do, he causes to cook.

456, 430. Kattari parassapadaṃ.

456, 430. Parassapada in the active voice.

Kattari parassapadaṃ hoti.

Parassapada endings occur in the active voice.

Karoti, pacati, paṭhati, gacchati.

He does, he cooks, he reads, he goes.

457, 424. Bhūvādayo dhātavo.

457, 424. The roots beginning with bhū.

Bhūiccevamādayo ye saddagaṇā, te dhātusaññā honti.

Those groups of words beginning with 'bhū', and so on, are designated as roots.

Bhavati, bhavanti, carati, caranti, pacati, pacanti, cintayati, cintayanti, hoti, honti, gacchati, gacchanti.

He becomes, they become; he moves, they move; he cooks, they cook; he thinks, they think; he is, they are; he goes, they go.

Iti ākhyātakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus the second section in the chapter on verbs.

Tatiyakaṇḍa

The Third Section

458, 461. Kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo.

458, 461. Sometimes, the reduplication of initial monosyllabic sounds.

Ādibhūtānaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ ekassarānaṃ kvaci dvebhāvo hoti.

Sometimes, a reduplication occurs for initial monosyllabic sounds.

Titikkhati[M 0.0234], jigucchati, tikicchati, vīmaṃsati, bubhukkhati, pivāsati, daddallati, dadāti, jahāti, caṅkamati.

He endures, he despises, he treats, he investigates, he is hungry, he is thirsty, he shines brightly, he gives, he abandons, he walks back and forth.

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Kampati, calati.

Why 'sometimes'? He trembles, he moves.

459, 462. Pubbo’bbhāso.

459, 462. The prior part is the 'abbhāsa'.

Dvebhūtassa dhātussa yo pubbo, so abbhāsasañño hoti.

Of a reduplicated root, the prior part is designated the 'abbhāsa'.

Dadhāti, dadāti, babhūva.

Dadhāti, dadāti, babhūva.

460, 506. Rasso.

460, 506. Shortening.

Abbhāse vattamānassa sarassa rasso hoti. Dadhāti, jahāti.

The vowel in the 'abbhāsa' becomes short. Dadhāti, jahāti.

461, 464. Dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā.

461, 464. The second and fourth consonants become the first and third.

Abbhāsagatānaṃ dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā honti.

The second and fourth consonants in the 'abbhāsa' become the first and third respectively.

Ciccheda, bubhukkhati, babhūva, dadhāti.

Ciccheda, bubhukkhati, babhūva, dadhāti.

462, 476. Kavaggassa cavaggo.

462, 476. The 'ka' group becomes the 'ca' group.

Abbhāse vattamānassa kavaggassa ca vaggo hoti.

In the 'abbhāsa', the 'ka' group becomes the 'ca' group.

Cikicchati[M 0.0235], jigucchati, jighacchati, jigīsati, jaṅgamati, caṅkamati.

He treats, he despises, he is hungry, he wishes to conquer, he walks about, he walks back and forth.

463, 532. Mānakitānaṃ vatattaṃ vā.
