463, 532. For the roots 'māna' and 'kita', the initial consonants are optionally substituted by 'v' and 't' respectively.

Mānakitaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ abbhāsagatānaṃ vakāra takārattaṃ hoti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

For these roots, `māna` and `kita`, when reduplicated, there is optionally a transformation to `va` and `ta` respectively.

Vīmaṃsati, tikicchati.

He investigates; he treats or heals.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Cikicchati.

For what purpose is `vā` stated? `Cikicchati`.

464, 504. Hassa jo.

Of `ha`, there is `ja`.

Abbhāse vattamānassa hakārassa jo hoti.

The sound `ha` present in the reduplicated syllable becomes `ja`.

Jahāti, juhvati, juhoti, jahāra.

He abandons; he sacrifices; he offers; he carried.

465, 463. Antassivaṇṇākāro vā.

The final vowel of the reduplicated syllable is optionally `i` or `a`.

Abbhāsassa antassa ivaṇṇo hoti, akāro vā.

The final vowel of the reduplicated syllable becomes `i` or `a`.

Jigucchati, pivāsati, vīmaṃsati, jighacchati, babhūva, dadhāti.

He despises; he is thirsty; he investigates; he is hungry; he became; he places.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Bubhukkhati.

For what purpose is `vā` stated? `Bubhukkhati`.

466, 489. Niggahitañca[M 0.0236].

And `niggahīta`.

Abbhāsassa ante niggahitāgamo hoti vā.

At the end of the reduplicated syllable, the `niggahīta` augment optionally occurs.

Caṅkamati, cañcalati, jaṅgamati.

He walks back and forth; he trembles; he moves.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Pivāsati, daddallati.

For what purpose is `vā` stated? He desires to drink; he glows.

467, 533. Tato pāmānānaṃ vā maṃ sesu.

After that, `pā` and `māna` become `vā` and `maṃ` respectively, when the desiderative suffixes follow.

Tato abbhāsato pāmānaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ vāmaṃiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ sapaccaye pare.

After that reduplication, for these roots, `pā` and `māna`, the substitutions `vā` and `maṃ` occur respectively, when the `sa` affix follows.

Pivāsati, vīmaṃsati.

He is thirsty; he investigates.

468, 462. Ṭhā tiṭṭho.

For `ṭhā`, there is `tiṭṭha`.

Ṭhāiccetassa dhātussa tiṭṭhādeso hoti vā.

For this root `ṭhā`, the substitution `tiṭṭha` optionally occurs.

Tiṭṭhati, tiṭṭhatu, tiṭṭheyya, tiṭṭheyyuṃ.

He stands; let him stand; he would stand; they would stand.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Ṭhāti.

For what purpose is `vā` stated? `Ṭhāti`.

469, 494. Pā pivo.

For `pā`, there is `piva`.

Pāiccetassa dhātussa pivādeso hoti vā.

For this root `pā`, the substitution `piva` optionally occurs.

Pivati, pivatu, piveyya, piveyyuṃ.

He drinks; let him drink; he might drink; they might drink.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Pāti.

For what purpose is `vā` stated? `Pāti`.

470, 514. Ñāssa [M 0.0237] jā jaṃ nā.

`Ñā` becomes `jā`, `jaṃ`, or `nā`.

Ñāiccetassa dhātussa jā jaṃ nāādesā honti vā.

For this root `ñā`, the substitutions `jā`, `jaṃ`, and `nā` optionally occur.

Jānāti, jāneyya, jāniyā, jaññā, nāyati.

He knows; he should know; he would know; he may know; he knows.

471, 483. Disassa passa dissa dakkhā vā.

`Dis` optionally becomes `passa`, `dissa`, or `dakkha`.

Disaiccetassa dhātussa passa dissa dakkhaiccete ādesā honti vā.

For this root `dis`, the substitutions `passa`, `dissa`, and `dakkha` optionally occur.

Passati, dissati, dakkhati, adakkha.

He sees, it is seen, he will see, he saw.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Addasa.

Why is 'vā' stated? Addasa.

472, 531. Byañjanantassa co chapaccayesu ca.

472, 531. For a root ending in a consonant, 'c' is also substituted when 'cha' affixes follow.

Byañjanantassa dhātussa co hoti chapaccayesu paresu.

For a root ending in a consonant, 'c' occurs when 'cha' affixes follow.

Jigucchati, tikicchati, jighacchati.

He despises, he treats, he is hungry.

473, 529. Ko khe ca.

473, 529. Also 'k' before 'kha'.

Byañjanantassa dhātussa ko hoti khapaccaye pare.

For a root ending in a consonant, 'k' occurs when a 'kha' affix follows.

Titikkhati[M 0.0238], bubhukkhati.

He tolerates, he is hungry.

474, 535. Harassa gīse.

474, 535. For 'hara', 'gī' is substituted before the 'sa' affix.

Haraiccetassa dhātussa sabbasseva gīādeso hoti sapaccaye pare.

For this entire root 'hara', the substitution 'gī' occurs when the 'sa' affix follows.

Jigīsati.

He wishes to conquer.

475, 565. Brūbhūnamāhabhūvā parokkhāyaṃ.

475, 565. For 'brū' and 'bhū', 'āha' and 'bhūva' are substituted in the perfect tense.

Brūbhūiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ āhabhūvaiccete ādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ parokkhāyaṃ vibhattiyaṃ.

For these roots 'brū' and 'bhū,' the substitutions 'āha' and 'bhūva' occur respectively in the perfect tense inflection.

Āha, āhu, babhūva, babhūvu.

Āha, āhu, babhūva, babhūvu. He said, they said, he became, they became.

Parokkhāyamiti kimatthaṃ? Abracuṃ.

Why is 'in the perfect tense' stated? Abracuṃ.

476, 442. Gamissanto ccho vā sabbāsu.

476, 442. The final letter of 'gam' optionally becomes 'cch' in all inflections.

Gamuiccetassa dhātussa anto makāro ccho hoti vā sabbāsu paccayavibhattīsu.

For this root 'gamu,' the final letter 'm' optionally becomes 'cch' in all affixes and inflections.

Gacchamāno, gacchanto. Gacchati, gameti. Gacchatu, gametu. Gaccheyya. Gameyya. Agacchā, agamā. Agacchī, agamī. Gacchissati, gamissati. Agacchissā, agamissā.

Gacchamāno, gacchanto. Gacchati, gameti. Gacchatu, gametu. Gaccheyya, gameyya. Agacchā, agamā. Agacchī, agamī. Gacchissati, gamissati. Agacchissā, agamissā.

Gamisseti [M 0.0239] kimatthaṃ? Icchati.

Why is 'gamu' stated? Icchati.

477, 479. Vacassajjatanimhi makāro o.

477, 479. Of 'vac', the 'a' becomes 'o' in the aorist.

Vacaiccetassa dhātussa akāro ottamāpajjate ajjatanimhi vibhattimhi.

Of this root 'vac', the vowel 'a' becomes 'o' in the aorist inflection.

Avoca. Avocuṃ.

He said. They said.

Ajjatanimhīti kimatthaṃ? Avaca, avacū.

Why is 'in the aorist' stated? Avaca, avacū.

478, 438. Akāro dīghaṃ hi mi mesu.

478, 438. The vowel 'a' is lengthened before 'hi', 'mi', and 'ma'.

Akāro dīghamāpajjate himimaiccetesu vibhattīsu.

The vowel 'a' becomes long before these inflections: 'hi', 'mi', and 'ma'.

Gacchāhi, gacchāmi, gacchāma, gacchāmhe.

Gacchāhi, gacchāmi, gacchāma, gacchāmhe.

Mikāraggahaṇena hivibhattimhi akāro kvaci na dīghamāpajjate. Gacchahi.

By the inclusion of 'mi', the vowel 'a' is sometimes not lengthened in the 'hi' inflection. Gacchahi.

479, 452. Ha lopaṃ vā.

479, 452. 'Hi' is optionally elided.

Hivibhatti lopamāpajjate vā.

The 'hi' inflection is optionally elided.

Gaccha, gacchāhi, gama, gamāhi, gamaya, gamayāhi.

Gaccha, gacchāhi, gama, gamāhi, gamaya, gamayāhi.

Hīti kimatthaṃ? Gacchati, gamayati.

For what purpose is 'hi'? Gacchati, gamayati.

480, 490. Hotissarehohe bhavissantimhissassa ca.

For the root hū, in the future tense, the vowel becomes e or oha; and also for ssa.

Hūiccetassa [M 0.0240] dhātussa saro e ha oha ettamāpajja te bhavissantimhi, ssassa ca lopo hoti vā.

For this root, hū, the vowel becomes 'e' or 'oha' in the future tense, and 'ssa' optionally undergoes elision.

Hehiti, hehinti, hohiti, hohinti, heti, henti, hehissati, hehissanti, hohissati, hohissanti, hessati, hessanti.

He will be, they will be; he will be, they will be; he will be, they will be; he will be, they will be; he will be, they will be; he will be, they will be.

Hūti kimatthaṃ? Bhavissati, bhavissanti.

For what purpose is 'hū' mentioned? Bhavissati, bhavissanti.

Bhavissantimhīti kimatthaṃ? Hoti.

Why is 'in the future tense' specified? Hoti.

481, 524. Karassa sapaccayassa kāho.

For the root kara with its affix, kāha is the substitute.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa sapaccayassa kāhādeso hoti vā bhavissantimhi vibhattimhi, sassa ca niccaṃ lopo hoti.

For this root, kara, with its affix, the substitution 'kāha' optionally occurs in the future tense inflection, and 'ssa' always undergoes elision.

Kāhati, kāhiti, kāhasi, kāhisi, kāhāmi, kāhāma.

He will do, he will do; you will do, you will do; I will do, we will do.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Karissati, karissanti.

For what purpose is 'vā'? Karissati, karissanti.

Sapaccayaggahaṇena aññehipi bhavissantiyā vibhattiyā khāmi khāma chāmi chāmaiccādayo ādesā honti. Vakkhāmi, vakkhāma, vacchāmi, vacchāma.

By the inclusion of 'sapaccaya', other substitutions such as khāmi, khāma, chāmi, chāma, etc., also occur for the future tense inflection. Vakkhāmi, vakkhāma, vacchāmi, vacchāma.

Iti ākhyātakappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section of the chapter on verbs.

Catutthakaṇḍa

The Fourth Section

482, 508. Dādantassaṃ [M 0.0241] mi mesu.

Of the root dā, the final vowel becomes aṃ before mi and me.

Dāiccetassa dhātussa antassa aṃ hoti mimaiccetesu.

For this root 'dā', its final vowel becomes 'aṃ' when the suffixes 'mi' and 'me' follow.

Dammi, damma.

Dammi, damma.

483, 527. Asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite.

For a root not ending in a conjunct consonant, there is strengthening in the causative.

Asaṃyogantassa dhātussa kārite vuddhi hoti.

For a root not ending in a conjunct consonant, strengthening occurs in the causative.

Kāreti, kārenti, kārayati, kārayanti, kārāpeti, kārāpenti, kārāpayati, kārāpayanti.

He causes to do, they cause to do; he causes to do, they cause to do; he causes another to do, they cause another to do; he causes another to do, they cause another to do.

Asaṃyogantasseti kimatthaṃ? Cintayati, mantayati.

Why is 'not ending in a conjunct consonant' specified? Cintayati, mantayati.

484, 542. Ghaṭādīnaṃ vā.

For ghaṭa and other roots, optionally.

Ghaṭādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ asaṃyogantānaṃ vuddhi hoti vā kārite.

For roots of the ghaṭa group, which do not end in a conjunct consonant, strengthening occurs optionally in the causative.

Ghāṭeti, ghaṭeti, ghāṭayati, ghaṭayati, ghāṭāpeti, ghaṭāpeti, ghāṭāpayati, ghaṭāpayati, gāmeti, gameti, gāmayati, gamayati, gāmāpeti, gamāpeti. Gāmāpayati, gamāpayati.

He causes to strive, he causes to strive; he causes to strive, he causes to strive; he causes another to strive, he causes another to strive; he causes another to strive, he causes another to strive. He causes to go, he causes to go; he causes to go, he causes to go; he causes another to go, he causes another to go; he causes another to go, he causes another to go.

Ghaṭādīnamiti kimatthaṃ? Kāreti.

Why is 'ghaṭa and other roots' specified? Kāreti.

485, 434. Aññesu [M 0.0242] ca.

And in other cases.

Aññesu ca paccayesu sabbesaṃ dhātūnaṃ asaṃyogantānaṃ vuddhi hoti.

And with other suffixes, strengthening occurs for all roots not ending in a conjunct consonant.

Jayati, hoti, bhavati.

Jayati, hoti, bhavati.

Caggahaṇena ṇupaccayassāpi vuddhi hoti. Abhisuṇoti.

By the inclusion of 'ca', strengthening also occurs before the 'ṇu' suffix. Example: Abhisuṇoti.

486, 543. Guha dusānaṃ dīghaṃ.

For guh and dus, the vowel is lengthened.

Guha dusaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ saro dīghamāpajjate kārite.

For these roots, 'guh' and 'dus', the vowel becomes long in the causative.

Gūhayati, dūsayati.

He conceals, he corrupts.

487, 478. Vaca vasa vahādīnamukāro vassa ye.

For roots such as 'vac', 'vas', 'vah', and so forth, 'v' becomes 'u' when 'ya' follows.

Vaca vasa vahaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ vakārassa ukāro hoti yapaccaye pare.

For roots such as 'vac', 'vas', 'vah', and so forth, the letter 'v' is replaced by 'u' when the suffix 'ya' follows.

Uccate, vuccati, gussati, vuyhati.

It is said, it is said, it is muttered, it is carried.

488, 481. Ha vipariyayo lo vā.

For 'h', there is transposition, or optionally, elision.

Hakārassa vipariyayo hoti yapaccaye pare, yapaccayassa ca lo hoti vā.

Transposition of the letter 'h' occurs when the suffix 'ya' follows, and the suffix 'ya' is optionally elided.

Vulhati, vuyhati.

It is carried, it is carried.

489, 519. Gahassa [M 0.0243] ghe ppe.

For 'gah', 'ghe' is substituted when 'ppa' follows.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa ghekāro hoti ppapaccaye pare.

For that root 'gah', the whole root becomes 'ghe' when the suffix 'ppa' follows.

Gheppati.

It is taken.

490, 518. Halo po ṇhāmhi.

'h' is elided when 'ṇhā' follows.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa hakārassa lopo hoti ṇhāmhi paccaye pare.

When the suffix 'ṇhā' follows, the 'h' of the root 'gah' is elided.

Gaṇhāti.

He grasps.

491, 523. Karassa kāsattamajjatanimhi.

For 'kar', 'kās' is substituted in the aorist.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa kāsattaṃ hoti vā ajjatanimhi vibhattimhi.

For that root 'kar', the whole root optionally becomes 'kās' in the aorist tense endings.

Akāsi, akāsuṃ. Akari, akaruṃ.

He did, they did. He did, they did.

Kāsattamitibhāvaniddesena aññatthāpi sāgamo hoti. Ahosi, adāsi.

By the designation 'kāsattaṃ' as a state, the 's' augment also occurs elsewhere. Examples: He was, he gave.

492, 499. Asasmā mimānaṃ mhimhā’ ntalopo ca.

From 'as', 'mhi' and 'mhā' are substituted for 'mi' and 'ma', and there is elision of the final letter of the root.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā mimaiccetesaṃ vibhattīnaṃ mhimhādesā honti vā, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'as', the substitutions 'mhi' and 'mhā' optionally occur for the suffixes 'mi' and 'ma', and there is elision of the final letter of the root.

Amhi[M 0.0244], amha, asmi, asma.

I am, we are, I am, we are.

493, 498. Thassa tthattaṃ.

For 'tha', 'ttha' is substituted.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā thassa vibhattissa tthattaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'as', the suffix 'tha' becomes 'ttha', and there is elision of the final letter of the root.

Attha.

You are.

494, 495. Tissa tthittaṃ.

For 'ti', 'tthi' is substituted.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā tissa vibhattissa tthittaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'as', the suffix 'ti' becomes 'tthi', and there is elision of the final letter of the root.

Atthi.

There is.

495, 500. Tussa tthuttaṃ.

For 'tu', 'tthu' is substituted.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā tussa vibhattissa tthuttaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'as', the suffix 'tu' becomes 'tthu', and there is elision of the final letter of the root.

Atthu.

Let there be.

496, 497. Simhi ca.

And when 'si' follows.

Asasseva dhātussa simhi vibhattimhi antassa lopo ca hoti.

For the root 'as' itself, when the 'si' suffix follows, there is also elision of the final letter.

Ko nu tvamasi mārisa.

Who are you, venerable sir?

497, 477. Labhasmā [M 0.0245] ī iṃnaṃ ttha tthaṃ.

From 'labh', 'ttha' and 'tthaṃ' are substituted for 'ī' and 'iṃ'.

Labhaiccetāya dhātuyā ī iṃnaṃ vibhattīnaṃ ttha tthaṃādesā honti, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'labh', the substitutions 'ttha' and 'tthaṃ' occur for the suffixes 'ī' and 'iṃ', and there is also elision of the final vowel of the root.

Alattha, alatthaṃ.

He obtained, I obtained.

498, 480. Kusasmā dī cchi.

From 'kus', 'cchi' is substituted for 'ī'.

Kusaiccetāya dhātuyā īvibhattissa cchihoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca.

For that root 'kus', the 'ī' suffix becomes 'cchi', and there is also elision of the final letter of the root.

Akkocchi.

He insulted.

499, 507. Dādhātussa dajjaṃ.

For the root 'dā', 'dajja' is substituted.

Dāiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa dajjādeso hoti vā.

For that root 'dā', the entire root optionally becomes 'dajja'.

Dajjāmi, dajjeyya, dadāmi, dadeyya.

I may give, he may give, I give, he may give.

500, 486. Vadassa vajjaṃ.

For 'vad', 'vajja' is substituted.

Vadaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa vajjādeso hoti vā.

For that root 'vad', the entire root optionally becomes 'vajja'.

Vajjāmi, vajjeyya, vadāmi, vadeyya.

I may speak, he may speak, I speak, he may speak.

501, 443. Gamissa [M 0.0246] ghammaṃ.

For 'gam', 'ghamma' is substituted.

Gamuiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa ghammādeso hoti vā.

For that root 'gam', the entire root optionally becomes 'ghamma'.

Ghammatu. Ghammāhi, ghammāmi.

Let him go. Go. Let me go.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Gacchatu, gacchāhi, gacchāmi.

Why 'optionally'? (Examples without substitution:) Let him go, go, let me go.

502, 493. Yamhi dā dhā mā ṭhā hā pā mahamathādīnamī.

When the 'ya' suffix follows, 'ī' is substituted for roots such as 'dā', 'dhā', 'mā', 'ṭhā', 'hā', 'pā', 'maha', and 'matha'.

Yamhi paccaye pare dā dhā mā ṭhā hā pā maha matha iccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto īkāramāpajjate.

When the 'ya' suffix follows, the final vowel of roots such as 'dā', 'dhā', 'mā', 'ṭhā', 'hā', 'pā', 'maha', and 'matha' becomes 'ī'.

Dīyati, dhīyati, mīyati, ṭhīyati, hīyati, pīyati, mahīyati, mathīyati.

Is given, is held, is measured, is stood, is diminished, is drunk, is honored, is churned.

503, 485. Yajassādissi.

For 'yaj', 'i' is substituted for the initial vowel.

Yajaiccetassa dhātussa ādissa ikārādeso hoti yapaccaye pare.

For that root 'yaj', the substitution 'i' occurs for the initial vowel when the 'ya' suffix follows.

Ijjate mayā buddho.

The Buddha is revered by me.

504, 470. Sabbato uṃ iṃsu.

From all roots, 'uṃ' becomes 'iṃsu'.

Sabbehi dhātūhi uṃvibhattissa iṃsuādeso hoti.

From all roots, the 'uṃ' suffix becomes 'iṃsu'.

Upasaṅkamiṃsu[M 0.0247], nisīdiṃsu.

They approached, they sat down.

505, 482. Jara marānaṃ jīra jiyya miyyā vā.

For 'jar' and 'mar', 'jīra', 'jiyya', and 'miyyā' are optionally substituted.

Jara mara iccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ jīra jiyya miyyādesā honti vā.

For these roots 'jar' and 'mar', the substitutions 'jīra', 'jiyya', and 'miyyā' optionally occur.

Jīrati, jīranti, jiyyati, jiyyanti, miyyati, miyyanti, marati, maranti.

It ages, they age; it decays, they decay; it dies, they die; it dies, they die.

506, 496. Sabbatthā’ sassādilopo ca.

And everywhere, elision of the initial vowel of the root as.

Sabbattha vibhattipaccayesu asaiccetassa dhātussa ādissa lopo hoti vā.

In all inflections and suffixes, the initial vowel of this root as is optionally elided.

Siyā, santi, sante, samāno.

He may be, they are, being, being.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Asi.

Why 'optionally'? (Example without elision:) You are.

507, 501. Asabbadhātuke bhū.

Before an asabbadhātuka affix, bhū.

Asasseva dhātussa bhūhoti vā asabbadhātuke.

For this very root as, bhū is optionally substituted before an asabbadhātuka affix.

Bhavissati. Bhavissanti.

He will be, they will be.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Āsuṃ.

Why 'optionally'? (Example without substitution:) They were.

508, 515. Eyyassa [M 0.0248] ñāto iyā ñā.

After the root ñā, iyā and ñā are substituted for the suffix eyya.

Eyyassa vibhattissa ñāiccetāya dhātuyā parassa iyā ñāādesā honti vā.

For the inflection eyya, when it follows this root ñā, the substitutions iyā and ñā optionally occur.

Jāniyā, jaññā.

One may know, one may know.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Jāneyya.

Why 'optionally'? (Example without substitution:) One may know.

509, 516. Nāssa lopo yakārattaṃ.

For the suffix nā, there is elision and it becomes y.

Ñāiccetāya dhātuyā parassa nāpaccayassa lopo hoti vā, yakārattañca.

Following this root ñā, the suffix nā is optionally elided, and also becomes y.

Jaññā, nāyati.

May know, he leads.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Jānāti.

Why 'optionally'? (Example without elision/substitution:) He knows.

510, 487. Lopañcettamakāro.

For the a-suffix, there is elision and also substitution by e.

Akārapaccayo lopamāpajjate, ettañca hoti vā.

The a-suffix undergoes elision, and also optionally becomes e.

Vajjemi, vademi, vajjāmi, vadāmi.

I speak, I speak, I speak, I speak.

511, 521. Uttamokāro.

The o-suffix becomes u.

Okārapaccayo uttamāpajjate vā.

The o-suffix is optionally changed to u.

Kurute, karoti.

He does, he does.

Okāroti [M 0.0249] kimatthaṃ? Hoti.

Why 'okāro'? (Example where it does not apply:) Hoti (he is).

512, 522. Karassākāro ca.

And the a of kar also becomes u.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa akāro uttamāpajjate vā.

For this root kar, the a optionally becomes u.

Kurute, taroti, tubbanti, kayirati.

He does, he crosses over, they become hollow, it is made.

Karasseti kimatthaṃ? Sarati, marati.

Why 'karassa'? (Examples where it does not apply:) He remembers, he dies.

513, 435. O ava sare.

'o' becomes 'ava' when a vowel follows.

Okārassa dhātvantassa sare pare avādeso hoti.

For an o at the end of a root, when a vowel follows, the substitution ava occurs.

Cavati. Bhavati.

He ceases, he becomes.

Oti kimatthaṃ? Jayati.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'o'? He conquers.

514, 491. E aya.

'E' becomes 'aya'.

Ekārassa dhātvantassa sare pare ayādeso hoti.

For a root ending in 'e', when a vowel follows, 'aya' is substituted.

Nayati, jayati.

He leads, he conquers.

515, 541. Te [M 0.0250] āvāyā kārite.

Those two, 'o' and 'e', become 'āva' and 'āya' respectively before the causative suffix.

Te o eiccete āva āyādese pāpuṇanti kārite.

Those two, 'o' and 'e', attain the substitutions 'āva' and 'āya' respectively before the causative suffix.

Lāveti, nāyeti.

He causes to cut, he causes to lead.

Yogavibhāgena aññasmimpi ekārassa āyādeso hoti. Gāyati, gāyanti.

By separation of the rule, the 'e' of other roots also becomes 'āya'. For example: He sings, they sing.

516, 466. Ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhi.

The augment 'i' [occurs] before an asabbadhātuka affix.

Sabbasmiṃ asabbadhātukamhi ikārāgamo hoti.

Before every asabbadhātuka affix, the augment 'i' occurs.

Gamissati, karissati, labhissati, pacissati.

He will go, he will do, he will obtain, he will cook.

Asabbadhātukamhīti kimatthaṃ? Gacchati, karoti, labhati, pacati.

What is the purpose of [the phrase] 'before an asabbadhātuka affix'? [As in:] He goes, he does, he obtains, he cooks.

517, 488. Kvaci dhātuvibhattipaccayānaṃ dīgha viparītādesalopāgamā ca.

Sometimes, for roots, endings, and suffixes, there are also lengthenings, alterations, substitutions, elisions, and augmentations.

Idha ākhyāte aniddiṭṭhesu sādhanesu kvaci dhātuvibhattipaccayānaṃ dīghaviparītādesalopāgamaiccetāni kāriyāni jinavacanānurūpāni kātabbāni.

Here in the chapter on verbs, for derivations not explicitly stated, these operations—namely lengthening, alteration, substitution, elision, and augmentation—should sometimes be performed on roots, endings, and suffixes in accordance with the speech of the Jina.

Jāyati[M 0.0251], kareyya, jāniyā, siyā, kare, gacche, jaññā, vakkhetha, dakkhetha, dicchati, agacchi, agacchuṃ, ahosi, ahesuṃ iccevamādīni aññānipi sādhanāni yojetabbāni.

He is born, he should do, he should know, he might be, he may do, he may go, he should know, you (pl.) will speak, you (pl.) will see, he wishes to give, he went, they went, he was, they were—and so on, other derivations should also be formed.

518, 446. Attanopadāni parassapadattaṃ.

Middle voice endings [are treated] as active voice endings.

Attanopadāni kvaci parassapadattamāpajjante.

Middle voice endings sometimes take on the nature of active voice endings.

Vuccati, labbhati, paccati.

It is said, it is obtained, it is cooked.

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Karīyate, labbhate, paccate.

What is the purpose of 'sometimes'? [As in:] It is made, it is obtained, it is cooked.

519, 457. Akārāgamo hiyyattanīajjatanīkālātipattīsu.

The augment 'a' [occurs] in the imperfect, aorist, and conditional.

Kvaci akārāgamo hoti hiyyattanī ajjatanīkālātipattiiccetāsu vibhattīsu.

Sometimes the augment 'a' occurs before these endings: the imperfect, aorist, and conditional.

Agamā, agamī, agamissā.

He went (imperfect), he went (aorist), he would have gone (conditional).

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Gamā, gamī, gamissā.

What is the purpose of 'sometimes'? [As in:] He went, he went, he would have gone.

520, 502. Brūto ī timhi.

After 'brū', 'ī' [is inserted] before 'ti'.

Brūiccetāya dhātuyā īkārāgamo hoti timhi vibhattimhi.

For this root 'brū', the augment 'ī' occurs before the 'ti' ending.

Bravīti.

He says.

521, 425. Dhātussanto [M 0.0252] lopo’nekasarassa.

Elision of the final [vowel] of a polysyllabic root.

Dhātussa anto kvaci lopo hoti anekasarassa.

The final [vowel] of a polysyllabic root is sometimes elided.

Gacchati, sarati, marati.

He goes, he remembers, he dies.

Anekasarasseti kimatthaṃ? Pāti, yāti, vāti.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'polysyllabic'? [As in:] He drinks, he goes, he blows.

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Mahīyati, mathīyati.

What is the purpose of 'kvaci'? It is honored; it is churned.

522, 476. Isuyamūnamanto ccho vā.

522, 476. For the roots isu and yamu, the final part is optionally ccho.

Isu yamu iccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto ccho hoti vā. Icchati, niyacchati.

For these roots, 'isu' and 'yamu,' the final part may optionally be 'ccho.' He desires; he restrains.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Esati, niyamati.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? He seeks; he controls.

523, 526. Kāritānaṃ ṇo lopaṃ.

523, 526. Elision of the ṇ of the causative suffixes.

Kāritaiccetesaṃ paccayānaṃ ṇo lopamāpajjate.

Of these causative suffixes, the ṇ undergoes elision.

Kāreti, kārayati, kārāpeti, kārāpayati.

He causes to do; he causes to do; he causes to have done; he causes to have done.

Sāsanatthaṃ samuddiṭṭhaṃ, mayākhyātaṃ samāsato;

Sakaṃ buddhivisesena, cintayantu vicakkhaṇā.

For the purpose of the Dispensation, it has been indicated, explained by me in brief; let the discerning reflect with their own special wisdom.

Iti ākhyātakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus, the fourth section in the chapter on verbal forms.

Ākhyātakappo niṭṭhito.

The chapter on verbal forms is concluded.

7. Kibbidhānakappa

7. The Chapter on Primary Derivatives

Paṭhamakaṇḍa

First Section

(Ka)

(Ka)

Buddhaṃ [M 0.0253] ñāṇasamuddaṃ, sabbaññuṃ lokahetu’khīṇamatiṃ;

Vanditvā pubbamahaṃ, vakkhāmi sasādhanaṃ hi kitakappaṃ.

Having first bowed to the Buddha—the ocean of wisdom, the Omniscient One, the benefactor of the world, whose wisdom is inexhaustible—I will explain the chapter on primary derivatives along with its derivations.

(Kha)

(Kha)

Sādhanamūlaṃ hi payogaṃ,

Āhu payogamūlamatthañca;

Atthesu visāradamatayo,

Sāsanassudharā jinassa matā.

Indeed, they say that application is the root of derivation, and meaning is the root of application; those whose minds are skilled in meanings are considered upholders of the Victor's Dispensation.

(Ga)

(Ga)

Andho desakavikalo,

Ghatamadhutelāni bhājanena vinā;

Naṭṭho naṭṭhāni yathā,

Payogavikalo tathā attho.

A blind man, one impaired in teaching; ghee, honey, and oil without a vessel; just as these are ruined, so too is meaning impaired without application.

(Gha)

(Gha)

Tasmā saṃrakkhaṇatthaṃ, munivacanatthassa dullabhassāhaṃ;

Vakkhāmi sissakahitaṃ, kitakappaṃ sādhanena yutaṃ.

Therefore, for the sake of preserving the rare meaning of the sage's words, I will explain for the benefit of students the chapter on primary derivatives, together with derivations.

524, 561. Dhātuyā kammādimhi ṇo.

524, 561. After a root, when preceded by an object, etc., the suffix ṇa.

Dhātuyā kammādimhi ṇapaccayo hoti.

After a root, when preceded by an object, etc., the suffix ṇa is applied.

Kammaṃ karotīti kammakāro, evaṃ kumbhakāro, mālākāro, kaṭṭhakāro, rathakāro, rajatakāro[M 0.0254], suvaṇṇakāro, pattaggāho, tantavāyo, dhaññamāyo, dhammakāmo, dhammacāro.

One who does work is a worker (kammakāro); similarly, a potter (kumbhakāro), a garland-maker (mālākāro), a woodworker (kaṭṭhakāro), a chariot-maker (rathakāro), a silversmith (rajatakāro), a goldsmith (suvaṇṇakāro), a bowl-receiver (pattaggāho), a weaver (tantavāyo), a grain-measurer (dhaññamāyo), one who loves the Dhamma (dhammakāmo), one who practices the Dhamma (dhammacāro).

525, 565. Saññāyama nu.

525, 565. In the sense of designation, [the suffix] a and [the augment] nu.

Saññāyamabhidheyyāyaṃ dhātuyā kammādimhi akārapaccayo hoti, nāmamhi ca nukārāgamo hoti.

When a designation is to be expressed, the suffix 'a' is applied to a root when it is preceded by an object, etc.; and to the preceding noun, the augment 'nu' is added.

Ariṃ dametīti arindamo, rājā. Vessaṃ taratīti vessantaro, rājā. Taṇhaṃ karotīti taṇhaṅkaro, bhagavā. Medhaṃ karotīti medhaṅkaro, bhagavā. Saraṇaṃ karotīti saraṇaṅkaro, bhagavā. Dīpaṃ karotīti dīpaṅkaro, bhagavā.

One who tames enemies is an Arindama, a king. One who crosses over to the merchants is a Vessantara, a king. One who makes an end of craving is Taṇhaṅkara, the Blessed One. One who makes wisdom is Medhaṅkara, the Blessed One. One who makes a refuge is Saraṇaṅkara, the Blessed One. One who makes an island is Dīpaṅkara, the Blessed One.

526, 567. Pure dadā ca iṃ.

526, 567. And for 'pura' before the root 'dā', its 'a' becomes 'iṃ'.

Purasadde ādimhi dadaiccetāya dhātuyā akārapaccayo hoti, purasaddassa akārassa ca iṃ hoti.

When the word 'pura' is at the beginning, the suffix 'a' is applied to this root 'dā', and the 'a' of 'pura' becomes 'iṃ'.

Pure dānaṃ adāsīti purindado devarājā.

One who gave gifts formerly is Purindada, the king of the gods.

527, 568. Sabbato ṇvu tvāvī vā.

527, 568. After all roots, the suffixes ṇvu, tu, and āvī are optionally used.

Sabbato dhātuto kammādimhi vā akammādimhi vā akāra ṇvu tu āvīiccete paccayā honti.

From all roots, whether in the sense of agent, etc., or non-agent, etc., these suffixes—a, ṇvu, tu, and āvī—occur.

Taṃ [M 0.0255] karotīti takkaro, hitaṃ karotīti hitakaro, vineti ettha, etenāti vā vinayo nissāya naṃ vasatīti nissayo.

He who does that is a `takkaro` (doer of that). He who does good is a `hitakaro` (doer of good). One trains in it, or by it, thus it is `vinayo` (training). Relying on it one dwells, thus it is `nissayo` (reliance).

Ṇvumhi – rathaṃ karotīti rathakārako, annaṃ, dadātīti annadāyako, vineti satteti vināyako, karotīti kārako, dadātīti dāyako, netīti nāyako.

With `ṇvu`: he who makes a chariot is a `rathakārako` (chariot-maker); he who gives food is an `annadāyako` (food-giver); he who trains beings is a `vināyako` (trainer); he who does is a `kārako` (doer); he who gives is a `dāyako` (giver); he who leads is a `nāyako` (leader).

Tumhi – taṃ karotīti takkattā, tassa kattāti vā takkattā. Bhojanaṃ dadātīti bhojanadātā, bhojanassa dātāti vā bhojanadātā. Karotīti kattā. Saratīti saritā.

With `tu`: he who does that is `takkattā`; or, the doer of that is `takkattā`. He who gives food is `bhojanadātā`; or, the giver of food is `bhojanadātā`. He who does is `kattā`. He who remembers is `saritā`.

Āvīmhi – bhayaṃ passatīti bhayadassāvī iccevamādi.

With `āvī`: he who sees danger is `bhayadassāvī` (one who sees danger), and so on.

528, 577. Visa ruja padādito ṇa.

528, 577. From `vis`, `ruj`, `pad`, etc., the suffix `ṇa`.

Visa ruja padaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi ṇa paccayo hoti.

From roots such as `vis`, `ruj`, `pad`, etc., the suffix `ṇa` occurs.

Pavisatīti paveso, rujatīti rogo, uppajjatīti uppādo, phusatīti phasso, ucatīti oko, bhavatīti bhāvo, ayatīti āyo, sammā bujjhatīti sambodho, viharatīti vihāro.

Entering is `paveso` (entrance); afflicting is `rogo` (disease); arising is `uppādo` (arising); touching is `phasso` (contact); taking delight is `oko` (dwelling); becoming is `bhāvo` (being); coming is `āyo` (income); rightly awakening is `sambodho` (perfect awakening); dwelling is `vihāro` (dwelling).

529, 580. Bhāve [M 0.0256] ca.

529, 580. And in the sense of action.

Bhāvatthābhidheyye sabbadhātūhi ṇapaccayo hoti.

When the sense of action is to be expressed, the suffix `ṇa` occurs from all roots.

Paccate, pacanaṃ vā pāto, cajate, cajanaṃ vā cāgo, evaṃ yāgo, yogo, bhāgo, paridāho.

It is cooked, or the act of cooking, is `pāko`; it is abandoned, or the act of abandoning, is `cāgo`. Similarly: `yāgo` (sacrificing), `yogo` (joining), `bhāgo` (sharing), `paridāho` (burning around).

530, 584. Kvi ca.

530, 584. And the suffix `kvi`.

Sabbadhātūhi kvipaccayo hoti.

From all roots, the suffix `kvi` occurs.

Sambhavatīti sambhū, visesena bhavatīti vibhū, bhujena gacchatīti bhujago, saṃ attānaṃ khanati, saṃ saṭṭhu khanatīti vā saṅkho.

One who arises completely is `sambhū` (an origin). One who is pre-eminent is `vibhū` (the mighty one). One who goes crookedly is `bhujago` (a serpent). One who digs into oneself, or one who digs well, is `saṅkho` (a conch).

531, 589. Dharādīhi rammo.

531, 589. From `dhar` and others, the suffix `ma`.

Dharaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rammapaccayo hoti.

From roots such as `dhar` and others, the suffix `ma` occurs.

Dharati tenāti dhammo, karīyate tanti kammaṃ.

That which bears is `dhammo`; that which is done is `kammaṃ`.

532, 590. Tassīlādīsu ṇītvāvī ca.

532, 590. And in the sense of habit, etc., the suffixes `ṇī`, `tu`, and `āvī`.

Sabbehi dhātūhi tassīlādīsvatthesu ṇī tu āvī iccete paccayā honti.

From all roots, in the sense of habit, etc., these suffixes—`ṇī`, `tu`, and `āvī`—occur.

Piyaṃ pasaṃsituṃ sīlaṃ yassa rañño, so hoti rājā piyapasaṃsī, brahmaṃ carituṃ sīlaṃ yassa puggalassa so [M 0.0257] hoti puggalo brahmacārī, pasayha pavattituṃ sīlaṃ yassa rañño, so hoti rājā pasayhapavatthā, bhayaṃ passituṃ sīlaṃ yassa samaṇassa, so hoti samaṇo bhayadassāvī iccevamādi.

A king whose nature it is to praise what is dear is a `rājā piyapasaṃsī`; a person whose nature it is to live the holy life is a `puggalo brahmacārī`; a king whose nature it is to act with force is a `rājā pasayhapavatthā`; an ascetic whose nature it is to see danger is a `samaṇo bhayadassāvī`, and so on.

533, 591. Sadda ku dha cala maṇḍattharudhādīhiyu.

533, 591. From `sadda`, `kudha`, `cala`, `maṇḍa`, `attha`, `rudha`, and others, the suffix `yu`.

Sadda kudha cala maṇḍatthehi ca rucādīhi ca dhātūhi yupaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu.

From the roots `sadda`, `kudha`, `cala`, `maṇḍa`, and `attha`, and from roots such as `ruc` and others, the suffix `yu` occurs in the sense of habit, etc.

Ghosanasīlo ghosano, bhāsanasīlo bhāsano. Evaṃ viggaho kātabbo. Kodhano, dosano, calano, kampano, phandano, maṇḍano, vibhūsano, rocano, jotano, vaḍḍhano.

One whose nature is to proclaim is `ghosano`; one whose nature is to speak is `bhāsano`. The analysis should be made in this way. `Kodhano`, `dosano`, `calano`, `kampano`, `phandano`, `maṇḍano`, `vibhūsano`, `rocano`, `jotano`, `vaḍḍhano`.

534, 562. Pārādigamimhā rū.

534, 562. From `gam` when preceded by `pāra` and others, the suffix `rū`.

Gamuiccetamhā dhātumhā pārasaddādimhā rūpaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu.

From the root `gam` when preceded by the word `pāra` and others, the suffix `rū` occurs in the sense of habit, etc.

Bhavassa pāraṃ bhavapāraṃ, bhavapāraṃ gantuṃ sīlaṃ yassa purisassa, so hoti puriso bhavapāragū.

The far shore of existence is `bhavapāraṃ`. A person whose nature it is to go to the far shore of existence is `bhavapāragū`.

Tassīlādīsvīti kimatthaṃ? Pāraṅgato.

What is the purpose of 'in the sense of habit, etc.'? `Pāraṅgato`.

Pārādigamimhāti kimatthaṃ? Anugāmī.

What is the purpose of 'from `gam` when preceded by `pāra`, etc.'? `Anugāmī`.

535, 593. Bhikkhādito [M 0.0258] ca.

535, 593. And from `bhikkha`, etc.

Bhikkhaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rūpaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu.

From roots such as `bhikkha`, etc., the suffix `rū` occurs in the sense of habit, etc.

Bhikkhanasīlo yācanasīlo bhikkhu, vijānanasīlo viññū.

One whose nature is to beg, whose nature is to ask, is a bhikkhu; one whose nature is to discern is a viññū.

536, 594. Tanatyādīnaṃ ṇuko.

536, 594. The suffix ṇuka [is employed] after tanati and so on.

Hanatyādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ ante ṇukapaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu.

After roots such as hanati, and so on, the suffix ṇuka occurs at the end in the senses of 'one whose nature is...', and so on.

Āhananasīlo āghātuko, karaṇasīlo kāruko.

One whose nature is to strike is an āghātuka; one whose nature is to do is a kāruka.

537, 566. Nu niggahitaṃ padante.

537, 566. Nu [becomes] niggahīta at the end of a word.

Padante nukārāgamo niggahitamāpajjate.

At the end of a word, the augment nu becomes niggahīta.

Ariṃ dametīti arindamo, rājā. Vessaṃ taratīti vessantaro, rājā. Pabhaṃ karotīti pabhaṅkaro, bhagavā.

'One who subdues enemies' [is] arindamo, a king. 'One who crosses over to the merchants' [is] vessantaro, a king. 'One who makes light' [is] pabhaṅkaro, the Blessed One.

538, 595. Saṃhanāññāya vā ro gho.

538, 595. After saṃ-han and other [roots], [the suffix] ra [is employed], and [han becomes] gha, optionally.

Saṃpubbāya hanaiccetāya dhātuyā, aññāya vā dhātuyā rapaccayo, hanassa ca gho hoti.

From the root han preceded by saṃ, or from another root, the suffix ra occurs, and gha is substituted for han.

Samaggaṃ [M 0.0259] kammaṃ samupagacchatīti saṅgho, samantato nagarassa māhire khaññatīti parikhā, antaṃ karotīti antako.

'That which comes together for harmonious action' [is] saṅgho; 'that which is dug around a city on all sides' [is] parikhā; 'one who makes an end' [is] antako.

Saṃiti kimatthaṃ? Upahananaṃ upaghāto.

For what purpose [is the word] 'saṃ'? [The form from] upahananaṃ is upaghāto.

539, 558. Ramhi ranto rādino.

539, 558. When ra [follows], the final part of a root beginning with ra [is elided].

Ramhi paccaye pare sabbo dhātvanto rakārādi lopo hoti.

When the suffix ra follows, the entire final part of the root that begins with ra is elided.

Antako, pāragū, satthā, diṭṭho iccevamādi.

Antako, pāragū, satthā, diṭṭho, and so on.

540, 545. Bhāvakammesu tabbānīyā.

540, 545. Tabba and anīya [occur] in the senses of state and action.

Bhāvakammaiccetesvatthesu tabba anīyaiccete paccayā honti sabbadhātūhi.

In these senses of state and action, the suffixes tabba and anīya occur after all roots.

Bhavitabbaṃ, bhavanīyaṃ, āsitabbaṃ, āsanīyaṃ, pajjitabbaṃ, pajjanīyaṃ, kattabbaṃ, karaṇīyaṃ, gantabbaṃ, gamanīyaṃ.

Bhavitabbaṃ, bhavanīyaṃ (what is to be); āsitabbaṃ, āsanīyaṃ (sitting); pajjitabbaṃ, pajjanīyaṃ (what is to be attained); kattabbaṃ, karaṇīyaṃ (what is to be done); gantabbaṃ, gamanīyaṃ (going).

541, 552. Ṇyo ca.

541, 552. And also ṇya.

Bhāvakammesu sabbadhātūhi ṇyapaccayo hoti.

In the senses of state and action, the suffix ṇya occurs after all roots.

Kattabbaṃ kāriyaṃ, jetabbaṃ jeyyaṃ, netabbaṃ neyyaṃ, iccevamādi.

Kattabbaṃ [becomes] kāriyaṃ; jetabbaṃ [becomes] jeyyaṃ; netabbaṃ [becomes] neyyaṃ, and so on.

Caggahaṇena [M 0.0260] teyyapaccayo hoti. Ñātabbaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyaṃ iccevamādi.

By the inclusion of 'ca' [in the rule], the suffix teyya occurs. Ñātabbaṃ [becomes] ñāteyyaṃ; [daṭṭhabbaṃ becomes] daṭṭheyyaṃ; [pattabbaṃ becomes] patteyyaṃ, and so on.

542, 557. Karamhā ricca.

542, 557. After kara, ricca [occurs].

Karaiccetamhā dhātumhā riccapaccayo hoti bhāvakammesu.

After this root kara, the suffix ricca occurs in the senses of state and action.

Kattabbaṃ kiccaṃ.

Kattabbaṃ [becomes] kiccaṃ.

543, 555. Bhūto’bba.

543, 555. After bhū, [the suffix ṇya becomes] abba.

Bhūiccetāya dhātuyā ṇyapaccayassa ūkārena saha abbādeso hoti bhāvakammesu.

After this root bhū, the suffix ṇya, together with the [root's] sound ū, is replaced by abba in the senses of state and action.

Bhavitabbo bhabbo, bhavitabbaṃ bhabbaṃ.

Bhavitabbo [becomes] bhabbo; bhavitabbaṃ [becomes] bhabbaṃ.

544, 556. Vada mada gamu yuja garahākārādīhi jja mma gga yheyyā gāro vā.

544, 556. After vada, mada, gamu, yuja, garaha, and roots ending in ā, and so on, [the substitutes are] jja, mma, gga, yha, eyya, and gāra, optionally.

Vada mada gamu yuja garahākārantaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi ṇyapaccayassa yathāsaṅkhyaṃ jja mma gga yha eyyādesā honti vā dhātvantena saha, garassaṃ ca gāro hoti bhāvakammesu.

From roots such as vada, mada, gamu, yuja, garaha, and those ending in ā, and so on, for the suffix ṇya the substitutes jja, mma, gga, yha, and eyya occur respectively, optionally, together with the end of the root; and for garaha, gāra occurs, in the senses of state and action.

Vattabbaṃ vajjaṃ, madanīyaṃ majjaṃ, gamanīyaṃ gammaṃ, yojanīyaṃ yoggaṃ, garahitabbaṃ gārayhaṃ, dātabbaṃ deyyaṃ, pātabbaṃ peyyaṃ, hātabbaṃ [M 0.0261] heyyaṃ, mātabbaṃ meyyaṃ, ñātabbaṃ ñeyyaṃ, iccevamādi.

Vattabbaṃ [becomes] vajjaṃ; madanīyaṃ [becomes] majjaṃ; gamanīyaṃ [becomes] gammaṃ; yojanīyaṃ [becomes] yoggaṃ; garahitabbaṃ [becomes] gārayhaṃ; dātabbaṃ [becomes] deyyaṃ; pātabbaṃ [becomes] peyyaṃ; hātabbaṃ [becomes] heyyaṃ; mātabbaṃ [becomes] meyyaṃ; ñātabbaṃ [becomes] ñeyyaṃ, and so on.

545, 548. Te kiccā.

545, 548. These are kicca.

Ye paccayā tabbādayo riccantā, te kiccasaññāti veditabbā.

The suffixes beginning with tabba and ending with ricca are to be known by the designation kicca.

Kiccasaññāya kiṃpayojanaṃ? Bhāvakammesu kiccattakhatthā.

What is the purpose of the designation kicca? For the rule that kicca, tta, kha, and ttha suffixes are used in the senses of bhāva and kamma.

546, 562. Aññe kita.

546, 562. Other [suffixes are] kita.

Aññe paccayā kita eva saññā honti.

Other suffixes are designated as kita.

Kita saññāya kiṃpayojanaṃ? Kattari kita.

What is the purpose of the designation kita? [It is for the rule] 'Kita [suffixes are used] in the sense of agent'.

547, 596. Nandādīhi yu.

547, 596. From nanda, etc., yu [occurs].

Nandādīhi dhātūhi yupaccayo hoti bhāvakammesu.

From roots such as nanda, etc., the suffix yu occurs in the senses of bhāva and kamma.

Nandīyate nandanaṃ, ninditabbaṃ vā nandanaṃ, gahaṇīyaṃ gahaṇaṃ, caritabbaṃ caraṇaṃ, evaṃ sabbattha yojetabbā.

Nandīyate (it is rejoiced at) is nandanaṃ (rejoicing); or, ninditabbaṃ (what is to be censured) is nandanaṃ; gahaṇīyaṃ (what is to be grasped) is gahaṇaṃ (grasping); caritabbaṃ (what is to be practiced) is caraṇaṃ (practice). Thus, it should be applied everywhere.

548, 597. Kattukaraṇapadesesu ca.

548, 597. And in the senses of agent, instrument, and location.

Kattukaraṇapadesaiccetesvatthesu ca yupaccayo hoti.

In the senses of agent, instrument, and location, the suffix yu also occurs.

Kattari [M 0.0262] tāva – rajaṃ haratīti rajoharaṇaṃ toyaṃ.

First, in the sense of agent: ‘it removes dust,’ thus rajoharaṇaṃ toyaṃ (dust-removing water).

Karaṇe tāva – karoti tenāti karaṇaṃ.

Next, in the sense of instrument: ‘one does with it,’ thus karaṇaṃ.

Padese tāva – tiṭṭhanti tasminti ṭhānaṃ. Evaṃ sabbattha yojetabbā.

Next, in the sense of location: ‘they stand in it,’ thus ṭhānaṃ (a place). Thus, it should be applied everywhere.

549, 550. Rahādito ṇa.

549, 550. After ra, ha, etc., ṇa [is substituted for na].

Rakārahakārādyantehi dhātūhi anādesassa nassa ṇo hoti.

After roots ending in the letters ra, ha, etc., ṇa is substituted for a non-substitute na.

Karoti tenāti karaṇaṃ, pūreti tenāti pūraṇaṃ. Gahaṇīyaṃ tenāti gahaṇaṃ. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

‘One does with it,’ thus karaṇaṃ; ‘one fills with it,’ thus pūraṇaṃ; ‘one is to grasp with it,’ thus gahaṇaṃ. Thus others too should be applied.

Iti kibbidhānakappe paṭhamo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the first section in the chapter on Kibbidhāna.

Dutiyakaṇḍa

The Second Section.

550, 546. Ṇādayo tekālikā.

550, 546. The suffixes beginning with ṇa are applicable to the three times.

Ṇādayo paccayā yupaccayantā tekālikāti veditabbā.

The suffixes beginning with ṇa and ending with the suffix yu are to be known as applicable to the three times.

Kumbhaṃ karoti akāsi karissatīti kumbhakāro, karoti akāsi karissati tenāti karaṇaṃ. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

‘He makes, made, or will make a pot,’ thus a kumbhakāro (potter); ‘one makes, made, or will make with it,’ thus a karaṇaṃ (instrument). Others should be construed similarly.

551, 598. Saññāyaṃ [M 0.0263] dā dhāto i.

551, 598. When it is a name, the suffix i [is added] to the root dā.

Saññāyamabhidheyyāyaṃ dā dhāto ipaccayo hoti.

When a name is to be expressed, the suffix i is applied to the root dā.

Paṭhamaṃ ādīyatīti ādi, udakaṃ dadhātīti udami, mahodakāni dadhātīti mahodadhi, vālāni dadhāti tasminti vāladhi, sammā dhīyatīti sandhi.

‘It is taken up first,’ thus ādi; ‘it holds water,’ thus udami; ‘it holds great waters,’ thus mahodadhi; ‘hairs are held in it,’ thus vāladhi; ‘it is put together well,’ thus sandhi.

552, 609. Ti kita cāsiṭṭhe.

552, 609. The suffix ti, and kita [suffixes], in the sense of a wish.

Saññāyamabhidheyyāyaṃ sabbadhātūhi tipaccayo hoti, kita ca āsiṭṭhe.

When a name is to be expressed, the suffix ti occurs after all roots; and kita [suffixes occur] in the sense of a wish.

Jino janaṃ bujjhatūti jinabuddhi, dhanaṃ assa bhavatūti dhanabhūti, bhavatūti bhūto, bhavatūti bhāvo, dhammo janaṃ dadātūti dhammadinno, vaḍḍhatūti vaḍḍhamāno. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

‘May the Conqueror awaken the people,’ thus jinabuddhi; ‘may there be wealth for him,’ thus dhanabhūti; ‘may it be,’ thus bhūto; ‘may it be,’ thus bhāvo; ‘may the Dhamma give to the people,’ thus dhammadinno; ‘may he grow,’ thus vaḍḍhamāno. Others should be construed similarly.

553, 599. Itthiyamatiyavo vā.

553, 599. In the feminine, a, ti, and yu [occur] optionally.

Itthiyamabhidheyyāyaṃ sabbadhātūhi akāra ti yu iccete paccayā honti vā.

When the feminine gender is to be expressed, these suffixes—a, ti, and yu—are optionally applied to all roots.

Jīratītī jarā, maññatīti mati, cetayatīti cetanā, vedayatīti vedanā. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

It ages—thus, 'jarā'. It thinks—thus, 'mati'. It intends—thus, 'cetanā'. It feels—thus, 'vedanā'. Others should be construed similarly.

554, 601. Karato [M 0.0264] ririya.

554, 601. From the root 'kar', the suffixes 'ri' and 'riya'.

Karato itthiyamanitthiyaṃ vā abhikheyyāyaṃ rirīyapaccayo hoti vā.

In the sense of 'doing', whether feminine or non-feminine, the suffixes 'ri' and 'riya' are optionally applied when the meaning is to be expressed.

Kattabbā kiriyā, karaṇīyaṃ kiriyaṃ.

What is to be done is 'kiriyā'; what is to be done is 'kiriyaṃ'.

555, 612. Atīte tatavantutāvī.

555, 612. In the past, 'ta', 'tavant', and 'tāvī'.

Atīte kāle sabbadhātūhi tatavantutāvīiccete paccayā honti.

In past time, these suffixes, 'ta', 'tavant', and 'tāvī', are applied to all roots.

Huto, hutavā, hutāvī. Vusito, vusitavā, vusitāvī. Bhutto, bhuttavā, bhuttāvī.

Offered, one who has offered, one who has offered. Dwelt, one who has dwelt, one who has dwelt. Eaten, one who has eaten, one who has eaten.

556, 622. Bhāvakammesu ta.

556, 622. In the sense of state and in the passive, 'ta'.

Bhāvakammesu atīte kāle tapaccayo hoti sabbadhātūhi.

In the sense of state and in the passive, in past time, the suffix 'ta' is applied to all roots.

Bhāve tāva – tassa gītaṃ, naccaṃ, naṭṭaṃ, hasitaṃ.

First, in the sense of state: his singing, dancing, acting, laughing.

Kammani tāva – tena bhāsitaṃ, desitaṃ.

Next, in the passive: spoken by him, taught by him.

557, 606. Budhagamāditthe kattari.

557, 606. After 'budh', 'gam', etc., in the sense of agent.

Budhagamuiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tadatthe gamyamāne tapaccayo hoti kattari sabbakāle.

The suffix 'ta' is applied to roots such as 'budh', 'gam', etc., in the sense of agent in all tenses, when that meaning is understood.

Sabbe [M 0.0265] saṅkhatāsaṅkhate dhamme bujjhati abujjhi bujjhissatīti buddho, saraṇaṅgato, samathaṅgato, amathaṅgato, jānāti ajāni jānissatīti ñāto, iccevamādi.

He understands, understood, will understand all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena—thus, 'buddho'. Gone to refuge, gone to calm, gone to the unperturbed. He knows, knew, will know—thus, 'ñāto'. And so on.

558, 602. Jito ina sabbattha.

558, 602. From 'ji', 'ina' everywhere.

Jiiccetāya dhātuyā inapaccayo hoti sabbakāle kattari.

From this root 'ji', the suffix 'ina' is applied in all tenses in the sense of agent.

Pāpake akusale dhamme jināti ajini jinissatīti jino.

He conquers, conquered, will conquer evil, unwholesome phenomena—thus, 'jino'.

559, 603. Supato ca.

559, 603. And from 'sup'.

Supaiccetāya dhātuyā inapaccayo hoti kattari, bhāve ca.

From this root 'sup', the suffix 'ina' is applied in the sense of agent and of state.

Supatīti supinaṃ, supīyate supinaṃ.

He sleeps—thus, 'supinaṃ'. It is slept—thus, 'supinaṃ'.

560, 604. Īsaṃdusūhi kha.

560, 604. After 'īsaṃ', 'du', and 'su', 'kha'.

Īsaṃdususaddādīhi sabbadhātūhi khapaccayo hoti.

After the words 'īsaṃ', 'du', 'su', etc., the suffix 'kha' is applied to all roots.

Īsassayo, dussayo, sussayo bhavatā, īsakkaraṃ, dukkaraṃ, sukaraṃ, bhavatā.

Easy to recline on, difficult to recline on, good to recline on, by you. Easy to do, difficult to do, easy to do, by you.

561, 636. Icchatthesu [M 0.0266] samānakattukesu tave tuṃ vā.

561, 636. In the sense of wishing, with the same agent, 'tave' or 'tuṃ' optionally.

Icchatthesu samānakattukesu sabbadhātūhitavetuṃiccete paccayā honti sabbakāle kattari.

In the sense of wishing, with the same agent, these suffixes 'tave' and 'tuṃ' are applied to all roots, in all tenses, in the sense of agent.

Puññāni kātave, saddhammaṃ sotu micchati.

He wishes to do meritorious deeds, to hear the good Dhamma.

562, 638. Arahasakkādīsu ca.

562, 638. And in the sense of 'araha', 'sakka', etc.

Arahasakkādīsu ca atthesu sabbadhātūhi tuṃpaccayo hoti.

And in the meanings of 'araha', 'sakka', etc., the suffix 'tuṃ' is applied to all roots.

Ko taṃ ninditumarahati, sakkā jetuṃ dhanena vā. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

Who is able to censure him? It is possible to conquer by wealth. Others should be construed similarly.

563, 639. Pattavacane alamatthesu ca.

563, 639. And in the sense of 'patta' and in the meanings of 'alam'.

Pattavacane alamatthesu sabbadhātūhi tuṃpaccayo hoti.

In the sense of 'fit' or 'proper' and in the sense of 'enough', the suffix 'tuṃ' is applied to all roots.

Alameva dānāni dātuṃ, alameva puññāni kātuṃ.

It is indeed enough to give gifts; it is indeed enough to do meritorious deeds.

564, 640. Pubbakāle’ kakattukānaṃ tuna tvāna tvāvā.

564, 640. In the sense of prior action, for actions with the same agent, the suffixes 'tūna', 'tvāna', and 'tvā' are used optionally.

Pubbakāle ekakattukānaṃ dhātūnaṃ tunatvāna tvāiccete paccayā honti vā.

In the sense of prior action, for roots with the same agent, these suffixes, 'tūna', 'tvāna', and 'tvā', are optionally applied.

Kātuna [M 0.0267] kammaṃ gacchati, akātuna puññaṃ kilissati, sattā sutvāna dhammaṃ modanti, ripuṃ jitvāna vasati, dhammaṃ sutvāna’ssa etadahosi, ito sutvāna amutra kathayanti, sutvā jānissāma. Evaṃ sabbattha yojetabbā.

Having done an action, he goes. Not having done merit, he is afflicted. Beings, having heard the Dhamma, rejoice. Having conquered the enemy, he dwells. Having heard the Dhamma, this occurred to him. Having heard here, they speak there. Having heard, we shall know. Thus it should be applied everywhere.

565, 646. Vattamāne mānantā.

565, 646. In the present tense, 'māna' and 'anta'.

Vattamāne kāle sabbadhātūhi mānaantaiccete paccayā honti.

In the present tense, these suffixes, 'māna' and 'anta', are applied to all roots.

Saramāno rodati. Gacchanto gaṇhāti.

Remembering, he weeps. Going, he takes.

566, 574. Sāsādīhi ratthu.

566, 574. From 'sāsa', etc., 'ratthu'.

Sāsaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi ratthupaccayo hoti.

From the root 'sāsa' and so on, the suffix 'ratthu' is applied.

Sāsatīti satthā, sāsati hiṃsatīti vā satthā.

He instructs—thus, 'satthā' (teacher); or, he harms—thus, 'satthā' (weapon).

567, 575. Pātitoritu.

567, 575. From 'pā', 'ritu'.

Pāiccetāya dhātuyā ritupaccayo hoti.

From this root 'pā', the suffix 'ritu' is applied.

Pāti puttanti pitā.

He protects his son—thus, 'pitā' (father).

568, 576. Mānādīhi [M 0.0268] rātu.

568, 576. From 'māna', etc., 'rātu'.

Mānaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rātupaccayo hoti, ritu paccayo ca.

From the root 'māna' and so on, the suffix 'rātu' is applied, and also the suffix 'ritu'.

Dhammena puttaṃ mānetīti mātā, pubbe bhāsatīti bhātā, mātāpitūhi dhārīyatīti dhītā.

She honors her son with the teaching—thus, 'mātā' (mother). He speaks first—thus, 'bhātā' (brother). She is supported by her mother and father—thus, 'dhītā' (daughter).

569, 610. Āgamā tuko.

569, 610. From 'ā-gam', 'tuka'.

Āiccādimhā gamito tukapaccayo hoti.

From the root 'gam' preceded by 'ā', the suffix 'tuka' is applied.

Āgacchatīti āgantuko, bhikkhu.

He comes—thus, 'āgantuko' (a visitor), a bhikkhu.

570, 611. Bhabbe ika.

570, 611. In the sense of 'fit', 'ika'.

Gamuiccetamhā dhātumhā ikapaccayo hoti bhabbe. Gamissati gantuṃ bhabboti gamiko, bhikkhu.

From this root 'gam', the suffix 'ika' is applied in the sense of 'fit'. He will go, he is fit to go—thus, 'gamiko' (one who goes), a bhikkhu.

Iti kibbidhānakappe dutiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the Second Section in the Chapter on Primary Derivatives.

Tatiyakaṇḍa

The Third Section

571, 624. Paccayādaniṭṭhā nipātanā sijjhanti,

571, 624. Those not established by suffixes are accomplished by irregular formation.

Saṅkhyānāmasamāsataddhitākhyātakitakappamhi sappaccayā ye saddā aniṭṭhaṅgatā, te sādhanena nirakkhitvā sakehi sakehi nāmehi nipātanā sijjhanti.

In the chapters on numerals, nouns, compounds, secondary derivatives, verbs, and primary derivatives, those words which are not established with their suffixes, having not been examined by regular derivation, are accomplished by irregular formation under their respective names.

Saṅkhyāyaṃ [M 0.0269] tāva – ekassa etā hoti, dasassa ca dakārassa rakārādeso hoti. Eko ca dasa ca ekārasa.

Firstly, in numerals: for 'eka', the final vowel is lengthened, and for 'dasa', the letter 'da' is substituted by 'ra'. 'Eka' and 'dasa' become 'ekārasa'.

Dvissa bā hoti, dasassa ca dakārassa rakārādeso hoti, dve ca dasa ca bārasa.

For 'dvi', there is the substitution 'bā', and for 'dasa', the letter 'da' is substituted by 'ra'. 'Dve' and 'dasa' become 'bārasa'.

Dvissa bā hoti, dasassa ca vīsaṃ hoti. Dve ca vīsañca bāvīsaṃ.

For 'dvi', there is the substitution 'bā', and for 'dasa', there is 'vīsaṃ'. 'Dve' and 'vīsaṃ' become 'bāvīsaṃ'.

Chassa so hoti, dasassa ca dakārassa ḷo hoti, cha ca dasa ca soḷasa.

For 'cha', there is the substitution 'so', and for 'dasa', the letter 'da' becomes 'ḷa'. 'Cha' and 'dasa' become 'soḷasa'.

Chaāyatanamhi chassa saḷo hoti, saḷāyatanaṃ. Evaṃ sesā saṅkhyā kātabbā.

In 'cha-āyatana' (six sense-bases), 'cha' becomes 'saḷa', hence 'saḷāyatanaṃ'. In this way, the remaining numbers should be treated.

Nāmike tāva-ima samāna aparaiccetehi jjajju paccayā honti, ima samānasaddānañca akārasakārādesā honti. Imasmiṃ kāle ajja, ajju, samāne kāle sajja, sajju, aparasmiṃ kāle aparajja, aparajju.

Firstly, in nouns: from 'ima', 'samāna', 'apara', and so on, the suffixes 'jja' and 'jju' are applied; and for the words 'ima' and 'samāna', there are the substitutions of 'a' and 'sa' respectively. Thus: from 'imasmiṃ kāle' are formed 'ajja' (today) and 'ajju' (today); from 'samāne kāle', 'sajja' (instantly) and 'sajju' (instantly); from 'aparasmiṃ kāle', 'aparajja' (on another day) and 'aparajju' (on another day).

Samāse tāva – bhūmigato, apāyagato, issarakataṃ. Sallaviddho, kathinadussaṃ, corabhayaṃ, dhaññarāsi, saṃsāradukkhaṃ, pubbāparaṃ.

Firstly, in compounds: 'bhūmigato' (gone to the earth), 'apāyagato' (gone to the lower realms), 'issarakataṃ' (made by a lord). 'Sallaviddho' (pierced by a dart), 'kathinadussaṃ' (kaṭhina cloth), 'corabhayaṃ' (fear of thieves), 'dhaññarāsi' (a heap of grain), 'saṃsāradukkhaṃ' (the suffering of transmigration), 'pubbāparaṃ' (former and latter).

Taddhite [M 0.0270] tāva – vāsiṭṭho, bhāradvājo, bhaggavo, paṇḍavo, kāleyyo.

Firstly, in secondary derivatives: 'Vāsiṭṭho', 'Bhāradvājo', 'Bhaggavo', 'Paṇḍavo', 'Kāleyyo'.

Ākhyāte tāva – “asa bhāve”ti dhātuto vattamānesu ekavacanabahuvacanesu ekavacanassa tissa sso hoti antena saha, bahuvacanassa antissa ssu hoti antena saha. Evamassa vacanīyo, evamassu vacanīyā.

Firstly, in verbs: from the root 'asa' (to be), in the present tense, singular and plural, the singular ending 'ti' becomes 'sso' together with the preceding vowel, and the plural ending 'anti' becomes 'ssu' together with the preceding vowel. Thus, 'evamassa vacanīyo' (thus it should be said), 'evamassu vacanīyā' (thus they should be said).

Āṇattiyaṃ hissa ssu hoti vā, gacchassu, gacchāhi.

In the imperative, 'hi' optionally becomes 'ssu'. For example: 'gacchassu' (go!), 'gacchāhi' (go!).

Kitake tāva – vada hanaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi kapaccayo hoti, vadassa ca vādo hoti, hanassa ca ghāto hoti. Vādako, ghātako.

Firstly, in primary derivatives: from roots such as 'vada' (to speak) and 'hana' (to strike), the suffix 'ka' is applied. And 'vada' becomes 'vāda', and 'hana' becomes 'ghāta'. Hence: 'vādako' (speaker), 'ghātako' (killer).

Naṭadhātuto tapañcayassa cca ṭṭādesā honti antena saha. Naccaṃ, naṭṭaṃ. Iccevamādayo nipātanā sijjhanti.

From the root 'naṭa' (to dance), the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'cca' and 'ṭṭa' together with the preceding vowel. Thus: 'naccaṃ' (dance), 'naṭṭaṃ' (danced). In this way, these and other such forms are established by special rule (nipātana).

572, 625. Sāsa disato tassa riṭṭho ca.

572, 625. And 'riṭṭha' for 'ta' after 'sāsa' and 'disa'.

Sāsa disaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa riṭṭhādeso hoti ṭhāne.

From roots such as 'sāsa' and 'disa', the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'riṭṭha'.

Anusiṭṭho so mayā, diṭṭhaṃ me rūpaṃ.

'Anusiṭṭho so mayā' (He has been instructed by me), 'diṭṭhaṃ me rūpaṃ' (The form has been seen by me).

Caggahaṇena [M 0.0271] kiccatakārassa ca tuṃ paccayassa ca raṭṭharaṭṭhuṃādesā honti. Dassanīyaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Daṭṭhuṃ vihāraṃ gacchanti samaṇānaṃ.

By the inclusion of 'ca', for the 'ta' of the gerundive suffix and for the infinitive suffix 'tuṃ', the replacements 'raṭṭha' and 'raṭṭhuṃ' occur. For example: 'dassanīyaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ' (to be seen). 'Daṭṭhuṃ vihāraṃ gacchanti samaṇānaṃ' (The ascetics go to the monastery to see).

573, 626. Sādisanta puccha bhanja hansādīhiṭṭho.

573, 626. After roots ending in 's', and after 'puccha', 'bhanja', 'hansa', etc., 'ṭṭha'.

Sakāranta puccha bhanja hansa iccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa sahādibyañjanena ṭṭhādeso hoti ṭhāne.

From roots ending in 's', and from 'puccha', 'bhanja', 'hansa', etc., the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'ṭṭha' together with the final consonant of the root.

Tuṭṭho, ahinā daṭṭho naro, mayā puṭṭho, bhaṭṭho, pabhaṭṭho, haṭṭho, pahaṭṭho, yiṭṭho. Evamaññepi dhātavo sabbattha yojetabbā.

'Tuṭṭho' (satisfied), 'ahinā daṭṭho naro' (a man bitten by a snake), 'mayā puṭṭho' (asked by me), 'bhaṭṭho' (fallen), 'pabhaṭṭho' (completely fallen), 'haṭṭho' (glad), 'pahaṭṭho' (very glad), 'yiṭṭho' (sacrificed). In this way, other roots should also be applied in all cases.

574, 613. Vasato uṭṭha.

574, 613. After 'vasa', 'uṭṭha'.

Vasaiccetamhā dhātumhā takārapaccayassa sahādibyañjanena uṭṭhādeso hoti ṭhāne.

From the root 'vasa', the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'uṭṭha' together with the final consonant of the root.

Vassaṃvuṭṭho.

'Vassaṃvuṭṭho' (one who has spent the rains retreat).

575, 614. Vassa vā vu.

575, 614. And optionally 'u' for 'va' of 'vasa'.

Vasasseva dhātussa tapaccaye pare vakārassa ukārādeso hoti vā.

For the root 'vasa' itself, when the suffix 'ta' follows, the 'va' is optionally replaced by 'u'.

Vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, uṭṭho. Vuṭho vā.

'Vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ' (the holy life has been lived), 'uṭṭho'. Or 'vuṭṭho'.

576, 607. Dha [M 0.0272] ḍha bha ye hi dha ḍhā ca.

576, 607. And after roots ending in 'dha', 'ḍha', 'bha', and 'ha', 'dha' and 'ḍha'.

Dha ḍha bha haiccevamantehi dhātūhi takārapaccayassa yathākkamaṃ dha ḍhādesā honti.

From roots ending in 'dha', 'ḍha', 'bha', 'ha', etc., the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'dha' and 'ḍha' respectively.

Yathā? Buddho bhagavā, vaḍḍho bhikkhu, laddhaṃ me patthacīvaraṃ, agginā daḍḍhaṃ vanaṃ.

For example: 'Buddho bhagavā' (the enlightened Blessed One), 'vaḍḍho bhikkhu' (a senior monk), 'laddhaṃ me pattacīvaraṃ' (a bowl and robe have been obtained by me), 'agginā daḍḍhaṃ vanaṃ' (a forest burnt by fire).

577, 628. Bhanjato gvo ca.

577, 628. And after 'bhanj', 'ggo'.

Bhanjato dhātumhā takārapaccayassa ggo ādeso hoti sahādibyañjanena.

From the root 'bhanj', the suffix 'ta' is replaced by 'ggo' together with the final consonant of the root.

Bhaggo.

'Bhaggo' (broken).

578, 560. Bhujādīnamanto no dvi ca.

578, 560. For 'bhuj', etc., the final consonant becomes 'na', and there is doubling.

Bhujaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto no hoti, tapaccayassa ca dvitāvo hoti.

For roots such as 'bhuj', the final consonant becomes 'na', and the suffix 'ta' is doubled.

Bhutto, bhuttāvī, catto, satto, ratto, yutto, vivitto.

'Bhutto' (eaten), 'bhuttāvī' (having eaten), 'catto' (abandoned), 'satto' (attached), 'ratto' (delighted), 'yutto' (joined), 'vivitto' (secluded).

579, 629. Vaca vāvu.

579, 629. For the root vac, u is an optional substitute.

Vacaiccetassa [M 0.0273] dhātvassa vakārassa ukārādeso hoti anto cakāro no hoti, tapaccayassa ca dvebhāvo hoti vā.

For this root vac, the letter va is replaced by u, the final letter ca is elided, and the suffix ta is optionally doubled.

Vuttaṃ bhagavatā, uttaṃ vā.

Spoken by the Blessed One (vuttaṃ bhagavatā), or uttaṃ.

580, 630. Gupādīnañca.

580, 630. And for gup, etc.

Gupaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto ca byañjano no hoti, tapaccayassa ca dvebhāvo hoti.

For roots such as gup, the final consonant is elided, and the suffix ta is doubled.

Sugutto, catto, litto, santatto, utto, vivitto, sitto. Evamaññepi yojetabbā.

Sugutto (well-guarded), catto (abandoned), litto (smeared), santatto (heated), utto (spoken), vivitto (secluded), sitto (sprinkled). In this way, others should also be formed.

581, 616. Tarādīhi iṇṇo.

581, 616. For tar, etc., there is the substitution iṇṇa.

Taraiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa iṇṇādeso hoti, anto ca byañjano no hoti.

From roots such as tar, the suffix ta is replaced by iṇṇa, and the final consonant is elided.

Taratīti tiṇṇo, uttaratīti uttiṇṇo, saṃpūratīti sampuṇṇo, turatīti tuṇṇo, parijīratīti parijiṇṇo, ākiratīti ākiṇṇo.

Taratīti tiṇṇo (he crosses, hence crossed); uttaratīti uttiṇṇo (he goes across, hence gone across); saṃpūratīti sampuṇṇo (he fills, hence full); turatīti tuṇṇo (he hastens, hence hastened); parijīratīti parijiṇṇo (it decays, hence decayed); ākiratīti ākiṇṇo (he scatters, hence scattered).

582, 631. Bhidādito [M 0.0274] inna anna īṇāvā.

582, 631. For bhid, etc., there are optionally the substitutions inna, anna, and īṇa.

Bhidiiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa inna anna īṇādesā honti vā, anto ca byañjano no hoti.

From roots such as bhid, the suffix ta is optionally replaced by inna, anna, or īṇa, and the final consonant is elided.

Bhinditabboti bhinno, chindīyatīti chinno, ucchindīyitthāti ucchinno, dīyatīti dinno, nisīdatīti nisinno, suṭṭhu chādīyatīti suchanno, khidatīti khinno, rodatīti runno, khīṇā jāti.

Bhinditabboti bhinno (it is to be broken, hence broken); chindīyatīti chinno (it is cut, hence cut); ucchindīyitthāti ucchinno (it was cut off, hence cut off); dīyatīti dinno (it is given, hence given); nisīdatīti nisinno (he sits down, hence seated); suṭṭhu chādīyatīti suchanno (it is well covered, hence well-covered); khidatīti khinno (he is afflicted, hence afflicted); rodatīti runno (he weeps, hence having wept); khīṇā jāti (birth is exhausted).

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Bhijjatīti bhitti.

Why is vā (optionally) used? For the case of bhijjatīti bhitti (it is broken, hence a wall).

583, 617. Susa paca sakato kkha kkā ca.

583, 617. For sus, pac, and sak, there are also the substitutions kkha and kkā.

Susa paca sakaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa kkhakkādesā honti, anto ca byañjano no hoti.

From roots such as sus, pac, and sak, the suffix ta is replaced by kkha and kkā, and the final consonant is elided.

Sussatīti sukkhaṃ, kaṭṭhaṃ, paccatīti pakkaṃ, phalaṃ. Sakati samattheti, pūjetīti vā sakko, sujampati.

Sussatīti sukkhaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ (it dries, hence dry wood); paccatīti pakkaṃ phalaṃ (it ripens, hence ripe fruit). Sakati means he is able (samattheti), or he honors (pūjetīti), hence Sakko, the lord of Sujā (sujampati).

584, 618. Pakkamādīhi nto ca.

584, 618. And for pakkam, etc., there is the substitution nta.

Pakkamaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tapaccayassa ntoādeso hoti, anto ca no hoti.

From roots such as pakkam, the suffix ta is replaced by nta, and the final consonant is elided.

Pakkamatīti [M 0.0275] pakkanto, vibbhamatīti vibbhanto, saṅkanto, khanto, santo, danto, vanto.

Pakkamatīti pakkanto (he departs, hence departed); vibbhamatīti vibbhanto (he wanders about, hence wandered about); saṅkanto (transferred); khanto (patient); santo (calm); danto (tamed); vanto (vomited).

Caggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Teheva dhātūhi tapaccayassanti hoti. Anto ca no hoti. Kanti, khanti. Evaṃ sabbattha.

For what purpose is the inclusion of ca? From those same roots, the suffix ta becomes nti, and the final consonant is elided. For example: kanti (affection), khanti (patience). Thus it is in all cases.

585, 619. Janādīnamā timhi ca.

585, 619. For jan, etc., the final consonant becomes ā, also when the suffix ti follows.

Janaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa byañjanassa āttaṃ hoti tapaccaye pare, timhi ca.

For roots such as jan, the final consonant becomes ā when the suffix ta follows, and also when the suffix ti follows.

Ajanīti jāto, jananaṃ jāti.

Ajanīti jāto (he was born, hence born); jananaṃ jāti (the act of being born is birth).

Timhīti kimatthaṃ? Aññasmimpi paccaye pare ākāranivattanatthaṃ. Janitvā, janitā, janituṃ, janitabbaṃ iccevamādi.

Why is timhi specified? For the purpose of preventing the substitution of ā when other suffixes follow. For example: janitvā (having been born), janitā (one who gives birth), janituṃ (to give birth), janitabbaṃ (what ought to be born), and so forth.

586, 600. Gama khana hana ramādīnamanto.

586, 600. Elision of the final consonant of gam, khan, han, ram, etc.

Gama khana hana ramuiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto byañjano no hoti vā tapaccaye pare timhi ca.

For roots such as gam, khan, han, and ram, the final consonant is optionally elided when the suffix ta follows, and also when the suffix ti follows.

Sundaraṃ nibbānaṃ gacchatīti sugato. Sundaraṃ nibbānaṃ gacchatīti sugati, khataṃ, khati. Upahataṃ, upahati. Rato, rati, mato, mati.

Sundaraṃ nibbānaṃ gacchatīti sugato (he goes to beautiful Nibbāna, hence well-gone); sundaraṃ nibbānaṃ gacchatīti sugati (going to beautiful Nibbāna is a happy destination). Khataṃ (dug), khati (injury). Upahataṃ (struck), upahati (striking). Rato (delighted), rati (delight). Mato (thought), mati (thought, mind).

Vāti [M 0.0276] kimatthaṃ? Ramato, ramati.

Why is vā (optionally) used? For cases like ramato (delighting) and ramati (he delights).

587, 632. Rakāro ca.

587, 632. And the letter r.

Rakāro ca dhātūnamantabhūto no hoti tapaccaye, pare timhi ca.

And the letter r, when it is the final of a root, is elided when the suffix ta follows, and also when the suffix ti follows.

Pakārena karīyatīti pakato, paṭhamaṃ karīyatīti pakati, visarīyatīti visato, visati.

'Done according to a method' is `pakato`; 'done first' is `pakati`; 'scattered' is `visato`; 'it scatters' is `visati`.

588, 620. Ṭhāpānami ī ca.

588, 620. For `ṭhā` and `pā`, `i` and `ī` respectively.

Ṭhā pāiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa ākārassa ikāra īkārādesā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ tapaccaye pare, timhi ca.

For the roots `ṭhā` and `pā`, their final `ā` is replaced by `i` and `ī` respectively when the `ta` suffix follows, and also when `ti` follows.

Yatra ṭhito, ṭhiti, pīto, pīti.

For example: `ṭhito` (stood), `ṭhiti` (standing); `pīto` (drunk), `pīti` (drinking).

589, 621. Hantehi ho hassa ḷo vā adahanahānaṃ.

589, 621. After roots ending in `h`, `ha` [is the substitute for the suffix], and for the `h` [of the root], `ḷa` optionally, excluding `adaha` and `nahāna`.

Hakārantehi dhātūhi tapaccayassa hakārādeso hoti, hakārassa dhātvantassa ḷo hoti vā adahanahānaṃ.

After roots ending in `h`, the substitution `ha` occurs for the `ta` suffix, and the final `h` of the root is optionally substituted by `ḷa`, excluding the roots `adaha` and `nahāna`.

Āruhitthāti āruḷho. Gāḷho, bāḷho. Mūḷo.

'He ascended' is `āruḷho`. `Gāḷho` (firm), `bāḷho` (strong). `Mūḷo` (foolish).

Adahanahānamiti [M 0.0277] kimatthaṃ? Dayhatīti daḍḍho, saṃsuṭṭhu nayhatīti sannaddho.

Why is it said 'excluding `adaha` and `nahāna`'? 'It is burnt' is `daḍḍho`; 'it is thoroughly bound' is `sannaddho`.

Iti kibbidhānakappe tatiyo kaṇḍo.

Thus ends the third section in the chapter on Kṛt suffixes.

Catutthakaṇḍa

The Fourth Section

590, 579. Ṇamhiranjassa jo bhāvakaraṇesu.

590, 579. For `rañj`, `ja` [is the substitute] when `ṇa` follows, in the sense of state or instrument.

Ṇamhi paccaye pare ranjaiccetassa dhātussa antabhūtassa njakārassa joādeso hoti bhāvakaraṇesu.

When the `ṇa` suffix follows, the final `ñj` of the root `rañj` is replaced by `ja`, when denoting state or instrument.

Rañjanaṃ rāgo, ranjanti etenāti rāgo.

`Rañjanaṃ` (coloring) is `rāgo`; 'they are colored by this', thus `rāgo`.

Bhāvakaraṇesūti kimatthaṃ? Ranjatīti raṅgo.

Why is it said 'in the sense of state or instrument'? 'He dyes' is `raṅgo`.

591, 544. Hanassa ghāto.

591, 544. For `han`, `ghāta` [is the substitute].

Hanaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa ghātādeso hoti ṇamhi paccaye pare.

For the entire root `han`, the substitution `ghāta` occurs when the `ṇa` suffix follows.

Upahanatīti upaghāto, gāvo hanatīti goghātako.

'He strikes' is `upaghāto`; 'he kills cows' is `goghātako`.

592, 503. Vadho [M 0.0278] vā sabbattha.

592, 503. Or `vadha` everywhere.

Hanaiccetassa dhātussa vadhādeso hoti vā sabbattha ṭhānesu.

For the root `han`, the substitution `vadha` occurs optionally in all contexts.

Hanatīti vadho, vadhako, avadhi, ahani vā.

'He kills' is `vadho`, `vadhako`; `avadhi` or `ahani` (he killed).

593, 564. Ākārantānamāyo.

593, 564. For roots ending in `ā`, `āya` [is the substitute].

Ākārantānaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa ākārassa āyādeso hoti ṇamhi paccaye pare.

For roots ending in `ā`, the final `ā` is replaced by `āya` when the `ṇa` suffix follows.

Dadātīti dāyako, dānaṃ dātuṃ sīlaṃ yassāti dānadāyī, majjaṃ dātuṃ sīlaṃ yassāti majjadāyī, nagaraṃ yātuṃ sīlaṃ yassāti nagarayāyī.

'He gives' is `dāyako`; 'one whose nature is to give gifts' is `dānadāyī`; 'one whose nature is to give intoxicants' is `majjadāyī`; 'one whose nature is to go to the city' is `nagarayāyī`.

594, 582. Pura samupa parīhi karotissa kha kharā vā tappaccayesuca.

594, 582. After `pura`, `saṃ`, `upa`, and `pari`, for `kar`, `kha` and `khara` are optional substitutes, also before the `ta`-suffixes.

Pura saṃ upa pariiccetehi karotissa dhātussa kha kharādesā honti vā tapaccaye pare, ṇamhi ca.

After these prefixes, `pura`, `saṃ`, `upa`, and `pari`, for the root `kar`, the substitutions `kha` and `khara` optionally occur when the `ta` suffix follows, and also when `ṇa` follows.

Pure karīyatīti purakkhato, sammā karīyatīti saṅkhato, upagantvā karīyatīti upakkhato, parisamantato karotīti parikkhāro, saṃkarīyatīti saṅkhāro.

'It is done before' is `purakkhato`; 'it is well done' is `saṅkhato`; 'having approached, it is done' is `upakkhato`; 'he does all around' is `parikkhāro`; 'it is put together' is `saṅkhāro`.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Upagantvā karotīti upakāro.

Why is 'optionally' stated? 'Having approached, he does' is `upakāro`.

595, 637. Tave [M 0.0279] tunādīsu kā.

595, 637. Before `tave`, `tuna`, etc., `kā`.

Tave tunaiccevamādīsu paccayesu karotissa dhātussa kāādeso hoti vā.

Before these suffixes, `tave`, `tuna`, etc., for the root `kar`, the substitution `kā` occurs optionally.

Kātave, kātuṃ, kattuṃ vā, kātuna, kattuna vā.

For example: `kātave`; `kātuṃ` or `kattuṃ`; `kātuna` or `kattuna`.

596, 551. Gama khana hanādīnaṃ tuṃ tabbādīsu na.

For the roots gama, khana, hana, and so on, 'n' is the substitute before the suffixes tuṃ, tabba, and so on.

Gama khana hanaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa nakāro hoti vā tuṃ tabbādīsu paccayesu.

For roots such as gama, khana, and hana, the letter 'n' is optionally substituted for their final letter when the suffixes tuṃ, tabba, and so on, follow.

Gantuṃ, gamituṃ, gantabbaṃ, gamitabbaṃ. Khantuṃ. Khanituṃ, khantabbaṃ, khanitabbaṃ. Hantuṃ, hanituṃ, hantabbaṃ. Hanitabbaṃ. Mantuṃ, manituṃ, mantabbaṃ, manitabbaṃ.

Gantuṃ, gamituṃ (to go); gantabbaṃ, gamitabbaṃ (to be gone to). Khantuṃ, khanituṃ (to dig); khantabbaṃ, khanitabbaṃ (to be dug). Hantuṃ, hanituṃ (to kill); hantabbaṃ, hanitabbaṃ (to be killed). Mantuṃ, manituṃ (to think); mantabbaṃ, manitabbaṃ (to be thought).

Ādiggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Tunaggahaṇatthaṃ. Gantuna, khantuna, hantuna, mantuna.

For what purpose is 'ādi' (and so on) included? For the purpose of including the suffix 'tuna'. Gantuna (having gone), khantuna (having dug), hantuna (having killed), mantuna (having thought).

597, 641. Sabbehi tunādīnaṃ yo.

After all roots, 'ya' is the substitute for the suffixes tuna, and so on.

Sabbehi dhātūhi tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ yakārādeso hoti vā.

After all roots, the letter 'ya' is optionally substituted for the suffixes tuna, and so on.

Abhivandiya, abhivanditvā, ohāya, ohitvā, upanīya, upanetvā, passiya, passitvā, uddissa, uddisitvā, ādāya, ādiyitvā.

Abhivandiya, abhivanditvā (having paid homage); ohāya, ohitvā (having abandoned); upanīya, upanetvā (having brought near); passiya, passitvā (having seen); uddissa, uddisitvā (having intended); ādāya, ādiyitvā (having taken).

598, 643. Canantehi [M 0.0280] raccaṃ.

After roots ending in 'c' and 'n', 'racca' is the substitute.

Cakāranakārantehi dhātūhi tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ raccādeso hoti vā.

After roots ending in the letters 'c' and 'n', the substitution 'racca' optionally occurs for the suffixes tuna, and so on.

Vivicca, āhacca, uhacca.

Vivicca (having been secluded), āhacca (having struck), uhacca (having removed).

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Hantvā.

For what purpose is 'vā' (optionally) stated? For the form hantvā (having killed).

599, 644. Disā svāna svāntalopo ca.

For the root dis, the substitutes are 'svāna' and 'svā', and there is elision of the final letter.

Disaiccetāya dhātuyā tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ svānasvādesā honti, antalopo ca.

For this root 'dis', the substitutions 'svāna' and 'svā' occur for the suffixes tuna, and so on, and there is also elision of the final letter.

Disvāna, disvā.

Disvāna (having seen), disvā (having seen).

600, 645. Ma ha da bhehi mma yha jja bbha ddhā ca.

After roots ending in m, h, d, and bh, the substitutes are mma, yha, jja, bbha, and ddhā, and there is also elision of the final letter.

Ma ha da bha iccevamantehi dhātūhi tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ mma yha jja bbha ddhā ādesā honti vā antalopo ca.

After roots ending in m, h, d, bh, and so on, the substitutions mma, yha, jja, bbha, and ddhā optionally occur for the suffixes tuna, and so on, and there is also elision of the final letter.

Āgamma, āgamitvā, okkamma. Okkamitvā, paggayha, paggaṇhitvā, uppajja, uppajjitvā, ārabbha, ārabhitvā, āraddha, ārabhitvā.

Āgamma, āgamitvā (having come); okkamma, okkamitvā (having entered); paggayha, paggaṇhitvā (having taken up); uppajja, uppajjitvā (having arisen); ārabbha, ārabhitvā (having begun); āraddha, ārabhitvā (having begun).

601, 334. Taddhitasamāsakitakā [M 0.0281] nāmaṃ vā’ tave tunādīsu ca.

Taddhita, samāsa, and kitaka formations are designated as 'nāma' (nominals), except for those ending in the suffixes tave, tuna, and so on.

Taddhitasamāsakitakaiccevamantā saddānāmaṃva daṭṭhabbā tave tuna tvāna tvādipaccayante vajjetvā.

Words ending in taddhita, samāsa, and kitaka formations should be understood as nominals, excluding those ending in suffixes such as tave, tuna, tvāna, and tvā.

Vāsiṭṭho, pattadhammo, kumbhakāro iccevamādi.

Vāsiṭṭho, pattadhammo, kumbhakāro, and so on.

602, 6. Dumhi garu.

Before a consonant cluster, the preceding syllable is heavy.

Dumhi akkhare yo pubbo akkharo, so garukova daṭṭhabbo.

The syllable that precedes a consonant cluster should be understood as heavy.

Bhitvā, chitvā, datvā, hutvā.

Bhitvā (having broken), chitvā (having cut), datvā (having given), hutvā (having sacrificed).

603, 7. Dīgho ca.

And a long syllable.

Dīgho ca saro garukova daṭṭhabbo.

And a long vowel should be understood as heavy.

Āhāro, nadī, vadhū, te dhammā, opanayiko.

Āhāro (food), nadī (river), vadhū (bride), te dhammā (those phenomena), opanayiko (leading inwards).

604, 684. Akkharehi kāra.

After letters, the suffix 'kāra' is used.

Akkharatthehi akkharābhidheyyehi kārapaccayo hoti payoge sati.

After letters that are to be named, the suffix 'kāra' is employed, according to usage.

A eva akāro, ā eva ākāro, ya eva yakāro.

The letter 'a' is itself 'akāro'; the letter 'ā' is itself 'ākāro'; the letter 'ya' is itself 'yakāro'.

605, 647. Yathāgamamikāro[M 0.0282].

The augment 'i' is inserted according to tradition.

Yathāgamaṃ sabbadhātūhi sabbapaccayesu ikārāgamo hoti.

According to tradition, the insertion of 'i' occurs for all roots before all suffixes.

Kāriyaṃ, bhavitabbaṃ, janitabbaṃ, viditabbaṃ, karitvā, icchitaṃ.

Kāriyaṃ, bhavitabbaṃ, janitabbaṃ, viditabbaṃ, karitvā, icchitaṃ.

606, 642. Dadhantato yo kvaci.

From that which ends in 'd' or 'dh', 'y' sometimes.

Dakāradhakārantāya dhātuyā yathāgamaṃ yakārāgamo hoti kvaci tunādīsu paccayesu.

For a root ending in the letter 'd' or the letter 'dh', the insertion of 'y' occurs according to tradition sometimes in suffixes beginning with 'tu'.

Buddho loke uppajjitvā, dhammaṃ bujjhitvā.

Buddho loke uppajjitvā, dhammaṃ bujjhitvā.

Dadhantatoti kimatthaṃ? Labhitvā.

Why is 'from that which ends in 'd' or 'dh'' stated? For the case of `labhitvā`.

Kvacīti kimatthaṃ? Uppādetvā.

Why is 'sometimes' stated? For the case of `uppādetvā`.

Iti kibbidhānakappe catuttho kaṇḍo.

Thus is the fourth section in the chapter on kṛt-affixes.

Pañcamakaṇḍa

The Fifth Section

607, 578. Niggahita saṃyogādino.

The niggahita is substituted for 'n' at the beginning of a conjunction.

Saṃyogādibhūto nakāro niggahitamāpajjate.

The letter 'n' which is the initial element of a conjunction becomes a niggahita.

Raṅgo, bhaṅgo, saṅgo.

Raṅgo, bhaṅgo, saṅgo.

608, 623. Sabbattha [M 0.0283] ge gī.

Everywhere, for 'ge', 'gī'.

Geiccetassa dhātussa gīādeso hoti sabbattha ṭhāne.

For this root 'ge', the substitution 'gī' occurs in all instances.

Gītaṃ gāyati.

Gītaṃ gāyati.

609, 484. Sadassa sīdattaṃ.

For 'sad', 'sīda'.

Sadaiccetassa dhātussa sīdādeso hoti sabbattha ṭhāne.

For this root 'sad', the substitution 'sīda' occurs in all instances.

Nisinno, nisīdati.

Nisinno, nisīdati.

610, 627. Yajassa sarassi ṭṭhe.

The vowel of 'yaj' becomes 'i' before 'ṭṭha'.

Yajaiccetassa dhātussa sarassa ikārādeso hoti ṭṭhe pare.

For this root 'yaj', its vowel is substituted by the letter 'i' when 'ṭṭha' follows.

Yiṭṭho, yiṭṭhā.

Yiṭṭho, yiṭṭhā.

Ṭṭheti kimatthaṃ? Yajanaṃ.

Why is 'before ṭṭha' stated? For the case of `yajanaṃ`.

611, 608. Hacatutthānamantānaṃ do dhe.

For those ending in 'h' or a fourth-class consonant, 'd' before 'dhe'.

Hacatutthānaṃ dhātvantānaṃ do ādeso hoti dhe pare.

For roots ending in 'h' or a fourth-class consonant, 'd' is substituted when 'dhe' follows.

Sannaddho, kuddho, yuddho, siddho, laddho, āraddho.

Sannaddho, kuddho, yuddho, siddho, laddho, āraddho.

612, 615. Ḍo [M 0.0284] ḍhakāre.

'ḍ' before the letter 'ḍh'.

Hacatutthānaṃ dhātvantānaṃ ḍo ādeso hoti ḍhakāre pare.

For roots ending in 'h' or a fourth-class consonant, 'ḍ' is substituted when the letter 'ḍh' follows.

Dayhatīti daḍḍho, vaḍḍhatīti vuḍḍho.

Dayhatīti daḍḍho, vaḍḍhatīti vuḍḍho.

Ḍhakāreti kimatthaṃ? Dāho.

Why is 'before the letter ḍh' stated? For the case of `dāho`.

613, 583. Gahassa ghara ṇe vā.

For 'gah', 'ghara' is optionally substituted before 'ṇa'.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa gharādeso hoti vā ṇapaccaye pare.

For the root 'gaha', the entire root optionally becomes 'ghara' when the suffix 'ṇa' follows.

Gharaṃ, gharāni.

Gharaṃ, gharāni.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Gāho.

Why 'vā'? Gāho.

614, 581. Dahassa do ḷaṃ.

614, 581. The 'd' of 'daha' becomes 'ḷa'.

Dahaiccetassa dhātussa dakāro ḷattamāpajjate vā ṇapaccaye pare.

For the root 'daha', the letter 'd' optionally becomes 'ḷ' when the suffix 'ṇa' follows.

Paridahanaṃ pariḷāho.

Paridahanaṃ pariḷāho.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Paridāho.

Why 'vā'? Paridāho.

615, 586. Dhātvantassa lopo kvimhi.

615, 586. Elision of the final element of a root before 'kvi'.

Dhātvantassa byañjanassa lopo hoti kvimhi paccaye pare.

The final consonant of a root is elided when the suffix 'kvi' follows.

Bhujena [M 0.0285] gacchatīti, bhujago. Urena gacchatīti urago, turago, saṅkho.

Bhujena gacchatīti, bhujago. Urena gacchatīti urago, turago, saṅkho.

616, 587. Vidante ū.

616, 587. At the end of 'vid', there is 'ū'.

Vidaiccetassa dhātussa ante ūkārāgamo hoti kvimhi paccaye pare.

For the root 'vid', the augment 'ū' occurs at the end when the suffix 'kvi' follows.

Lokaṃ vidati jānātīti lokavidū.

Lokaṃ vidati jānātīti lokavidū.
